238		addRedaction(row, RedactionFileReference)

241	func inspectReferences(row *Declaration, value string) {
242		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
243		patterns := []*regexp.Regexp{wholeOpenCodeEnvPattern}
244		for _, pattern := range patterns {
245			match := pattern.FindStringSubmatch(value)
246			if len(match) == 2 {
247				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialEnvironmentReference, Name: match[1]})
248				return
249			}
250		}
251	}

253	func validEnvironmentName(value string) bool {
254		return len(value) <= maximumReferenceBytes && environmentNamePattern.MatchString(value) && !looksSecretString(value)
255	}
256	
257	func validHeaderName(value string) bool {
258		return len(value) <= maximumReferenceBytes && headerNamePattern.MatchString(value) && !looksSecretString(value)
259	}
260	
261	func setCommand(row *Declaration, command string) {
262		command = strings.TrimSpace(command)
263		if command == "" {
264			return
265		}
266		inspectReferences(row, command)
267		if openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(command) {
268			inspectFileReference(row, command)
269			row.Command = "[dynamic]"
270			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
271			return
272		}
273		if strings.Contains(command, "${") || strings.Contains(command, "{env:") ||
274			dollarPattern.MatchString(command) || percentPattern.MatchString(command) {
275			row.Command = "[dynamic]"
276			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
277			return
278		}
279		normalized := strings.ReplaceAll(command, `\`, "/")
280		basename := path.Base(normalized)
281		if basename == "." || basename == "/" || basename == "" || len(basename) > maximumNameBytes ||
282			!executableNamePattern.MatchString(basename) || strings.ContainsFunc(command, unicode.IsSpace) ||
283			looksSecretString(basename) {
284			row.Command = "[redacted]"
285			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
286			addRedaction(row, RedactionArguments)
287			return
288		}
289		row.Command = basename
290		if basename != command {
291			addRedaction(row, RedactionCommandPath)
292		}
293	}
294	
295	func setEndpoint(row *Declaration, raw string) {
296		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
297		if raw == "" {
298			return
299		}
300		inspectReferences(row, raw)
301		if openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(raw) {
302			inspectFileReference(row, raw)
303			addRedaction(row, RedactionEndpointTemplate)
304			row.Endpoint = "[dynamic]"
305			return
306		}
307		if dollarBracePattern.MatchString(raw) || dollarPattern.MatchString(raw) || percentPattern.MatchString(raw) || openCodeEnvPattern.MatchString(raw) {
308			addRedaction(row, RedactionEndpointTemplate)
309			row.Endpoint = "[dynamic]"
310			return
311		}
312		parsed, err := url.Parse(raw)
313		if err != nil || parsed.Opaque != "" || parsed.Scheme == "" || parsed.Host == "" || !schemePattern.MatchString(parsed.Scheme) || stringContainsControl(parsed.Host) || looksSecretString(parsed.Host) {
314			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidEndpoint)
315			return
316		}
317		if parsed.User != nil {
318			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLUserinfo)
319		}
320		if parsed.RawQuery != "" || parsed.ForceQuery {
321			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLQuery)
322		}
323		if parsed.Fragment != "" {
324			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLFragment)
325		}
326		endpoint := strings.ToLower(parsed.Scheme) + "://" + strings.ToLower(parsed.Host)
327		if parsed.EscapedPath() != "" && parsed.EscapedPath() != "/" {
328			endpoint += "/[path]"
329			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLPath)
330		} else if parsed.EscapedPath() == "/" {
331			endpoint += "/"
332		}
333		row.Endpoint = endpoint
334	}
335	
336	func addCredential(row *Declaration, credential CredentialReference) {
337		if credential.Name != "" && (!utf8.ValidString(credential.Name) || stringContainsControl(credential.Name) || len(credential.Name) > maximumReferenceBytes) {
338			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
339			return
340		}
341		for _, existing := range row.Credentials {
342			if existing == credential {
343				return
344			}
345		}
346		row.Credentials = append(row.Credentials, credential)
347	}
348	
349	func addRedaction(row *Declaration, redaction Redaction) {
350		for _, existing := range row.Redactions {
351			if existing == redaction {
352				return
353			}
354		}
355		row.Redactions = append(row.Redactions, redaction)
356	}
357	
358	func addCoverage(row *Declaration, code DiagnosticCode) {
359		for _, existing := range row.Coverage {
360			if existing.Code == code {
361				return
362			}
363		}
364		row.Coverage = append(row.Coverage, coverage(code))
365	}
366	
367	func addPolicy(row *Declaration, kind PolicyKind, value string, count int) {
368		fact := PolicyFact{Kind: kind, Value: value, Count: count}
369		for _, existing := range row.Policies {
370			if existing == fact {
371				return
372			}
373		}
374		row.Policies = append(row.Policies, fact)
375	}
376	
377	func addBooleanPolicy(row *Declaration, kind PolicyKind, value bool) {
378		addPolicy(row, kind, strconv.FormatBool(value), 0)
379	}
380	
381	func finalizeDeclaration(row *Declaration) {
382		sort.Slice(row.Credentials, func(i, j int) bool {
383			if row.Credentials[i].Kind != row.Credentials[j].Kind {
384				return row.Credentials[i].Kind < row.Credentials[j].Kind
385			}
386			return row.Credentials[i].Name < row.Credentials[j].Name
387		})
388		sort.Slice(row.Redactions, func(i, j int) bool { return row.Redactions[i] < row.Redactions[j] })
389		sort.Slice(row.Policies, func(i, j int) bool {
390			if row.Policies[i].Kind != row.Policies[j].Kind {
391				return row.Policies[i].Kind < row.Policies[j].Kind
392			}
393			if row.Policies[i].Value != row.Policies[j].Value {
394				return row.Policies[i].Value < row.Policies[j].Value
395			}
396			return row.Policies[i].Count < row.Policies[j].Count
397		})
398		sort.Slice(row.Coverage, func(i, j int) bool { return row.Coverage[i].Code < row.Coverage[j].Code })
399	}

18	type tuiFuture[T any] struct {
19		ready chan struct{}
20		value T

24	func startTUIFuture[T any](work func() (T, error)) *tuiFuture[T] {
25		future := &tuiFuture[T]{ready: make(chan struct{})}
26		go func() {
27			future.value, future.err = work()
28			close(future.ready)
29		}()
30		return future

33	func (f *tuiFuture[T]) wait(ctx context.Context) (T, error) {
34		select {
35		case <-ctx.Done():
36			var zero T
37			return zero, ctx.Err()
38		case <-f.ready:
39			return f.value, f.err
40		}
41	}

68		if ctx == nil {
69			ctx = context.Background()
70		}

72		if l.current != nil {

82			loadRuntime = func(ctx context.Context) (tuiRuntimeSnapshot, error) {

84				if err != nil {
85					return tuiRuntimeSnapshot{}, err
86				}
87				snapshot := tuiRuntimeSnapshot{runtime: rt}

90				}
91				finish := appSnapshot.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIRuntimeList, perftrace.Fields{})
92				sessions, listErr := rt.List(ctx)
93				finish(resolverOutcome(listErr))
94				if listErr == nil {

100		}

240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}

50	func (m Model) startLocalLoad() tea.Cmd {
51		if m.actions.Local.Start == nil {
52			return nil
53		}
54		request := LocalLoadRequest{
55			CycleGeneration: m.localGeneration,
56			TasksGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTasks).generation,
57			ReposGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).generation,
58			TriesGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTries).generation,
59			ShowAllTries:    m.showAllTries,
60			ForceSizes:      m.forceSizeReload,
61		}
62		load := m.actions.Local.Start(m.localReadContext(), request)
63		load.Request = request
64		if load.ID == 0 || load.Results == nil {
65			return nil
66		}
67		return waitForLocal(load)
68	}
69	
70	func waitForLocal(load LocalLoad) tea.Cmd {
71		return func() tea.Msg {
72			result, ok := <-load.Results
73			if !ok {
74				return localMsg{load: load, done: true}
75			}
76			return localMsg{load: load, result: result}
77		}
78	}

85				ViewTasks, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
86				len(result.Tasks), result.Err, result.Valid,
87			)
88			if accepted && result.Valid {
89				m.rows = append([]inventory.Row(nil), result.Tasks...)
90			}
91		case ViewRepos:
92			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
93				ViewRepos, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
94				len(result.Repos), result.Err, result.Valid,
95			)
96			if accepted && result.Valid {
97				m.repos = append([]RepoRow(nil), result.Repos...)
98				m.matchRemoteLocals()
99			}
100		case ViewTries:
101			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
102				ViewTries, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
103				len(result.Tries), result.Err, result.Valid,
104			)
105			if accepted && result.Valid {

107				m.matchRemoteLocals()
108			}
109		}

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	### Added
10	
11	- Agent skill inventory is now provider-independent and repository-aware. A
12	  versioned snapshot of the `skills@1.5.23` 77-agent path registry scans the
13	  current checkout, a selected repository, or every canonical repository plus
14	  global scope without executing Node; explicit source checks group shared
15	  Git/ref inputs once and keep local presence/integrity separate from upstream
16	  freshness.
17	- `dev mcp list` and a lazy MCP TUI view inventory static declarations for
18	  Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Output is scope-qualified,
19	  never claims runtime health/effective precedence, and strips command arguments,
20	  environment/header/OAuth values, URL credentials, and indirect file contents.
21	- Wide TASKS tables now show the repository for each row; compact terminals keep
22	  the previous layout and the detail pane continues to show the full repo/path.
23	- Stable releases now render and publish `Formula/dev-cli.rb` to
24	  `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. The release job requires a fine-grained
25	  `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, fails visibly when the distribution update cannot be
26	  published, and has a manual workflow for retrying or backfilling an existing
27	  stable release without creating another tag. Homebrew installs remain
28	  package-manager-owned rather than letting `dev upgrade` overwrite a Cellar
29	  binary.
30	
31	### Fixed
32	
33	- Read-only skill listing no longer treats the presence of `npx` as proof that
34	  the `skills` package is cached. It never runs `npx --no-install skills`, so npm
35	  cannot resolve a missing package from the registry and cancel the inventory.
36	- Repository-scoped skill mutations now require a directly installed `skills`
37	  executable, use the canonical lock key, reject option-like names, and pin the
38	  confirmed checkout through TUI post-update verification. This prevents selected
39	  repositories from substituting an npm-local provider or redirecting a named
40	  update to a broader scope.
41	- Explicit skill source checks terminate Git option parsing and reject unsafe
42	  refs before fetch, preventing lock-controlled refs from becoming Git options.
43	  Native skill/MCP readers reject non-regular files before opening them, unsafe
44	  terminal names never reach tables, and malformed hashes stay unverifiable.
45	- MCP command strings containing inline arguments are now redacted as a whole;
46	  Codex dynamic header helpers, Claude project approval state, OpenCode project
47	  config layers, Eve subagent skills, and MCP policy/required/trust details are
48	  represented without exposing their values.
49	
50	## [0.2.3] - 2026-09-01
51	
52	### Added
53	
54	- The TUI can write an opt-in, versioned performance trace when
55	  `DEV_TUI_TRACE` names an absolute new file. Relative timings distinguish CLI
56	  load, initial view construction, requested-tab cache/live snapshots, aggregate
57	  row counts, producer completion, discarded stale generations, and key-update
58	  work without recording repository/task/host/tool names, paths, commands, key
59	  values, URLs, handles, or raw errors. Traces are bounded, private, local-only,
60	  and written after the alternate screen is restored; activity `stats.db`
61	  remains unchanged.
62	- TASKS, REPOS, and TRY now publish independently from one shared local load
63	  cycle. Each cycle reads task intent, runtime sessions, and repository discovery
64	  once, shares an eight-slot TASKS/REPOS enrichment limit, and lets FLEET and
65	  REMOTE reuse the accepted REPOS snapshot instead of rescanning local projects.
66	
67	### Fixed
68	
69	- TUI construction and rendering no longer wait for runtime auto-detection,
70	  project-root discovery, cache decoding, interactive shell tool probes, or the
71	  passive release refresh. Per-view generations reject late results, cancel
72	  superseded reads, retain usable rows on refresh failure, and distinguish a
73	  successful empty result from no result.
74	- Successful empty forge refreshes now replace obsolete cached repositories;
75	  fleet cache identity includes the SSH port; forge cache identity includes
76	  configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets; GitLab inventory no longer infers its
77	  host from cwd; canceled refreshes cannot commit cache state; oversized or
78	  malformed forge/fleet caches are ignored; and cached repository names cannot
79	  escape `project_root` when cloning.
80	
81	## [0.2.2] - 2026-08-31
82	
83	### Added
84	
85	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch an explicit command to the
86	  exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree.
87	  `--focus` remains an independent opt-in for switching to that workspace;
88	  reuse, fallback, non-Herdr runtimes, non-worktree modes, and `--json` fail
89	  closed without guessing another pane.
90	
91	### Changed
92	
93	- The dashboard's FLEET view now hides this machine by default because REPOS
94	  already provides its richer local inventory. Press `a` to include local rows;
95	  the non-interactive `dev fleet list` contract still includes this machine.
96	
97	### Fixed
98	
99	- REMOTE keeps the top navigation bar visible while cached repositories refresh;
100	  its extra refresh banner is now included in the terminal-height budget.
101	- TASKS no longer opens a stale artifact directory or the canonical checkout for
102	  an unavailable worktree task. Missing/unregistered worktrees point to
103	  `dev sweep`, while a normal COLD worktree task points to explicit `dev resume`.
104	
105	## [0.2.1] - 2026-08-30
106	
107	### Added
108	
109	- `dev repo new` now has a confirmed interactive repository-bootstrap wizard, with
110	  `dev repo create` as an alias; `dev repo clone` can optionally apply the same setup,
111	  and `dev repo setup` safely merges preset files into an existing clean checkout.
112	  A clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/repository argument to `new`/`create` is
113	  acquired as a clone, preserving its history and remote. The no-argument wizard
114	  detects the same references. Its default-no “Customize preset and template options?”
115	  gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` path short while still exposing every detailed
116	  question on request.
117	  Presets live in versioned `scaffolds.toml`, support typed inputs, safe templates,
118	  phased hooks, project skills with setup entrypoints, optional GitHub/GitLab
119	  publication, and explicit stay/cd/runtime/start handoffs. The two recommended
120	  agent skills use reviewed built-in project initializers instead of executing
121	  newly downloaded setup code. Skills with the same source and agent targets are
122	  installed in one provider invocation; the history initializer also adds
123	  `.specstory/.gitignore` rules for machine-local identity/statistics while keeping
124	  session history trackable; existing custom content is preserved and missing managed
125	  rules are appended.
126	- `dev repo new` can seed a new Git history from a safe snapshot of a local directory,
127	  local repository, Git URL, or owner/repository reference. `--template-ref` selects a
128	  branch, tag, or commit and `--template-subdir` selects one confined folder; preset
129	  `template`, `template_ref`, and `template_subdir` fields support catalog repositories
130	  containing several starters. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, and symlinks,
131	  special files, and path traversal are rejected. Plans redact URL userinfo, preview
132	  selected paths, and warn when a local live snapshot is not pinned to a commit.
133	- Repository bootstrap now has `--check-in <auto|commit|stage|none>`. `stage` leaves
134	  generated changes staged for review and seeds lazygit's worktree-local pending
135	  message as a best-effort convenience for lowercase `c`; staged setup cannot be
136	  published, and the `start` handoff still requires committed setup. Presets can set
137	  `initial_check_in`, and project setup defaults can set `repo.setup.check_in`. A draft
138	  write failure is a warning after staging succeeds; it never rolls the index back.
139	- TTY text prompts in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards now use an inline
140	  editor with cursor movement, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux / zellij
11	                a per-host live runtime
12	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
13	```
14	
15	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
16	only human intent Git cannot answer: task **state/owner/next action/context**,
17	stable asset identity, a catalog metadata summary, multiple repository quick
18	notes, and experiment lifecycle. Live Git status stays live; logical size
19	measurements are explicitly disposable cache.
20	
21	## The problem
22	
23	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
24	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
25	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
26	defeats the point of having one.
27	
28	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
29	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
30	
31	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
32	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
33	expected.
34	
35	```
36	$ dev ls
37	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
38	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
39	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
40	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
41	```
42	
43	## Install
44	
45	### Homebrew (macOS)
46	
47	```bash
48	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
49	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
50	```
51	
52	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
53	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
54	Each stable release updates the tap automatically. A Homebrew-owned `dev`
55	never self-replaces: `dev upgrade` reports the matching `brew upgrade` command,
56	which preserves Homebrew's install records, linking, rollback, and cleanup.
57	Maintainers can retry or backfill formula publication for an existing release
58	with `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.
59	
60	### Scoop (Windows)
61	
62	```powershell
63	scoop bucket add dev-cli https://github.com/daviddwlee84/scoop-bucket
64	scoop install dev-cli
65	```
66	
67	The manifest for each release is also attached to the GitHub release as
68	`dev-cli.json` if you prefer `scoop install <url>`.
69	
70	### Go or source
71	
72	```bash
73	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
74	# Pin @v0.2.3 instead when you need a reproducible install.
75	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
76	```
77	
78	Every release also publishes `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/amd64`,
79	`linux/arm64` (`.tar.gz`) and `windows/amd64`, `windows/arm64` (`.zip`) archives
80	with a `SHA256SUMS` file, so a binary can be verified without a Go toolchain.
81	
82	To find out whether the binary you have is current, and to update it:
83	
84	```bash
85	dev version           # what this build is, and whether it is a published release
86	dev version --check    # also ask GitHub for the newest release (cached for a day)
87	dev doctor            # reports the running version alongside every other check
88	dev upgrade --check    # report whether a newer release exists
89	dev upgrade            # download, verify against SHA256SUMS, and replace this binary
90	```
91	
92	`dev upgrade` replaces the binary in place only for a standalone install. If
93	Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` owns the file, it prints that tool's upgrade
94	command instead; release automation advances the Homebrew tap so that command
95	can see every stable tag. Once a day an interactive `dev` command prints a one-line hint
96	when a newer release is cached; set `[update] check = false` in `config.toml`
97	(or export `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`) to silence it. Every network call here is
98	either explicit or a best-effort background refresh — `dev --version` and
99	`dev doctor` stay local and work offline.
100	
101	### Windows
102	
103	`dev` builds and runs on Windows, and core commands work. There is no tmux,
104	Zellij or Herdr there, so `dev` uses the no-multiplexer backend (it prints a
105	`cd` directive the shell wrapper consumes). Use the PowerShell wrapper:
106	
107	```powershell
108	Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)
109	```
110	
111	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
112	them:
113	
114	```bash
115	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
116	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
117	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
118	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
119	```
120	
121	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
122	worktrees, help topics and bundled gitignore templates. Completion never queries
123	a forge or the network.
124	
125	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
126	
127	```bash
128	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
129	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
130	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
131	```
132	
133	```powershell
134	Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)   # PowerShell
135	```
136	
137	A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
138	passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
139	while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
140	the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
141	
142	The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
143	
144	```bash
145	dev skill install
146	dev skill list --all    # native project/global inventory across repositories
147	dev mcp list --all     # static, sanitized MCP declarations for five agents
148	dev doctor             # what works on this machine, and what degrades
149	```
150	
151	Only **git** is required at runtime. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
152	Azure CLI each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent.
153	
154	## Create, clone, or set up a repository
155	
156	Repository bootstrap works from any directory. Bare `dev repo new` opens an
157	interactive flow that chooses the destination under the configured
158	`project_root`, previews the setup, and confirms before writing anything:
159	
160	```bash
161	dev repo new                                  # interactive new-repository flow
162	dev repo create api --preset agent-ready      # `create` is an alias for `new`
163	dev repo new owner/api                        # clear clone reference: preserve history/origin
164	dev repo new api --template owner/starters --template-subdir go/service
165	dev repo new api --check-in stage -m "chore: initialize api"
166	dev repo clone owner/api                      # owner/name or a Git URL
167	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready         # add the same setup to an existing repo
168	```
169	
170	`repo new NAME` keeps the small scripted default: `main`, README, and an
171	initial commit. When the argument is clearly a Git URL, local Git path, or
172	owner/name, however, `new`/`create` routes to the clone flow and preserves the
173	source history and configured remote; `repo clone` remains the explicit spelling.
174	Clone can optionally apply a preset after the checkout exists, while `repo setup` repeat-safely merges native
175	initializers and preset files into a repository you already have. Custom hooks
176	and skill setup remain responsible for their own idempotency. Use `--dry-run`
177	to inspect the available plan without mutating the target repository.
178	
179	`repo new` can also start from a content snapshot rather than an empty tree.
180	`--template` accepts a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name;
181	`--template-ref` selects a branch, tag, or commit, and `--template-subdir`
182	selects a confined folder within the source. The snapshot becomes a fresh Git
183	history: source `.git` metadata is never copied, template files win scaffold
184	conflicts, regular-file modes are preserved, and traversal, symlinks, and
185	special files fail before the destination is created. A local Git working tree
186	without `--template-ref` includes existing tracked files plus untracked,
187	non-ignored files; Git-ignored files are omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots
188	its complete current tree. The same `template`, `template_ref`, and
189	`template_subdir` keys can live in a preset, which makes one starter catalog
190	repository with a preset per subfolder practical.
191	
192	Human confirmation and dry-run plans preview the selected file paths (with a
193	bounded list) and warn when the source is a live local snapshot rather than a
194	commit. URL userinfo is removed from rendered summaries and errors. Filesystem
195	walking and writes are confined relative to held `os.Root` handles, and source
196	file content is read from the handle that was validated instead of reopening a
197	mutable path.
198	
199	Bootstrap's check-in is explicit:
200	
201	| `--check-in` | Result |
202	|---|---|
203	| `commit` | stage and commit generated files, then permit commit-dependent publishing/hooks |
204	| `stage` | `git add -A` for human review, but do not commit or run `after_commit` hooks |
205	| `none` | leave generated files unstaged and uncommitted |
206	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use the preset's compatible default; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
207	
208	`--message` supplies the commit or staged draft message. In `stage` mode dev
209	best-effort writes the worktree-local `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`; current lazygit
210	uses it to prefill lowercase `c`. An existing different draft is preserved with
211	a warning. This is a lazygit integration detail, not Git `commit.template`.
212	Staged setup cannot create an upstream or use the worktree-creating `start`
213	handoff; review and commit it first. The existing `repo setup --commit` remains
214	a compatibility spelling for `--check-in=commit`. If the lazygit draft cannot
215	be written, dev reports a warning but keeps the successfully staged index for
216	manual review and commit.
217	
218	The built-in `agent-ready` preset adds a starter `AGENTS.md`, a common
219	`.gitignore` section, and project-scoped Claude plans. If selected, the optional
220	`agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` skills are installed and
221	dev's reviewed built-in initializers create the pre-commit/gitleaks and
222	TODO/backlog/pitfalls surfaces during bootstrap; setup does not wait for a later
223	agent to happen to trigger the skill. The history initializer also ensures
224	`.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's machine-local
225	`.project.json` and generated `statistics.json`—not `.specstory/history/`, which
226	remains part of the review trail. Existing custom ignore content and file mode
227	are preserved; only missing managed rules are appended. Skills with the same
228	source and identical agent targets are sent to the installer together, while
229	each skill's declared setup still runs in its own phase. Presets may also declare
230	typed inputs, repository-contained file templates, and ordered
231	`before_commit`/`after_commit`/`after_remote` hooks.
232	
233	When `gh` or `glab` is installed and authenticated, the wizard can create a
234	GitHub or GitLab upstream using the local repository name and description,
235	choose its namespace and visibility, add `origin`, and optionally push the
236	initial/current branch. Local-only is the default and published repos
237	default private. A forge or push failure leaves the local repository and any
238	already-created upstream intact, with recovery information instead of deleting
239	work.
240	
241	TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards support
242	inline insertion plus Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, and Esc/Ctrl-C
243	cancellation. Arrow keys are interpreted by the editor rather than appearing
244	as literal `^[[C`/`^[[D`; piped and buffered non-TTY input keeps its existing
245	line-oriented behavior.
246	
247	The no-argument new-repository wizard places detailed file, template, input,
248	and skill questions behind a default-no “Customize preset and template
249	options?” gate. The normal `agent-ready` path therefore uses its reviewed
250	defaults; answer yes when you want to override individual choices.
251	
252	The final handoff is explicit:
253	
254	| Handoff | Result |
255	|---|---|
256	| `stay` | print the result and leave the shell where it is |
257	| `cd` | enter the repository through the trusted `shell-init` wrapper |
258	| `open` | open the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime; fall back to `cd` when runtime is `none` |
259	| `start` | continue into the existing `dev start` task wizard with this repository fixed |
260	
261	Neither bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. They
262	prepare the repository, checkout, and optional runtime surface. An explicit
263	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch one command to a
264	new first-class Herdr root pane; it never chooses an agent profile or permission
265	mode on the user's behalf.
266	
267	Global custom presets live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`. A project
268	may commit `.dev-cli/config.toml` for allowlisted worktree/setup wizard defaults
269	and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` for project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
270	setup. Project files cannot override host paths, runtime selection, forge
271	inventory, credentials, state, stats, update policy, or TUI policy. Legacy
272	`.dev.toml` worktree settings remain readable; the `.dev-cli` files win when
273	both are present. See [Commands and configuration](docs/reference/commands-config.md#repository-bootstrap)
274	for the schema, precedence, and executable-config trust boundary.
275	
276	## The lifecycle
277	
278	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
279	|---|---|---|---|
280	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
281	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session normally closed | back within days |
282	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
283	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | **MERGED**, waiting for external retirement |
284	
285	READY/MERGED/RETIRED are derived milestones, not new persisted task states.
286	An agent prepares and exits; an external coordinator integrates and retires it.
287	
288	```bash
289	dev start                                            # interactive managed-task wizard
290	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main     # non-interactive fast path → hot
291	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main \
292	  --run 'specstory run codex -c "codex"' --focus      # dispatch, then switch to the exact new pane
293	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip      # → warm; self-runtime stays alive until exit
294	dev park --cold --push                               # → cold, only from outside the target runtime
295	dev resume "token refresh"                           # → hot, rebuilt if needed
296	
297	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
298	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped # manual post-wrapper proof
299	dev done                                             # TTY finish wizard
300	dev done --ff                                        # → done/MERGED; runtime + worktree kept
301	dev retire "token refresh" --delete-branch           # external close/wait/remove → RETIRED
302	
303	dev done --pr                                        # open review; keep task/worktree
304	dev done --merged --base-ref origin/main             # verify commit-preserving merge
305	dev sweep                                            # report drift and cleanup-pending work
306	dev sweep --merged-worktrees                         # from main: audit contained linked worktrees
307	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply                 # confirm each safe retirement
308	```
309	
310	On a TTY, bare `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind and classifies every
311	staged, unstaged and untracked path against the base before offering
312	commit-all, discard-all or cancel. Unique discard requires typing `DROP`;
313	scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or `--dirty=discard --yes`.
314	
315	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
316	
317	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
318	
319	```bash
320	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
321	dev repo open api
322	
323	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
324	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
325	
326	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
327	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
328	
329	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
330	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
331	```
332	
333	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
334	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
335	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
336	
337	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
338	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
339	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
340	the parallel task depends on them.
341	
342	### Guarded Git transactions
343	
344	`dev git` wraps only operations that need durable receipts or failure recovery;
345	it does not replace ordinary Git aliases:
346	
347	```bash
348	dev git uncommit              # soft reset; save old OID/message receipt
349	dev git recommit              # commit -C the receipt, then clear it
350	dev git pull-rebase           # exact stash OID + --index restore; never stash@{0}
351	dev git amend-all             # add -A + amend --no-edit, with normal hooks
352	dev git amend-all --exclude-agent-artifacts
353	dev git setup --print         # print optional aliases; never edit config
354	```
355	
356	Published commit rewrites require `--rewrite-published`. `amend-all` includes
357	agent artifacts by default only when a project scanner is present (or the user
358	explicitly accepts `--allow-unscanned-artifacts`).
359	
360	For automation, `dev start … --json` emits one pure creation object with absolute
361	paths and transient runtime facts. Only a newly created first-class Herdr
362	worktree with a non-empty exact `root_pane_id` is a launch target; reuse,
363	fallback, Tmux, none, or missing pane data fails closed. Worktree starts use the
364	same `repo/branch` label as `dev wt create` and pins the Git-derived parent
365	checkout with Herdr `--cwd`, preserving native nested repository/worktree
366	grouping without separate provenance metadata.
367	
368	For a human one-liner, `--run '<shell command>'` uses that same exact-pane proof
369	and sends the command to the new worktree's interactive shell. It is incompatible
370	with `--json`, `--direct`, `--branch-only`, and non-Herdr runtimes. It only
371	confirms dispatch, never waits for command completion or reports its exit code;
372	add `--focus` when the caller should switch or attach after dispatch.
373	
374	Herdr-aware writer claims—`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
375	`resume`—reject another recognized agent in the same canonical Git worktree.
376	Every state, including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied. Pure
377	`repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter reuse/focus the live owner without
378	claiming another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is only for explicitly
379	coordinated disjoint ownership; normal new-worktree creation remains allowed.
380	
381	Task runtime handles carry their backend name and are validated against live
382	checkout coverage before reuse or close. Destructive cleanup additionally
383	resolves every covering pane. A caller inside the target, a mixed workspace, or
384	a working/blocked/waiting agent always stops retirement; unknown status needs an
385	external `--close-unknown`. `dev done` never closes or removes anything.
386	
387	### The dashboard
388	
389	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens seven lists, switched with `tab`:
390	
391	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
392	- **REPOS** — durable repositories under the scan roots, with branch, dirty
393	  state, owned size, runtime, worktrees and task tally. What do I have here.
394	- **FLEET** — repository and activity facts from configured remote machines.
395	  The TUI hides this machine by default because REPOS already shows it; `a`
396	  includes local rows. Enter opens the remote checkout through Herdr when
397	  possible, then SSH. `dev fleet list` continues to include this machine.
398	- **TRY** — dated scratch experiments, including non-Git folders, with durable
399	  tags/notes and explicit active/deprecated/archived/graduated state.
400	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through authenticated forge CLIs, including

5	
6	# dev-cli
7	
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10	
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux / zellij
15	                a per-host live runtime
16	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
17	```
18	
19	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
20	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
21	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
22	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
23	
24	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
25	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
26	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
27	abandoning a task.
28	
29	## Check it is there first
30	
31	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
32	
33	```bash
34	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
35	dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
36	```
37	
38	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
39	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
40	hard-depend on one.
41	
42	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
43	
44	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
45	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
46	
47	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
50	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
51	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
52	
53	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
54	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
55	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
56	
57	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
58	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
59	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
60	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
61	
62	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
63	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
64	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
65	
66	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## The task lifecycle
69	
70	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
73	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
74	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
75	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
76	
77	```bash
78	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
79	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
80	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
81	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
82	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
83	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
84	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
85	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
86	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
87	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
88	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
89	```
90	
91	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
92	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
93	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
94	
95	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`. Before integrating or deleting an
96	agent-owned checkout, read `references/agent-retirement.md`.

98	## Pick the task's checkout mode
99	
100	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
101	
102	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
103	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
104	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
105	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
106	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
107	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
108	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
109	
110	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
111	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
112	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
113	
114	## Parallel background work
115	
116	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
117	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
118	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
119	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
120	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
121	
122	For a human one-liner, `dev start --run '<shell command>'` uses the same exact
123	new-worktree/root-pane proof and `--focus` independently switches afterward.
124	It does not choose a launcher profile, permission mode, agent name, or wait
125	policy; use the full JSON workflow when those require separate validation.
126	
127	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
128	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
129	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
130	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
131	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
132	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
133	
134	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
135	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
136	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
137	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.

189	dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
190	
191	dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
192	dev tries mark redis-streams --add important  # durable personal metadata
193	dev tries archive redis-streams               # reversible; does not delete
194	dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
195	
196	dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
197	dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
198	dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
199	dev summary                # current machine-wide agent context
200	dev journal                # today's agent-ready development journal
201	dev journal --since 7d --metrics | opencode run "summarize this"
202	dev cache list             # regenerable forge/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-index caches
203	dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages; dev help wt also works
204	```
205	
206	Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
207	
208	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
209	
210	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
211	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
212	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
213	
214	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
215	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
216	
217	```bash
218	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
219	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
220	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
221	```
222	
223	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
224	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
225	
226	## Creating and setting up repositories
227	
228	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
229	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
230	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
231	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
232	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
233	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
234	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
235	directly.
236	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
237	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
238	exact source tree.
239	
240	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
241	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
242	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
243	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
244	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
245	`start`.
246	
247	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
248	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
249	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
250	
251	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
252	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
253	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
254	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
255	
256	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
257	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
258	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
259	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
260	
261	## Dashboard and forge inventory
262	
263	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY, REMOTE, SKILLS and MCP views, switched
264	with tab or vim-style h/l. Wide TASKS tables show `REPO`; compact layouts keep it
265	in detail. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
266	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
267	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
268	
269	The initial view never waits for runtime/project-root resolution, cache decoding,
270	or shell tool probes. TASKS/REPOS/TRY publish independently from one shared local
271	cycle; optional tabs remain lazy. Refreshes are generation-scoped: late results
272	are ignored, failed refreshes keep usable rows, and valid empty results clear
273	obsolete rows. For a one-run diagnostic, set `DEV_TUI_TRACE` to an absolute new
274	file. The private bounded trace is written after TUI teardown with relative
275	startup/view timings and aggregate row counts only; it excludes names, paths,
276	commands, key values, URLs, handles and raw errors, and never enters `stats.db`
277	or a network sink. SKILLS and MCP reuse the accepted REPOS snapshot and add a
278	distinct startup linked checkout. Skill listing uses the native versioned
279	77-agent path registry and never runs Node/`npx`; `c` is the explicit grouped
280	upstream check. MCP inventories only sanitized static declarations for Claude
281	Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode—it never starts or health-checks a
282	server and never exposes secret-bearing values. Full detail:
283	`references/agent-capabilities.md`.
284	
285	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
286	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
287	account can access. A private cache is decoded after the first view; stale rows
288	stay searchable while refresh runs. Malformed/oversized payloads and caches
289	fingerprinted for another configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored.
290	GitLab uses explicit `GITLAB_HOST`/`GLAB_HOST` (default `gitlab.com`) instead of
291	cwd inference; a successful empty refresh clears obsolete rows. `/` filters provider,
292	owner/name, visibility and description, with `vis:private` for an exact visibility match. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
293	confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
294	for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query and `--refresh`
295	forces a complete synchronization.
296	
297	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
298	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
299	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
300	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
301	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
302	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
303	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
304	does not launch the receiving agent.
305	
306	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
307	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
308	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
309	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
310	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
311	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
312	one repository.
313	
314	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
315	
316	```toml
317	[[forge.azure_devops]]
318	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
319	project = "Platform"
320	```
321	
322	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
323	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
324	
325	FLEET reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot for the local host, then calls each
326	configured host's own `dev` over SSH, preserving its XDG paths. If the current
327	REPOS generation is still loading, FLEET waits while keeping usable cached rows
328	visible rather than rescanning local repositories. The TUI hides this machine
329	by default because REPOS already shows its richer local state; `a` includes
330	local rows. Host cache identity includes the SSH port. `dev fleet list` remains
331	local plus remote. Enter prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an
332	SSH login shell.
333	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
334	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
335	
336	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
337	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
338	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
339	expand linked worktrees; children
340	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
341	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
342	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
343	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
344	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
345	it.
346	
347	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
348	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
349	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
350	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
351	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
352	
353	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
354	explicitly. Runtime
355	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
356	
357	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
358	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
359	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
360	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
361	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
362	the binding should be portable across machines.
363	
364	## Repository quick notes
365	
366	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
367	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
368	
369	Quick notes are multiple timestamped Markdown files under configured
370	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/` (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`); the
371	catalog ID attaches them to the canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and
372	moves. `dev` does not synchronize notes or catalog state, so cross-host
373	attachment requires syncing both. SQLite FTS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db`
374	is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts and the next search rebuilds it.
375	
376	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
377	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
378	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
379	
380	## Editing configuration
381	
382	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
383	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
384	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
385	
386	## Rules for agents
387	
388	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
389	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
390	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
391	
392	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
393	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
394	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
395	   history unattended.
396	
397	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
398	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
399	   user before overriding it.
400	
401	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
402	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
403	   for them. For merged worktree cleanup, run `dev sweep --merged-worktrees`
404	   from the canonical main checkout, present every candidate and blocker as a
405	   QA question, and use `--apply --yes` only after the user explicitly approves
406	   that exact set. Branch deletion remains a separate `--delete-branches` opt-in.
407	
408	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
409	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
410	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
411	
412	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
413	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
414	   pushed.
415	
416	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
417	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
418	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
419	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
420	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
421	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
422	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
423	
424	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
425	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
426	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
427	
428	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
429	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json` or the same
430	   internal proof used by explicit `dev start --run`. Never infer from
431	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
432	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
433	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
434	
435	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
436	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
437	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
438	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
439	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
440	
441	11. **Cleanup is external, never self-triggered by agent state.** Herdr `done`
442	    means a turn settled. Arm and finalize exact artifacts first; `dev done`
443	    integrates only, and `dev retire` must run outside the target workspace.
444	    Never run raw `git worktree remove --force` against the caller's checkout.
445	
446	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
447	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
448	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
449	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
450	
451	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
452	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
453	   their judgement, not yours.
454	
455	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
456	   configured `paths.state_dir/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes`
457	   and reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation, and `dev`
458	   does not synchronize note/catalog state between hosts.
459	
460	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
461	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
462	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-FTS caches.
463	
464	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
465	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
466	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
467	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
468	
469	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
470	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
471	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
472	
473	18. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
474	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
475	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
476	   does not duplicate them.
477	
478	19. **Never bypass `.dev-cli` project-config trust.** Inspect the rendered hooks
479	    and skill entrypoints, then use `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. A changed
480	    executable hash is a new decision. Pre-commit/gitleaks inspect generated
481	    content; they do not make an untrusted command safe to execute. Legacy
482	    `.dev.toml` remains a compatibility surface rather than acquiring this trust
483	    contract retroactively.
484	
485	## When to use this skill
486	
487	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
488	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
489	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
490	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
491	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
492	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
493	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
494	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
495	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
496	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
497	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
498	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
499	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
500	
501	## When NOT to use it
502	
503	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
504	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
505	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
506	  `dev start --json` and explicit `--run` cross-tool launch paths remain here.
507	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
508	
509	## Reference files
510	
511	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
512	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
513	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
514	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
515	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
516	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
517	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
518	  work moves between machines.
519	- `references/agent-retirement.md` — prepare/finalize/integrate/retire, caller
520	  safety, exact transcript handling and orphaned-runtime recovery.
521	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
522	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
523	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
524	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
525	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
526	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
527	- `references/repository-bootstrap.md` — new/clone/setup presets, project
528	  overrides, skill initialization, upstream publishing, trust and handoff.
529	
530	## Gotchas
531	
532	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
533	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
534	  (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
535	  file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
536	  `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
537	  wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
538	  shell — that is not a bug.
539	- **Windows runs without a multiplexer.** There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on
540	  Windows, so the runtime backend is always `none`; `dev fleet open` starts a
541	  child shell instead of replacing the process. `dev upgrade` self-replaces only
542	  a standalone install and otherwise prints the Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`
543	  command. Stable releases advance the Homebrew tap; never overwrite its Cellar
544	  binary manually.
545	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
546	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
547	  skips that and leaves you to it.
548	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
549	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
550	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
551	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
552	- **A repository template is a snapshot, not a clone.** Source Git metadata,
553	  remotes and history are excluded. A local Git worktree without a ref includes
554	  tracked plus nonignored untracked files; a non-Git directory includes its
555	  complete current tree. Human plans preview paths and warn about live unpinned
556	  sources. URL userinfo is redacted, while held root/directory/file handles
557	  confine traversal. Symlinks, special files, traversal and source changes fail
558	  closed, and the snapshot applies only to an otherwise-empty new repo.
559	- **Lazygit commit drafts are a best-effort adapter.** `--check-in=stage` writes
560	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in that worktree's Git directory so lowercase `c`
561	  can preload the proposed message. This is not `commit.template` or
562	  `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, uppercase `C` and other clients need not read it, and an
563	  existing different draft is preserved. Draft write/sync failure is a warning,
564	  not rollback: the successfully staged index remains ready for manual commit.
565	- **Agent history remains reviewable.** Built-in `agent-history-hygiene` seeds
566	  `.specstory/.gitignore` only for machine-local `.project.json` and generated
567	  `statistics.json`; it does not ignore `.specstory/history/*.md`. An existing
568	  nested ignore keeps its custom content and mode while missing required rules
569	  are appended. Correct any broader parent `.specstory/` rule explicitly.
570	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
571	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
572	- **Bare `dev done` is interactive only on a TTY.** It reports branch relation
573	  and dirty-content equivalence, then offers commit/discard and FF/PR/cleanup.
574	  Non-interactive use remains report-only without `--ff`/`--pr`. Unique discard
575	  requires `DROP` or explicit `--dirty=discard --yes`.
576	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
577	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
578
```

19	dev skill list --all --check --json

10	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project --json
11	```
12	
13	The initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
14	Project, local, user, custom, system, and managed declarations remain separate
15	rows. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` describe fields present in source
16	configuration; they are not connectivity or authentication health.
17	
18	The scanner never executes agent MCP list/debug commands, configured commands,
19	header helpers, servers, or URLs. It does not expand environment placeholders,
20	read OAuth/token stores, or dereference OpenCode `{file:…}` values. Normalized
21	output retains only safe facts such as the command basename, credential reference
22	names, argument count, and a URL scheme/host with userinfo, path, query, and
23	fragment redacted.
24	
25	Static inventory cannot reproduce every runtime layer. Plugin caches, hosted
26	connectors, remote organization configuration, inline
27	`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted and reported
28	as coverage limits. Duplicate names in different files/scopes are not merged
29	into a guessed effective configuration.
30	
31	The MCP TUI view reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot, includes the exact startup
32	linked worktree when distinct, and offers navigation, filtering, and reload only.
33	It never starts, connects, adds, removes, or authenticates a server. Filters
34	include `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, and `state:`.
35

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./internal/help/topics/skills.md`

```text
1	# Agent skills
2	
3	A provider-independent inventory of agent skills in the current checkout, any
4	selected repository, every configured repository, and global agent paths.
5	
6	## Reading the inventory
7	
8	```bash
9	dev skill list                         # current checkout + global
10	dev skill list --repo api --project    # one repository/checkout
11	dev skill list --all                   # canonical repositories + global once
12	dev skill list --all --check --json    # explicit upstream freshness check
13	```
14	
15	Project/global copies of one skill remain separate rows. Repository identity,
16	logical installations, compatible agent paths, local presence/integrity, source,
17	and update freshness are reported independently.
18	
19	## Where the data comes from
20	
21	Reads are native. `dev` scans a versioned snapshot of all 77 paths in the
22	`skills@1.5.23` registry plus project/global lock files. It never runs `skills`,
23	Node, npm, `npx`, agent detectors, or project code to list inventory. Shared
24	paths such as `.agents/skills` report registry compatibility; they do not claim
25	the corresponding agent executables are installed.
26	
27	Project scope defaults to the exact current checkout, including a linked
28	worktree. `--all` scans canonical configured repositories. The TUI reuses its
29	accepted REPOS snapshot and additionally includes the startup checkout when it
30	is a distinct linked worktree. Global paths are scanned once.
31	
32	A missing lock is normal. Malformed, unreadable, oversized, unsupported, or
33	ambiguous lock data is diagnosed without hiding valid neighboring rows. Absolute
34	`$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` is the global lock when configured;
35	otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` is used.
36	
37	## Freshness and integrity
38	
39	Listing is local-only. `--check` (or TUI `c`) is the explicit network operation:
40	it groups equal Git source/ref pairs and compares current upstream content with
41	the lock-recorded hash without modifying installed files or locks.
42	
43	`current` therefore means upstream still matches the lock record. It does not
44	prove installed bytes are intact. Presence is tracked separately, and only the
45	embedded `dev-cli` skill can verify that every bundled file matches; additional user files are not treated as drift.
46	
47	## Updating
48	
49	```bash
50	dev skill add
51	dev skill update <name> --project [--repo api]
52	dev skill update <name> --global
53	```
54	
55	Only explicit add/install/update operations invoke the provider to change
56	skills. They require a directly installed `skills` executable and may access the
57	network; `dev doctor` may separately run that trusted executable's `--version`
58	probe. `dev` never invokes `npx` from a repository checkout, so a local
59	`node_modules/.bin/skills` cannot substitute for the provider. Updates require one explicit scope
60	and confirmation (or `--yes`); no bulk update is implied by inventory.
61	
62	`dev doctor` reports native inventory separately from the optional mutation
63	provider.
64	
65	## dev's own skill is different
66	
67	The `dev-cli` skill is compiled into the binary. It updates when `dev` updates,
68	not through the upstream provider, and `make install` links it into agent
69	directories. The inventory marks it as directly managed and can verify its local
70	content against the embedded files.
71
```
</details></tool-use>
