213	func skillLock(row Skill) *LockMetadata { return row.Lock }
214	
215	func sourceURL(entry LockMetadata) (string, bool) {
216		if entry.SourceType == "local" || entry.SourceType == "node_modules" || entry.SourceType == "well-known" {
217			return "", false
218		}
219		if entry.SourceURL != "" {
220			return entry.SourceURL, true
221		}
222		if entry.SourceType == "github" {
223			parts := strings.Split(strings.Trim(entry.Source, "/"), "/")
224			if len(parts) >= 2 {
225				return "https://github.com/" + parts[0] + "/" + parts[1] + ".git", true
226			}
227		}
228		if strings.Contains(entry.Source, "://") || strings.HasSuffix(entry.Source, ".git") {
229			return entry.Source, true
230		}
231		return "", false
232	}
233	
234	func cloneSourceCheckout(ctx context.Context, url, ref string) (sourceCheckout, error) {
235		dir, err := cloneSource(ctx, url, ref)
236		if err != nil {
237			return sourceCheckout{}, err
238		}
239		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
240		return sourceCheckout{dir: dir, cleanup: func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(parent) }}, nil
241	}
242	
243	func cloneSource(ctx context.Context, url, ref string) (string, error) {
244		if !safeFetchRef(ref) {
245			return "", errors.New("skill source ref is not safe to pass to Git")
246		}
247		parent, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-skill-check-*")
248		if err != nil {
249			return "", err
250		}
251		dir := filepath.Join(parent, "source")
252		if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, "", "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", "--", url, dir); err != nil {
253			_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
254			return "", err
255		}
256		if ref != "" {
257			if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "fetch", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "--", "origin", ref); err != nil {
258				_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
259				return "", err
260			}
261			if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", "FETCH_HEAD"); err != nil {
262				_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
263				return "", err
264			}
265		}
266		return dir, nil
267	}
268	
269	func safeFetchRef(ref string) bool {
270		if ref == "" {
271			return true
272		}
273		if strings.TrimSpace(ref) != ref || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "-") {
274			return false
275		}
276		return !strings.ContainsFunc(ref, func(r rune) bool {
277			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf)
278		})
279	}
280	
281	func normalizeRecordedHash(metadata *LockMetadata) {
282		metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = "", ""
283		computed := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.ComputedHash)
284		folder := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.SkillFolderHash)
285		content := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.ContentHash)
286	
287		setFolderHash := func(hash string) bool {
288			switch {
289			case validHexHash(hash, 40):
290				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "git-tree"
291				return true
292			case validHexHash(hash, 64):
293				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "sha256-folder"
294				return true
295			default:
296				return false
297			}
298		}
299		if metadata.Scope == ScopeGlobal {
300			if setFolderHash(folder) {
301				return
302			}
303			if validHexHash(content, 64) {
304				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
305			}
306			return
307		}
308		if validHexHash(computed, 64) {
309			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = computed, "sha256-folder"
310			return
311		}
312		// Scope-less package tests and older callers may still supply either global
313		// representation; parsed project-v1 locks never reach this branch with them.
314		if metadata.Scope == "" && setFolderHash(folder) {
315			return
316		}
317		if metadata.Scope == "" && validHexHash(content, 64) {
318			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
319		}
320	}
321	
322	func validHexHash(value string, length int) bool {
323		if len(value) != length {
324			return false
325		}
326		_, err := hex.DecodeString(value)
327		return err == nil
328	}
329	
330	func checkOneResult(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, row Skill) (UpdateStatus, string) {
331		entry := skillLock(row)
332		if entry == nil {
333			return UpdateUnknown, "skill has no lock metadata"
334		}
335		folder, ok := safeSkillFolder(entry.SkillPath)
336		if !ok {
337			return UpdateUnknown, "invalid skill path in lock entry"
338		}
339		abs := filepath.Join(repoDir, filepath.FromSlash(folder))
340		info, err := os.Stat(abs)
341		if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
342			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
343				return UpdateMissing, "skill path no longer exists upstream"
344			}
345			return UpdateFailed, "could not inspect upstream skill path"
346		}
347		if !insidePath(repoDir, abs) {
348			return UpdateUnknown, "skill path escapes the fetched source"
349		}
350	
351		expected, kind := entry.RecordedHash, entry.HashKind
352		if expected == "" {
353			copy := *entry
354			normalizeRecordedHash(&copy)
355			expected, kind = copy.RecordedHash, copy.HashKind
356		}
357		var actual string
358		var hashErr error
359		switch kind {
360		case "git-tree":
361			spec := "HEAD^{tree}"
362			if folder != "" {
363				spec = "HEAD:" + folder
364			}
365			actual, hashErr = gitOutput(ctx, repoDir, "rev-parse", spec)
366		case "sha256-folder":
367			actual, hashErr = folderHashContext(ctx, abs)
368		case "sha256-skill-file":
369			actual, hashErr = fileHashContext(ctx, filepath.Join(abs, "SKILL.md"))
370		}
371		if hashErr != nil {
372			if ctx.Err() != nil {
373				return UpdateFailed, "update check canceled"
374			}
375			return UpdateFailed, "could not compute upstream content hash"
376		}
377		if expected == "" || actual == "" {
378			return UpdateUnknown, "lock entry has no comparable content hash"
379		}
380		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(actual), strings.TrimSpace(expected)) {
381			return UpdateCurrent, "matches the recorded upstream content"
382		}
383		return UpdateAvailable, "upstream content changed"
384	}
385	
386	func safeSkillFolder(skillPath string) (string, bool) {
387		p := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(skillPath), "\\", "/")
388		if p == "" || strings.ContainsRune(p, '\x00') {
389			return "", false
390		}
391		// filepath.VolumeName follows the host OS, so reject a Windows drive prefix
392		// explicitly even when dev is checking a lock file on Unix.
393		if len(p) >= 2 && p[1] == ':' && ((p[0] >= 'a' && p[0] <= 'z') || (p[0] >= 'A' && p[0] <= 'Z')) {
394			return "", false
395		}
396		if strings.EqualFold(path.Base(p), "SKILL.md") {
397			p = path.Dir(p)
398		}
399		if p == "." {
400			p = ""
401		}
402		clean := path.Clean(p)
403		if clean == "." {
404			clean = ""
405		}
406		if path.IsAbs(clean) || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") || filepath.VolumeName(filepath.FromSlash(clean)) != "" {
407			return "", false
408		}
409		return clean, true
410	}
411	
412	func folderHash(dir string) (string, error) {
413		return folderHashContext(context.Background(), dir)
414	}
415	
416	func folderHashContext(ctx context.Context, dir string) (string, error) {
417		type file struct {
418			name string
419			path string
420		}
421		var files []file
422		err := filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(filename string, entry fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
423			if err != nil {
424				return err
425			}
426			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
427				return ctxErr
428			}
429			if entry.IsDir() && filename != dir && (entry.Name() == ".git" || entry.Name() == "node_modules") {
430				return filepath.SkipDir
431			}
432			if entry.Type().IsRegular() {
433				relative, err := filepath.Rel(dir, filename)
434				if err != nil {
435					return err
436				}
437				files = append(files, file{name: filepath.ToSlash(relative), path: filename})
438			}
439			return nil
440		})
441		if err != nil {
442			return "", err
443		}
444		collator := collate.New(language.English)
445		sort.SliceStable(files, func(i, j int) bool {
446			if order := collator.CompareString(files[i].name, files[j].name); order != 0 {
447				return order < 0
448			}
449			return files[i].name < files[j].name
450		})
451		hash := sha256.New()
452		buffer := make([]byte, 32*1024)
453		for _, file := range files {
454			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
455				return "", err
456			}
457			_, _ = io.WriteString(hash, file.name)
458			input, err := os.Open(file.path)
459			if err != nil {
460				return "", err
461			}
462			for {
463				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
464					_ = input.Close()
465					return "", err
466				}
467				read, readErr := input.Read(buffer)
468				if read > 0 {
469					_, _ = hash.Write(buffer[:read])
470				}
471				if readErr != nil {
472					_ = input.Close()
473					if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
474						break
475					}
476					return "", readErr
477				}
478			}
479		}
480		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
481	}
482	
483	func fileHashContext(ctx context.Context, filename string) (string, error) {
484		info, err := os.Lstat(filename)
485		if err != nil {
486			return "", err
487		}
488		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
489			return "", errors.New("skill hash target is not a regular file")
490		}
491		input, err := os.Open(filename)
492		if err != nil {
493			return "", err
494		}
495		defer input.Close()
496		openedInfo, err := input.Stat()
497		if err != nil || !openedInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
498			return "", errors.New("opened skill hash target is not a regular file")
499		}
500		currentInfo, err := os.Lstat(filename)
501		if err != nil || !os.SameFile(openedInfo, currentInfo) {
502			return "", errors.New("skill hash target changed while opening")
503		}
504		hash := sha256.New()
505		buffer := make([]byte, 32*1024)
506		for {
507			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
508				return "", err
509			}
510			read, readErr := input.Read(buffer)
511			if read > 0 {
512				_, _ = hash.Write(buffer[:read])
513			}
514			if readErr != nil {
515				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
516					break
517				}
518				return "", readErr
519			}
520		}
521		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
522	}
523	
524	func insidePath(root, candidate string) bool {
525		inside, err := pathx.Contains(root, candidate)
526		return err == nil && inside
527	}
528	
529	func gitOutput(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
530		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
531		cmd.Dir = dir
532		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
533		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
534		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
535			return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s failed: %s", args[0], strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()))
536		}
537		return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
538	}

1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8	
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20	
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28	
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37	
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54	
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69	
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76	
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89	
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104	
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129	
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and the TUI consume this joined view.
59	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
60	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
61	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
62	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
63	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
64	
65	The principal task flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Lifecycle behavior lives in `park.go`, `resume.go`, `done.go`, and `sweep.go`; preserve their report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering.
66	
67	State is split intentionally:
68	
69	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
70	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
71	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
72	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
73	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
74	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
75	
76	## Behavioral contracts
77	
78	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`.
79	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
80	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
81	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
82	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews.
83	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
84	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
85	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
86	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
87	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
88	
89	## Versioning and changelog
90	
91	The current published baseline is `v0.2.3` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
92	
93	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
94	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
95	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
96	
97	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
98	
99	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
100	
101	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
102	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
103	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
104	
105	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
106	
107	For a release:
108	
109	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
110	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
111	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
112	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
113	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
114	
115	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
116	
117	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
118	
119	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned

338	 // New builds the dashboard.
339	 func New(actions Actions, rows []inventory.Row, repos []RepoRow) Model {
340	 	in := textinput.New()
341	 	in.CharLimit = 200
342	 
343	 	m := Model{
344	 		actions:        actions,
345	 		rows:           rows,
346	 		repos:          repos,
347	 		input:          in,
348	 		width:          100,
349	 		height:         30,
350	 		firstViewReady: make(chan struct{}),
351	 		firstViewOnce:  &sync.Once{},
352	 	}
353	 	if len(actions.Tools) > 0 {
354	 		m.toolGeneration = 1
355	 	}
356	 	if rows != nil {
357	 		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTasks, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
358	 	}
359	 	if repos != nil {
360	 		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRepos, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
361	 	}
362	 	return m
363	 }

900	 // taskRecoveryCommand returns the explicit lifecycle command required before
901	 // a task can be navigated to. Generic TUI open remains navigation-only: it
902	 // must not reconcile task state, claim a writer, or enter an artifact shell
903	 // that Git no longer recognizes as a worktree.
904	 func taskRecoveryCommand(row inventory.Row) string {
905	 	if row.Task == nil {
906	 		return ""
907	 	}
908	 	if row.WorktreeMissing || !row.CheckoutExists {
909	 		return "dev sweep"

1058	 // compareRepos returns negative when a belongs before b.
1059	 func compareRepos(a, b RepoRow, sortBy string) int {
1060	 	nameCmp := strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.Repo.Display()), strings.ToLower(b.Repo.Display()))
1061	 	descInt := func(x, y int) int {
1062	 		switch {
1063	 		case x > y:
1064	 			return -1
1065	 		case x < y:
1066	 			return 1
1067	 		default:
1068	 			return 0
1069	 		}
1070	 	}
1071	 	descBool := func(x, y bool) int {
1072	 		if x == y {
1073	 			return 0
1074	 		}
1075	 		if x {
1076	 			return -1
1077	 		}
1078	 		return 1
1079	 	}
1080	 	latest := func() int {
1081	 		if a.LastActivity.Equal(b.LastActivity) {
1082	 			return 0
1083	 		}
1084	 		if a.LastActivity.After(b.LastActivity) {
1085	 			return -1
1086	 		}
1087	 		return 1
1088	 	}
1089	 
1090	 	switch sortBy {
1091	 	case "name":
1092	 		return nameCmp
1093	 	case "latest":
1094	 		if c := latest(); c != 0 {
1095	 			return c
1096	 		}
1097	 	case "git":
1098	 		if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
1099	 			return c
1100	 		}
1101	 		if c := descInt(a.Status.Changed, b.Status.Changed); c != 0 {
1102	 			return c
1103	 		}
1104	 	case "size":
1105	 		switch {
1106	 		case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage == nil:
1107	 			return -1
1108	 		case a.Usage == nil && b.Usage != nil:
1109	 			return 1
1110	 		case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage != nil && a.Usage.OwnedBytes > b.Usage.OwnedBytes:
1111	 			return -1
1112	 		case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage != nil && a.Usage.OwnedBytes < b.Usage.OwnedBytes:
1113	 			return 1
1114	 		}
1115	 	case "tasks":
1116	 		if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
1117	 			return c
1118	 		}
1119	 		if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
1120	 			return c
1121	 		}
1122	 	default: // activity
1123	 		if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
1124	 			return c
1125	 		}
1126	 		if c := descBool(a.Live, b.Live); c != 0 {
1127	 			return c
1128	 		}
1129	 		if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
1130	 			return c
1131	 		}
1132	 		if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
1133	 			return c
1134	 		}
1135	 		if c := latest(); c != 0 {
1136	 			return c
1137	 		}
1138	 	}
1139	 	return nameCmp
1140	 }

1311	 // matchRemoteLocals fills cached remote rows from the freshly loaded local
1312	 // inventory without another scan.
1313	 func (m *Model) matchRemoteLocals() {
1314	 	m.remotes = append([]RemoteRow(nil), m.remotes...)
1315	 	byRemote := map[string]RepoRow{}
1316	 	ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1317	 	for _, r := range m.repos {
1318	 		if r.RemoteName == "" {
1319	 			continue
1320	 		}
1321	 		key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)
1322	 		if ambiguous[key] {
1323	 			continue
1324	 		}
1325	 		if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
1326	 			delete(byRemote, key)
1327	 			ambiguous[key] = true
1328	 			continue
1329	 		}
1330	 		byRemote[key] = r
1331	 	}
1332	 	triesByIdentity := map[string]TryRow{}
1333	 	ambiguousTry := map[string]bool{}
1334	 	for _, row := range m.tries {
1335	 		identity := row.Item.RemoteIdentity
1336	 		if !row.Present() || identity == "" || ambiguousTry[identity] {
1337	 			continue
1338	 		}
1339	 		if _, exists := triesByIdentity[identity]; exists {
1340	 			delete(triesByIdentity, identity)
1341	 			ambiguousTry[identity] = true
1342	 			continue
1343	 		}
1344	 		triesByIdentity[identity] = row
1345	 	}
1346	 	for i := range m.remotes {
1347	 		key := string(m.remotes[i].Repo.Forge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(m.remotes[i].Repo.FullName)
1348	 		identity := ""
1349	 		for _, raw := range []string{m.remotes[i].Repo.CloneURL, m.remotes[i].Repo.SSHURL, m.remotes[i].Repo.URL} {
1350	 			if identity = catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw); identity != "" {
1351	 				break
1352	 			}
1353	 		}
1354	 		repository, repoOK := byRemote[key]
1355	 		try, tryOK := triesByIdentity[identity]
1356	 		sameCheckout := repoOK && tryOK && remotePathsOverlap(repository, try)
1357	 		if ambiguous[key] || ambiguousTry[identity] || (repoOK && tryOK && !sameCheckout) {
1358	 			m.remotes[i].LocalPath, m.remotes[i].LocalName, m.remotes[i].LocalKind = "", "", ""
1359	 			continue
1360	 		}
1361	 		if repoOK {
1362	 			m.remotes[i].LocalPath = repository.Repo.Path
1363	 			m.remotes[i].LocalName = repository.Repo.Display()
1364	 			m.remotes[i].LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1365	 			if repository.Asset != nil {
1366	 				m.remotes[i].LocalKind = repository.Asset.Kind
1367	 			}
1368	 			continue
1369	 		}
1370	 		if tryOK {
1371	 			m.remotes[i].LocalPath = try.Item.Live.CurrentPath
1372	 			m.remotes[i].LocalName = try.Item.DisplayName()
1373	 			m.remotes[i].LocalKind = catalog.KindTry
1374	 			continue
1375	 		}
1376	 		m.remotes[i].LocalPath, m.remotes[i].LocalName, m.remotes[i].LocalKind = "", "", ""
1377	 	}
1378	 }

1383	 			if left != "" && right != "" && filepath.Clean(left) == filepath.Clean(right) {
1384	 				return true
1385	 			}
1386	 		}
1387	 	}
1388	 	return false
1389	 }

2429	 func (m Model) launchTool(key string) tea.Cmd {
2430	 	for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
2431	 		if t.Key != key {
2432	 			continue
2433	 		}
2434	 		if t.Probe != nil && t.Availability != ToolAvailable {
2435	 			detail := "availability is still being checked"
2436	 			if t.Availability == ToolUnavailable {
2437	 				detail = "is not installed"

2440	 				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s %s", t.Command[0], detail)}
2441	 			}
2442	 		}
2443	 		dir := m.currentDir()

2445	 			return func() tea.Msg {
2446	 				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("nothing selected with a checkout on disk")}

2449	 		c := exec.Command(t.Command[0], t.Command[1:]...)

2455	 			return actionMsg{status: "back from " + t.Name, forceSizes: true}
2456	 		})
2457	 	}
2458	 	return nil

241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())

250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
316

237	// Match reports whether a declaration satisfies f.
238	func (f Filter) Match(d Declaration) bool {
239		if f.Agent != "" && d.Agent != f.Agent ||
240			f.Scope != "" && d.Scope != f.Scope ||
241			f.Source != "" && d.Source != f.Source ||
242			f.Transport != "" && d.Transport != f.Transport ||
243			f.Repository != "" && d.Repository != f.Repository {
244			return false
245		}
246		if f.NameContains != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(d.Name), strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.NameContains))) {
247			return false
248		}
249		if f.Enabled != nil && (d.Enabled == nil || *d.Enabled != *f.Enabled) {
250			return false
251		}
252		if f.HasCredentials != nil && (len(d.Credentials) > 0) != *f.HasCredentials {
253			return false
254		}
255		return true
256	}
257	
258	// FilterDeclarations returns matching rows without changing their order.
259	func FilterDeclarations(rows []Declaration, f Filter) []Declaration {
260		out := make([]Declaration, 0, len(rows))
261		for _, row := range rows {
262			if f.Match(row) {
263				out = append(out, row)
264			}
265		}
266		return out
267	}

269	// SortDeclarations establishes the stable order used by Scan.
270	func SortDeclarations(rows []Declaration) {
271		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
272			a, b := rows[i], rows[j]
273			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Source), strings.ToLower(a.Plugin), a.Plugin, strings.ToLower(a.Name), a.Name}
274			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Source), strings.ToLower(b.Plugin), b.Plugin, strings.ToLower(b.Name), b.Name}
275			for n := range ak {
276				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
277					return ak[n] < bk[n]
278				}
279			}
280			return false
281		})
282	}

171	// NewScanner creates a scanner for explicitly supplied host paths.
172	func NewScanner(options Options) *Scanner {
173		options = normalizeOptions(options)

184	// Scan returns all static declarations it can decode and fixed diagnostics for
185	// individual source failures. Cancellation is the only normal top-level scan
186	// failure and is returned as ctx.Err(), with any rows already collected.
187	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
188		if ctx == nil {
189			ctx = context.Background()
190		}
191		targets = normalizeTargets(targets, s.options.WorkingDirectory)
192		result := Result{Coverage: defaultCoverage()}
193	
194		for _, spec := range s.hostSources() {
195			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
196				finalizeResult(&result)
197				return result, err
198			}
199			rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, targets)
200			result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, rows...)
201			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)

409	func (s *Scanner) scanSource(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec, targets []Target) ([]Declaration, []Diagnostic) {
410		read := s.readSource(ctx, spec)
411		if !read.present {
412			if read.code == "" {
413				return nil, nil
414			}
415			return nil, []Diagnostic{diagnosticFor(spec, read.code)}
416		}
417		var rows []Declaration
418		var codes []DiagnosticCode
419		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
420		switch spec.adapter {
421		case adapterClaudeProject:
422			rows, codes = parseClaudeProject(read.data, spec)
423			for _, approvalPath := range spec.approvalPaths {
424				approvalSpec := spec
425				approvalSpec.path = approvalPath
426				approval := s.readSource(ctx, approvalSpec)
427				switch {
428				case approval.code != "":
429					diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, approval.code))
430				case approval.present:
431					enabled, disabled, enableAll, code := parseClaudeProjectApproval(approval.data)
432					if code != "" {
433						diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, code))
434					} else {
435						applyClaudeProjectApproval(rows, enabled, disabled, enableAll)
436					}
437				}
438			}
439		case adapterClaudeUser:
440			var localDiagnostics []Diagnostic
441			rows, codes, localDiagnostics = parseClaudeUser(read.data, spec, targets)
442			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, localDiagnostics...)
443		case adapterCodex:
444			rows, codes = parseCodex(read.data, spec)
445		case adapterCursor:
446			rows, codes = parseCursor(read.data, spec)
447		case adapterGemini:
448			rows, codes = parseGemini(read.data, spec)
449		case adapterOpenCode:
450			rows, codes = parseOpenCode(read.data, spec)
451		case adapterOpenCodePlist:
452			rows, codes = parseOpenCodePlist(read.data, spec)
453		default:
454			codes = []DiagnosticCode{DiagnosticMalformed}
455		}
456		if diagnostics == nil {
457			diagnostics = make([]Diagnostic, 0, len(codes))
458		}
459		for _, code := range codes {
460			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(spec, code))
461		}
462		return rows, diagnostics
463	}
464	
465	func diagnosticFor(spec sourceSpec, code DiagnosticCode) Diagnostic {
466		return Diagnostic{
467			Agent: spec.agent, Scope: spec.scope, Repository: spec.repository,
468			RepositoryPath: spec.repositoryPath, Checkout: spec.checkout, ConfigPath: spec.path,
469			Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code),
470		}
471	}

473	func finalizeResult(result *Result) {
474		SortDeclarations(result.Declarations)
475		sort.SliceStable(result.Diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool {
476			a, b := result.Diagnostics[i], result.Diagnostics[j]
477			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Code)}
478			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Code)}
479			for n := range ak {
480				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
481					return ak[n] < bk[n]
482				}
483			}
484			return false
485		})
486	}

105	// resolveBoundedSymlinks follows symlinks in every path component while placing
106	// a small deterministic bound on cycles and unusually deep chains.
107	func resolveBoundedSymlinks(filename string, limit int) (string, error) {
108		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(filename)
109		if err != nil {
110			return "", err
111		}
112		return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(absolute), limit, 0)
113	}
114	
115	func resolveSymlinkPath(absolute string, limit, followed int) (string, error) {
116		volume := filepath.VolumeName(absolute)
117		root := volume + string(filepath.Separator)
118		relative := strings.TrimPrefix(absolute, root)
119		components := strings.FieldsFunc(relative, func(r rune) bool { return r == rune(filepath.Separator) })
120		current := root
121		for index, component := range components {
122			candidate := filepath.Join(current, component)
123			info, err := os.Lstat(candidate)
124			if err != nil {
125				return "", err
126			}
127			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
128				current = candidate
129				continue
130			}
131			if followed >= limit {
132				return "", errSymlinkLimit
133			}
134			target, err := os.Readlink(candidate)
135			if err != nil {
136				return "", err
137			}
138			if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
139				target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(candidate), target)
140			}
141			if index+1 < len(components) {
142				target = filepath.Join(target, filepath.Join(components[index+1:]...))
143			}
144			target, err = filepath.Abs(target)
145			if err != nil {
146				return "", err
147			}
148			return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(target), limit, followed+1)
149		}
150		return filepath.Clean(current), nil
151	}

276			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)

1	---
2	description: Record dev-cli dependencies, upstream preview status, documentation constraints, and behavior that is intentionally incomplete.
3	authority: project-and-upstream
4	status: evolving
5	verified_on: 2026-09-01

8	
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| native skill inventory | local filesystem plus the versioned `skills@1.5.23` path registry | always available; explicit add/update requires a directly installed `skills` executable and may use the network; repository-local npm bins are never provider candidates |
25	| static MCP inventory | readable supported agent config files | missing sources are empty; malformed/unsupported sources produce partial diagnostics, and runtime health is intentionally unavailable |
26	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
27	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
28	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
29	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
30	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
31	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
32	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` prints the package manager's upgrade command instead |
33	
34	## Confirmed project limitations
35	
36	### MCP inventory is static and intentionally incomplete
37	
38	`dev mcp list` reads documented static files for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. It does not start servers, execute helpers, contact endpoints, query health, resolve credentials, or reproduce each agent's runtime merge. Plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted. Keep the JSON `coverage` object and scope-qualified duplicate rows when automating against this inventory.
39	
40	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
41	
42	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
43	
44	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
45	
46	### Pull-request completion is not tracked automatically
47	
48	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge to infer that a request later merged. Verify integration and finish/reconcile deliberately; do not assume remote merge implies local DONE.
49	
50	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
51	
52	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
53	
54	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
55	
56	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Freshness also requires a source fingerprint matching the configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets, so an endpoint change is never hidden by the zero TTL. Legacy source-less caches remain available only through explicit `--cached` and are reported stale. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
57	
58	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
59	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
60	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
61	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
62	inventory has been searched.
63	
64	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
65	
66	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
67	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
68	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
69	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
70	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
71	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
72	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
73	and printed message remain the recovery path.
74	
75	### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
76	
77	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
78	
79	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
80	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
81	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
82	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
83	
84	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
85	
86	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
87	
88	## Current behaviors that are implemented
89	
90	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
91	
92	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
93	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
94	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
95	- Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
96	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
97	
98	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
99	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
100	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
101	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
102	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
103	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
104	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
105	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
106	
107	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
108	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
109	- `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
110	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
111	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
112	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
113	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
114	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
115	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
116	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
117	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
118	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
119	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
120	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
121	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
122	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
123	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.
124	- `dev upgrade` downloads the current release for this platform, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, and replaces the running binary with an atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run). It defers to Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` when one of them owns the file; Homebrew users receive releases through the automatically advanced tap instead of an in-place Cellar overwrite.
125	- An interactive `dev` command prints one dim "newer release available" line at most once a day, read from the day-old release cache; it never blocks on the network. For the TUI, a stale-cache background refresh starts only after the initial view returns. `[update] check = false` or `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` disables it.
126	
127	## Claude Code status matrix
128	
129	| Surface | Status on 2026-08-28 | Compatibility note |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| core agentic loop/tools | official | exact tools depend on surface/model/policy |
132	| worktree isolation | official, rapidly evolving | cleanup, baseRef, resume, and safety details are version-sensitive |
133	| subagents | official | fork/background defaults and naming changed across 2.1.x |
134	| Agent view | research preview | retain manual sessions/worktrees fallback |
135	| agent teams | experimental, disabled by default | no automatic worktree isolation; resumption/task/shutdown limitations |
136	| Dynamic Workflows | versioned feature | requires v2.1.154+; availability/config and limits vary by release |
137	| Agent SDK | official SDK | language SDK parity and event availability can differ |
138	
139	`TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` are historical tools removed in v2.1.178. The old `Task` worker tool name was replaced by `Agent`; do not confuse either with Task-list metadata tools.
140	
141	## Documentation-stack limitations
142	
143	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` reports that `zh-TW` is not a Lunr language, so Chinese search does not receive a dedicated Lunr stemmer/segmenter. Navigation and pages still build.
144	- `mkdocs-llmstxt` skips pages after static-i18n remaps them. This project replaces that empty output with a deterministic local generator and runs strict builds again.
145	- The copy-to-LLM plugin's button labels remain English on zh-TW pages; this is cosmetic.
146	- MkDocs and Material are pinned below their next major versions because the selected plugin stack targets MkDocs 1.x/Material 9.x.
147	
148	## Reporting a compatibility change
149	
150	Update the owning guide, both languages, this matrix, and [Sources and freshness](sources-freshness.md). Include the tested binary/version and a code/test or official-source link. Never preserve a known false statement for backward documentation compatibility.

17	## dev-cli capability matrix
18	
19	| Capability | Dependency | 缺少時 |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| 核心 repository/task/worktree 操作 | Git | 無法使用；Git 是唯一 hard runtime dependency |
22	| grouped runtime 與 agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` 改試 tmux、Zellij，最後 none |
23	| named terminal session | tmux 或相容 Zellij | `none` 保留核心 behavior 與 shell navigation |
24	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | authenticated `gh` | Git 可用時 branch 仍能 push，可能需 browser/manual flow |
25	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | authenticated `glab` | 同樣 graceful fallback |
26	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` 或 `glab` | local repository/scaffold 仍可使用；wizard 會說明如何 login |
27	| remote repository snapshot template | Git，加上 source 所需的 network/authentication | validation 會在建立 destination 前失敗，rendered URL userinfo 會 redact；local template 仍可使用 |
28	| native skill inventory | local filesystem 加 versioned `skills@1.5.23` path registry | 永遠可用；explicit add/update 需要直接安裝的 `skills` executable，且可能使用 network；repository-local npm bins 絕不作為 provider candidate |
29	| static MCP inventory | 可讀取的 supported agent config files | 缺少 source 代表 empty；malformed/unsupported source 產生 partial diagnostics，runtime health 刻意不提供 |
30	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider 與 entrypoint interpreter | 未選取的 skill 會跳過；selected required setup 若缺少 interpreter，會在 scaffold mutation 前失敗；先取得的 clone 會保留 |
31	| staged lazygit message prefill | 會讀取 `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` 的 lazygit version | files 仍保持 staged，dev 會印出建議 message；一般 Git commit 仍可使用 |
32	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager（`uv`、npm、Cargo 等） | plan 回報 missing tool 並保留 checkout |
33	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | 透過 pipe 執行 bare `dev` 時輸出 plain task list |
34	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` 與 FTS5 | 不需要外部 `sqlite3` executable |
35	| Windows 上的 terminal multiplexing | tmux/Zellij/Herdr（僅 POSIX） | Windows 一律使用 `none` backend；`dev shell-init powershell` 仍能移動 shell |
36	| in-place self-update | standalone install（非 Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`） | `dev upgrade` 改為印出對應套件管理器的升級指令 |
37	
38	## 已確認的專案限制
39	
40	### MCP inventory 是 static 且刻意不完整
41	
42	`dev mcp list` 會讀取 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 與 OpenCode 的 documented static files；不會啟動 server、執行 helper、連線 endpoint、查詢 health、解析 credentials，或重現每個 agent 的 runtime merge。Plugin caches、hosted connectors、remote organization config、inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` 與 command-line-only inputs 都會省略。對 inventory 做 automation 時必須保留 JSON `coverage` object 與 scope-qualified duplicate rows。
43	
44	### Note search 與 filesystem durability 依文字及平台而異
45	
46	Latin note query 使用 term-wise prefix FTS 與 SQLite ranking。Non-ASCII query 改用 literal term-wise substring matching，因為 SQLite 的 `unicode61` tokenizer 不會切分任意 CJK substrings；這些結果不使用相同的 FTS ranking。
47	
48	所有支援平台的 note write 都會 sync file 並 atomic rename。Unix 也會在 rename/delete 後 sync containing directory。Windows implementation 無法提供 directory-fsync 步驟，因此 sudden power loss 時的 durability guarantee 較窄。Cooperating `dev` processes 的 concurrent mutations 會被 serialized，且每次 Markdown replacement 都是 atomic；任意 external writer 不會參與這個 lock。
49	
50	### Pull request completion 不會自動追蹤
51	
52	`dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。目前 `dev sweep` 不會 query forge 推斷 request 後來已 merge。請驗證 integration 後再刻意 finish/reconcile；不能假設 remote merge 代表 local DONE。
53	
54	### Agent session capture 只有保留欄位，尚未接線
55	
56	Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
57	
58	### Built-in forge cache TTL 與 generated config 不同
59	
60	`dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 也要求 source fingerprint 符合 configured GH/GL hosts 與 Azure targets，因此 endpoint change 不會被 zero TTL 隱藏。Legacy source-less cache 只能透過 explicit `--cached` 使用，並會標為 stale。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
61	
62	較舊的 generated config 可能包含 `forge.remote_limit = 100`。此欄位仍可解析，
63	但 forge inventory 現在會完整 pagination，因此不再限制 synchronization。
64	`dev config init` 不再寫入它；`dev repo remote --limit` 只在完整 inventory 搜尋
65	完成後限制 rendered matches。
66	
67	### Lazygit staged-message prefill 是 best effort
68	
69	`repo --check-in=stage` 會在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入 pending message。
70	[Lazygit v0.59.0 的小寫 `c` 會使用該
71	檔案](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，但這是 lazygit implementation detail，不是 Git
72	interface；大寫 `C` 與一般 `git commit` 不會讀取它。Dev 不會覆寫內容不同的既有
73	draft。Draft write failure 只會產生 warning；staging 仍視為成功且不會 rollback。若
74	upstream integration 日後改變，staged index 與已印出的 message 仍是 recovery path。
75	
76	### Windows 是 build target，不是 full-feature 平台
77	
78	`dev` 可在 `windows/amd64` 與 `windows/arm64` 編譯並執行，每個 release 都會附各自的 `.zip`。核心的 repository、task 與 worktree 操作可用。差異：
79	
80	- 沒有 tmux、Zellij 或 Herdr，因此 runtime backend 一律是 `none`。Grouped runtime/agent activity 與 named session 無法使用；`cd` 指令與 PowerShell wrapper 仍可運作。
81	- Shell integration 是 `dev shell-init powershell`。POSIX shell 透過 file descriptor 3 回傳目錄；PowerShell 無法繼承它，wrapper 改用 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳入 temp-file path。
82	- `dev fleet open` 會啟動子 shell（`%COMSPEC%`），而非取代 process，因為 Windows 沒有 `exec(2)`。
83	- Domain test suites 仍有部分假設 POSIX filesystem，因此 Windows CI 的 test 僅供參考，compilation、`go vet` 與 build 則為強制項。
84	
85	### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
86	
87	Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
88	
89	## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
90	
91	以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
92	
93	- `dev repo new|create`、`repo clone` 與 `repo setup` 共用 preset-driven bootstrap pipeline。Plain explicit `repo new NAME` 仍維持 minimal；清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name 會改走 clone acquisition，保留 source history/remote。無參數 wizard 的第一個欄位也會偵測同樣 reference；建立新 repository 時，預設為 no 的 customization gate 讓正常 `agent-ready` flow 保持精簡。Text fields 使用 TTY inline editor，因此 cursor keys 會編輯內容，不會插入 raw escape bytes；non-TTY reader 維持 line-oriented behavior。
94	- `repo new` 可從 local directory/repository 或 Git source 的 optional branch、tag、commit 與 confined subdirectory 建立 fresh-history snapshot。未 pin 的 local Git tree 包含 tracked 加 untracked non-ignored files；non-Git directory 包含完整 current tree。Source `.git` metadata 會排除、URL userinfo 會 redact，不安全的 file types/paths 會在 destination 建立前失敗，held root/file handles 會限制 mutable-path races。Human plan 會預覽 paths 並警告 live snapshot，preset 也可選擇 catalog-repository subfolder。
95	- Repository setup 支援 `--check-in=commit|stage|none`（`auto` 用於 preset compatibility）。Staged setup 會執行 before-commit setup 與 `git add -A`，但不執行 `after_commit` phase；它不能 publish 或 handoff 到 `start`，並可依前述方式預填 lazygit 小寫 `c`。
96	- Source 與 agent targets 相同的 selected skills 會共用一次 installer invocation。`agent-history-hygiene` initializer 會寫入 pre-commit/gitleaks policy，並將缺少的 machine-local `.project.json`／`statistics.json` 規則 merge 進 `.specstory/.gitignore`；custom content 與 transcript history 都保持可追蹤。
97	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` 與 `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 僅能保存 portable setup policy。Executable project configuration 會綁定 canonical Git common directory 與 exact content hash；hash 改變後必須重新信任。
98	
99	- `dev start --focus` 會在 non-JSON creation 後 activate runtime。
100	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` 只會 dispatch 到本次新建 first-class Herdr
101	  worktree 的 exact root pane。它不能與 `--json`、non-worktree modes 或 non-Herdr
102	  runtimes 併用，也不等待 command exit。
103	- TUI navigation 會拒絕開啟 checkout 不存在的 COLD task，並要求使用 `dev resume`。
104	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` 從 `cli.Execute` 起算，無法涵蓋 OS process loading。`tui.initial_view_returned` 量測 model construction，不是 renderer flush 或 physical terminal paint；它適合同 profile 比較，不是跨硬體／network 的 universal guarantee。
105	- Runtime handle 現在保存 backend provenance，cleanup 前會重新驗證。
106	- `auto` runtime selection 已在 tmux 與 none 之間加入 Zellij。
107	
108	- `dev done` 在省略 `--ff`/`--pr` 且為 TTY 時會開啟 interactive finish wizard，把 dirty checkout 拿去跟 base 比較（commit、discard 或 cancel），不再直接拒絕任何 uncommitted change；non-interactive caller 仍須明確傳入 `--dirty` policy，且 destructive discard 需要 `--yes`。
109	- Human-readable output 現在具備 semantic color（`--color auto|always|never`），在 `NO_COLOR` 已設定、`TERM=dumb`，或 stdout/stderr 不是 terminal 時會自動停用。
110	- `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED：它不會關閉呼叫端 runtime、移除 worktree 或刪除 branch。Cleanup 已移交 `dev retire`，後者必須從目標 workspace 之外執行，會拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，並在每次關閉 runtime 之後重新驗證 Git state。`dev done --delete-branch` 現在會直接報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`，`--keep-worktree` 則以 no-op 警告。
111	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` 直接從 Git 列舉 linked worktrees，而非從 task registry，因此 branch 已被 base 包含的 unmanaged worktree 也能被 retire。Containment 本身絕不等於許可；dirty state、未 finalize 的 artifact、進行中的 Git operation 與 runtime 拒絕條件都仍會阻擋，且未加 `--delete-branches` 時 branch 一律保留。
112	- `dev sweep` 會把 branch 已不存在於 Git 的 branch-backed task 視為 dead，並提供 reap 該 record 的建議。這種 task 無法 finish、resume 或 retire，因為這些路徑都必須先解析 branch；在 `--apply` 之前該建議仍只是報告。
113	- 未知 command 會被回報，而不是被丟棄。`dev` 關閉了 cobra 自己的 error 輸出，先前又額外略過所有訊息開頭為 `unknown command` 的 error，因此打錯 command 時兩個 stream 都沒有任何輸出。現在會把訊息、cobra 的「Did you mean this?」建議，以及指向 `--help` 的提示寫到 stderr，exit status 為 1。
114	- 對 command family 傳入多餘的 argument 現在是 error，而不是安靜地印出 help。`dev wt bogus` 過去會印出 `dev wt` help 並 exit 0，因為 family 本身沒有 `Run`；現在每個 family node 都會回報未知 subcommand 並 exit 1，而單獨執行 family 仍會印出 help 並 exit 0。
115	- Argument 數量與 flag 錯誤會印出該 command 的 usage block。該 block 是否上色仍由 `--color` 決定。
116	- 每個 command family 的 help 都附上 ASCII orientation diagram 與 `See also: dev help <topic>` 指引，且 `dev help <command>` 會把 command 名稱或 alias 解析成對應 topic，因此 `dev help wt` 會連到 worktrees 頁面。
117	- Semantic color 已覆蓋所有 human-readable 介面，包含 interactive dashboard：`dev --color never`、`NO_COLOR` 與 `TERM=dumb` 現在也會關閉 dashboard 的顏色，先前並不會。
118	- `dev sweep` 會 reap repository 目錄已不存在的 task。這種 record 先前無法被 binary 中任何 command 觸及：`done`、`resume`、`park` 與 `retire` 都會先解析 repository，dead-branch 規則排除 direct mode，stale-worktree 規則又需要有記錄的 worktree path。若有 live runtime session 則不會提出此建議，且 reap 只移除 dev 的 intent record。
119	- `dev sweep` 會回報 task 記錄中存在、但 Git 未註冊，且只包含 agent artifact 目錄的 checkout。只有在其中每個檔案都與 repository 既有檔案 byte-identical 時才提議移除；其餘一律回報為 salvage 工作，即使加上 `--apply` 也絕不移除。
120	- `dev sweep` 會處理 worktree 仍在磁碟上的 cold task。Inventory 一直有為 `dev ls` 與 dashboard 計算這項 drift，但 sweep 從未讀取它，因此只能顯示、無法處理。
121	- `dev retire <path>` 會 reap 對應的 task record。先前只有 by-task 形式會設定 task identity，因此以 path 退休同一個 checkout 會留下 record；DONE 狀態與 identity 檢查維持不變。
122	- `dev version` 會回報目前執行的 build 是否為已發布的 release，`dev doctor` 也帶有同一行資訊。先前工具中沒有任何地方能回答「我是不是最新的？」，而 `go install ...@latest` 只會解析到最新的 tag，因此未 tag 的 feature 對安裝者而言等同不存在。
123	- Release 會發布各平台 archive 與 `SHA256SUMS`，並以 `CHANGELOG.md` 對應段落作為 release notes。先前的 release 只產生 GitHub release 物件，因此那些版本本來就沒有附加檔案。
124	- Release 會在 Unix `.tar.gz` 之外一併發布 Windows `.zip`、更新附在 release 上的 in-repo Scoop manifest（設定 token 時也會 push 到 bucket），並把對應的 source formula 發布到 `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`。Homebrew 發布是必要的 release step；repository token 缺失或被拒絕時會明確讓 job 失敗。Manual workflow 可為既有 stable release retry 或 backfill formula，不會建立或移動 tag。
125	- `dev upgrade` 會下載此平台目前的 release、以 release `SHA256SUMS` 驗證，再以 atomic rename 取代執行中的 binary（Windows 會把 live `.exe` 移到旁邊，下次執行時清除）。若 Homebrew、Scoop 或 `go install` 擁有該檔案，則改為印出對應指令；Homebrew 使用者透過自動推進的 tap 收到 release，不會就地覆寫 Cellar binary。
126	- Interactive `dev` command 每天最多印一行 dim 的「有新版」提示，來源是一天內的 release cache，永不因網路而 block。TUI 的 stale-cache background refresh 只會在 initial view return 後啟動。`[update] check = false` 或 `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可停用。
127

129

131	|---|---|---|

142	## Documentation stack 限制
143	
144	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` 回報 `zh-TW` 不是 Lunr language，因此 Chinese search 沒有專用 Lunr stemmer/segmenter；navigation 與 pages 仍正常 build。
145	- `mkdocs-llmstxt` 在 static-i18n 重映射 pages 後會跳過內容；本專案以 deterministic local generator 取代空輸出，並恢復 strict build。

8	# Commands and configuration
9	
10	Use the authored map for intent and the embedded generated reference for exact flags. The generated block comes from the binary's Cobra command tree and is checked by `dev skill sync --check`.

12	## Command map

17	| agent artifacts | `prepare`, `artifact finalize`, `artifact list`, `artifact discard` |

19	| linked worktrees | `wt list`, `wt create`, `wt open`, `wt rm`, `wt plan`, `wt provision` |
