```text
746	 // setAt moves the cursor, clamped to the current view's length.
747	 func (m *Model) setAt(i int) {
```

```text
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {

177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
178		if len(components) == 0 {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
180		}
181		for i, component := range components {
182			if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
183				return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
184			}
185		}
186		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
187		if err != nil {
188			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
189		}
190		return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
191	}
192	
193	func driveQualified(component string) bool {
194		if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
195			return false
196		}
197		letter := component[0]
198		return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'
199	}
```

```text
2829	func (m Model) viewWaitsForRepos(view View) bool {
2830		return m.viewUsesRepos(view) && m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).loading
2831	}
2832	
2833	func (m Model) dependentReposUnavailable(view View) error {
2834		if !m.viewUsesRepos(view) {
2835			return nil
2836		}
2837		repos := m.viewLoad(ViewRepos)
2838		if repos.loading || (repos.hasSnapshot && repos.freshness == perftrace.FreshnessFresh) {
2839			return nil
2840		}
2841		if err := m.viewError(ViewRepos); err != nil {
2842			return fmt.Errorf("local repository inventory: %w", err)
2843		}
2844		return errors.New("local repository inventory is unavailable")
2845	}
2846	
2847	func dependentLoadingStatus(view View) string {
2848		switch view {
2849		case ViewFleet:
2850			return "loading configured dev hosts…"
2851		case ViewSkills:
2852			return "loading agent skills across repositories…"
2853		case ViewMCP:
2854			return "loading MCP declarations across repositories…"
2855		default:
2856			return "loading…"
2857		}
2858	}
2859	
2860	func (m Model) reloadDependentView(view View) tea.Cmd {
2861		switch view {
2862		case ViewFleet:
2863			return m.reloadFleet()
2864		case ViewSkills:
2865			return m.reloadSkills()
2866		case ViewMCP:
2867			return m.reloadMCP()
2868		default:
2869			return nil
2870		}
2871	}
2872	
2873	func (m *Model) afterReposResult(valid bool, err error) tea.Cmd {
2874		fresh := valid && err == nil
2875		var commands []tea.Cmd
2876		for _, view := range []View{ViewFleet, ViewSkills, ViewMCP} {
2877			if !m.viewUsesRepos(view) {
2878				continue
2879			}
2880			state := m.viewLoad(view)
2881			if state.loading || (m.view == view && state.hasSnapshot) {
2882				m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
2883				if fresh {
2884					m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
2885					commands = append(commands, m.reloadDependentView(view))
2886					continue
2887				}
2888				dependencyErr := err
2889				if dependencyErr == nil {
2890					dependencyErr = errors.New("local repository inventory is unavailable")
2891				}
2892				current := m.viewLoad(view)
2893				m.applyViewResult(view, current.generation, false, "", "", 0, dependencyErr, false)
2894				continue
2895			}
2896			if state.hasSnapshot {
2897				m.invalidateView(view)
2898			}
2899		}
2900		return batchCommands(commands...)
2901	}
2902	
2903	// afterViewSwitch lazily loads optional inventories only when their view is
2904	// first opened, so starting the dashboard never waits on the network, a forge
2905	// CLI, or Node tooling.
2906	func (m Model) afterViewSwitch() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
2907		m.setAt(m.at())
2908		switch m.view {
2909		case ViewFleet:
2910			if m.viewNeedsLoad(ViewFleet) {
2911				m.beginViewLoad(ViewFleet, loadVisit)
2912				if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(ViewFleet); err != nil {
2913					fleet := m.viewLoad(ViewFleet)
2914					m.applyViewResult(ViewFleet, fleet.generation, false, "", "", 0, err, false)
2915					return m, nil
2916				}
2917				if m.viewWaitsForRepos(ViewFleet) {
2918					m.setViewStatus(ViewFleet, "waiting for local repositories…")
2919					return m, nil
2920				}
2921				m.setViewStatus(ViewFleet, "loading configured dev hosts…")
2922				return m, m.reloadFleet()
2923			}
2924		case ViewRemote:
2925			if m.viewNeedsLoad(ViewRemote) {
2926				m.beginViewLoad(ViewRemote, loadVisit)
2927				m.setViewStatus(ViewRemote, "refreshing remote repositories…")
2928				return m, m.reloadRemote()
2929			}
2930		case ViewSkills:
2931			if m.viewNeedsLoad(ViewSkills) {
2932				m.beginViewLoad(ViewSkills, loadVisit)
2933				if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(ViewSkills); err != nil {
2934					state := m.viewLoad(ViewSkills)
2935					m.applyViewResult(ViewSkills, state.generation, false, "", "", 0, err, false)
2936					return m, nil
2937				}
2938				if m.viewWaitsForRepos(ViewSkills) {
2939					m.setViewStatus(ViewSkills, "waiting for local repositories…")
2940					return m, nil
2941				}
2942				m.setViewStatus(ViewSkills, dependentLoadingStatus(ViewSkills))
2943				return m, m.reloadSkills()
2944			}
2945		case ViewMCP:
2946			if m.viewNeedsLoad(ViewMCP) {
2947				m.beginViewLoad(ViewMCP, loadVisit)
2948				if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(ViewMCP); err != nil {
2949					state := m.viewLoad(ViewMCP)
2950					m.applyViewResult(ViewMCP, state.generation, false, "", "", 0, err, false)
2951					return m, nil
2952				}
2953				if m.viewWaitsForRepos(ViewMCP) {
2954					m.setViewStatus(ViewMCP, "waiting for local repositories…")
2955					return m, nil
2956				}
2957				m.setViewStatus(ViewMCP, dependentLoadingStatus(ViewMCP))
2958				return m, m.reloadMCP()
2959			}
```

```text
1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}

89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
```

```text
3:`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
9:- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
11:- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
```

158	MCP reads static declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and

160	configured/enabled/disabled never means connected or healthy. Environment,

163	never runs a server, helper, URL, or agent MCP command. Filters include `repo:`,
164	`agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, and `state:`; `r` only rereads
165	static files.
166	
167	## External tools
168	
169	```bash
170	dev tui tools
171	```
172	
173	Configured tools run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout while the alternate screen is suspended. `interactive = true` uses `$SHELL -lic` so local aliases/functions can resolve; use a real executable on `PATH` when the binding must be portable. Availability probes run in a bounded background load after the first view; rendering never starts a login shell, and unresolved bindings fail closed.
174	
175	```toml
176	[[tui.tools]]
177	key = "L"
178	name = "lazygit"
179	run = "lazygit"
180	```
181	
182	Keys are case-sensitive and cannot shadow dashboard-owned bindings. Returning from an editor can reload most config; switching runtime backend requires restarting the TUI.
183	
184	## Inventory an existing machine
185	
186	Start with a report:
187	
188	```bash
189	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work
190	dev bootstrap ~/code --json
191	```
192	
193	The scanner identifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories, and symlink aliases, then deduplicates them by Git identity.
194	
195	The recommended organization layer is a non-destructive symlink index:
196	
197	```bash
198	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat
199	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --layout flat --apply
200	```
201	
202	Physical moves are a separate, stricter mode. A move plan blocks dirty repositories, linked worktrees, live sessions/current working directories, aliases that would break, occupied destinations, and cross-filesystem renames. If any row is blocked, apply moves none.

205	
206	Bootstrap answers **where repositories are**. Adoption answers **which existing branches, worktrees, and sessions are active work**:

```text
13	func resolverOutcome(err error) perftrace.Outcome {
14		if err != nil {
15			return perftrace.OutcomeFailed
16		}
17		return perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
18	}
19	
20	// tuiRuntimeResolver moves runtime auto-detection off the first-view path while
21	// sharing exactly one result across inventory loads and actions.
22	type tuiRuntimeResolver struct {
23		trace   *perftrace.Recorder
24		resolve func() runtime.Runtime
25		once    sync.Once
26		ready   chan struct{}
27		rt      runtime.Runtime
28	}
29	
30	func newTUIRuntimeResolver(app *App) *tuiRuntimeResolver {
31		snapshot := *app
32		return &tuiRuntimeResolver{
33			trace: app.trace, resolve: snapshot.Runtime, ready: make(chan struct{}),
34		}
35	}
36	
37	func (r *tuiRuntimeResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
38		r.once.Do(func() {
39			go func() {
40				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIRuntimeResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
41				r.rt = r.resolve()
42				finish(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
43				close(r.ready)
44			}()
45		})
46		if ctx == nil {
47			ctx = context.Background()
48		}
49		select {
50		case <-ctx.Done():
51			return nil, ctx.Err()
52		case <-r.ready:
53			return r.rt, nil
54		}
55	}
56	
57	// tuiProjectRootResolver keeps Git project-root discovery lazy and shared by
58	// SKILLS reads/actions.
59	type tuiProjectRootResolver struct {
60		trace       *perftrace.Recorder
61		ctx         context.Context
62		getwd       func() (string, error)
63		projectRoot func(context.Context, string) string
64		once        sync.Once
65		ready       chan struct{}
66		root        string
67		err         error
68	}
69	
70	func newTUIProjectRootResolver(trace *perftrace.Recorder, ctx context.Context) *tuiProjectRootResolver {
71		if ctx == nil {
72			ctx = context.Background()
73		}
74		return &tuiProjectRootResolver{
75			trace: trace, ctx: ctx, getwd: os.Getwd, projectRoot: agentskill.ProjectRoot,
76			ready: make(chan struct{}),
77		}
78	}
79	
80	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
81		r.once.Do(func() {
82			go func() {
83				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProjectRootResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
84				cwd, err := r.getwd()
85				if err == nil {
86					r.root = r.projectRoot(r.ctx, cwd)
87				}
88				r.err = err
89				finish(resolverOutcome(err))
90				close(r.ready)
91			}()
92		})
93		if ctx == nil {
94			ctx = context.Background()
95		}
96		select {
97		case <-ctx.Done():
98			return "", ctx.Err()
99		case <-r.ready:
100			return r.root, r.err
101		}
102	}
103	
104	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Current() (string, bool) {
105		select {
106		case <-r.ready:
107			return r.root, r.err == nil
108		default:
109			return "", false
110		}
111	}
```

```text
1	package repo
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"net/url"
6		"sort"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// RedactCloneRef removes URL userinfo before a clone source is rendered or
11	// persisted in a result. SSH usernames such as git@host remain visible; an
12	// scp-like prefix containing a password/token separator is redacted.
13	func RedactCloneRef(ref string) string {
14		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
15		parsed, err := url.Parse(ref)
16		if err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" && parsed.User != nil {
17			parsed.User = nil
18			return parsed.String()
19		}
20		at := strings.LastIndex(ref, "@")
21		if at > 0 && strings.Contains(ref[:at], ":") {
22			return "***@" + ref[at+1:]
23		}
24		return ref
25	}
26	
27	// RedactCloneError returns an error whose displayed message cannot echo
28	// credential-bearing clone references passed to Git.
29	func RedactCloneError(err error, refs ...string) error {
30		if err == nil {
31			return nil
32		}
33		message := err.Error()
34		refs = append([]string(nil), refs...)
35		sort.SliceStable(refs, func(i, j int) bool { return len(refs[i]) > len(refs[j]) })
36		for _, ref := range refs {
37			if ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref); ref != "" {
38				message = strings.ReplaceAll(message, ref, RedactCloneRef(ref))
39			}
40		}
41		return errors.New(message)
42	}
43
```

```text
func gitOutput(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
	cmd.Dir = dir
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s failed: %s", args[0], strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()))
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
}
```

```text
10	// LocalLoadRequest identifies the three view generations sharing one source
11	// snapshot. Each result remains independently replaceable.
12	type LocalLoadRequest struct {
13		CycleGeneration uint64
14		TasksGeneration uint64
15		ReposGeneration uint64
16		TriesGeneration uint64
17		ShowAllTries    bool
18		ForceSizes      bool
19	}
20	
21	// LocalResult is one terminal TASKS, REPOS, or TRY snapshot.
22	type LocalResult struct {
23		View       View
24		Generation uint64
25		Tasks      []inventory.Row
26		Repos      []RepoRow
27		Tries      []TryRow
28		Valid      bool
29		Err        error
30	}
31	
32	// LocalLoad is a cancellable stream owned by the caller's context.
33	type LocalLoad struct {
34		ID      uint64
35		Request LocalLoadRequest
36		Results <-chan LocalResult
37	}
38	
39	// LocalActions starts one shared local source cycle.
40	type LocalActions struct {
41		Start func(context.Context, LocalLoadRequest) LocalLoad
42	}
43	
44	type localMsg struct {
45		load   LocalLoad
46		result LocalResult
47		done   bool
48	}
49	
50	func (m Model) startLocalLoad() tea.Cmd {
51		if m.actions.Local.Start == nil {
52			return nil
53		}
54		request := LocalLoadRequest{
55			CycleGeneration: m.localGeneration,
56			TasksGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTasks).generation,
57			ReposGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).generation,
58			TriesGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTries).generation,
59			ShowAllTries:    m.showAllTries,
60			ForceSizes:      m.forceSizeReload,
61		}
62		load := m.actions.Local.Start(m.localReadContext(), request)
63		load.Request = request
64		if load.ID == 0 || load.Results == nil {
65			return nil
66		}
67		return waitForLocal(load)
68	}
69	
70	func waitForLocal(load LocalLoad) tea.Cmd {
71		return func() tea.Msg {
72			result, ok := <-load.Results
73			if !ok {
74				return localMsg{load: load, done: true}
75			}
76			return localMsg{load: load, result: result}
77		}
78	}
79	
80	func (m Model) applyLocalResult(result LocalResult) (Model, bool) {
81		accepted := false
82		switch result.View {
83		case ViewTasks:
84			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
85				ViewTasks, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
86				len(result.Tasks), result.Err, result.Valid,
87			)
88			if accepted && result.Valid {
89				m.rows = append([]inventory.Row(nil), result.Tasks...)
90			}
91		case ViewRepos:
92			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
93				ViewRepos, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
94				len(result.Repos), result.Err, result.Valid,
95			)
96			if accepted && result.Valid {
97				m.repos = append([]RepoRow(nil), result.Repos...)
98				m.matchRemoteLocals()
99			}
100		case ViewTries:
101			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
102				ViewTries, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
103				len(result.Tries), result.Err, result.Valid,
104			)
105			if accepted && result.Valid {
106				m.tries = append([]TryRow(nil), result.Tries...)
107				m.matchRemoteLocals()
108			}
109		}
110		m.setAt(m.at())
111		return m, accepted
112	}
113
```

```text
}

// ProjectRoot uses the current linked-worktree checkout root. Falling back to
// cwd outside Git keeps the upstream project-scope convention useful for
// ordinary folders too.
func ProjectRoot(ctx context.Context, cwd string) string {
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(cwd)
	if err == nil {
		cwd = abs
	}
	if repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd); err == nil && repo.Root != "" {
		return repo.Root
	}
	return cwd
}

// Managed reports whether name has an upstream lock entry in the requested
// scope. Direct-managed skills such as dev-cli and herdr must use their own
// update mechanism rather than being handed to `skills update`.
func Managed(ctx context.Context, cwd, name string, scope Scope) bool {
	root := ProjectRoot(ctx, cwd)
	filename := filepath.Join(root, "skills-lock.json")
	if scope == ScopeGlobal {
		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
		filename = filepath.Join(home, ".agents", ".skill-lock.json")
	}
	_, ok := findLockEntry(readLock(filename).Skills, name)
	return ok
}

// List returns a merged, stable inventory. It never downloads the provider;
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
4	
5	The intended result is a provider-independent, no-network skill inventory across repositories with explicit upstream freshness checks; a separate secret-safe MCP declaration inventory; and an unambiguous responsive Tasks table. Read paths must never execute `npx`, start MCP servers, resolve credentials, or claim live MCP health.
6	
7	## Agreed product behavior
8	
9	- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
10	- Native skill discovery covers the complete path registry represented by upstream `skills` v1.5.23 (77 agent IDs), with a versioned, table-driven snapshot. Shared paths such as `.agents/skills` are reported as registry-compatible rather than pretending `dev` detected every installed agent executable.
11	- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
12	- MCP is an independent domain and user surface: `dev mcp list` plus a lazy MCP TUI view. Initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
13	- MCP rows represent static declarations, not effective merged runtime configuration or connectivity. Duplicate declarations remain scope-qualified rows; unsupported/runtime-only sources are diagnosed as partial coverage.
14	
15	# Implementation plan
16	
17	## 1. Resolve reusable repository scan targets
18	
19	- Add a small neutral target type under `internal/agenttarget/` containing repository name/display, canonical path/common-dir identity, and the exact checkout root being scanned.
20	- Build targets by reusing `config.Config.DiscoveryRoots`, `repo.Discover`, `repo.Resolve`, and `gitx.Discover` rather than adding another filesystem walk.
21	- Encode selection policy in this package, not Cobra handlers:
22	  - current mode resolves the exact current checkout, including a linked worktree;
23	  - `--all` returns non-bare canonical discovered checkouts once;
24	  - `--repo` accepts existing repository references and explicit linked-worktree paths;
25	  - TUI aggregation appends the startup checkout when it is not the accepted canonical REPOS row;
26	  - targets are deduplicated by common-dir plus checkout root and sorted deterministically.
27	- Reuse accepted `tui.RepoRow` snapshots for lazy TUI loads so SKILLS/MCP do not rediscover repositories or delay initial startup.
28	
29	## 2. Replace provider-based skill reads with native inventory
30	
31	Refactor `internal/agentskill/agentskill.go` into focused types/registry/scanner/lock/freshness/provider files while preserving the existing mutation command API.
32	
33	### Registry and filesystem scan
34	
35	- Check in a provenance/version-tagged Go registry corresponding to upstream `skills@1.5.23` agent paths, including project/global paths and supported environment overrides (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, XDG config roots, and the other registry-defined homes).
36	- Collapse identical logical directories before reading them; scan only immediate child directories with a valid, size-bounded `SKILL.md` rather than recursively walking repositories or home directories.
37	- Parse the skill frontmatter name with a real YAML parser, merge duplicate logical installations by `(scope, target checkout, normalized skill name)`, and retain all installation paths/agent IDs. Resolve physical symlinks for deduplication without losing the logical path that explains agent attribution.
38	- Treat shared paths as compatible with the registry entries that consume that path; expose an attribution/registry-version field so this is not confused with executable detection.
39	- Make exact lock names win. Only use normalized-name matching when unique; emit a deterministic diagnostic for collisions instead of selecting a random Go map entry.
40	
41	### Locks and local status
42	
43	- Split project and global lock decoding and normalize them internally:
44	  - project `<checkout>/skills-lock.json` (current v1 fields such as source, ref, skill path, and `computedHash`);
45	  - global v3 metadata and compatible older fields from `$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is absolute, otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
46	- Bound lock reads and distinguish missing, malformed, unreadable, unsupported-version, and structurally invalid files. Missing is normal; the other cases become safe per-source diagnostics while other repositories continue.
47	- Include lock-only entries whose installation is absent, and unlocked installed directories as externally managed rows.
48	- Add repository/checkout identity, logical installations, local presence, attribution, and normalized lock metadata to `agentskill.Skill`/result types without removing existing fields.
49	- Keep upstream freshness (`unchecked/current/update_available/upstream_missing/unverifiable/check_failed`) separate from local presence/integrity. Only the embedded `dev-cli` skill receives verified/drifted byte-integrity status; do not claim generic lock hashes verify installed bytes.
50	- Convert `Managed` and `FindProject` to the native lock/scanner primitives so repository scaffolding and selected-skill updates no longer require provider JSON.
51

53	
54	- Preserve and isolate the existing `safeSkillFolder`, folder hashing, Git-source derivation, and grouped `(source URL, ref)` comparisons.
55	- Aggregate all project/global rows first, then run one bounded, cancellation-aware freshness pass so a shared source/ref is cloned once across all repositories. Preserve deterministic row order, clean every temporary clone, and mark only affected rows failed.
56	- Keep local/node_modules/well-known sources unverifiable unless their lock metadata provides a supported comparison; do not silently reinterpret them as Git.
57	- Delete the read-time `npx --no-install skills` path. Read/list/provider-version checks must not invoke npm, a registry, or project Node code.
58	- Retain `interactiveProvider` for explicit add/install/update operations, but require a directly installed `skills` executable after the security review found repository-local `npx` provider substitution. Update `dev doctor` to describe native inventory as always available and report the optional mutation provider separately.

60	## 3. Aggregate skills across repositories and expose them in CLI
61	
62	- Add an inventory collector (representatively `internal/inventory/agent_skills.go`) that scans project targets with the existing context-aware `inventory.Limiter`, scans global paths exactly once, merges diagnostics, and optionally performs one grouped freshness check.
63	- Extend `dev skill list` in `internal/cli/skill.go` with mutually exclusive `--all` and `--repo <ref>` target selection while preserving `--project`, `--global`, `--check`, and the current-checkout default.
64	- Keep the existing JSON array and every existing key/type; add repository/checkout, installations, presence/integrity, attribution/registry-version, and normalized lock fields. Write partial diagnostics to stderr so JSON stdout stays valid.
65	- Add `--repo` to project `dev skill update`; reject repo targeting for global updates. In the TUI, update a selected project skill from that row’s checkout root, while the interactive add wizard continues to use the startup checkout.
66	- Render a repository-aware human table and keep global rows repository-less rather than duplicating them per target.
67	
68	## 4. Add a normalized, secret-safe MCP domain
69	
70	Create `internal/agentmcp/` with normalized types, a scanner, sanitization helpers, and one adapter per supported agent.
71	
72	### Static sources covered
73	
74	- **Claude Code:** project `.mcp.json`; user and per-project local declarations in `~/.claude.json`.
75	- **Codex:** `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` or `~/.codex/config.toml`; trusted-project `.codex/config.toml`; direct and plugin override declarations.

81	### Normalization and safety
82	
83	- Normalize only non-secret facts: server name, agent, declaration scope, repository, config path, managed/direct source, declared enabled/required/trust policy, transport, safe endpoint host or command basename, argument count, and names/kinds of credential references.
84	- Keep each declaration scope-qualified; do not emulate undocumented merge/precedence rules or label a row “effective.” When transport cannot be proven (for example a Cursor URL declaration), report `remote/unknown` rather than guessing.
85	- Sanitize during adapter conversion so raw values never enter normalized rows, diagnostics, traces, CLI JSON, or TUI state:

87	  - never read OpenCode `{file:…}` targets or OAuth/token stores;
88	  - never retain env/header/OAuth values or raw command arguments;
89	  - reduce commands to a safe basename and URLs to a credential-free representation with userinfo/query/fragment removed or redacted;
90	  - use fixed diagnostic codes/messages that cannot echo decoder snippets containing secrets;

92	  - confine project config symlinks to the selected checkout, while allowing bounded user-config symlinks for dotfile managers.
93	- Never invoke agent MCP list/debug commands, helper commands, servers, URLs, or health checks. Document omitted plugin caches, hosted connectors, runtime-only config, remote organization config, and unsupported agent formats as coverage limitations.
94

96
```

1	# Agent skill and MCP inventory
2	
3	Use these inventories to answer two different questions:
4	
5	- `dev skill list`: which reusable instruction packages are present, and whether
6	  an explicit upstream source check reports newer lock-recorded content.
7	- `dev mcp list`: which external MCP capabilities are declared in supported
8	  static agent configuration files.
9	
10	Do not treat an MCP declaration as a skill, a live connection, or permission to
11	invoke tools.
12	
13	## Skill inventory
14	
15	```bash
16	dev skill list
17	dev skill list --repo <repo-or-checkout> --project
18	dev skill list --all
19	dev skill list --all --check --json
20	```
21	
22	Reads use a versioned snapshot of all 77 agent paths from `skills@1.5.23` plus
23	project/global locks. They never execute `skills`, Node, npm, `npx`, agent
24	detectors, or project code. `--all` scans canonical repositories; the TUI also
25	adds its startup linked checkout when distinct and scans global paths once.
26	
27	Keep status dimensions separate:
28	
29	- presence: local directory present or lock-only/missing;
30	- integrity: only embedded `dev-cli` files can be verified against the binary; additional user files are ignored;
31	- update: lock-recorded upstream content is unchecked/current/changed/missing or
32	  unverifiable.
33	
34	`--check` is the explicit network action. It groups equal Git source/ref pairs
35	and does not write installed skills or locks. `skill add` and `skill update` are
36	explicit mutations and require a directly installed `skills` executable; `dev`
37	never resolves a provider through repository-local npm bins.
38	
39	## MCP inventory
40	
41	```bash
42	dev mcp list
43	dev mcp list --repo <repo-or-checkout>
44	dev mcp list --all --json
45	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project
46	```
47	
48	Adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Rows remain
49	scope-qualified declarations; `dev` does not guess effective precedence across
50	files. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` are declaration facts, not health.
51	
52	The scanner never runs agent MCP commands, configured commands/helpers, servers,
53	or URLs. It never expands environment variables, reads OAuth/token stores, or
54	loads OpenCode `{file:…}` content. Normalized output retains only safe command
55	basenames, endpoint scheme/host, argument counts, credential reference names,
56	policy counts, and redaction markers.
57	
58	Omitted sources include plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization
59	configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs.

857	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
858	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
859	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
860	Regenerable data lives separately:

875	inventory, note FTS, size measurements and gitignore templates) and never touch
876	`stats.db`, durable note Markdown or project data.
877	
878	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
879	
880	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
881	below `scan_roots` and at exact `repo_paths`, and never requires a particular physical layout.
882	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
883	explicit path:
884	
885	```bash
886	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
887	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
888	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
889	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
890	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
891	```
892	
893	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
894	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
895	path.
896	
897	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
898	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
899	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
900	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
901	paths.
902	
903	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
904	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
905	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
906	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
907	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
908	
909	## Adopting work in flight
910	
911	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
912	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
913	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
914	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
915	and writes only the ones that exist:
916	
917	```
918	$ dev config init
919	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
920	
921	Detected:
922	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
923	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
924	~/src                16     scan root
925	```
926	
927	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
928	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
929	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
930	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
931	up itself:
932	
933	```bash
934	dev adopt            # report only
935	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
936	```
937	
938	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
939	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
940	`dev help adopting`.
941	
942	## .gitignore
943	
944	```bash
945	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
946	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
947	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
948	```
949	
950	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
951	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
952	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and
953	ephemeral coding-agent state such as linked worktrees and local settings.
954	Review artifacts such as SpecStory histories and agent plans remain trackable
955	unless you add your own ignore rule for them.
956	
957	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
958	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
959	
960	## Configuration
961	
962	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
963	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
964	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
965	
966	```bash
967	dev edit
968	dev config edit
969	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
970	```
971	
972	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
973	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
974	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
975	
976	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
977	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
978	
979	```toml
980	[paths]
981	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
982	repo_paths    = ["~/.local/share/chezmoi"] # exact repos outside useful roots
983	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
984	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
985	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
986	```
987	
988	`state_dir/tasks/*.toml` stores task intent; `state_dir/assets/*.toml` stores
989	stable repository/Try identity, tags, one metadata summary, experiment
990	lifecycle and per-host locations; `state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/*.md` stores
991	multiple repository quick notes; `state_dir/artifact-intents/v1/*.json` stores
992	versioned post-writer handoffs and commit receipts. Git status, logical byte
993	counts and `.specstory/statistics.json` are derived rather than durable review
994	history. Size cache lives in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/sizes-v1.json` and is safe to
995	delete.
996	
997	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
998	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
999	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
1000	named `{{rep}}`.
1001	
1002	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
1003	special mode:
1004	
1005	```toml
1006	[paths]
1007	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
1008	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
1009	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
1010	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"

```text
// CheckUpdates compares lock-recorded content with the current Git source.
// It never invokes `skills update` because that command writes immediately.
func CheckUpdates(ctx context.Context, rows []Skill) []Skill {
	out := append([]Skill(nil), rows...)
	type member struct {
		index int
		url   string
		ref   string
	}
	groups := map[string][]member{}
	for i := range out {
		row := &out[i]
		if row.ManagedBy != ManagedBySkills || row.lock == nil {
			continue
		}
		url, ok := sourceURL(*row.lock)
		if !ok || row.lock.SkillPath == "" {
			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnknown
			row.UpdateDetail = "lock entry has no checkable Git source and skill path"
			continue
		}
		key := url + "\x00" + row.lock.Ref
		groups[key] = append(groups[key], member{index: i, url: url, ref: row.lock.Ref})
	}

	for _, members := range groups {
		dir, err := cloneSource(ctx, members[0].url, members[0].ref)
		if err != nil {
			for _, member := range members {
				out[member.index].UpdateStatus = UpdateFailed
				out[member.index].UpdateDetail = "could not fetch source"
			}
			continue
		}
		for _, member := range members {
			checkOne(ctx, dir, &out[member.index])
		}
		os.RemoveAll(filepath.Dir(dir))
	}
	return out
}

func sourceURL(entry lockEntry) (string, bool) {
	if entry.SourceType == "local" || entry.SourceType == "node_modules" || entry.SourceType == "well-known" {
		return "", false
	}
	if entry.SourceURL != "" {
		return entry.SourceURL, true
	}
	if entry.SourceType == "github" {
		parts := strings.Split(strings.Trim(entry.Source, "/"), "/")
		if len(parts) >= 2 {
			return "https://github.com/" + parts[0] + "/" + parts[1] + ".git", true
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(entry.Source, "://") || strings.HasSuffix(entry.Source, ".git") {
		return entry.Source, true
	}
	return "", false
}

func cloneSource(ctx context.Context, url, ref string) (string, error) {
	parent, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-skill-check-*")
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	dir := filepath.Join(parent, "source")
	if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, "", "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", url, dir); err != nil {
		os.RemoveAll(parent)
		return "", err
	}
	if ref != "" {
		if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "fetch", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "origin", ref); err != nil {
			os.RemoveAll(parent)
			return "", err
		}
		if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", "FETCH_HEAD"); err != nil {
			os.RemoveAll(parent)
			return "", err
		}
	}
	return dir, nil
}

func checkOne(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, row *Skill) {
	entry := row.lock
	folder, ok := safeSkillFolder(entry.SkillPath)
	if !ok {
		row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnknown
		row.UpdateDetail = "invalid skill path in lock entry"
		return
	}
	abs := filepath.Join(repoDir, filepath.FromSlash(folder))
	if info, err := os.Stat(abs); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateMissing
			row.UpdateDetail = "skill path no longer exists upstream"
		} else {
			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateFailed
			row.UpdateDetail = "could not inspect upstream skill path"
		}
		return
	}

	expected := entry.ComputedHash
	actual := ""
	if row.Scope == ScopeGlobal {
		expected = entry.SkillFolderHash
		if len(expected) == 40 {
			spec := "HEAD^{tree}"
			if folder != "" {
				spec = "HEAD:" + folder
			}
			actual, _ = gitOutput(ctx, repoDir, "rev-parse", spec)
		} else if len(expected) == 64 {
			actual, _ = folderHash(abs)
		}
	} else if len(expected) == 64 {
		actual, _ = folderHash(abs)
	}
	if expected == "" || actual == "" {
		row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnknown
		row.UpdateDetail = "lock entry has no comparable content hash"
		return
	}
	if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(actual), strings.TrimSpace(expected)) {
		row.UpdateStatus = UpdateCurrent
		row.UpdateDetail = "matches the recorded upstream content"
	} else {
		row.UpdateStatus = UpdateAvailable
		row.UpdateDetail = "upstream content changed"
	}
}

func safeSkillFolder(skillPath string) (string, bool) {
	p := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(skillPath), "\\", "/")
	if strings.EqualFold(path.Base(p), "SKILL.md") {
		p = path.Dir(p)
	}
	if p == "." {
		p = ""
	}
	clean := path.Clean(p)
	if clean == "." {
		clean = ""
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(clean, "/") || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") {
		return "", false
	}
	return clean, true
}

func folderHash(dir string) (string, error) {
	type file struct {
		name string
		body []byte
	}
	var files []file
	err := filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(filename string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if d.IsDir() && filename != dir && (d.Name() == ".git" || d.Name() == "node_modules") {
			return filepath.SkipDir
		}
		if d.Type().IsRegular() {
			body, err := os.ReadFile(filename)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
```

```text
13	func resolverOutcome(err error) perftrace.Outcome {
14		if err != nil {
15			return perftrace.OutcomeFailed
16		}
17		return perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
18	}
19	
20	// tuiRuntimeResolver moves runtime auto-detection off the first-view path while
21	// sharing exactly one result across inventory loads and actions.
22	type tuiRuntimeResolver struct {
23		trace   *perftrace.Recorder
24		resolve func() runtime.Runtime
25		once    sync.Once
26		ready   chan struct{}
27		rt      runtime.Runtime
28	}
29	
30	func newTUIRuntimeResolver(app *App) *tuiRuntimeResolver {
31		snapshot := *app
32		return &tuiRuntimeResolver{
33			trace: app.trace, resolve: snapshot.Runtime, ready: make(chan struct{}),
34		}
35	}
36	
37	func (r *tuiRuntimeResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
38		r.once.Do(func() {
39			go func() {
40				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIRuntimeResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
41				r.rt = r.resolve()
42				finish(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
43				close(r.ready)
44			}()
45		})
46		if ctx == nil {
47			ctx = context.Background()
48		}
49		select {
50		case <-ctx.Done():
51			return nil, ctx.Err()
52		case <-r.ready:
53			return r.rt, nil
54		}
55	}
56	
57	// tuiProjectRootResolver keeps Git project-root discovery lazy and shared by
58	// SKILLS reads/actions.
59	type tuiProjectRootResolver struct {
60		trace       *perftrace.Recorder
61		ctx         context.Context
62		getwd       func() (string, error)
63		projectRoot func(context.Context, string) string
64		once        sync.Once
65		ready       chan struct{}
66		root        string
67		err         error
68	}
69	
70	func newTUIProjectRootResolver(trace *perftrace.Recorder, ctx context.Context) *tuiProjectRootResolver {
71		if ctx == nil {
72			ctx = context.Background()
73		}
74		return &tuiProjectRootResolver{
75			trace: trace, ctx: ctx, getwd: os.Getwd, projectRoot: agentskill.ProjectRoot,
76			ready: make(chan struct{}),
77		}
78	}
79	
80	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
81		r.once.Do(func() {
82			go func() {
83				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProjectRootResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
84				cwd, err := r.getwd()
85				if err == nil {
86					r.root = r.projectRoot(r.ctx, cwd)
87				}
88				r.err = err
89				finish(resolverOutcome(err))
90				close(r.ready)
91			}()
92		})
93		if ctx == nil {
94			ctx = context.Background()
95		}
96		select {
97		case <-ctx.Done():
98			return "", ctx.Err()
99		case <-r.ready:
100			return r.root, r.err
101		}
102	}
103	
104	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Current() (string, bool) {
105		select {
106		case <-r.ready:
107			return r.root, r.err == nil
108		default:
109			return "", false
110		}
111	}
```

```text
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.

54		}
```

```text
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}

298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
```

```text
5	// Limiter bounds expensive local enrichment across collectors that would
6	// otherwise each create their own worker pool.
7	type Limiter struct {
8		permits chan struct{}
9	}
10	
11	// NewLimiter returns a context-aware concurrency bound.
12	func NewLimiter(limit int) *Limiter {
13		if limit <= 0 {
14			limit = 8
15		}
16		return &Limiter{permits: make(chan struct{}, limit)}
17	}
18	
19	// Acquire waits for one permit and returns a matching release function.
20	func (l *Limiter) Acquire(ctx context.Context) (func(), bool) {
21		if l == nil {
22			return func() {}, true
23		}
24		if ctx == nil {
25			ctx = context.Background()
26		}
27		select {
28		case l.permits <- struct{}{}:
29			return func() { <-l.permits }, true
30		case <-ctx.Done():
31			return nil, false
32		}
33	}
```

```text
31	}
32	
33	type repoSkillResult struct {
34		Installed []string `json:"installed,omitempty"`
35		Setup     []string `json:"setup,omitempty"`
36		Warnings  []string `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
37	}
38	
39	func installRepoSkills(ctx context.Context, app *App, root string, specs []repoSkillSpec) (repoSkillResult, error) {
40		var result repoSkillResult
41		type installGroup struct {
42			source string
43			agents []string
44			names  []string
45		}
46		var groups []installGroup
47		for _, spec := range specs {
48			key := spec.Source + "\x00" + strings.Join(spec.Agents, "\x00")
49			groupIndex := -1
50			for index := range groups {
51				if groups[index].source+"\x00"+strings.Join(groups[index].agents, "\x00") == key {
52					groupIndex = index
53					break
54				}
55			}
56			if groupIndex < 0 {
57				groups = append(groups, installGroup{source: spec.Source, agents: append([]string(nil), spec.Agents...)})
58				groupIndex = len(groups) - 1
59			}
60			groups[groupIndex].names = append(groups[groupIndex].names, spec.Name)
61		}
62		for _, group := range groups {
63			process, err := agentskill.InstallCommand(ctx, root, group.source, group.names, group.agents)
64			if err != nil {
65				return result, fmt.Errorf("prepare skills %s install: %w", strings.Join(group.names, ", "), err)
66			}
67			process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = app.In, app.Out, app.Err
68			if err := process.Run(); err != nil {
69				return result, fmt.Errorf("install skills %s: %w", strings.Join(group.names, ", "), err)
70			}
71			result.Installed = append(result.Installed, group.names...)
72		}
73		return result, nil
74	}
75	
76	func runRepoSkillSetups(ctx context.Context, app *App, root string, phase repoHookPhase, specs []repoSkillSpec) (repoSkillResult, error) {
77		var result repoSkillResult
78		for _, spec := range specs {
79			if spec.Setup == nil || spec.Setup.Phase != phase ||
80				(strings.TrimSpace(spec.Setup.Script) == "" && strings.TrimSpace(spec.Setup.Builtin) == "") {
81				continue
82			}
83			if err := runRepoSkillSetup(ctx, app, root, spec.Name, *spec.Setup); err != nil {
84				if spec.Setup.Required {
85					return result, fmt.Errorf("set up skill %s: %w", spec.Name, err)
86				}
87				warning := fmt.Sprintf("skill %s setup: %v", spec.Name, err)
88				result.Warnings = append(result.Warnings, warning)
89				app.warnf("%s", warning)
90				continue
91			}
92			result.Setup = append(result.Setup, spec.Name)
93		}
94		return result, nil
95	}
96	
97	func runRepoSkillSetup(ctx context.Context, app *App, root, name string, setup repoSkillSetup) error {
98		if setup.Timeout <= 0 {
99			setup.Timeout = 10 * time.Minute
100		}
101		commandCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, setup.Timeout)
102		defer cancel()
103		if setup.Builtin != "" {
104			return runBuiltinRepoSkillSetup(commandCtx, app, root, setup.Builtin, setup.Args)
105		}
106		skill, err := agentskill.FindProject(ctx, root, name)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		skillRoot, err := pathx.Canonical(skill.Path)
111		if err != nil {
112			return err
113		}
114		script, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(skillRoot, filepath.Join(skillRoot, filepath.FromSlash(setup.Script)))
115		if err != nil {
116			return fmt.Errorf("setup entrypoint must stay within installed skill: %w", err)
117		}
118		command := setup.Interpreter
119		args := append([]string{script}, setup.Args...)
120		if command == "" {
121			command = script
122			args = setup.Args
123		}
124		if _, err := exec.LookPath(command); err != nil {
125			return fmt.Errorf("interpreter/executable %q is unavailable", command)
126		}
127		process := exec.CommandContext(commandCtx, command, args...)
128		process.Dir = root
129		process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = app.In, app.Out, app.Err
130		if err := process.Run(); err != nil {
131			if commandCtx.Err() != nil {
132				return commandCtx.Err()
133			}
134			return err
135		}
136		return nil
137	}
138	
139	func runUpstreamSkillCatalog(ctx context.Context, app *App, root, source string) error {
140		process, err := agentskill.AddCommand(ctx, root, source)
141		if err != nil {
142			return err
143		}
144		process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = app.In, app.Out, app.Err
145		return process.Run()
146	}
```

```text
487	func validateRepoWorkflowRequest(app *App, request repoWorkflowRequest, yes bool) error {
488		if request.JSON && request.Handoff != repoHandoffStay {
489			return errors.New("--json requires --handoff=stay")
490		}
491		if request.Handoff == repoHandoffStart && !app.interactive() {
492			return errors.New("--handoff=start requires an interactive terminal")
493		}
494		if request.JSON && request.BrowseSkills {
495			return errors.New("--json cannot open the interactive upstream skills installer")
496		}
497		if request.BrowseSkills && !app.interactive() {
498			return errors.New("--browse-skills requires an interactive terminal")
499		}
500		if request.Kind == repo.AcquireNew && request.Publish != nil && request.Publish.Push {
501			if request.CheckIn != repoCheckInCommit {
502				return errors.New("pushing a new upstream requires --check-in=commit; use --push=false to create an empty upstream")
503			}
504		}
505		if request.Publish != nil && request.CheckIn == repoCheckInStage {
506			return errors.New("--check-in=stage cannot create an upstream; review and commit locally before publishing")
507		}
508		if request.Handoff == repoHandoffStart && request.CheckIn != repoCheckInCommit &&
509			(request.Kind == repo.AcquireNew || request.Scaffold.Preset != "" || request.Prepared.Plan.Root != "") {
510			return errors.New("--handoff=start requires --check-in=commit when repository setup changes files")
511		}
512		if request.Kind != repo.AcquireNew && request.Publish != nil {
513			remoteName := strings.TrimSpace(request.Publish.RemoteName)
514			if remoteName == "" {
515				remoteName = "origin"
516			}
517			if current := gitx.Remote(ctxOf(), request.Destination, remoteName); current != "" {
518				return fmt.Errorf("remote %s already points to %s; omit --remote or remove it explicitly before publishing", remoteName, current)
519			}
520		}
521		if !app.interactive() && !yes && (len(request.Prepared.Plan.Hooks) > 0 || len(request.Prepared.Plan.Skills) > 0 || request.BrowseSkills) {
522			return errors.New("non-interactive hooks or skill setup require --yes")
523		}
524		for _, skill := range request.Prepared.Plan.Skills {
525			if _, err := agentskill.InstallCommand(ctxOf(), request.Destination, skill.Source, []string{skill.Name}, skill.Agents); err != nil {
526				return fmt.Errorf("skill %s cannot be installed: %w", skill.Name, err)
527			}
528			if skill.Setup == nil || skill.Setup.Builtin != "" || skill.Setup.Interpreter == "" {
529				continue
530			}
531			if _, err := exec.LookPath(skill.Setup.Interpreter); err != nil && skill.Setup.Required {
532				return fmt.Errorf("skill %s setup requires unavailable interpreter %q", skill.Name, skill.Setup.Interpreter)
533			}
534		}
535		for _, hook := range request.Prepared.Plan.Hooks {
536			if runtime.GOOS == "windows" && strings.TrimSpace(hook.Run) != "" {
537				return fmt.Errorf("hook %s uses a POSIX shell expression, which is unsupported on Windows; use command = [...]", hook.ID)
538			}
539			if len(hook.Command) > 0 && hook.Required && !isRepoLocalExecutable(request.Destination, hook.Command[0]) {
540				if _, err := exec.LookPath(hook.Command[0]); err != nil {
541					return fmt.Errorf("hook %s requires unavailable executable %q", hook.ID, hook.Command[0])
542				}
543			}
544		}
545		return nil
546	}
547	
548	func isRepoLocalExecutable(root, executable string) bool {
549		if !filepath.IsAbs(executable) {
550			return strings.ContainsAny(executable, `/\\`)
551		}
552		relative, err := filepath.Rel(root, executable)
553		return err == nil && relative != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(relative, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
554	}
555	
556	func executeRepoWorkflow(app *App, request repoWorkflowRequest) error {
557		if request.Kind == repo.AcquireClone && request.DryRun {
558			return renderCloneDryRun(app, request)
559		}
```

```text
- macOS managed preferences: On macOS, OpenCode reads managed preferences from the ai.opencode.managed preference domain; administrators can deploy settings via .mobileconfig (MDM) and those are applied at highest priority (not user-overridable). - Precedence order: Typical merge/order (from lowest to highest priority) — remote org defaults (.well-known/opencode), global (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json), custom/OPENCODE_CONFIG, project opencode.json, .opencode directories (agents/commands/plugins), OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT inline, managed files / MDM as highest priority. 2	
```
3	Use these inventories to answer two different questions:
4

6	  an explicit upstream source check reports newer lock-recorded content.
7	- `dev mcp list`: which external MCP capabilities are declared in supported
8	  static agent configuration files.
9	
10	Do not treat an MCP declaration as a skill, a live connection, or permission to
11	invoke tools.
12	
13	## Skill inventory

18	dev skill list --all
19	dev skill list --all --check --json

25	adds its startup linked checkout when distinct and scans global paths once.

27	Keep status dimensions separate:
28	
29	- presence: local directory present or lock-only/missing;
30	- integrity: only embedded `dev-cli` files can be verified against the binary; additional user files are ignored;
31	- update: lock-recorded upstream content is unchecked/current/changed/missing or
32	  unverifiable.
33	
34	`--check` is the explicit network action. It groups equal Git source/ref pairs
35	and does not write installed skills or locks. `skill add` and `skill update` are
36	explicit mutations and require a directly installed `skills` executable; `dev`
37	never resolves a provider through repository-local npm bins.

39	## MCP inventory

43	dev mcp list --repo <repo-or-checkout>
44	dev mcp list --all --json
45	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project
46	```

48	Adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Rows remain

52	The scanner never runs agent MCP commands, configured commands/helpers, servers,

58	Omitted sources include plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization

```text
1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
16		// its own entry below the shared common directory.
17		GitDir string
18		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
19		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
20		GitCommonDir string
21		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
22		Name string
23		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
24		// the main checkout.
25		IsLinkedWorktree bool
26		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
27		MainRoot string
28		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
29		Bare bool
30	}
31	
32	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
33	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
34	
35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {
81			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}
89	
90	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
91	// a full Discover.
92	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
93		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
94		return err == nil
95	}
96	
97	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
98	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
99	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
100	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
```

```text
+		{name: "repository boundary", width: 97, wantWidth: 97, wantRepo: true},
+		{name: "wide", width: 120, wantWidth: 120, wantRepo: true},
+	}
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			m := tui.New(newActions(&recorder{}, []inventory.Row{r}), []inventory.Row{r}, nil)
+			m = send(m, tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: tt.width, Height: 24})
+			lines := strings.Split(m.View(), "\n")
+			headerAt := -1
+			for i, line := range lines {
+				if strings.Contains(line, "TASK") && strings.Contains(line, "STATE") && strings.Contains(line, "BRANCH") {
+					headerAt = i
+					break
+				}
+			}
+			if headerAt < 0 || headerAt+1 >= len(lines) {
+				t.Fatalf("TASKS table not found:\n%s", m.View())
+			}
+			header, taskRow := lines[headerAt], lines[headerAt+1]
+			if got := lipgloss.Width(header); got != tt.wantWidth {
+				t.Errorf("header width = %d, want %d:\n%s", got, tt.wantWidth, header)
+			}
+			if got := lipgloss.Width(taskRow); got != tt.wantWidth {
+				t.Errorf("row width = %d, want %d:\n%s", got, tt.wantWidth, taskRow)
+			}
+			if got := strings.Contains(header, "REPO"); got != tt.wantRepo {
+				t.Errorf("REPO header present = %t, want %t:\n%s", got, tt.wantRepo, header)
+			}
+			if got := strings.Contains(taskRow, r.Task.Repo); got != tt.wantRepo {
+				t.Errorf("repository value present = %t, want %t:\n%s", got, tt.wantRepo, taskRow)
+			}
+			if !strings.Contains(taskRow, r.Task.Title()) {
+				t.Errorf("CJK task title missing:\n%s", taskRow)
+			}
+
+			columns := []string{"TASK", "STATE"}
+			if tt.wantRepo {
+				columns = append(columns, "REPO")
+			}
+			columns = append(columns, "BRANCH", "GIT", "AGE", "NEXT")
+			previous := -1
+			for _, column := range columns {
+				at := strings.Index(header, column)
+				if at <= previous {
+					t.Fatalf("column %s is missing or out of order:\n%s", column, header)
+				}
+				previous = at
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

 func TestSkillsCheckWaitsForInitialLocalSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
 	started := make(chan struct{})
 	release := make(chan struct{})
 	checks := 0
 	actions := newActions(&recorder{}, nil)
 	actions.ReloadSkills = func(context.Context) ([]agentskill.Skill, error) {
 		close(started)
 		<-release
 		return []agentskill.Skill{{Name: "loaded", Scope: agentskill.ScopeProject}}, nil
 	}
 	actions.CheckSkills = func(_ context.Context, rows []agentskill.Skill) []agentskill.Skill {
 		checks++
 		return rows
 	}
 	m := tui.New(actions, nil, nil)
 	m = send(m, key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"))
 	next, loadCommand := m.Update(key("tab"))
 	m = next.(tui.Model)
 	loadResult := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
 	go func() { loadResult <- loadCommand() }()
 	<-started
 
 	next, checkCommand := m.Update(key("c"))
 	m = next.(tui.Model)
 	if checkCommand != nil || checks != 0 || !strings.Contains(m.View(), "wait for local agent skills") {
 		t.Fatalf("check superseded initial skills load (checks=%d cmd=%v):\n%s", checks, checkCommand, m.View())
 	}
 	close(release)
 	m = send(m, <-loadResult)
 	m = send(m, key("c"))
 	if checks != 1 || !strings.Contains(m.View(), "loaded") {
 		t.Fatalf("check after local load failed (checks=%d):\n%s", checks, m.View())
 	}
 }

+func TestMCPWaitsForAcceptedRepositorySnapshot(t *testing.T) {
+	localResults := make(chan tui.LocalResult, 3)
+	var request tui.LocalLoadRequest
+	var gotRepos []tui.RepoRow
+	loads := 0
+	actions := newActions(&recorder{}, nil)
+	actions.Local.Start = func(_ context.Context, got tui.LocalLoadRequest) tui.LocalLoad {
+		request = got
+		return tui.LocalLoad{ID: 41, Request: got, Results: localResults}
+	}
+	actions.ReloadMCPWithRepos = func(_ context.Context, repos []tui.RepoRow) ([]agentmcp.Declaration, error) {
+		loads++
+		gotRepos = append([]tui.RepoRow(nil), repos...)
+		return []agentmcp.Declaration{{
+			Name: "shared", Agent: agentmcp.AgentClaudeCode, Scope: agentmcp.ScopeProject,
+			Repository: "shared-api", Transport: agentmcp.TransportStdio,
+		}}, nil
+	}
+	m := tui.New(actions, nil, nil).BeginLoading()
+	initial := m.Init()().(tea.BatchMsg)
+	m = send(m, key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"), key("tab"))
+	if loads != 0 || !strings.Contains(m.View(), "waiting for local repositories") {
+		t.Fatalf("MCP did not wait for REPOS (loads=%d):\n%s", loads, m.View())
+	}
+
+	localResults <- tui.LocalResult{
+		View: tui.ViewRepos, Generation: request.ReposGeneration,
+		Repos: []tui.RepoRow{repoRow("shared-api")}, Valid: true,
+	}
+	next, command := m.Update(initial[1]())
+	m = next.(tui.Model)
+	batch := command().(tea.BatchMsg)
+	m = send(m, batch[1]())
+	if loads != 1 || len(gotRepos) != 1 || gotRepos[0].Repo.Name != "shared-api" {
+		t.Fatalf("MCP loads=%d repos=%+v", loads, gotRepos)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(m.View(), "shared") {
+		t.Fatalf("MCP result missing:\n%s", m.View())
+	}
+	close(localResults)
+}

 func TestFilterByState(t *testing.T) {
 	rows := []inventory.Row{
 		row("a", "hot task", task.Hot, ""),
 		row("b", "warm task", task.Warm, ""),
 		row("c", "done task", task.Done, ""),
 	}
 	m := tui.New(newActions(&recorder{}, rows), rows, nil)
 
 	// Done tasks are hidden by default — a finished task is not work in progress.
 	if strings.Contains(m.View(), "done task") {
 		t.Error("done tasks should be hidden by default")
 	}
 
 	got := send(m, key("1")).View()
 	if !strings.Contains(got, "hot task") || strings.Contains(got, "warm task") {
 		t.Errorf("filter 1 should show only hot:\n%s", got)
 	}
 	got = send(m, key("2")).View()
 	if !strings.Contains(got, "warm task") || strings.Contains(got, "hot task") {
 		t.Errorf("filter 2 should show only warm:\n%s", got)
 	}
 	got = send(m, key("a")).View()
 	if !strings.Contains(got, "done task") {
 		t.Errorf("a should reveal done tasks:\n%s", got)
 	}
 }
```

```text
# MCP servers with Gemini CLI

This document provides a guide to configuring and using Model Context Protocol
(MCP) servers with Gemini CLI.

## What is an MCP server?

An MCP server is an application that exposes tools and resources to the Gemini
CLI through the Model Context Protocol, allowing it to interact with external
systems and data sources. MCP servers act as a bridge between the Gemini model
and your local environment or other services like APIs.

An MCP server enables Gemini CLI to:

- **Discover tools:** List available tools, their descriptions, and parameters
  through standardized schema definitions.
- **Execute tools:** Call specific tools with defined arguments and receive
  structured responses.
- **Access resources:** Read data from specific resources that the server
  exposes (files, API payloads, reports, etc.).

With an MCP server, you can extend Gemini CLI's capabilities to perform actions
beyond its built-in features, such as interacting with databases, APIs, custom
scripts, or specialized workflows.

## Core integration architecture

Gemini CLI integrates with MCP servers through a sophisticated discovery and
execution system built into the core package (`packages/core/src/tools/`):

### Discovery Layer (`mcp-client.ts`)

The discovery process is orchestrated by `discoverMcpTools()`, which:

1. **Iterates through configured servers** from your `settings.json`
   `mcpServers` configuration
2. **Establishes connections** using appropriate transport mechanisms (Stdio,
   SSE, or Streamable HTTP)
3. **Fetches tool definitions** from each server using the MCP protocol
4. **Sanitizes and validates** tool schemas for compatibility with the Gemini
   API
5. **Registers tools** in the global tool registry with conflict resolution
6. **Fetches and registers resources** if the server exposes any

### Execution layer (`mcp-tool.ts`)

Each discovered MCP tool is wrapped in a `DiscoveredMCPTool` instance that:
```

```text
211	func defaultCoverage() Coverage {
212		return Coverage{
213			Agents:                 []Agent{AgentClaudeCode, AgentCodex, AgentCursor, AgentGeminiCLI, AgentOpenCode},
214			StaticDeclarationsOnly: true,
215			OmittedSources: []string{
216				"runtime health and command-line-only configuration",
217				"plugin caches and hosted connectors",
218				"remote organization configuration",
219				"inline OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT",
220			},
221		}
222	}

224	// Filter selects declarations for CLI or TUI consumers. Empty fields are
225	// wildcards; Enabled and HasCredentials distinguish an omitted filter from false.
226	type Filter struct {
227		Agent          Agent
228		Scope          Scope
229		Source         DeclarationSource
230		Transport      Transport
231		Repository     string
232		NameContains   string
233		Enabled        *bool
234		HasCredentials *bool
235	}
236	
237	// Match reports whether a declaration satisfies f.
238	func (f Filter) Match(d Declaration) bool {
239		if f.Agent != "" && d.Agent != f.Agent ||
240			f.Scope != "" && d.Scope != f.Scope ||
241			f.Source != "" && d.Source != f.Source ||
242			f.Transport != "" && d.Transport != f.Transport ||
243			f.Repository != "" && d.Repository != f.Repository {
244			return false
245		}
246		if f.NameContains != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(d.Name), strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.NameContains))) {
247			return false
248		}
249		if f.Enabled != nil && (d.Enabled == nil || *d.Enabled != *f.Enabled) {
250			return false
251		}
252		if f.HasCredentials != nil && (len(d.Credentials) > 0) != *f.HasCredentials {
253			return false
254		}
255		return true
256	}
257	
258	// FilterDeclarations returns matching rows without changing their order.
259	func FilterDeclarations(rows []Declaration, f Filter) []Declaration {
260		out := make([]Declaration, 0, len(rows))
261		for _, row := range rows {
262			if f.Match(row) {
263				out = append(out, row)
264			}
265		}
266		return out
267	}
268	
269	// SortDeclarations establishes the stable order used by Scan.
270	func SortDeclarations(rows []Declaration) {
271		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
272			a, b := rows[i], rows[j]
273			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Source), strings.ToLower(a.Plugin), a.Plugin, strings.ToLower(a.Name), a.Name}
274			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Source), strings.ToLower(b.Plugin), b.Plugin, strings.ToLower(b.Name), b.Name}
275			for n := range ak {
276				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
277					return ak[n] < bk[n]
278				}
279			}
280			return false
281		})
282	}
283	
284	func scopeSortKey(scope Scope) string {
285		switch scope {
286		case ScopeProject:
287			return "0-project"
288		case ScopeLocal:
289			return "1-local"
290		case ScopeUser:
291			return "2-user"
292		case ScopeCustom:
293			return "3-custom"
294		case ScopeSystemDefaults:
295			return "4-system-defaults"
296		case ScopeSystemOverride:
297			return "5-system-override"
298		case ScopeManaged:
299			return "6-managed"
300		default:
301			return "9-" + string(scope)
302		}
303	}
304	
305	func diagnosticMessage(code DiagnosticCode) string {
306		switch code {
307		case DiagnosticUnreadable:
308			return "configuration file could not be read"
309		case DiagnosticTooLarge:
310			return "configuration file exceeds the scan size limit"
311		case DiagnosticNotRegular:
312			return "configuration source is not a regular file"
313		case DiagnosticSymlinkLimit:
314			return "configuration symlink chain exceeds the scan limit"
315		case DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape:
316			return "project configuration resolves outside the checkout"
317		case DiagnosticMalformed:
318			return "configuration file could not be decoded"
319		case DiagnosticControlCharacter:
320			return "configuration contains an unsupported control character"
321		case DiagnosticInvalidDeclaration:
322			return "server declaration has an invalid field"
323		case DiagnosticInvalidName:
324			return "server declaration has an invalid name"
325		case DiagnosticUnknownTransport:
326			return "server transport cannot be determined statically"
327		case DiagnosticConflictingTransport:
328			return "server declaration contains conflicting transport fields"
329		case DiagnosticInvalidEndpoint:
330			return "server endpoint could not be represented safely"
331		case DiagnosticInvalidReference:
332			return "credential reference name is invalid"
333		case DiagnosticPluginDefinitionAbsent:
334			return "plugin override does not include the plugin server definition"
335		case DiagnosticTransportPrecedence:
336			return "lower-precedence transport fields were ignored"
337		default:
338			return "configuration could not be fully represented"
339		}
340	}
341	
342	func coverage(code DiagnosticCode) CoverageDiagnostic {
343		return CoverageDiagnostic{Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code)}
344	}
```
