171	// NewScanner creates a scanner for explicitly supplied host paths.
172	func NewScanner(options Options) *Scanner {
173		options = normalizeOptions(options)
174		s := &Scanner{options: options}
175		s.readSource = s.readSourceFromDisk
176		return s

179	// Scan uses documented host defaults.
180	func Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
181		return NewScanner(DefaultOptions()).Scan(ctx, targets)
182	}
183	
184	// Scan returns all static declarations it can decode and fixed diagnostics for
185	// individual source failures. Cancellation is the only normal top-level scan
186	// failure and is returned as ctx.Err(), with any rows already collected.
187	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
188		if ctx == nil {
189			ctx = context.Background()
190		}
191		targets = normalizeTargets(targets, s.options.WorkingDirectory)
192		result := Result{Coverage: defaultCoverage()}
193	
194		for _, spec := range s.hostSources() {
195			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
196				finalizeResult(&result)
197				return result, err
198			}
199			rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, targets)
200			result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, rows...)
201			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
202		}
203		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
204			finalizeResult(&result)
205			return result, err
206		}
207	
208		projectResults := make([]Result, len(targets))
209		jobs := make(chan int)
210		workers := s.options.Concurrency
211		if workers > len(targets) {
212			workers = len(targets)
213		}
214		var wg sync.WaitGroup
215		for range workers {
216			wg.Add(1)
217			go func() {
218				defer wg.Done()
219				for {
220					select {
221					case <-ctx.Done():
222						return
223					case index, ok := <-jobs:
224						if !ok {
225							return
226						}
227						for _, spec := range projectSources(targets[index]) {
228							if ctx.Err() != nil {
229								return
230							}
231							rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, nil)
232							projectResults[index].Declarations = append(projectResults[index].Declarations, rows...)
233							projectResults[index].Diagnostics = append(projectResults[index].Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
234						}
235					}
236				}
237			}()
238		}
239		for index := range targets {
240			select {
241			case jobs <- index:
242			case <-ctx.Done():
243				close(jobs)
244				wg.Wait()
245				for _, partial := range projectResults {
246					result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, partial.Declarations...)
247					result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, partial.Diagnostics...)
248				}
249				finalizeResult(&result)
250				return result, ctx.Err()
251			}
252		}
253		close(jobs)
254		wg.Wait()
255		for _, partial := range projectResults {
256			result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, partial.Declarations...)
257			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, partial.Diagnostics...)
258		}
259		finalizeResult(&result)
260		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
261			return result, err
262		}
263		return result, nil
264	}

270		if options.XDGConfigHome != "" && !filepath.IsAbs(options.XDGConfigHome) {

279		if options.Concurrency <= 0 {
280			options.Concurrency = defaultConcurrency
281		} else if options.Concurrency > maximumConcurrency {
282			options.Concurrency = maximumConcurrency
283		}
284		if options.MaxFileBytes <= 0 {
285			options.MaxFileBytes = DefaultMaxFileBytes
286		} else if options.MaxFileBytes > maximumMaxFileBytes {

288		}
289		if options.MaxSymlinkDepth <= 0 {

291		} else if options.MaxSymlinkDepth > maximumSymlinkDepth {
292			options.MaxSymlinkDepth = maximumSymlinkDepth
293		}
294		return options

297	func normalizeTargets(targets []Target, cwd string) []Target {
298		out := make([]Target, 0, len(targets))
299		for _, target := range targets {
300			if strings.TrimSpace(target.CheckoutRoot) == "" {
301				continue
302			}
303			checkout := target.CheckoutRoot
304			if !filepath.IsAbs(checkout) {
305				checkout = filepath.Join(cwd, checkout)
306			}
307			absolute, err := filepath.Abs(checkout)
308			if err != nil {
309				continue
310			}
311			target.CheckoutRoot = filepath.Clean(absolute)
312			if target.RepoPath == "" {
313				target.RepoPath = target.CheckoutRoot
314			} else if !filepath.IsAbs(target.RepoPath) {
315				target.RepoPath = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(cwd, target.RepoPath))
316			}
317			target.RepoDisplay = strings.TrimSpace(target.RepoDisplay)
318			if target.RepoDisplay == "" {
319				target.RepoDisplay = target.RepoName
320			}
321			if target.CommonDir == "" {
322				target.CommonDir = target.RepoPath
323			}
324			out = append(out, target)
325		}
326		return agenttarget.Dedupe(out)
327	}

375			add(sourceSpec{agent: AgentOpenCode, scope: ScopeManaged, source: SourceManaged, path: path, adapter: adapter})
376		}
377		return sources
378	}

380	func projectSources(target Target) []sourceSpec {

384		}
385		makeSpec := func(agent Agent, relative string, adapter adapterKind) sourceSpec {
386			spec := base

388			spec.path = filepath.Join(target.CheckoutRoot, filepath.FromSlash(relative))
389			spec.adapter = adapter
390			return spec

392		claude := makeSpec(AgentClaudeCode, ".mcp.json", adapterClaudeProject)
393		claude.approvalPaths = []string{

396		}

409	func (s *Scanner) scanSource(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec, targets []Target) ([]Declaration, []Diagnostic) {
410		read := s.readSource(ctx, spec)
411		if !read.present {
412			if read.code == "" {
413				return nil, nil
414			}
415			return nil, []Diagnostic{diagnosticFor(spec, read.code)}
416		}
417		var rows []Declaration
418		var codes []DiagnosticCode
419		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
420		switch spec.adapter {
421		case adapterClaudeProject:
422			rows, codes = parseClaudeProject(read.data, spec)
423			for _, approvalPath := range spec.approvalPaths {
424				approvalSpec := spec
425				approvalSpec.path = approvalPath
426				approval := s.readSource(ctx, approvalSpec)
427				switch {
428				case approval.code != "":
429					diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, approval.code))
430				case approval.present:
431					enabled, disabled, enableAll, code := parseClaudeProjectApproval(approval.data)
432					if code != "" {
433						diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, code))
434					} else {
435						applyClaudeProjectApproval(rows, enabled, disabled, enableAll)
436					}
437				}
438			}
439		case adapterClaudeUser:
440			var localDiagnostics []Diagnostic
441			rows, codes, localDiagnostics = parseClaudeUser(read.data, spec, targets)
442			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, localDiagnostics...)
443		case adapterCodex:
444			rows, codes = parseCodex(read.data, spec)
445		case adapterCursor:
446			rows, codes = parseCursor(read.data, spec)
447		case adapterGemini:
448			rows, codes = parseGemini(read.data, spec)
449		case adapterOpenCode:
450			rows, codes = parseOpenCode(read.data, spec)
451		case adapterOpenCodePlist:
452			rows, codes = parseOpenCodePlist(read.data, spec)
453		default:
454			codes = []DiagnosticCode{DiagnosticMalformed}
455		}
456		if diagnostics == nil {
457			diagnostics = make([]Diagnostic, 0, len(codes))
458		}
459		for _, code := range codes {
460			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(spec, code))
461		}
462		return rows, diagnostics
463	}
464	
465	func diagnosticFor(spec sourceSpec, code DiagnosticCode) Diagnostic {
466		return Diagnostic{
467			Agent: spec.agent, Scope: spec.scope, Repository: spec.repository,
468			RepositoryPath: spec.repositoryPath, Checkout: spec.checkout, ConfigPath: spec.path,
469			Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code),
470		}
471	}
472	
473	func finalizeResult(result *Result) {
474		SortDeclarations(result.Declarations)
475		sort.SliceStable(result.Diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool {
476			a, b := result.Diagnostics[i], result.Diagnostics[j]
477			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Code)}
478			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Code)}
479			for n := range ak {
480				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
481					return ak[n] < bk[n]
482				}
483			}
484			return false
485		})
486	}

16	var errSymlinkLimit = errors.New("symlink limit reached")
17	
18	func (s *Scanner) readSourceFromDisk(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
19		if ctx.Err() != nil {
20			return readResult{}
21		}
22		resolved, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
23		if err != nil {
24			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
25				return readResult{}
26			}
27			if errors.Is(err, errSymlinkLimit) {
28				return readResult{code: DiagnosticSymlinkLimit}
29			}
30			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
31		}
32		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
33			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, resolved)
34			if err != nil || !inside {
35				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
36			}
37		}
38	
39		info, err := os.Stat(resolved)
40		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
41			return readResult{}
42		}
43		if err != nil {
44			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
45		}
46		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
47			return readResult{code: DiagnosticNotRegular}
48		}
49		if info.Size() > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
50			return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
51		}
52		file, err := os.Open(resolved)
53		if err != nil {
54			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return readResult{}
56			}
57			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
58		}
59		defer file.Close()
60		openedInfo, err := file.Stat()
61		if err != nil || !openedInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
62			return readResult{code: DiagnosticNotRegular}
63		}
64		if openedInfo.Size() > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
65			return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
66		}
67		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
68			currentPath, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
69			if err != nil {
70				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
71			}
72			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, currentPath)
73			currentInfo, statErr := os.Stat(currentPath)
74			if err != nil || !inside || statErr != nil || !os.SameFile(openedInfo, currentInfo) {
75				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
76			}
77		}
78	
79		var body bytes.Buffer
80		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
81		for {
82			if ctx.Err() != nil {
83				return readResult{}
84			}
85			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
86			if n > 0 {
87				if int64(body.Len()+n) > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
88					return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
89				}
90				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
91			}
92			if readErr != nil {
93				if !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
94					return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
95				}
96				break
97			}
98		}
99		if ctx.Err() != nil {
100			return readResult{}
101		}
102		return readResult{data: body.Bytes(), present: true}
103	}
104	
105	// resolveBoundedSymlinks follows symlinks in every path component while placing
106	// a small deterministic bound on cycles and unusually deep chains.
107	func resolveBoundedSymlinks(filename string, limit int) (string, error) {
108		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(filename)
109		if err != nil {
110			return "", err
111		}
112		return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(absolute), limit, 0)
113	}
114	
115	func resolveSymlinkPath(absolute string, limit, followed int) (string, error) {
116		volume := filepath.VolumeName(absolute)
117		root := volume + string(filepath.Separator)
118		relative := strings.TrimPrefix(absolute, root)
119		components := strings.FieldsFunc(relative, func(r rune) bool { return r == rune(filepath.Separator) })
120		current := root
121		for index, component := range components {
122			candidate := filepath.Join(current, component)
123			info, err := os.Lstat(candidate)
124			if err != nil {
125				return "", err
126			}
127			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
128				current = candidate
129				continue
130			}
131			if followed >= limit {
132				return "", errSymlinkLimit
133			}
134			target, err := os.Readlink(candidate)
135			if err != nil {
136				return "", err
137			}
138			if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
139				target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(candidate), target)
140			}
141			if index+1 < len(components) {
142				target = filepath.Join(target, filepath.Join(components[index+1:]...))
143			}
144			target, err = filepath.Abs(target)
145			if err != nil {
146				return "", err
147			}
148			return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(target), limit, followed+1)
149		}
150		return filepath.Clean(current), nil
151	}

34	func decodeJSON(data []byte, target any) DiagnosticCode {

47	func containsControl(value any) bool {

51	func reflectContainsControl(value reflect.Value) bool {
52		if !value.IsValid() {
53			return false
54		}
55		if value.Kind() == reflect.Interface || value.Kind() == reflect.Pointer {
56			if value.IsNil() {
57				return false
58			}
59			return reflectContainsControl(value.Elem())
60		}
61		switch value.Kind() {
62		case reflect.String:
63			return stringContainsControl(value.String())
64		case reflect.Map:
65			iter := value.MapRange()
66			for iter.Next() {
67				if reflectContainsControl(iter.Key()) || reflectContainsControl(iter.Value()) {
68					return true
69				}
70			}
71		case reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:
72			for index := range value.Len() {
73				if reflectContainsControl(value.Index(index)) {
74					return true
75				}
76			}
77		case reflect.Struct:
78			for index := range value.NumField() {
79				if reflectContainsControl(value.Field(index)) {
80					return true
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		return false
85	}

92		}

94	}

90-## How to set up your MCP server
91-
92:Gemini CLI uses the `mcpServers` configuration in your `settings.json` file to
93-locate and connect to MCP servers. This configuration supports multiple servers
94-with different transport mechanisms.
95-
96:### Configure the MCP server in settings.json
97-
98:You can configure MCP servers in your `settings.json` file in two main ways:
99:through the top-level `mcpServers` object for specific server definitions, and
100-through the `mcp` object for global settings that control server discovery and
101-execution.
102-
103-#### Global MCP settings (`mcp`)
104-
105:The `mcp` object in your `settings.json` lets you define global rules for all
106-MCP servers.
107-
108-- **`mcp.serverCommand`** (string): A global command to start an MCP server.
109:- **`mcp.allowed`** (array of strings): A list of MCP server names to allow. If
110-  this is set, only servers from this list (matching the keys in the
111:  `mcpServers` object) will be connected to.
112:- **`mcp.excluded`** (array of strings): A list of MCP server names to exclude.
113-  Servers in this list will not be connected to.
114-
115-**Example:**
116-
117-```json
118-{
119-  "mcp": {
120:    "allowed": ["my-trusted-server"],
121:    "excluded": ["experimental-server"]
122-  }
123-}
124-```
125-
126:#### Server-specific configuration (`mcpServers`)
127-
128:The `mcpServers` object is where you define each individual MCP server you want
129-the CLI to connect to.
130-
131-### Configuration structure
132-
133:Add an `mcpServers` object to your `settings.json` file:
134-
135-```json
136-{ ...file contains other config objects
137:  "mcpServers": {
138-    "serverName": {
139-      "command": "path/to/server",
140-      "args": ["--arg1", "value1"],
141-      "env": {
142-        "API_KEY": "$MY_API_TOKEN"
143-      },
144-      "cwd": "./server-directory",
145-      "timeout": 30000,
--
153-
154-Each server configuration supports the following properties:
155-
156-#### Required (one of the following)
157-
158-- **`command`** (string): Path to the executable for Stdio transport
159-- **`url`** (string): SSE endpoint URL (for example,
160-  `"http://localhost:8080/sse"`)
161:- **`httpUrl`** (string): HTTP streaming endpoint URL
162-
163-#### Optional
164-
165-- **`args`** (string[]): Command-line arguments for Stdio transport
166:- **`headers`** (object): Custom HTTP headers when using `url` or `httpUrl`
167-- **`env`** (object): Environment variables for the server process. Values can
168-  reference environment variables using `$VAR_NAME` or `${VAR_NAME}` syntax (all
169-  platforms), or `%VAR_NAME%` (Windows only).
170-- **`cwd`** (string): Working directory for Stdio transport
171-- **`timeout`** (number): Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 600,000ms =
172-  10 minutes)
173-- **`trust`** (boolean): When `true`, bypasses all tool call confirmations for
174-  this server (default: `false`)
175:- **`includeTools`** (string[]): List of tool names to include from this MCP
176-  server. When specified, only the tools listed here will be available from this
177-  server (allowlist behavior). If not specified, all tools from the server are
178-  enabled by default.
179:- **`excludeTools`** (string[]): List of tool names to exclude from this MCP
180-  server. Tools listed here will not be available to the model, even if they are
181:  exposed by the server. `excludeTools` takes precedence over `includeTools`. If
182:  a tool is in both lists, it will be excluded.
183-- **`targetAudience`** (string): The OAuth Client ID allowlisted on the
184-  IAP-protected application you are trying to access. Used with
185:  `authProviderType: 'service_account_impersonation'`.
186-- **`targetServiceAccount`** (string): The email address of the Google Cloud
187-  Service Account to impersonate. Used with
188:  `authProviderType: 'service_account_impersonation'`.
189-
190-### Environment variable expansion
191-
192-Gemini CLI automatically expands environment variables in the `env` block of
193-your MCP server configuration. This lets you securely reference variables
194-defined in your shell or environment without hardcoding sensitive information
195:directly in your `settings.json` file.
196-
197-The expansion utility supports:
198-
199-- **POSIX/Bash syntax:** `$VARIABLE_NAME` or `${VARIABLE_NAME}` (supported on
200-  all platforms)
201-- **Windows syntax:** `%VARIABLE_NAME%` (supported only when running on Windows)
202-
203-If a variable is not defined in the current environment, it resolves to an empty
--
229-- Core project keys: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, etc.
230-- Variables matching sensitive patterns: `*TOKEN*`, `*SECRET*`, `*PASSWORD*`,
231-  `*KEY*`, `*AUTH*`, `*CREDENTIAL*`.
232-- Certificates and private key patterns.
233-
234-#### Explicit overrides
235-
236-If an environment variable must be passed to an MCP server, you must explicitly
237:state it in the `env` property of the server configuration in `settings.json`
238-(or `mcp_config.json` if configuring standard MCP clients or remote skills).
239-Explicitly defined variables (including those from extensions) are trusted and
240-are **not** subjected to the automatic redaction process.
241-
242-This follows the security principle that if a variable is explicitly configured
243-by the user for a specific server, it constitutes informed consent to share that
244-specific data with that server.
245-
--
251-> environment at runtime.

364-#### Authentication provider type
365-
366:You can specify the authentication provider type using the `authProviderType`
367-property:
368-
369:- **`authProviderType`** (string): Specifies the authentication provider. Can be
370-  one of the following:
371-  - **`dynamic_discovery`** (default): The CLI will automatically discover the
372-    OAuth configuration from the server.
373-  - **`google_credentials`**: The CLI will use the Google Application Default
374-    Credentials (ADC) to authenticate with the server. When using this provider,
375-    you must specify the required scopes.
376-  - **`service_account_impersonation`**: The CLI will impersonate a Google Cloud
377-    Service Account to authenticate with the server. This is useful for
378-    accessing IAP-protected services (this was specifically designed for Cloud
379-    Run services).

391-      }
392-    }
393-  }
394-}

399-To authenticate with a server using Service Account Impersonation, you must set

401-following properties:
402-
403-- **`targetAudience`** (string): The OAuth Client ID allowlisted on the
404-  IAP-protected application you are trying to access.
405-- **`targetServiceAccount`** (string): The email address of the Google Cloud
406-  Service Account to impersonate.

557-## Discovery process deep dive
558-
559-When Gemini CLI starts, it performs MCP server discovery through the following
560-detailed process:
561-
562-### 1. Server iteration and connection
563-
564:For each configured server in `mcpServers`:
565-
566-1. **Status tracking begins:** Server status is set to `CONNECTING`
567-2. **Transport selection:** Based on configuration properties:
568:   - `httpUrl` → `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`
569-   - `url` → `SSEClientTransport`
570-   - `command` → `StdioClientTransport`
571-3. **Connection establishment:** The MCP client attempts to connect with the
572-   configured timeout
573-4. **Error handling:** Connection failures are logged and the server status is
574-   set to `DISCONNECTED`
575-
576-### 2. Tool discovery
577-
578-Upon successful connection:
579-
580-1. **Tool listing:** The client calls the MCP server's tool listing endpoint
581-2. **Schema validation:** Each tool's function declaration is validated
582:3. **Tool filtering:** Tools are filtered based on `includeTools` and
583:   `excludeTools` configuration
584-4. **Name sanitization:** Tool names are cleaned to meet Gemini API
585-   requirements:
586-   - Characters other than letters, numbers, underscore (`_`), hyphen (`-`), dot
587-     (`.`), and colon (`:`) are replaced with underscores
588-   - Names longer than 63 characters are truncated with middle replacement
589-     (`...`)
590-
591-### 3. Tool naming and namespaces
--
758-### Connection states
759-
760-The MCP integration tracks several states:
761-
762-#### Overriding extension configurations
763-
764-If an MCP server is provided by an extension (for example, the
765-`google-workspace` extension), you can still override its settings in your local
766:`settings.json`. Gemini CLI merges your local configuration with the extension's
767-defaults:
768-
769-- **Tool lists:** Tool lists are merged securely to ensure the most restrictive
770-  policy wins:
771-
772:  - **Exclusions (`excludeTools`):** Arrays are combined (unioned). If either
773-    source blocks a tool, it remains disabled.
774:  - **Inclusions (`includeTools`):** Arrays are intersected. If both sources
775-    provide an allowlist, only tools present in **both** lists are enabled. If
776-    only one source provides an allowlist, that list is respected.
777:  - **Precedence:** `excludeTools` always takes precedence over `includeTools`.
778-
779-  This ensures you always have veto power over tools provided by an extension
780-  and that an extension cannot re-enable tools you have omitted from your
781-  personal allowlist.
782-
783-- **Environment variables:** The `env` objects are merged. If the same variable
784:  is defined in both places, your local value takes precedence.
785-- **Scalar properties:** Properties like `command`, `url`, and `timeout` are
786-  replaced by your local values if provided.
787-
788-**Example override:**
789-
790-```json
791-{
792:  "mcpServers": {
793-    "google-workspace": {
794:      "excludeTools": ["gmail.send"]
795-    }
796-  }
797-}
798-```
799-
800-#### Server status (`MCPServerStatus`)
801-
802-- **`DISCONNECTED`:** Server is not connected or has errors

1055-## Managing MCP servers with `gemini mcp`
1056-
1057-While you can always configure MCP servers by manually editing your
1058:`settings.json` file, Gemini CLI provides a convenient set of commands to manage
1059-your server configurations programmatically. These commands streamline the
1060-process of adding, listing, and removing MCP servers without needing to directly
1061-edit JSON files.
1062-
1063-### Adding a server (`gemini mcp add`)
1064-
1065:The `add` command configures a new MCP server in your `settings.json`. Based on
1066-the scope (`-s, --scope`), it will be added to either the user config
1067:`~/.gemini/settings.json` or the project config `.gemini/settings.json` file.
1068-
1069-**Command:**
1070-
1071-```bash
1072-gemini mcp add [options] <name> <commandOrUrl> [args...]
1073-```
1074-
1075-- `<name>`: A unique name for the server.
--
1195-- `-s, --scope`: Configuration scope (user or project). [default: "project"]
1196-
1197-**Example:**
1198-
1199-```bash
1200-gemini mcp remove my-server
1201-```
1202-
1203:This will find and delete the "my-server" entry from the `mcpServers` object in
1204:the appropriate `settings.json` file based on the scope (`-s, --scope`).
1205-
1206-### Enabling/disabling a server (`gemini mcp enable`, `gemini mcp disable`)
1207-
1208-Temporarily disable an MCP server without removing its configuration, or
1209-re-enable a previously disabled server.

# MCP servers with Gemini CLI

This document provides a guide to configuring and using Model Context Protocol
(MCP) servers with Gemini CLI.

## What is an MCP server?

An MCP server is an application that exposes tools and resources to the Gemini
CLI through the Model Context Protocol, allowing it to interact with external
systems and data sources. MCP servers act as a bridge between the Gemini model
and your local environment or other services like APIs.

An MCP server enables Gemini CLI to:

- **Discover tools:** List available tools, their descriptions, and parameters
  through standardized schema definitions.
- **Execute tools:** Call specific tools with defined arguments and receive
  structured responses.
- **Access resources:** Read data from specific resources that the server
  exposes (files, API payloads, reports, etc.).

With an MCP server, you can extend Gemini CLI's capabilities to perform actions
beyond its built-in features, such as interacting with databases, APIs, custom
scripts, or specialized workflows.

## Core integration architecture

Gemini CLI integrates with MCP servers through a sophisticated discovery and
execution system built into the core package (`packages/core/src/tools/`):

### Discovery Layer (`mcp-client.ts`)

The discovery process is orchestrated by `discoverMcpTools()`, which:

1. **Iterates through configured servers** from your `settings.json`
   `mcpServers` configuration
2. **Establishes connections** using appropriate transport mechanisms (Stdio,
   SSE, or Streamable HTTP)
3. **Fetches tool definitions** from each server using the MCP protocol
4. **Sanitizes and validates** tool schemas for compatibility with the Gemini
   API
5. **Registers tools** in the global tool registry with conflict resolution
6. **Fetches and registers resources** if the server exposes any

### Execution layer (`mcp-tool.ts`)

Each discovered MCP tool is wrapped in a `DiscoveredMCPTool` instance that:

...

---
title: MCP servers
description: Add local and remote MCP tools.
---

You can add external tools to OpenCode using the _Model Context Protocol_, or MCP. OpenCode supports both local and remote servers.

Once added, MCP tools are automatically available to the LLM alongside built-in tools.

---

#### Caveats

When you use an MCP server, it adds to the context. This can quickly add up if you have a lot of tools. So we recommend being careful with which MCP servers you use.

:::tip
MCP servers add to your context, so you want to be careful with which ones you enable.
:::

Certain MCP servers, like the GitHub MCP server, tend to add a lot of tokens and can easily exceed the context limit.

---

## Enable

You can define MCP servers in your [OpenCode Config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/) under `mcp`. Add each MCP with a unique name. You can refer to that MCP by name when prompting the LLM.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc" {6}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "name-of-mcp-server": {
      // ...
      "enabled": true,
    },
    "name-of-other-mcp-server": {
      // ...
    },
  },
}
```

You can also disable a server by setting `enabled` to `false`. This is useful if you want to temporarily disable a server without removing it from your config.

---

### Overriding remote defaults

Organizations can provide default MCP servers via their `.well-known/opencode` endpoint. These servers may be disabled by default, allowing users to opt-in to the ones they need.

To enable a specific server from your organization's remote config, add it to your local config with `enabled: true`:

```json title="opencode.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "jira": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://jira.example.com/mcp",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Your local config values override the remote defaults. See [config precedence](/docs/config#precedence-order) for more details.

---

## Local

Add local MCP servers using `type` to `"local"` within the MCP object.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc" {15}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-local-mcp-server": {
      "type": "local",
      // Or ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command"]
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "my-mcp-command"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": {
        "MY_ENV_VAR": "my_env_var_value",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The command is how the local MCP server is started. You can also pass in a list of environment variables as well.

For example, here's how you can add the test [`@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything) MCP server.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "mcp_everything": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
    },
  },
}
```

And to use it I can add `use the mcp_everything tool` to my prompts.

```txt "mcp_everything"
use the mcp_everything tool to add the number 3 and 4
```

---

#### Options

Here are all the options for configuring a local MCP server.

| Option        | Type    | Required | Description                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`        | String  | Y        | Type of MCP server connection, must be `"local"`.                                        |
| `command`     | Array   | Y        | Command and arguments to run the MCP server.                                             |
| `cwd`         | String  |          | Working directory for the MCP server process. Relative paths resolve from the workspace. |
| `environment` | Object  |          | Environment variables to set when running the server.                                    |
| `enabled`     | Boolean |          | Enable or disable the MCP server on startup.                                             |
| `timeout`     | Number  |          | Timeout in ms for fetching tools from the MCP server. Defaults to 5000 (5 seconds).      |

---

## Remote

Add remote MCP servers by setting `type` to `"remote"`.

```json title="opencode.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-remote-mcp": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://my-mcp-server.com",
      "enabled": true,
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer MY_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `url` is the URL of the remote MCP server and with the `headers` option you can pass in a list of headers.

---

#### Options

| Option    | Type    | Required | Description                                                                         |
| --------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`    | String  | Y        | Type of MCP server connection, must be `"remote"`.                                  |
| `url`     | String  | Y        | URL of the remote MCP server.                                                       |
| `enabled` | Boolean |          | Enable or disable the MCP server on startup.                                        |
| `headers` | Object  |          | Headers to send with the request.                                                   |
| `oauth`   | Object  |          | OAuth authentication configuration. See [OAuth](#oauth) section below.              |
| `timeout` | Number  |          | Timeout in ms for fetching tools from the MCP server. Defaults to 5000 (5 seconds). |

---

## OAuth

OpenCode automatically handles OAuth authentication for remote MCP servers. When a server requires authentication, OpenCode will:

1. Detect the 401 response and initiate the OAuth flow
2. Use **Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591)** if supported by the server
3. Store tokens securely for future requests

---

### Automatic

For most OAuth-enabled MCP servers, no special configuration is needed. Just configure the remote server:

```json title="opencode.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-oauth-server": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

If the server requires authentication, OpenCode will prompt you to authenticate when you first try to use it. If not, you can [manually trigger the flow](#authenticating) with `opencode mcp auth <server-name>`.

---

### Pre-registered

If you have client credentials from the MCP server provider, you can configure them:

```json title="opencode.json" {7-11}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-oauth-server": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "oauth": {
        "clientId": "{env:MY_MCP_CLIENT_ID}",
        "clientSecret": "{env:MY_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET}",
        "scope": "tools:read tools:execute"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

### Authenticating

You can manually trigger authentication or manage credentials.

Authenticate with a specific MCP server:

```bash
opencode mcp auth my-oauth-server
```

List all MCP servers and their auth status:

```bash
opencode mcp list
```

Remove stored credentials:

```bash
opencode mcp logout my-oauth-server
```

The `mcp auth` command will open your browser for authorization. After you authorize, OpenCode will store the tokens securely in `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json`.

---

#### Disabling OAuth

If you want to disable automatic OAuth for a server (e.g., for servers that use API keys instead), set `oauth` to `false`:

```json title="opencode.json" {7}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-api-key-server": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "oauth": false,
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MY_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

#### OAuth Options

| Option         | Type            | Description                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `oauth`        | Object \| false | OAuth config object, or `false` to disable OAuth auto-detection.                 |
| `clientId`     | String          | OAuth client ID. If not provided, dynamic client registration will be attempted. |
| `clientSecret` | String          | OAuth client secret, if required by the authorization server.                    |
| `scope`        | String          | OAuth scopes to request during authorization.                                    |

#### Debugging

If a remote MCP server is failing to authenticate, you can diagnose issues with:

```bash
# View auth status for all OAuth-capable servers
opencode mcp auth list

# Debug connection and OAuth flow for a specific server
opencode mcp debug my-oauth-server
```

The `mcp debug` command shows the current auth status, tests HTTP connectivity, and attempts the OAuth discovery flow.

---

## Manage

Your MCPs are available as tools in OpenCode, alongside built-in tools. So you can manage them through the OpenCode config like any other tool.

---

### Global

This means that you can enable or disable them globally.

```json title="opencode.json" {14}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-mcp-foo": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-foo"]
    },
    "my-mcp-bar": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-bar"]
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "my-mcp-foo": false
  }
}
```

We can also use a glob pattern to disable all matching MCPs.

```json title="opencode.json" {14}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-mcp-foo": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-foo"]
    },
    "my-mcp-bar": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-bar"]
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "my-mcp*": false
  }
}
```

Here we are using the glob pattern `my-mcp*` to disable all MCPs.

---

### Per agent

If you have a large number of MCP servers you may want to only enable them per agent and disable them globally. To do this:

1. Disable it as a tool globally.
2. In your [agent config](/docs/agents#tools), enable the MCP server as a tool.

```json title="opencode.json" {11, 14-18}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "my-mcp": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  },
  "tools": {
    "my-mcp*": false
  },
  "agent": {
    "my-agent": {
      "tools": {
        "my-mcp*": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

#### Glob patterns

The glob pattern uses simple regex globbing patterns:

- `*` matches zero or more of any character (e.g., `"my-mcp*"` matches `my-mcp_search`, `my-mcp_list`, etc.)
- `?` matches exactly one character
- All other characters match literally

:::note
MCP server tools are registered with server name as prefix, so to disable all tools for a server simply use:

```
"mymcpservername_*": false
```

:::

---

## Examples

Below are examples of some common MCP servers. You can submit a PR if you want to document other servers.

---

### Sentry

Add the [Sentry MCP server](https://mcp.sentry.dev) to interact with your Sentry projects and issues.

```json title="opencode.json" {4-8}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "sentry": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp",
      "oauth": {}
    }
  }
}
```

After adding the configuration, authenticate with Sentry:

```bash
opencode mcp auth sentry
```

This will open a browser window to complete the OAuth flow and connect OpenCode to your Sentry account.

Once authenticated, you can use Sentry tools in your prompts to query issues, projects, and error data.

```txt "use sentry"
Show me the latest unresolved issues in my project. use sentry
```

---

### Context7

Add the [Context7 MCP server](https://github.com/upstash/context7) to search through docs.

```json title="opencode.json" {4-7}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "context7": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

If you have signed up for a free account, you can use your API key and get higher rate-limits.

```json title="opencode.json" {7-9}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "context7": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "CONTEXT7_API_KEY": "{env:CONTEXT7_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Here we are assuming that you have the `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` environment variable set.

Add `use context7` to your prompts to use Context7 MCP server.

```txt "use context7"
Configure a Cloudflare Worker script to cache JSON API responses for five minutes. use context7
```

Alternatively, you can add something like this to your [AGENTS.md](/docs/rules/).

```md title="AGENTS.md"
When you need to search docs, use `context7` tools.
```

---

### Grep by Vercel

Add the [Grep by Vercel](https://grep.app) MCP server to search through code snippets on GitHub.

```json title="opencode.json" {4-7}
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "gh_grep": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.grep.app"
    }
  }
}
```

Since we named our MCP server `gh_grep`, you can add `use the gh_grep tool` to your prompts to get the agent to use it.

```txt "use the gh_grep tool"
What's the right way to set a custom domain in an SST Astro component? use the gh_grep tool
```

Alternatively, you can add something like this to your [AGENTS.md](/docs/rules/).

```md title="AGENTS.md"
If you are unsure how to do something, use `gh_grep` to search code examples from GitHub.
```
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
4	
5	The intended result is a provider-independent, no-network skill inventory across repositories with explicit upstream freshness checks; a separate secret-safe MCP declaration inventory; and an unambiguous responsive Tasks table. Read paths must never execute `npx`, start MCP servers, resolve credentials, or claim live MCP health.
6	
7	## Agreed product behavior
8	
9	- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
10	- Native skill discovery covers the complete path registry represented by upstream `skills` v1.5.23 (77 agent IDs), with a versioned, table-driven snapshot. Shared paths such as `.agents/skills` are reported as registry-compatible rather than pretending `dev` detected every installed agent executable.
11	- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
12	- MCP is an independent domain and user surface: `dev mcp list` plus a lazy MCP TUI view. Initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
13	- MCP rows represent static declarations, not effective merged runtime configuration or connectivity. Duplicate declarations remain scope-qualified rows; unsupported/runtime-only sources are diagnosed as partial coverage.
14	
15	# Implementation plan
16	
17	## 1. Resolve reusable repository scan targets
18	
19	- Add a small neutral target type under `internal/agenttarget/` containing repository name/display, canonical path/common-dir identity, and the exact checkout root being scanned.
20	- Build targets by reusing `config.Config.DiscoveryRoots`, `repo.Discover`, `repo.Resolve`, and `gitx.Discover` rather than adding another filesystem walk.
21	- Encode selection policy in this package, not Cobra handlers:
22	  - current mode resolves the exact current checkout, including a linked worktree;
23	  - `--all` returns non-bare canonical discovered checkouts once;
24	  - `--repo` accepts existing repository references and explicit linked-worktree paths;
25	  - TUI aggregation appends the startup checkout when it is not the accepted canonical REPOS row;
26	  - targets are deduplicated by common-dir plus checkout root and sorted deterministically.
27	- Reuse accepted `tui.RepoRow` snapshots for lazy TUI loads so SKILLS/MCP do not rediscover repositories or delay initial startup.
28	
29	## 2. Replace provider-based skill reads with native inventory
30	
31	Refactor `internal/agentskill/agentskill.go` into focused types/registry/scanner/lock/freshness/provider files while preserving the existing mutation command API.
32	
33	### Registry and filesystem scan
34	
35	- Check in a provenance/version-tagged Go registry corresponding to upstream `skills@1.5.23` agent paths, including project/global paths and supported environment overrides (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, XDG config roots, and the other registry-defined homes).
36	- Collapse identical logical directories before reading them; scan only immediate child directories with a valid, size-bounded `SKILL.md` rather than recursively walking repositories or home directories.
37	- Parse the skill frontmatter name with a real YAML parser, merge duplicate logical installations by `(scope, target checkout, normalized skill name)`, and retain all installation paths/agent IDs. Resolve physical symlinks for deduplication without losing the logical path that explains agent attribution.
38	- Treat shared paths as compatible with the registry entries that consume that path; expose an attribution/registry-version field so this is not confused with executable detection.
39	- Make exact lock names win. Only use normalized-name matching when unique; emit a deterministic diagnostic for collisions instead of selecting a random Go map entry.
40	
41	### Locks and local status
42	
43	- Split project and global lock decoding and normalize them internally:
44	  - project `<checkout>/skills-lock.json` (current v1 fields such as source, ref, skill path, and `computedHash`);
45	  - global v3 metadata and compatible older fields from `$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is absolute, otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
46	- Bound lock reads and distinguish missing, malformed, unreadable, unsupported-version, and structurally invalid files. Missing is normal; the other cases become safe per-source diagnostics while other repositories continue.
47	- Include lock-only entries whose installation is absent, and unlocked installed directories as externally managed rows.
48	- Add repository/checkout identity, logical installations, local presence, attribution, and normalized lock metadata to `agentskill.Skill`/result types without removing existing fields.
49	- Keep upstream freshness (`unchecked/current/update_available/upstream_missing/unverifiable/check_failed`) separate from local presence/integrity. Only the embedded `dev-cli` skill receives verified/drifted byte-integrity status; do not claim generic lock hashes verify installed bytes.
50	- Convert `Managed` and `FindProject` to the native lock/scanner primitives so repository scaffolding and selected-skill updates no longer require provider JSON.
51	
52	### Explicit freshness and mutation boundary
53	
54	- Preserve and isolate the existing `safeSkillFolder`, folder hashing, Git-source derivation, and grouped `(source URL, ref)` comparisons.
55	- Aggregate all project/global rows first, then run one bounded, cancellation-aware freshness pass so a shared source/ref is cloned once across all repositories. Preserve deterministic row order, clean every temporary clone, and mark only affected rows failed.
56	- Keep local/node_modules/well-known sources unverifiable unless their lock metadata provides a supported comparison; do not silently reinterpret them as Git.
57	- Delete the read-time `npx --no-install skills` path. Read/list/provider-version checks must not invoke npm, a registry, or project Node code.
58	- Retain `interactiveProvider` for explicit add/install/update operations, but require a directly installed `skills` executable after the security review found repository-local `npx` provider substitution. Update `dev doctor` to describe native inventory as always available and report the optional mutation provider separately.
59	
60	## 3. Aggregate skills across repositories and expose them in CLI
61	
62	- Add an inventory collector (representatively `internal/inventory/agent_skills.go`) that scans project targets with the existing context-aware `inventory.Limiter`, scans global paths exactly once, merges diagnostics, and optionally performs one grouped freshness check.
63	- Extend `dev skill list` in `internal/cli/skill.go` with mutually exclusive `--all` and `--repo <ref>` target selection while preserving `--project`, `--global`, `--check`, and the current-checkout default.
64	- Keep the existing JSON array and every existing key/type; add repository/checkout, installations, presence/integrity, attribution/registry-version, and normalized lock fields. Write partial diagnostics to stderr so JSON stdout stays valid.
65	- Add `--repo` to project `dev skill update`; reject repo targeting for global updates. In the TUI, update a selected project skill from that row’s checkout root, while the interactive add wizard continues to use the startup checkout.
66	- Render a repository-aware human table and keep global rows repository-less rather than duplicating them per target.
67	
68	## 4. Add a normalized, secret-safe MCP domain
69	
70	Create `internal/agentmcp/` with normalized types, a scanner, sanitization helpers, and one adapter per supported agent.
71	
72	### Static sources covered
73	
74	- **Claude Code:** project `.mcp.json`; user and per-project local declarations in `~/.claude.json`.
75	- **Codex:** `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` or `~/.codex/config.toml`; trusted-project `.codex/config.toml`; direct and plugin override declarations.
76	- **Cursor:** project `.cursor/mcp.json`; user `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
77	- **Gemini CLI:** project `.gemini/settings.json`; user `~/.gemini/settings.json`; readable documented system default/override files, with source scope retained.
78	- **OpenCode:** project `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc`; XDG user config; an explicit local `OPENCODE_CONFIG` file and readable managed files. Do not fetch remote `.well-known` config or parse inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` as durable inventory.
79	- Use the existing BurntSushi TOML dependency for Codex, `encoding/json` for strict JSON, and a maintained JSONC normalizer for OpenCode rather than an ad-hoc comment stripper.
80	
81	### Normalization and safety
82	
83	- Normalize only non-secret facts: server name, agent, declaration scope, repository, config path, managed/direct source, declared enabled/required/trust policy, transport, safe endpoint host or command basename, argument count, and names/kinds of credential references.
84	- Keep each declaration scope-qualified; do not emulate undocumented merge/precedence rules or label a row “effective.” When transport cannot be proven (for example a Cursor URL declaration), report `remote/unknown` rather than guessing.
85	- Sanitize during adapter conversion so raw values never enter normalized rows, diagnostics, traces, CLI JSON, or TUI state:
86	  - never expand environment variables or `{env:…}`/`${…}` placeholders;
87	  - never read OpenCode `{file:…}` targets or OAuth/token stores;
88	  - never retain env/header/OAuth values or raw command arguments;
89	  - reduce commands to a safe basename and URLs to a credential-free representation with userinfo/query/fragment removed or redacted;
90	  - use fixed diagnostic codes/messages that cannot echo decoder snippets containing secrets;
91	  - reject control characters and bound config size;
92	  - confine project config symlinks to the selected checkout, while allowing bounded user-config symlinks for dotfile managers.
93	- Never invoke agent MCP list/debug commands, helper commands, servers, URLs, or health checks. Document omitted plugin caches, hosted connectors, runtime-only config, remote organization config, and unsupported agent formats as coverage limitations.
94	
95	## 5. Add MCP CLI and TUI surfaces
96	
97	- Register a new `dev mcp list [--repo <ref> | --all] [--agent ...] [--scope ...] [--json]` command in `internal/cli/root.go`/a new `internal/cli/mcp.go`.
98	- Human output shows repo, scope, agent, server, transport, declared state, source, sanitized target, and config path.
99	- Start the new JSON contract as an envelope containing `servers`, `diagnostics`, and coverage metadata; serialize normalized fields only. Missing files are a successful empty source; malformed individual files preserve partial results; target-discovery/cancellation failures remain non-zero.
100	- Add `ViewMCP` next to SKILLS and parallel model/action/message/filter/detail state in `internal/tui/`. It is lazy and depends on the accepted REPOS generation just like the broadened SKILLS view.
101	- Generalize the existing Fleet REPOS-dependency pattern so waiting, invalidation, superseding generations, and cancellation work for SKILLS and MCP. Preserve existing rows during refresh/check (stale-while-revalidate) instead of replacing them with a progress-only screen.
102	- Add repository-aware structured filters:
103	  - SKILLS: `repo:`, `scope:`, `agent:`, `update:`, `presence:`, `integrity:`;
104	  - MCP: `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, `state:`.
105	- Give MCP only navigation/filter/reload actions; it has no start/connect/add/remove operation. Update the tab strip to remain within narrow terminals after adding the seventh view.
106	
107	## 6. Show repository in the Tasks table
108	
109	- Change only the TASKS renderer in `internal/tui/view.go`; use the already persisted `Task.Repo` rather than joining asynchronous repository rows.
110	- At widths that can retain the existing flexible minimum (target boundary: 97 cells), insert a 16-cell `REPO` column after `STATE` and redistribute TASK/BRANCH/NEXT widths.
111	- At narrower widths preserve the current `TASK STATE BRANCH GIT AGE NEXT` layout exactly; selected detail still shows the full repo/path.
112	- Build headers and rows with the existing `fitCell`/`lipgloss.Width` pattern so CJK/wide names do not shift columns. Do not change task identity, sort, filter, detail, or `dev ls --json`—those already contain repository data.
113

61	- **Streamable HTTP Transport:** Uses HTTP streaming for communication
62	
63	## Working with MCP resources
64	
65	Some MCP servers expose contextual “resources” in addition to the tools and
66	prompts. Gemini CLI discovers these automatically and gives you the possibility
67	to reference them in the chat. For more information on the tools used to
68	interact with these resources, see [MCP resource tools](mcp-resources.md).
69	
70	### Discovery and listing
71	
72	- When discovery runs, the CLI fetches each server’s `resources/list` results.
73	- The `/mcp` command displays a Resources section alongside Tools and Prompts
74	  for every connected server.
75	
76	This returns a concise, plain-text list of URIs plus metadata.
77	
78	### Referencing resources in a conversation
79	
80	You can use the same `@` syntax already known for referencing local files:
81	
82	```
83	@server://resource/path
84	```
85	
86	Resource URIs appear in the completion menu together with filesystem paths. When
87	you submit the message, the CLI calls `resources/read` and injects the content
88	in the conversation.
89	
90	## How to set up your MCP server
91	
92	Gemini CLI uses the `mcpServers` configuration in your `settings.json` file to
93	locate and connect to MCP servers. This configuration supports multiple servers
94	with different transport mechanisms.
95	
96	### Configure the MCP server in settings.json
97	
98	You can configure MCP servers in your `settings.json` file in two main ways:
99	through the top-level `mcpServers` object for specific server definitions, and
100	through the `mcp` object for global settings that control server discovery and
101	execution.
102	
103	#### Global MCP settings (`mcp`)
104	
105	The `mcp` object in your `settings.json` lets you define global rules for all
106	MCP servers.
107	
108	- **`mcp.serverCommand`** (string): A global command to start an MCP server.
109	- **`mcp.allowed`** (array of strings): A list of MCP server names to allow. If
110	  this is set, only servers from this list (matching the keys in the
111	  `mcpServers` object) will be connected to.
112	- **`mcp.excluded`** (array of strings): A list of MCP server names to exclude.
113	  Servers in this list will not be connected to.
114	
115	**Example:**
116	
117	```json
118	{
119	  "mcp": {
120	    "allowed": ["my-trusted-server"],
121	    "excluded": ["experimental-server"]
122	  }
123	}
124	```
125	
126	#### Server-specific configuration (`mcpServers`)
127	
128	The `mcpServers` object is where you define each individual MCP server you want
129	the CLI to connect to.
130	
131	### Configuration structure
132	
133	Add an `mcpServers` object to your `settings.json` file:
134	
135	```json
136	{ ...file contains other config objects
137	  "mcpServers": {
138	    "serverName": {
139	      "command": "path/to/server",
140	      "args": ["--arg1", "value1"],
141	      "env": {
142	        "API_KEY": "$MY_API_TOKEN"
143	      },
144	      "cwd": "./server-directory",
145	      "timeout": 30000,
146	      "trust": false
147	    }
148	  }
149	}
150	```
151	
152	### Configuration properties
153	
154	Each server configuration supports the following properties:
155	
156	#### Required (one of the following)
157	
158	- **`command`** (string): Path to the executable for Stdio transport
159	- **`url`** (string): SSE endpoint URL (for example,
160	  `"http://localhost:8080/sse"`)
161	- **`httpUrl`** (string): HTTP streaming endpoint URL
162	
163	#### Optional
164	
165	- **`args`** (string[]): Command-line arguments for Stdio transport
166	- **`headers`** (object): Custom HTTP headers when using `url` or `httpUrl`
167	- **`env`** (object): Environment variables for the server process. Values can
168	  reference environment variables using `$VAR_NAME` or `${VAR_NAME}` syntax (all
169	  platforms), or `%VAR_NAME%` (Windows only).
170	- **`cwd`** (string): Working directory for Stdio transport
171	- **`timeout`** (number): Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 600,000ms =
172	  10 minutes)
173	- **`trust`** (boolean): When `true`, bypasses all tool call confirmations for
174	  this server (default: `false`)
175	- **`includeTools`** (string[]): List of tool names to include from this MCP
176	  server. When specified, only the tools listed here will be available from this
177	  server (allowlist behavior). If not specified, all tools from the server are
178	  enabled by default.
179	- **`excludeTools`** (string[]): List of tool names to exclude from this MCP
180	  server. Tools listed here will not be available to the model, even if they are
181	  exposed by the server. `excludeTools` takes precedence over `includeTools`. If
182	  a tool is in both lists, it will be excluded.
183	- **`targetAudience`** (string): The OAuth Client ID allowlisted on the
184	  IAP-protected application you are trying to access. Used with
185	  `authProviderType: 'service_account_impersonation'`.
186	- **`targetServiceAccount`** (string): The email address of the Google Cloud
187	  Service Account to impersonate. Used with
188	  `authProviderType: 'service_account_impersonation'`.
189	
190	### Environment variable expansion
191	
192	Gemini CLI automatically expands environment variables in the `env` block of
193	your MCP server configuration. This lets you securely reference variables
194	defined in your shell or environment without hardcoding sensitive information
195	directly in your `settings.json` file.
196	
197	The expansion utility supports:
198	
199	- **POSIX/Bash syntax:** `$VARIABLE_NAME` or `${VARIABLE_NAME}` (supported on
```

166-
167-For STDIO servers (local command-line servers), configure these fields in your `mcp.json`:
168-
169-| Field       | Required | Description                                                                                             | Examples                                  |
170-| :---------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------- |
171:| **type**    | Yes      | Server connection type                                                                                  | `"stdio"`                                 |
172-| **command** | Yes      | Command to start the server executable. Must be available on your system path or contain its full path. | `"npx"`, `"node"`, `"python"`, `"docker"` |
173-| **args**    | No       | Array of arguments passed to the command                                                                | `["server.py", "--port", "3000"]`         |
174-| **env**     | No       | Environment variables for the server                                                                    | `{"API_KEY": "${env:api-key}"}`           |
175:| **envFile** | No       | Path to an environment file to load more variables                                                      | `".env"`, `"${workspaceFolder}/.env"`     |
176-
177:The `envFile` option is only available for STDIO servers. Remote servers (HTTP/SSE) do not support `envFile`. For remote servers, use [config interpolation](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp.md#config-interpolation) with environment variables set in your shell profile or system environment instead.
178-

180-
181-For programmatic MCP server registration, Cursor provides an extension API that allows dynamic configuration without modifying `mcp.json` files. This is particularly useful for enterprise environments and automated setup workflows.

4-
5-## Format
6-
7-OpenCode supports both **JSON** and **JSONC** (JSON with Comments) formats.
8-
9:```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
10-{
11-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",

35----
36-
37-### Precedence order
38-
39-Config sources are loaded in this order (later sources override earlier ones):
40-
41-1. **Remote config** (from `.well-known/opencode`) - organizational defaults
42:2. **Global config** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) - user preferences
43:3. **Custom config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG` env var) - custom overrides
44:4. **Project config** (`opencode.json` in project) - project-specific settings
45:5. **`.opencode` directories** - agents, commands, plugins
46:6. **Inline config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var) - runtime overrides
47:7. **Managed config files** (`/Library/Application Support/opencode/` on macOS) - admin-controlled
48:8. **macOS managed preferences** (`.mobileconfig` via MDM) - highest priority, not user-overridable
49-
50-This means project configs can override global defaults, and global configs can override remote organizational defaults. Managed settings override everything.
51-
52-:::note
53:The `.opencode` and `~/.config/opencode` directories use **plural names** for subdirectories: `agents/`, `commands/`, `modes/`, `plugins/`, `skills/`, `tools/`, and `themes/`. Singular names (e.g., `agent/`) are also supported for backwards compatibility.
54-:::
55-

57-
58-### Remote
59-
60-Organizations can provide default configuration via the `.well-known/opencode` endpoint. This is fetched automatically when you authenticate with a provider that supports it.

72-      "enabled": false
73-    }
74-  }
75-}

95-
96:Place your global OpenCode config in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. Use global config for user-wide server/runtime preferences like providers, models, and permissions.

120-### Custom path
121-
122:Specify a custom config file path using the `OPENCODE_CONFIG` environment variable.
123-

125:export OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/my/custom-config.json
126-opencode run "Hello world"
127-```

129-Custom config is loaded between global and project configs in the precedence order.
130-
131----
132-
133-### Custom directory
134-
135:Specify a custom config directory using the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`
136-environment variable. This directory will be searched for agents, commands,
137:modes, and plugins just like the standard `.opencode` directory, and should
138-follow the same structure.
139-
140-```bash
141:export OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/my/config-directory
142-opencode run "Hello world"
143-```
144-
145:The custom directory is loaded after the global config and `.opencode` directories, so it **can override** their settings.

149-### Managed settings
150-
151-Organizations can enforce configuration that users cannot override. Managed settings are loaded at the highest priority tier.
152-
153-#### File-based
154-
155:Drop an `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc` file in the system managed config directory:
156-
157-| Platform | Path                                     |
158-| -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
159:| macOS    | `/Library/Application Support/opencode/` |
160-| Linux    | `/etc/opencode/`                         |
161-| Windows  | `%ProgramData%\opencode`                 |
162-
163-These directories require admin/root access to write, so users cannot modify them.

166-
167:On macOS, OpenCode reads managed preferences from the `ai.opencode.managed` preference domain. Deploy a `.mobileconfig` via MDM (Jamf, Kandji, FleetDM) and the settings are enforced automatically.

171:1. `/Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/ai.opencode.managed.plist`
172:2. `/Library/Managed Preferences/ai.opencode.managed.plist`

174:The plist keys map directly to `opencode.json` fields. MDM metadata keys (`PayloadUUID`, `PayloadType`, etc.) are stripped automatically.

324-### Shell
325-
326-You can configure the shell used for the interactive terminal using the `shell` option. Compatible shells are also used for agent tool calls.

328:```json title="opencode.json"
329-{

335-If not specified, OpenCode will automatically discover and use a sensible default based on your operating system (e.g. `pwsh` or `cmd.exe` on Windows, `/bin/zsh` or `/bin/bash` on macOS/Linux). You can provide an absolute path or a short name.

420-### Image attachments
421-
422-OpenCode normalizes image attachments before sending them to the model. By default, images are resized when they exceed `2000x2000` pixels or `5242880` base64 bytes.
423-
424-Configure image attachment limits with the `attachment.image` option:
425-
426:```json title="opencode.json"
427-{
428-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
429-  "attachment": {
430-    "image": {
431-      "auto_resize": true,
432-      "max_width": 2000,
433-      "max_height": 2000,
434-      "max_base64_bytes": 5242880
--
449-#### Provider-Specific Options
450-
451-Some providers support additional configuration options beyond the generic `timeout` and `apiKey` settings.
452-
453-##### Amazon Bedrock
454-

498-
499-### Agents
500-
501-You can configure specialized agents for specific tasks through the `agent` option.
502-
503:```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
504-{
505-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
506-  "agent": {
507-    "code-reviewer": {
508-      "description": "Reviews code for best practices and potential issues",
509-      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
510-      "prompt": "You are a code reviewer. Focus on security, performance, and maintainability.",
511-      "tools": {
--
513-        "write": false,
514-        "edit": false,
515-      },
516-    },
517-  },
518-}
519-```
520-
521:You can also define agents using markdown files in `~/.config/opencode/agents/` or `.opencode/agents/`. [Learn more here](/docs/agents).
522-
523----
524-
525-### Default agent
526-
527-You can set the default agent using the `default_agent` option. This determines which agent is used when none is explicitly specified.
528-
529:```json title="opencode.json"
530-{
531-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
532-  "default_agent": "plan"
533-}
534-```
535-
536-The default agent must be a primary agent (not a subagent). This can be a built-in agent like `"build"` or `"plan"`, or a [custom agent](/docs/agents) you've defined. If the specified agent doesn't exist or is a subagent, OpenCode will fall back to `"build"` with a warning.
537-
538-This setting applies across all interfaces: TUI, CLI (`opencode run`), desktop app, and GitHub Action.
539-
540----
541-
542-### Subagent depth
543-
544-You can control how deeply subagents can invoke other subagents using the `subagent_depth` option.
545-
546:```json title="opencode.json"
547-{
548-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
549-  "subagent_depth": 2
550-}
551-```
552-
553-The default is `1`, which allows primary agents to launch subagents but prevents those subagents from launching additional subagents. Set it to `2` to allow one additional level of nested subagents, or `0` to prevent all subagent launches.
554-
555----
556-
557-### Sharing
558-
559-You can configure the [share](/docs/share) feature through the `share` option.
560-
561:```json title="opencode.json"
562-{
563-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
564-  "share": "manual"
565-}
566-```
567-
568-This takes:
569-
--
574-By default, sharing is set to manual mode where you need to explicitly share conversations using the `/share` command.

576----
577-
578-### Commands
579-
580-You can configure custom commands for repetitive tasks through the `command` option.
581-
582:```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
583-{
584-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
585-  "command": {
586-    "test": {
587-      "template": "Run the full test suite with coverage report and show any failures.\nFocus on the failing tests and suggest fixes.",
588-      "description": "Run tests with coverage",
589-      "agent": "build",
590-      "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",
--
592-    "component": {
593-      "template": "Create a new React component named $ARGUMENTS with TypeScript support.\nInclude proper typing and basic structure.",
594-      "description": "Create a new component",
595-    },
596-  },
597-}
598-```
599-
600:You can also define commands using markdown files in `~/.config/opencode/commands/` or `.opencode/commands/`. [Learn more here](/docs/commands).
601-
602----
603-
604-### Keybinds
605-
606-Customize TUI keyboard shortcuts in `tui.json` with `keybinds`.
607-
608-```json title="tui.json"
--
621----
622-
623-### Snapshot
624-
625-OpenCode uses snapshots to track file changes during agent operations, enabling you to undo and revert changes within a session. Snapshots are enabled by default.
626-
627-For large repositories or projects with many submodules, the snapshot system can cause slow indexing and significant disk usage as it tracks all changes using an internal git repository. You can disable snapshots using the `snapshot` option.
628-
629:```json title="opencode.json"
630-{
631-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
632-  "snapshot": false
633-}
634-```
635-
636-Note that disabling snapshots means changes made by the agent cannot be rolled back through the UI.
637-
638----
639-
640-### Autoupdate
641-
642-OpenCode will automatically download any new updates when it starts up. You can disable this with the `autoupdate` option.
643-
644:```json title="opencode.json"
645-{
646-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
647-  "autoupdate": false
648-}
649-```
650-
651-If you don't want updates but want to be notified when a new version is available, set `autoupdate` to `"notify"`.
652-Notice that this only works if it was not installed using a package manager such as Homebrew.
653-
654----
655-
656-### Formatters
657-
658-You can enable and configure code formatters through the `formatter` option. Omit it to keep formatters disabled.
659-
660:```json title="opencode.json"
661-{
662-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
663-  "formatter": true
664-}
665-```
666-
667-Use an object to keep built-ins enabled while configuring overrides or custom formatters.
668-
669:```json title="opencode.json"
670-{
671-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
672-  "formatter": {
673-    "prettier": {
674-      "disabled": true
675-    },
676-    "custom-prettier": {
677-      "command": ["npx", "prettier", "--write", "$FILE"],
--
687-[Learn more about formatters here](/docs/formatters).
688-
689----
690-
691-### LSP Servers
692-
693-You can enable and configure LSP servers through the `lsp` option. Omit it to keep LSP disabled.
694-
695:```json title="opencode.json"
696-{
697-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
698-  "lsp": true
699-}
700-```
701-
702-Use an object to keep built-ins enabled while configuring overrides or custom LSP servers.
703-
704:```json title="opencode.json"
705-{
706-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
707-  "lsp": {
708-    "typescript": {
709-      "disabled": true
710-    }
711-  }
712-}
--
717----
718-
719-### Permissions
720-
721-By default, opencode **allows all operations** without requiring explicit approval. You can change this using the `permission` option.
722-
723-For example, to ensure that the `edit` and `bash` tools require user approval:
724-
725:```json title="opencode.json"
726-{
727-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
728-  "permission": {
729-    "edit": "ask",
730-    "bash": "ask"
731-  }
732-}
733-```
--
735-[Learn more about permissions here](/docs/permissions).
736-
737----
738-
739-### Compaction
740-
741-You can control context compaction behavior through the `compaction` option.
742-
743:```json title="opencode.json"
744-{
745-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
746-  "compaction": {
747-    "auto": true,
748-    "prune": false,
749-    "reserved": 10000
750-  }
751-}
--
756-- `reserved` - Token buffer for compaction. Leaves enough window to avoid overflow during compaction.
757-
758----
759-
760-### Watcher
761-
762-You can configure file watcher ignore patterns through the `watcher` option.
763-
764:```json title="opencode.json"
765-{
766-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
767-  "watcher": {
768-    "ignore": ["node_modules/**", "dist/**", ".git/**"]
769-  }
770-}
771-```
772-
773-Patterns follow glob syntax. Use this to exclude noisy directories from file watching.
774-

776-
777-### MCP servers
778-
779-You can configure MCP servers you want to use through the `mcp` option.

781:```json title="opencode.json"
782-{
783-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
784-  "mcp": {}
785-}
786-```
787-
788-[Learn more here](/docs/mcp-servers).

791-
792-### Plugins
793-
794-[Plugins](/docs/plugins) extend OpenCode with custom tools, hooks, and integrations.
795-
796:Place plugin files in `.opencode/plugins/` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. You can also load plugins from npm through the `plugin` option.
797-
798:```json title="opencode.json"
799-{
800-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
801-  "plugin": ["opencode-helicone-session", "@my-org/custom-plugin"]
802-}
803-```
804-
805-[Learn more here](/docs/plugins).

807----
808-
809-### Instructions
810-
811-You can configure the instructions for the model you're using through the `instructions` option.
812-
813:```json title="opencode.json"
814-{
815-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
816-  "instructions": ["CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guidelines.md", ".cursor/rules/*.md"]
817-}
818-```
819-
820-This takes an array of paths and glob patterns to instruction files. [Learn more
821-about rules here](/docs/rules).
822-
823----
824-
825-### Disabled providers
826-
827-You can disable providers that are loaded automatically through the `disabled_providers` option. This is useful when you want to prevent certain providers from being loaded even if their credentials are available.
828-
829:```json title="opencode.json"
830-{
831-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
832-  "disabled_providers": ["openai", "gemini"]
833-}
834-```
835-
836-:::note
837-The `disabled_providers` takes priority over `enabled_providers`.
--
844-- The provider's models won't appear in the model selection list.
845-
846----
847-
848-### Enabled providers
849-
850-You can specify an allowlist of providers through the `enabled_providers` option. When set, only the specified providers will be enabled and all others will be ignored.
851-
852:```json title="opencode.json"
853-{
854-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
855-  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic", "openai"]
856-}
857-```
858-
859-This is useful when you want to restrict OpenCode to only use specific providers rather than disabling them one by one.
860-
--
865-If a provider appears in both `enabled_providers` and `disabled_providers`, the `disabled_providers` takes priority for backwards compatibility.
866-
867----
868-
869-### Experimental
870-
871-The `experimental` key contains options that are under active development.
872-
873:```json title="opencode.json"
874-{
875-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
876-  "experimental": {}
877-}
878-```
879-
880-:::caution
881-Experimental options are not stable. They may change or be removed without notice.

896:```json title="opencode.json"

898-  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",

900-  "provider": {
901-    "anthropic": {
902-      "models": {},
903-      "options": {
904-        "apiKey": "{env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
--
911-If the environment variable is not set, it will be replaced with an empty string.

915-### Files
916-
917-Use `{file:path/to/file}` to substitute the contents of a file:

919:```json title="opencode.json"
920-{

923-  "provider": {
924-    "openai": {
925-      "options": {
926-        "apiKey": "{file:~/.secrets/openai-key}"
927-      }
```
