430	 
431	 # dev-cli
432	 
433	 The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
434	 runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
435	 
436	 ```
437	 git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
438	 git worktree    a disposable local checkout
439	 herdr / tmux / zellij
440	                 a per-host live runtime
441	 dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
442	 ```
443	 
444	 Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
445	 human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
446	 action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
447	 (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
448	 
449	 **The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
450	 record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
451	 record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
452	 abandoning a task.
453	 
454	 ## Check it is there first
455	 
456	 `dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
457	 
458	 ```bash
459	 command -v dev || echo "not installed"
460	 dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
461	 ```
462	 
463	 Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
464	 each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
465	 hard-depend on one.
466	 
467	 ## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
468	 
469	 There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
470	 is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
471	 
472	 | Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
473	 |---|---|---|---|
474	 | Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
475	 | Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
476	 | `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
477	 
478	 **Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
479	 return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
480	 entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
481	 
482	 Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
483	 hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
484	 plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
485	 sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
486	 
487	 Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
488	 checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
489	 the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
490	 
491	 Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
492	 
493	 ## The task lifecycle
494	 
495	 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
496	 |---|---|---|---|
497	 | 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
498	 | 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
499	 | ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
500	 | ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
501	 
502	 ```bash
503	 dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
504	 dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
505	 dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
506	 dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
507	 dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
508	 dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
509	@@ -183,176 +183,181 @@ dev repo sync --all        # fetch + prune, and report what moved
510	 dev fleet list              # aggregate repo/task/runtime state over SSH
511	 dev fleet sync api --push   # publish, then fast-forward safe matching checkouts
512	 dev repo remote [query]     # search configured forge inventories
513	 dev bootstrap ~/code       # recursively inventory an existing machine
514	 dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects   # plan a non-destructive symlink catalog
515	 dev gitignore              # .gitignore from GitHub templates + the common bits
516	 dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
517	 
518	 dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
519	 dev tries mark redis-streams --add important  # durable personal metadata
520	 dev tries archive redis-streams               # reversible; does not delete
521	 dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
522	 
523	 dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
524	 dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
525	 dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
526	 dev summary                # current machine-wide agent context
527	 dev journal                # today's agent-ready development journal
528	 dev journal --since 7d --metrics | opencode run "summarize this"
529	 dev cache list             # regenerable forge/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-index caches
530	 dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages; dev help wt also works
531	 ```
532	 
533	 Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
534	 
535	 ## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
536	 
537	 Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
538	 symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
539	 is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
540	 
541	 There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
542	 `paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
543	 
544	 ```bash
545	 dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
546	 dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
547	 dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
548	 ```
549	 
550	 Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
551	 or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
552	 
553	 ## Creating and setting up repositories
554	 
555	 Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
556	 running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
557	 `dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
558	 minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
559	 `owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
560	 its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
561	 Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
562	 directly.
563	 `repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
564	 history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
565	 exact source tree.
566	 
567	 Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
568	 committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
569	 repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
570	 remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
571	 Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
572	 `start`.
573	 
574	 On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
575	 Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
576	 Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
577	 
578	 The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
579	 selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
580	 README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
581	 a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
582	 
583	 Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
584	 `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
585	 configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
586	 it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
587

610	+distinct startup linked checkout. Skill listing uses the native versioned
611	+77-agent path registry and never runs Node/`npx`; `c` is the explicit grouped
612	+upstream check. MCP inventories only sanitized static declarations for Claude
613	+Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode—it never starts or health-checks a

617	 REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
618	 organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
619	 account can access. A private cache is decoded after the first view; stale rows
620	 stay searchable while refresh runs. Malformed/oversized payloads and caches
621	 fingerprinted for another configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored.
622	 GitLab uses explicit `GITLAB_HOST`/`GLAB_HOST` (default `gitlab.com`) instead of
623	 cwd inference; a successful empty refresh clears obsolete rows. `/` filters provider,
624	 owner/name, visibility and description, with `vis:private` for an exact visibility match. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
625	 confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
626	 for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query and `--refresh`
627	 forces a complete synchronization.
628	 
629	 `dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
630	 second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
631	 session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
632	 snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
633	 commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
634	 unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
635	 and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
636	 does not launch the receiving agent.
637	 
638	 `dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
639	 combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
640	 worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
641	 expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
642	 selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
643	 complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
644	 one repository.
645	 
646	 Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
647	 
648	 ```toml
649	 [[forge.azure_devops]]
650	 organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
651	 project = "Platform"
652	 ```
653	 
654	 Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
655	 the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
656	 
657	 FLEET reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot for the local host, then calls each
658	 configured host's own `dev` over SSH, preserving its XDG paths. If the current
659	 REPOS generation is still loading, FLEET waits while keeping usable cached rows
660	 visible rather than rescanning local repositories. The TUI hides this machine
661	 by default because REPOS already shows its richer local state; `a` includes
662	 local rows. Host cache identity includes the SSH port. `dev fleet list` remains
663	 local plus remote. Enter prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an
664	 SSH login shell.
665	 `dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
666	 of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
667	 
668	 REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
669	 checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
670	 shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
671	 expand linked worktrees; children
672	 show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
673	 checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
674	 copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
675	 worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
676	 `[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
677	 it.

1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
4	
5	The intended result is a provider-independent, no-network skill inventory across repositories with explicit upstream freshness checks; a separate secret-safe MCP declaration inventory; and an unambiguous responsive Tasks table. Read paths must never execute `npx`, start MCP servers, resolve credentials, or claim live MCP health.
6	
7	## Agreed product behavior
8	
9	- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
10	- Native skill discovery covers the complete path registry represented by upstream `skills` v1.5.23 (77 agent IDs), with a versioned, table-driven snapshot. Shared paths such as `.agents/skills` are reported as registry-compatible rather than pretending `dev` detected every installed agent executable.
11	- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
12	- MCP is an independent domain and user surface: `dev mcp list` plus a lazy MCP TUI view. Initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
13	- MCP rows represent static declarations, not effective merged runtime configuration or connectivity. Duplicate declarations remain scope-qualified rows; unsupported/runtime-only sources are diagnosed as partial coverage.
14	
15	# Implementation plan
16	
17	## 1. Resolve reusable repository scan targets
18	
19	- Add a small neutral target type under `internal/agenttarget/` containing repository name/display, canonical path/common-dir identity, and the exact checkout root being scanned.
20	- Build targets by reusing `config.Config.DiscoveryRoots`, `repo.Discover`, `repo.Resolve`, and `gitx.Discover` rather than adding another filesystem walk.
21	- Encode selection policy in this package, not Cobra handlers:
22	  - current mode resolves the exact current checkout, including a linked worktree;
23	  - `--all` returns non-bare canonical discovered checkouts once;
24	  - `--repo` accepts existing repository references and explicit linked-worktree paths;
25	  - TUI aggregation appends the startup checkout when it is not the accepted canonical REPOS row;
26	  - targets are deduplicated by common-dir plus checkout root and sorted deterministically.
27	- Reuse accepted `tui.RepoRow` snapshots for lazy TUI loads so SKILLS/MCP do not rediscover repositories or delay initial startup.
28	
29	## 2. Replace provider-based skill reads with native inventory
30	
31	Refactor `internal/agentskill/agentskill.go` into focused types/registry/scanner/lock/freshness/provider files while preserving the existing mutation command API.
32	
33	### Registry and filesystem scan
34	
35	- Check in a provenance/version-tagged Go registry corresponding to upstream `skills@1.5.23` agent paths, including project/global paths and supported environment overrides (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, XDG config roots, and the other registry-defined homes).
36	- Collapse identical logical directories before reading them; scan only immediate child directories with a valid, size-bounded `SKILL.md` rather than recursively walking repositories or home directories.
37	- Parse the skill frontmatter name with a real YAML parser, merge duplicate logical installations by `(scope, target checkout, normalized skill name)`, and retain all installation paths/agent IDs. Resolve physical symlinks for deduplication without losing the logical path that explains agent attribution.
38	- Treat shared paths as compatible with the registry entries that consume that path; expose an attribution/registry-version field so this is not confused with executable detection.
39	- Make exact lock names win. Only use normalized-name matching when unique; emit a deterministic diagnostic for collisions instead of selecting a random Go map entry.
40	
41	### Locks and local status
42	
43	- Split project and global lock decoding and normalize them internally:
44	  - project `<checkout>/skills-lock.json` (current v1 fields such as source, ref, skill path, and `computedHash`);
45	  - global v3 metadata and compatible older fields from `$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is absolute, otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
46	- Bound lock reads and distinguish missing, malformed, unreadable, unsupported-version, and structurally invalid files. Missing is normal; the other cases become safe per-source diagnostics while other repositories continue.
47	- Include lock-only entries whose installation is absent, and unlocked installed directories as externally managed rows.
48	- Add repository/checkout identity, logical installations, local presence, attribution, and normalized lock metadata to `agentskill.Skill`/result types without removing existing fields.
49	- Keep upstream freshness (`unchecked/current/update_available/upstream_missing/unverifiable/check_failed`) separate from local presence/integrity. Only the embedded `dev-cli` skill receives verified/drifted byte-integrity status; do not claim generic lock hashes verify installed bytes.
50	- Convert `Managed` and `FindProject` to the native lock/scanner primitives so repository scaffolding and selected-skill updates no longer require provider JSON.
51	
52	### Explicit freshness and mutation boundary
53	
54	- Preserve and isolate the existing `safeSkillFolder`, folder hashing, Git-source derivation, and grouped `(source URL, ref)` comparisons.
55	- Aggregate all project/global rows first, then run one bounded, cancellation-aware freshness pass so a shared source/ref is cloned once across all repositories. Preserve deterministic row order, clean every temporary clone, and mark only affected rows failed.
56	- Keep local/node_modules/well-known sources unverifiable unless their lock metadata provides a supported comparison; do not silently reinterpret them as Git.
57	- Delete the read-time `npx --no-install skills` path. Read/list/provider-version checks must not invoke npm, a registry, or project Node code.
58	- Retain `interactiveProvider` for explicit add/install/update operations, but require a directly installed `skills` executable after the security review found repository-local `npx` provider substitution. Update `dev doctor` to describe native inventory as always available and report the optional mutation provider separately.
59	
60	## 3. Aggregate skills across repositories and expose them in CLI
61	
62	- Add an inventory collector (representatively `internal/inventory/agent_skills.go`) that scans project targets with the existing context-aware `inventory.Limiter`, scans global paths exactly once, merges diagnostics, and optionally performs one grouped freshness check.
63	- Extend `dev skill list` in `internal/cli/skill.go` with mutually exclusive `--all` and `--repo <ref>` target selection while preserving `--project`, `--global`, `--check`, and the current-checkout default.
64	- Keep the existing JSON array and every existing key/type; add repository/checkout, installations, presence/integrity, attribution/registry-version, and normalized lock fields. Write partial diagnostics to stderr so JSON stdout stays valid.
65	- Add `--repo` to project `dev skill update`; reject repo targeting for global updates. In the TUI, update a selected project skill from that row’s checkout root, while the interactive add wizard continues to use the startup checkout.
66	- Render a repository-aware human table and keep global rows repository-less rather than duplicating them per target.
67	
68	## 4. Add a normalized, secret-safe MCP domain
69	
70	Create `internal/agentmcp/` with normalized types, a scanner, sanitization helpers, and one adapter per supported agent.
71	
72	### Static sources covered
73	
74	- **Claude Code:** project `.mcp.json`; user and per-project local declarations in `~/.claude.json`.
75	- **Codex:** `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` or `~/.codex/config.toml`; trusted-project `.codex/config.toml`; direct and plugin override declarations.
76	- **Cursor:** project `.cursor/mcp.json`; user `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
77	- **Gemini CLI:** project `.gemini/settings.json`; user `~/.gemini/settings.json`; readable documented system default/override files, with source scope retained.
78	- **OpenCode:** project `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc`; XDG user config; an explicit local `OPENCODE_CONFIG` file and readable managed files. Do not fetch remote `.well-known` config or parse inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` as durable inventory.
79	- Use the existing BurntSushi TOML dependency for Codex, `encoding/json` for strict JSON, and a maintained JSONC normalizer for OpenCode rather than an ad-hoc comment stripper.
80	
81	### Normalization and safety
82	
83	- Normalize only non-secret facts: server name, agent, declaration scope, repository, config path, managed/direct source, declared enabled/required/trust policy, transport, safe endpoint host or command basename, argument count, and names/kinds of credential references.
84	- Keep each declaration scope-qualified; do not emulate undocumented merge/precedence rules or label a row “effective.” When transport cannot be proven (for example a Cursor URL declaration), report `remote/unknown` rather than guessing.
85	- Sanitize during adapter conversion so raw values never enter normalized rows, diagnostics, traces, CLI JSON, or TUI state:
86	  - never expand environment variables or `{env:…}`/`${…}` placeholders;
87	  - never read OpenCode `{file:…}` targets or OAuth/token stores;
88	  - never retain env/header/OAuth values or raw command arguments;
89	  - reduce commands to a safe basename and URLs to a credential-free representation with userinfo/query/fragment removed or redacted;
90	  - use fixed diagnostic codes/messages that cannot echo decoder snippets containing secrets;
91	  - reject control characters and bound config size;
92	  - confine project config symlinks to the selected checkout, while allowing bounded user-config symlinks for dotfile managers.
93	- Never invoke agent MCP list/debug commands, helper commands, servers, URLs, or health checks. Document omitted plugin caches, hosted connectors, runtime-only config, remote organization config, and unsupported agent formats as coverage limitations.

When it invokes `prepareRepoDependentsForReload`, if the dependent is currently loading, it increments generation and sets loading status. This can lead to outdated context being used, which isn't good. If a repo reload never produces a result, dependents might get stuck waiting forever while the repo itself does too. There are some complexities here I need to resolve. 

**Examining production actions**

I'm analyzing the new production actions. When the current Skills state has a partial stale snapshot and the user switches views, the config reload starts. If `prepareDepends` sees `state.hasSnapshot` not current, it invalidates. Later, when it checks `state.hasSnapshot` as true but requested as false, a second `invalidateView` is triggered, incrementing generation again, which is fine. If the user switches to Skills while a repo is loading, the process looks good, but there’s a potential issue with tracking dependency generation during `afterReposResult`. 

**Exploring repo and skill interactions**

This situation happens when the user presses `r` on Skills while the repos aren't loading, and the current repos are fresh. It initiates a skill scan. However, what if an unrelated repo result from the same generation arrives? I need to remember that each repo generation can only return one result, and if a fresh result has already been accepted, no later results will be accepted. Managing these interactions is crucial to ensure the system behaves as expected.

 func TestShellInit(t *testing.T) {
 	h := newHarness(t)
 	for _, shell := range []string{"bash", "zsh", "fish"} {
 		out := h.mustRun("shell-init", shell)
 		if !strings.Contains(out, "DEV_SHELL_INIT") {
 			t.Errorf("%s wrapper should export the marker doctor looks for", shell)
 		}
 		if !strings.Contains(out, "cd ") {
 			t.Errorf("%s wrapper should handle the cd directive", shell)
 		}
 	}
 }
 
 func TestRawOutputsNeverContainColor(t *testing.T) {
 	h := newHarness(t)
 	for _, args := range [][]string{
 		{"--color=always", "ls", "--json"},
 		{"--color=always", "shell-init", "zsh"},
 		{"--color=always", "skill", "print"},
 		{"--color=always", "completion", "zsh"},
 	} {
 		out, errOut, err := h.run(args...)
 		if err != nil {
 			t.Fatalf("dev %s: %v\nstderr: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, errOut)
 		}
 		if strings.Contains(out, "\x1b[") {
 			t.Errorf("dev %s emitted ANSI in raw output", strings.Join(args, " "))
 		}
 	}
 }
 
 func min(a, b int) int {
 	if a < b {
 		return a
 	}
 	return b

 // runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
 // practice means the cursor blink timers.
 func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
 	done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
 	go func() { done <- cmd() }()
 	select {
 	case msg := <-done:
 		return msg, true
 	case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
 		return nil, false
 	}
 }
 
 func key(s string) tea.KeyMsg {
 	switch s {
 	case "enter":
 		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter}
 	case "esc":
 		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc}
 	case "down":
 		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown}
 	case "up":
 		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp}
 	}
 	return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(s)}
 }

10	// LocalLoadRequest identifies the three view generations sharing one source
11	// snapshot. Each result remains independently replaceable.
12	type LocalLoadRequest struct {
13		CycleGeneration uint64
14		TasksGeneration uint64
15		ReposGeneration uint64
16		TriesGeneration uint64
17		ShowAllTries    bool
18		ForceSizes      bool
19	}
20	
21	// LocalResult is one terminal TASKS, REPOS, or TRY snapshot.
22	type LocalResult struct {
23		View       View
24		Generation uint64
25		Tasks      []inventory.Row
26		Repos      []RepoRow
27		Tries      []TryRow
28		Valid      bool
29		Err        error
30	}
31	
32	// LocalLoad is a cancellable stream owned by the caller's context.
33	type LocalLoad struct {
34		ID      uint64
35		Request LocalLoadRequest
36		Results <-chan LocalResult
37	}
38	
39	// LocalActions starts one shared local source cycle.
40	type LocalActions struct {
41		Start func(context.Context, LocalLoadRequest) LocalLoad
42	}
43	
44	type localMsg struct {
45		load   LocalLoad
46		result LocalResult
47		done   bool
48	}
49	
50	func (m Model) startLocalLoad() tea.Cmd {
51		if m.actions.Local.Start == nil {
52			return nil
53		}
54		request := LocalLoadRequest{
55			CycleGeneration: m.localGeneration,
56			TasksGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTasks).generation,
57			ReposGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).generation,
58			TriesGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTries).generation,
59			ShowAllTries:    m.showAllTries,
60			ForceSizes:      m.forceSizeReload,
61		}
62		load := m.actions.Local.Start(m.localReadContext(), request)
63		load.Request = request
64		if load.ID == 0 || load.Results == nil {
65			return nil
66		}
67		return waitForLocal(load)
68	}
69	
70	func waitForLocal(load LocalLoad) tea.Cmd {
71		return func() tea.Msg {
72			result, ok := <-load.Results
73			if !ok {
74				return localMsg{load: load, done: true}
75			}
76			return localMsg{load: load, result: result}
77		}
78	}
79	
80	func (m Model) applyLocalResult(result LocalResult) (Model, bool) {
81		accepted := false
82		switch result.View {
83		case ViewTasks:
84			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
85				ViewTasks, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
86				len(result.Tasks), result.Err, result.Valid,
87			)
88			if accepted && result.Valid {
89				m.rows = append([]inventory.Row(nil), result.Tasks...)
90			}
91		case ViewRepos:
92			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
93				ViewRepos, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
94				len(result.Repos), result.Err, result.Valid,
95			)
96			if accepted && result.Valid {
97				m.repos = append([]RepoRow(nil), result.Repos...)
98				m.matchRemoteLocals()

100		case ViewTries:
101			accepted = m.applyViewResult(

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230
```

1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
4	
5	The intended result is a provider-independent, no-network skill inventory across repositories with explicit upstream freshness checks; a separate secret-safe MCP declaration inventory; and an unambiguous responsive Tasks table. Read paths must never execute `npx`, start MCP servers, resolve credentials, or claim live MCP health.
6	
7	## Agreed product behavior
8	
9	- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
10	- Native skill discovery covers the complete path registry represented by upstream `skills` v1.5.23 (77 agent IDs), with a versioned, table-driven snapshot. Shared paths such as `.agents/skills` are reported as registry-compatible rather than pretending `dev` detected every installed agent executable.
11	- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
12	- MCP is an independent domain and user surface: `dev mcp list` plus a lazy MCP TUI view. Initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
13	- MCP rows represent static declarations, not effective merged runtime configuration or connectivity. Duplicate declarations remain scope-qualified rows; unsupported/runtime-only sources are diagnosed as partial coverage.

1	package repo
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"net/url"
6		"sort"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// RedactCloneRef removes URL userinfo before a clone source is rendered or
11	// persisted in a result. SSH usernames such as git@host remain visible; an
12	// scp-like prefix containing a password/token separator is redacted.
13	func RedactCloneRef(ref string) string {
14		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
15		parsed, err := url.Parse(ref)
16		if err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" && parsed.User != nil {
17			parsed.User = nil
18			return parsed.String()
19		}
20		at := strings.LastIndex(ref, "@")
21		if at > 0 && strings.Contains(ref[:at], ":") {
22			return "***@" + ref[at+1:]
23		}
24		return ref
25	}
26	
27	// RedactCloneError returns an error whose displayed message cannot echo
28	// credential-bearing clone references passed to Git.
29	func RedactCloneError(err error, refs ...string) error {
30		if err == nil {
31			return nil
32		}
33		message := err.Error()
34		refs = append([]string(nil), refs...)
35		sort.SliceStable(refs, func(i, j int) bool { return len(refs[i]) > len(refs[j]) })
36		for _, ref := range refs {
37			if ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref); ref != "" {
38				message = strings.ReplaceAll(message, ref, RedactCloneRef(ref))
39			}
40		}
41		return errors.New(message)
42	}
43

```text
> Qualified Names (`mcp_server_tool`) using the first underscore after the
> `mcp_` prefix. An underscore in your server alias will cause the parser to
> misidentify the server name, which can cause security policies to fail
> silently.

- **`mcpServers.<SERVER_NAME>`** (object): The server parameters for the named
  server.
  - `command` (string, optional): The command to execute to start the MCP server
    via standard I/O.
  - `args` (array of strings, optional): Arguments to pass to the command.
  - `env` (object, optional): Environment variables to set for the server
    process.
  - `cwd` (string, optional): The working directory in which to start the
    server.
  - `url` (string, optional): The URL of an MCP server that uses Server-Sent
    Events (SSE) for communication.
  - `httpUrl` (string, optional): The URL of an MCP server that uses streamable
    HTTP for communication.
  - `headers` (object, optional): A map of HTTP headers to send with requests to
    `url` or `httpUrl`.
  - `timeout` (number, optional): Timeout in milliseconds for requests to this
    MCP server.
  - `trust` (boolean, optional): Trust this server and bypass all tool call
    confirmations.
  - `description` (string, optional): A brief description of the server, which
    may be used for display purposes.
  - `includeTools` (array of strings, optional): List of tool names to include
    from this MCP server. When specified, only the tools listed here will be
    available from this server (allowlist behavior). If not specified, all tools
    from the server are enabled by default.
  - `excludeTools` (array of strings, optional): List of tool names to exclude
    from this MCP server. Tools listed here will not be available to the model,
    even if they are exposed by the server. **Note:** `excludeTools` takes
    precedence over `includeTools` - if a tool is in both lists, it will be
    excluded.

#### `telemetry`

Configures logging and metrics collection for Gemini CLI. For more information,
see [Telemetry](../cli/telemetry.md).

- **Properties:**
  - **`enabled`** (boolean): Whether or not telemetry is enabled.
  - **`traces`** (boolean): Whether detailed traces with large attributes (like
    tool outputs and file reads) are captured. Defaults to `false`.
  - **`target`** (string): The destination for collected telemetry. Supported
    values are `local` and `gcp`.
  - **`otlpEndpoint`** (string): The endpoint for the OTLP Exporter.
  - **`otlpProtocol`** (string): The protocol for the OTLP Exporter (`grpc` or
    `http`).
  - **`logPrompts`** (boolean): Whether or not to include the content of user
    prompts in the logs.
  - **`outfile`** (string): The file to write telemetry to when `target` is
    `local`.
  - **`useCollector`** (boolean): Whether to use an external OTLP collector.

### Example `settings.json`

Here is an example of a `settings.json` file with the nested structure, new as

41	func newTUICmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
42		cmd := &cobra.Command{
43			Use:   "tui",
44			Short: "Interactive dashboard over the inventory",
45			Long: `Browse and act on your work in progress.
46	
47	Shows exactly what "dev ls" shows, from the same code path, plus the ability
48	to open, park and annotate a task without retyping its name.
49	
50	Seven lists, switched with tab:
51	
52	  TASKS   change streams dev is tracking — what am I working on
53	  REPOS   durable repositories under the scan roots — what do I have here
54	  FLEET   repositories and active work across configured SSH machines
55	  TRY     scratch experiments and retained lifecycle history
56	  REMOTE  repositories visible through configured forge CLIs — what can I clone/open
57	  SKILLS  repository/global agent skills, local status and update freshness
58	  MCP     sanitized static MCP declarations for supported agents
59	
60	Navigation is vim-style, with arrows alongside:
61	
62	  j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
63	  g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
64	  /          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
65	
66	Actions depend on the list:
67	
68	  TASKS   enter open · p park · c edit next
69		  REPOS   enter ad hoc · space worktrees · m metadata · s worktree task · d direct task
70		  FLEET   enter Herdr/SSH open · Git changes are read-only here
71		  TRY     enter open · n create · space lifecycle/metadata actions
72	  REMOTE  enter open local · c clone after confirmation
73	  SKILLS  a interactive add · c check updates · u update selected after confirmation
74	  MCP     r reload static declarations; no server is started or probed
75	
76	  y       copy menu: yy context · yp path · yb branch · ys sessions · yw WT paths
77	  H       selected repo heatmap; b backfills it when empty
78	  e       edit config; returning live-reloads data, columns, sort and tools
79	  O / R   cycle / reverse REPOS or TRY sort
80	  r       reload config + data     1 / 2 / 3  hot / warm / cold
81	  0       clear filters            a include history  ? help  q quit
82	
83	External tools are configured, not fixed — see [[tui.tools]] in the config,
84	and "dev tui tools" for what is bound here. They run in the selected row's checkout;
85	the dashboard suspends while they do and redraws afterwards, and bindings for
86	programs that are not installed are not offered.`,
87			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
88			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
89				return runTUI(app)
90			},
91		}
92		cmd.AddCommand(newTUIToolsCmd(app))
93		return cmd
94	}

96	func newTUIToolsCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
97		return &cobra.Command{
98			Use:   "tools",
99			Short: "List the external tool bindings and whether each one works here",
100			Long: `Show which programs the dashboard will hand the terminal to.
101	
102	Bindings come from [[tui.tools]] in the config; with none configured, the
103	built-in set applies. A configured list replaces the defaults entirely, so
104	what is bound is always exactly what is written down.
105	
106	Add your own — an editor, a script, anything you already reach for:
107	
108	    [[tui.tools]]
109	    key  = "V"
110	    name = "nvim"
111	    run  = "nvim ."
112	
113	    [[tui.tools]]
114	    key  = "B"
115	    name = "vibe"
116	    run  = "vibe"
117	
118	The command runs through your shell in the selected row's checkout, so
119	arguments, environment variables and your own scripts all behave as typed.
120	Set interactive = true only for aliases/functions from your shell rc; that
121	binding runs through $SHELL -lic and the mode is shown in this listing.`,
122			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
123			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
124				configured := len(app.Cfg.TUI.Tools) > 0
125				source := "built-in defaults"
126				if configured {
127					source = config.Contract(app.Cfg.Source)
128				}
129				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "tool bindings from %s\n\n", source)
130	
131				t := app.newTable("KEY", "NAME", "MODE", "RUNS", "AVAILABLE")
132				style := app.outStyle()
133				configuredTools := app.Cfg.EffectiveTools()
134				for i, tool := range externalTools(app) {
135					status := "yes"
136					if tool.Probe != nil && !tool.Probe(ctxOf()) {
137						status = style.warning("no — not on PATH")
138					} else {
139						status = style.success(status)
140					}
141					// Command is [shell, -c/-lic, run]; show the run itself.
142					run := tool.Command[len(tool.Command)-1]
143					mode := "shell"
144					if i < len(configuredTools) && configuredTools[i].Interactive {
145						mode = "interactive"
146					}
147					t.Add(tool.Key, tool.Name, mode, run, status)
148				}
149				t.Render(app.Out)
150	
151				if !configured {
152					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nOverride them with [[tui.tools]] in your config; see \"dev tui tools --help\".")
153				}
154				fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nA tool cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.")
155				return nil
156			},
157		}
158	}

160	// interactive reports whether a real terminal is attached. Piping `dev` into
161	// anything must produce the plain listing, not terminal control sequences.
162	func interactive() bool {
163		for _, f := range []*os.File{os.Stdin, os.Stdout} {
164			info, err := f.Stat()
165			if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice == 0 {
166				return false
167			}
168		}
169		return true
170	}

190	func tuiRemoteCloneDestination(app *App, name string) (string, error) {
191		projectRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot)
192		if err := os.MkdirAll(projectRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
193			return "", err
194		}
195		destination, err := pathx.JoinChild(projectRoot, name)
196		if err != nil {
197			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote repository name %q is not a safe clone destination: %w", name, err)
198		}
199		return destination, nil
200	}

775					worktreeCount = len(worktrees) - 1

793			}

1048	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
1049	//
1050	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
1051	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
1052	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
1053	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
1054		var out []tui.Tool
1055		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
1056			run := t.Run
1057			name := t.Name
1058			if name == "" {
1059				name = firstWord(run)
1060			}
1061			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
1062			if t.Interactive {
1063				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
1064				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
1065				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
1066				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
1067				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
1068			}
1069			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
1070				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
1071				Probe: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
1072			})
1073		}
1074		return out
1075	}

1137	func remoteCacheSourceID(app *App) string {
1138		parts := []string{
1139			"forge-source-v1",
1140			"GH_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GH_HOST"),
1141			"GITLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GITLAB_HOST"),
1142			"GLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GLAB_HOST"),
1143		}
1144		for _, target := range app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps {
1145			parts = append(parts, "azure="+target.Organization+"\x00"+target.Project)
1146		}
1147		sort.Strings(parts)
1148		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\x00")))
1149		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum[:])
1150	}

1178	func matchRemoteRepoRows(remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo, locals []tui.RepoRow) []tui.RemoteRow {
1179		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
1180		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1181		for _, r := range locals {
1182			if r.RemoteForge == forge.Unknown || r.RemoteName == "" {
1183				continue
1184			}
1185			key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)
1186			if ambiguous[key] {
1187				continue
1188			}
1189			if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
1190				delete(byRemote, key)
1191				ambiguous[key] = true
1192				continue
1193			}
1194			byRemote[key] = r
1195		}
1196		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1197		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1198			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1199			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1200				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
1201				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1202				if local.Asset != nil {
1203					row.LocalKind = local.Asset.Kind
1204				}
1205			}
1206			out = append(out, row)
1207		}
1208		return out
1209	}

1248	func collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, options remoteCollectOptions) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1249		type result struct {
1250			kind  forge.Kind
1251			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
1252			err   error
1253		}
1254		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
1255		matchRows := func(repos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
1256			if options.LocalsSet {
1257				return matchRemoteRepoRows(repos, options.Locals)
1258			}
1259			return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, repos)
1260		}
1261		providers := options.Providers
1262		if !options.ProvidersSet {
1263			providers = configuredForges(app)
1264		}
1265		ch := make(chan result, len(providers))
1266		var wg sync.WaitGroup
1267		available := 0
1268		var unavailable []error
1269		expected := map[forge.Kind]bool{}
1270		var unavailableKinds []forge.Kind
1271		for _, f := range providers {
1272			if !f.Available() {
1273				// GitHub and GitLab remain opportunistic, but an explicit Azure
1274				// target should report why it did not contribute any repositories.
1275				if f.Kind() == forge.AzureDevOps {
1276					unavailable = append(unavailable, &forge.ErrNoCLI{Kind: forge.AzureDevOps, Bin: "az"})
1277					expected[f.Kind()] = true
1278					unavailableKinds = append(unavailableKinds, f.Kind())
1279				}
1280				continue
1281			}
1282			expected[f.Kind()] = true
1283			available++
1284			wg.Add(1)
1285			go func(f forge.Forge) {
1286				defer wg.Done()
1287				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx)
1288				ch <- result{kind: f.Kind(), repos: r, err: err}
1289			}(f)
1290		}
1291		wg.Wait()
1292		close(ch)
1293		if available == 0 {
1294			if cached, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath()); ok && cached.SourceID == sourceID {
1295				rows := matchRows(cached.Repos)
1296				if len(unavailable) > 0 {
1297					return rows, errors.Join(unavailable...)
1298				}
1299				return rows, fmt.Errorf("no supported forge CLI is installed")
1300			}
1301			if len(unavailable) > 0 {
1302				return nil, errors.Join(unavailable...)
1303			}
1304			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no supported forge CLI is installed")
1305		}
1306	
1307		old, _ := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1308		if old.SourceID != sourceID {
1309			old = forge.Cache{}
1310		}
1311		byProvider := map[forge.Kind][]forge.RemoteRepo{}
1312		statuses := map[forge.Kind]forge.ProviderStatus{}
1313		for _, r := range old.Repos {
1314			byProvider[r.Forge] = append(byProvider[r.Forge], r)
1315		}
1316		for kind, status := range old.Providers {
1317			statuses[kind] = status
1318		}
1319		errs := append([]error(nil), unavailable...)
1320		successful := 0
1321		now := time.Now().UTC()
1322		for _, kind := range unavailableKinds {
1323			status := statuses[kind]
1324			status.Error = "provider CLI unavailable"
1325			statuses[kind] = status
1326		}
1327		for res := range ch {
1328			if res.err != nil {
1329				errs = append(errs, res.err)
1330				status := statuses[res.kind]
1331				status.Error = res.err.Error()
1332				if len(byProvider[res.kind]) == 0 && len(res.repos) > 0 {
1333					byProvider[res.kind] = res.repos
1334					status.FetchedAt = now
1335					status.Complete = false
1336				}
1337				statuses[res.kind] = status
1338				continue
1339			}
1340			successful++
1341			byProvider[res.kind] = res.repos
1342			statuses[res.kind] = forge.ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
1343		}
1344		var remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
1345		complete := true
1346		providerStatuses := map[forge.Kind]forge.ProviderStatus{}
1347		for kind := range expected {
1348			status, ok := statuses[kind]
1349			if !ok || !status.Complete {
1350				complete = false
1351			}
1352			if ok {
1353				providerStatuses[kind] = status
1354			}
1355			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, byProvider[kind]...)
1356		}
1357		sortRemoteRepos(remoteRepos)
1358		if successful > 0 {
1359			_ = forge.SaveCacheStateContext(ctx, remoteCachePath(), forge.Cache{
1360				Version: forge.CacheVersion, SourceID: sourceID, FetchedAt: now, Complete: complete,
1361				Providers: providerStatuses, Repos: remoteRepos,
1362			})
1363		}
1364		return matchRows(remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
1365	}

1367	func sortRemoteRepos(repos []forge.RemoteRepo) {
1368		sort.SliceStable(repos, func(i, j int) bool {
1369			if !repos[i].UpdatedAt.Equal(repos[j].UpdatedAt) {
1370				return repos[i].UpdatedAt.After(repos[j].UpdatedAt)
1371			}
1372			return repos[i].Label() < repos[j].Label()
1373		})
1374	}

1376	func configuredForges(app *App) []forge.Forge {
1377		providers := forge.All()
1378		if app == nil || len(app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps) == 0 {
1379			return providers
1380		}
1381		targets := make([]forge.AzureDevOpsTarget, 0, len(app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps))
1382		for _, target := range app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps {
1383			targets = append(targets, forge.AzureDevOpsTarget{

1385				Project:      target.Project,
1386			})

1391	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
1392		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
1393		assets, _, assetErr := joinRepoAssets(app, locals)
1394		if assetErr != nil {
1395			app.warnf("could not join catalog metadata to remote locals: %v", assetErr)
1396			assets = make([]*catalog.Entry, len(locals))
1397		}
1398		type localMatch struct {
1399			repository repo.Repo
1400			asset      *catalog.Entry
1401		}
1402		localByRemote := map[string]localMatch{}
1403		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1404		for index, r := range locals {
1405			if r.Bare {
1406				continue
1407			}
1408			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
1409			if kind == forge.Unknown || name == "" {
1410				continue
1411			}
1412			key := string(kind) + "/" + strings.ToLower(name)
1413			if ambiguous[key] {
1414				continue
1415			}
1416			if _, exists := localByRemote[key]; exists {
1417				delete(localByRemote, key)
1418				ambiguous[key] = true
1419				continue
1420			}
1421			localByRemote[key] = localMatch{repository: r, asset: assets[index]}
1422		}
1423		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1424		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1425			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1426			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1427				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.repository.Path, local.repository.Display()
1428				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1429				if local.asset != nil {
1430					row.LocalKind = local.asset.Kind
1431				}
1432			}
1433			out = append(out, row)
1434		}
1435		// Linked-worktree Tries are intentionally absent from repo.Discover's project
1436		// inventory, so use their explicit catalog identity as a second safe source.
1437		applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app, out)
1438		return out
1439	}
1440	
1441	func applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app *App, rows []tui.RemoteRow) {
1442		if app == nil || app.Catalog == nil || len(rows) == 0 {
1443			return
1444		}
1445		entries, diagnostics, err := app.Catalog.ListWithDiagnostics()
1446		if err != nil {
1447			app.warnf("could not read catalog for remote matching: %v", err)
1448			return
1449		}
1450		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
1451			app.warnf("%s", diagnostic.Error())
1452		}
1453		if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
1454			return
1455		}
1456		host := config.Hostname()
1457		byIdentity := make(map[string][]*catalog.Entry)
1458		for _, entry := range entries {
1459			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(host)
1460			if !ok || location.State != catalog.LocationPresent || entry.RemoteIdentity == "" ||
1461				liveCatalogLocationPath(location) == "" {
1462				continue
1463			}
1464			byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity] = append(byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity], entry)
1465		}
1466		for index := range rows {
1467			identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(rows[index].Repo.CloneURL)
1468			matches := byIdentity[identity]
1469			if identity == "" || len(matches) != 1 {
1470				continue
1471			}
1472			location, _ := matches[0].LocationFor(host)
1473			rows[index].LocalPath = liveCatalogLocationPath(location)
1474			rows[index].LocalName = matches[0].Name
1475			rows[index].LocalKind = matches[0].Kind
1476		}
1477	}
1478	
1479	func liveCatalogLocationPath(location catalog.Location) string {
1480		for _, candidate := range []string{location.CurrentPath, location.RealPath} {
1481			if candidate == "" {
1482				continue
1483			}
1484			if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
1485				return candidate
1486			}
1487		}
1488		return ""
1489	}

1491	func prepareTUINoteEdit(app *App, n *note.Note) (tui.NoteEdit, error) {
1492		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-*.md")
1493		if err != nil {
1494			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1495		}
1496		path := tmp.Name()
1497		if _, err := io.WriteString(tmp, n.Body); err != nil {
1498			_ = tmp.Close()
1499			_ = os.Remove(path)
1500			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1501		}
1502		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
1503			_ = os.Remove(path)
1504			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1505		}
1506		proc, _, err := editorProcess(path, "")
1507		if err != nil {
1508			_ = os.Remove(path)
1509			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1510		}
1511		return tui.NoteEdit{
1512			Command: proc,
1513			Complete: func(runErr error) error {
1514				if runErr != nil {
1515					_ = os.Remove(path)
1516					return runErr
1517				}
1518				body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
1519				if err != nil {
1520					return fmt.Errorf("read edited body (preserved at %s): %w", path, err)
1521				}
1522				if strings.TrimSpace(string(body)) == "" {
1523					_ = os.Remove(path)
1524					return fmt.Errorf("edited note body is empty; not saved")
1525				}
1526				_, err = app.Notes.Update(context.Background(), n.ID, n.Revision(), string(body), n.Tags)
1527				if err != nil {
1528					return fmt.Errorf("save edited note: %w; edited body preserved at %s", err, path)
1529				}
1530				_ = os.Remove(path)
1531				return nil
1532			},
1533		}, nil
1534	}

138			detail := "not found — Azure DevOps PRs unavailable"
139			if azureTargets > 0 {
140				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d configured inventory target(s) skipped", azureTargets)
141			}
142			checks = append(checks, check{"az", checkWarn, detail})
143		} else if err := forge.CheckAzureDevOps(ctx); err != nil {
144			checks = append(checks, check{"az", checkWarn, path + " — " + err.Error()})
145		} else {
146			detail := path + " — Azure DevOps: PRs"
147			if azureTargets == 0 {
148				detail += "; inventory disabled (no forge.azure_devops targets)"
149			} else {
150				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d inventory target(s)", azureTargets)
151			}
152			checks = append(checks, check{"az", checkOK, detail})
153		}
154	
155		// Shell integration: without the wrapper, `dev resume` prints a path
156		// instead of moving the user, which looks broken if unexplained.
157		if os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_INIT") == "1" {
158			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkOK, "active"})
159		} else {
160			hint := `not detected — add: eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`
161			if goruntime.GOOS == "windows" {
162				hint = "not detected — add to your PowerShell profile: " +
163					"Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)"
164			}
165			checks = append(checks, check{"shell wrapper", checkWarn, hint})
166		}
167	
168		// Paths.
169		cfgSrc := app.Cfg.Source
170		if cfgSrc == "" {
171			cfgSrc = "built-in defaults (no config.toml)"
172		}
173		checks = append(checks, check{"config", checkOK, cfgSrc})
174		stateStatus, stateDetail := pathCheck(app.Cfg.StateDir())
175		checks = append(checks, check{"state dir", stateStatus, stateDetail})
176	
177		for _, root := range app.Cfg.ScanRoots() {
178			st, detail := pathCheck(root)
179			if st != checkOK {
180				detail = "missing — no repos will be discovered here"
181				st = checkWarn
182			}
183			checks = append(checks, check{"scan root", st, config.Contract(root) + " — " + detail})
184		}
185		for _, path := range app.Cfg.RepoPaths() {
186			st, detail := pathCheck(path)
187			if st != checkOK {
188				detail = "missing — this exact repository will be skipped"
189				st = checkWarn
190			}
191			checks = append(checks, check{"repo path", st, config.Contract(path) + " — " + detail})
192		}
193	
194		wtRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot)
195		sample, err := app.Cfg.WorktreePathFor("example", "/repo/example", "feat/demo", "")
196		if err != nil {
197			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkFail, err.Error()})
198		} else {
199			checks = append(checks, check{"worktree path", checkOK,
200				config.Contract(sample) + fmt.Sprintf("  (root %s, %s)", config.Contract(wtRoot), writableNote(wtRoot))})
201		}
202	
203		// Render.
204		failures := 0
205		style := app.outStyle()
206		for _, c := range checks {
207			if c.status == checkFail {
208				failures++
209			}
210			icon := c.status.icon()
211			detail := c.detail
212			switch c.status {
213			case checkOK:
214				icon = style.success(icon)
215			case checkWarn:
216				icon, detail = style.warning(icon), style.warning(detail)
217			case checkFail:
218				icon, detail = style.danger(icon), style.danger(detail)
219			}
220			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s %s\n", icon, style.label(fmt.Sprintf("%-16s", c.name)), detail)
221		}
222		if failures > 0 {
223			return fmt.Errorf("%d required check(s) failed", failures)
224		}
225		return nil
226	}
227	
228	func pathCheck(p string) (checkStatus, string) {
229		info, err := os.Stat(p)
230		switch {
231		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
232			return checkOK, config.Contract(p)
233		case os.IsNotExist(err):
234			return checkWarn, config.Contract(p) + " (will be created on first use)"
235		case err != nil:
236			return checkFail, err.Error()
237		default:
238			return checkFail, config.Contract(p) + " is not a directory"
239		}
240	}
241	
242	// writableNote reports whether dev could actually create a worktree under the
243	// configured root, walking up to the nearest existing ancestor. A root on an
244	// unmounted volume or a read-only mount is the failure this catches early,
245	// before a `dev wt create` gets halfway through.
246	func writableNote(root string) string {
247		dir := root
248		for {
249			if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
250				if !info.IsDir() {
251					return "not a directory"
252				}
253				if dirWritable(dir) {
254					return "writable"
255				}
256				return "NOT WRITABLE"
257			}
258			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
259			if parent == dir {
260				return "unreachable"
261			}
262			dir = parent
263		}
264	}
265	
266	// dirWritable probes by creating and removing a temp file. There is no
267	// portable stdlib permission check, and the mode bits alone would lie about
268	// read-only mounts and ACLs.
269	func dirWritable(dir string) bool {
270		f, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".dev-write-probe-*")
271		if err != nil {
272			return false
273		}
274		name := f.Name()
275		f.Close()
276		os.Remove(name)
277		return true
278	}

201	// mistake can be answered with that command's usage rather than the root's.
202	func Execute() int {
203		trace, tracePath, traceErr := traceFromEnvironment()
204		app := &App{
205			In: os.Stdin, Out: os.Stdout, Err: os.Stderr,
206			trace: trace, tracePath: tracePath, traceOnce: &sync.Once{},
207		}
208		if traceErr != nil {
209			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: performance trace disabled: %v\n", traceErr)

211		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.CLIExecuteBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
212		defer app.finishTrace()
213	
214		sweepStaleUpgradeArtifacts()
215		finishRoot := app.trace.Start(perftrace.CLIRootBuild, perftrace.Fields{})
216		root := newRootCommand(app)
217		finishRoot(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
218		cmd, err := root.ExecuteC()
219		if err == nil {
220			return 0
221		}
222		style := styleForWriter(os.Stderr, colorModeFromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
223		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, style.danger("dev:")+" "+err.Error())
224		if cmd != nil && wantsUsage(err) {
225			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, renderCobraHelp(cmd.UsageString(), style))
226		}
227		return 1
228	}

153	func (m Model) focusOverlayField(index int) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
154		if m.overlay.fieldCount == 0 {
155			return m, nil
156		}
157		if index < 0 {
158			index = m.overlay.fieldCount - 1
159		}
160		if index >= m.overlay.fieldCount {
161			index = 0
162		}
163		for fieldIndex := 0; fieldIndex < m.overlay.fieldCount; fieldIndex++ {
164			m.overlay.fields[fieldIndex].input.Blur()
165		}
166		m.overlay.fieldIndex = index
167		return m, m.overlay.fields[index].input.Focus()
168	}

170	func (m Model) updateOverlay(message tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
171		switch m.overlay.kind {
172		case overlayHelp:
173			switch message.String() {
174			case "esc", "?", "q":
175				m.overlay = overlayState{}
176			}
177			return m, nil
178	
179		case overlayTryMenu:
180			switch message.String() {
181			case "esc", "q":
182				m.overlay = overlayState{}
183				return m, nil
184			case "j", "down":
185				if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
186					m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
187				}
188				return m, nil
189			case "k", "up":
190				if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
191					m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + m.overlay.optionCount - 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
192				}
193				return m, nil
194			case "enter":
195				if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
196					return m, nil
197				}
198				action := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex]
199				row := m.overlay.target
200				switch action {
201				case TryMark, TryRestore, TryGraduate:
202					return m.openTryForm(action, row)
203				case TryArchive:
204					return m.openTryConfirmation(action, row)
205				case TryDeprecate, TryReactivate:
206					m.overlay = overlayState{}
207					m.status = string(action) + " in progress…"
208					return m, m.applyTry(TryRequest{Action: action, ID: row.Item.ID})
209				}
210			}
211			return m, nil
212	
213		case overlayRepoForm, overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
214			switch message.String() {
215			case "esc":
216				m.overlay = overlayState{}
217				m.err = nil
218				return m, nil
219			case "tab", "down":
220				return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex + 1)
221			case "shift+tab", "up":
222				return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex - 1)
223			case "enter":
224				return m.submitTryOverlay()
225			}
226			index := m.overlay.fieldIndex
227			input, command := m.overlay.fields[index].input.Update(message)
228			m.overlay.fields[index].input = input

234	func (m Model) submitTryOverlay() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
235		value := func(key string) string {

248			m.err = nil

251		}
252	
253		request := TryRequest{Action: m.overlay.action, ID: m.overlay.target.Item.ID}
254		switch m.overlay.action {
255		case TryCreate:
256			request.Name, request.Clone = value("name"), value("clone")
257			if request.Name == "" && request.Clone == "" {
258				m.err = fmt.Errorf("a new Try needs a name or clone reference")

262			if !ok {

264				return m, nil
265			}
266			request.NoGit = !gitInit
267		case TryMark:
268			request.Tags = splitTagInput(value("tags"))
269			request.Note = value("note")
270		case TryRestore:
271			request.To = value("to")
272		case TryGraduate:
273			request.Category, request.Name = value("category"), value("name")
274		case TryArchive:

277				return m, nil
278			}
279		default:

281			return m, nil
282		}
283		m.overlay = overlayState{}
284		m.err = nil
285		m.status = string(request.Action) + " in progress…"
286		return m, m.applyTry(request)
287	}
