53			return false
54		}
55		if value.Kind() == reflect.Interface || value.Kind() == reflect.Pointer {
56			if value.IsNil() {
57				return false
58			}
59			return reflectContainsControl(value.Elem())
60		}
61		switch value.Kind() {
62		case reflect.String:
63			return stringContainsControl(value.String())
64		case reflect.Map:
65			iter := value.MapRange()
66			for iter.Next() {
67				if reflectContainsControl(iter.Key()) || reflectContainsControl(iter.Value()) {
68					return true
69				}
70			}
71		case reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:
72			for index := range value.Len() {
73				if reflectContainsControl(value.Index(index)) {
74					return true
75				}
76			}
77		case reflect.Struct:
78			for index := range value.NumField() {
79				if reflectContainsControl(value.Field(index)) {
80					return true
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		return false
85	}
86	
87	func stringContainsControl(value string) bool {
88		for _, r := range value {
89			if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf) {
90				return true
91			}
92		}
93		return false
94	}
95	
96	func normalizedName(value string) (string, bool) {
97		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) || len(value) > maximumNameBytes ||
98			!utf8.ValidString(value) || stringContainsControl(value) || looksSecretString(value) {
99			return "", false
100		}
101		return value, true
102	}
103	
104	func normalizedPlugin(value string) (string, bool) {
105		return normalizedName(value)
106	}
107	
108	func looksSecretString(value string) bool {
109		lower := strings.ToLower(value)
110		if strings.Contains(lower, "sentinel") && (strings.Contains(lower, "secret") || strings.Contains(lower, "token") || strings.Contains(lower, "password")) {
111			return true
112		}
113		if (strings.HasPrefix(lower, "sk-") || strings.HasPrefix(lower, "ghp_") || strings.HasPrefix(lower, "github_pat_")) && len(value) >= 16 {
114			return true
115		}
116		if len(value) >= 64 {
117			letters := 0
118			for _, r := range value {
119				if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r) || strings.ContainsRune("_-/+=", r) {
120					letters++
121				}
122			}
123			if letters == len([]rune(value)) {
124				return true
125			}
126		}
127		return false
128	}
129	
130	func newDeclaration(spec sourceSpec, rawName string) (Declaration, bool) {
131		name, ok := normalizedName(rawName)
132		if !ok {
133			return Declaration{}, false
134		}
135		return Declaration{
136			Name: name, Agent: spec.agent, Scope: spec.scope,
137			Repository: spec.repository, RepositoryPath: spec.repositoryPath, Checkout: spec.checkout,
138			ConfigPath: spec.path, Source: spec.source, Transport: TransportUnknown,
139		}, true
140	}
141	
142	func inspectArguments(row *Declaration, arguments []string) {
143		row.ArgumentCount = len(arguments)
144		if len(arguments) == 0 {
145			return
146		}
147		addRedaction(row, RedactionArguments)
148		for _, argument := range arguments {
149			inspectReferences(row, argument)
150			if openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(argument) {
151				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialFile})
152				addRedaction(row, RedactionFileReference)
153			}
154		}
155	}
156	
157	func inspectEnvironment(row *Declaration, environment map[string]string) {
158		if len(environment) == 0 {
159			return
160		}
161		addRedaction(row, RedactionEnvironmentValue)
162		for name, value := range environment {
163			if validEnvironmentName(name) {
164				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialEnvironment, Name: name})
165			} else {
166				addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
167			}
168			inspectReferences(row, value)
169			inspectFileReference(row, value)
170		}
171	}
172	
173	func inspectHeaders(row *Declaration, headers map[string]string) {
174		if len(headers) == 0 {
175			return
176		}
177		addRedaction(row, RedactionHeaderValue)
178		for name, value := range headers {
179			if validHeaderName(name) {
180				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialHeader, Name: strings.ToLower(name)})
181			} else {
182				addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
183			}
184			inspectReferences(row, value)
185			inspectFileReference(row, value)
186		}
187	}
188	
189	func inspectBearerEnvironment(row *Declaration, name string) {
190		if strings.TrimSpace(name) == "" {
191			return
192		}
193		if validEnvironmentName(name) {
194			addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialBearerEnvironment, Name: name})
195		} else {
196			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
197		}
198	}
199	
200	func inspectEnvironmentHeaders(row *Declaration, headers map[string]string) {
201		for header, environment := range headers {
202			if validHeaderName(header) {
203				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialHeader, Name: strings.ToLower(header)})
204			} else {
205				addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
206			}
207			if validEnvironmentName(environment) {
208				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialEnvironmentReference, Name: environment})
209			} else {
210				addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
211			}
212		}
213	}
214	
215	func inspectOAuthValue(row *Declaration, field, value string) {
216		if value == "" {
217			return
218		}
219		addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialOAuth, Name: field})
220		addRedaction(row, RedactionOAuthValue)
221		inspectReferences(row, value)
222		inspectFileReference(row, value)
223	}
224	
225	func inspectHelper(row *Declaration, configured bool) {
226		if !configured {
227			return
228		}
229		addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialHelper})
230		addRedaction(row, RedactionHelperCommand)
231	}
232	
233	func inspectFileReference(row *Declaration, value string) {
234		if !openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(value) {
235			return
236		}
237		addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialFile})
238		addRedaction(row, RedactionFileReference)
239	}
240	
241	func inspectReferences(row *Declaration, value string) {
242		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
243		patterns := []*regexp.Regexp{wholeOpenCodeEnvPattern}
244		for _, pattern := range patterns {
245			match := pattern.FindStringSubmatch(value)
246			if len(match) == 2 {
247				addCredential(row, CredentialReference{Kind: CredentialEnvironmentReference, Name: match[1]})
248				return
249			}
250		}
251	}
252	
253	func validEnvironmentName(value string) bool {
254		return len(value) <= maximumReferenceBytes && environmentNamePattern.MatchString(value) && !looksSecretString(value)
255	}
256	
257	func validHeaderName(value string) bool {
258		return len(value) <= maximumReferenceBytes && headerNamePattern.MatchString(value) && !looksSecretString(value)
259	}
260	
261	func setCommand(row *Declaration, command string) {
262		command = strings.TrimSpace(command)
263		if command == "" {
264			return
265		}
266		inspectReferences(row, command)
267		if openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(command) {
268			inspectFileReference(row, command)
269			row.Command = "[dynamic]"
270			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
271			return
272		}
273		if strings.Contains(command, "${") || strings.Contains(command, "{env:") ||
274			dollarPattern.MatchString(command) || percentPattern.MatchString(command) {
275			row.Command = "[dynamic]"
276			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
277			return
278		}
279		normalized := strings.ReplaceAll(command, `\`, "/")
280		basename := path.Base(normalized)
281		if basename == "." || basename == "/" || basename == "" || len(basename) > maximumNameBytes ||
282			!executableNamePattern.MatchString(basename) || strings.ContainsFunc(command, unicode.IsSpace) ||
283			looksSecretString(basename) {
284			row.Command = "[redacted]"
285			addRedaction(row, RedactionDynamicCommand)
286			addRedaction(row, RedactionArguments)
287			return
288		}
289		row.Command = basename
290		if basename != command {
291			addRedaction(row, RedactionCommandPath)
292		}
293	}
294	
295	func setEndpoint(row *Declaration, raw string) {
296		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
297		if raw == "" {
298			return
299		}
300		inspectReferences(row, raw)
301		if openCodeFilePattern.MatchString(raw) {
302			inspectFileReference(row, raw)
303			addRedaction(row, RedactionEndpointTemplate)
304			row.Endpoint = "[dynamic]"
305			return
306		}
307		if dollarBracePattern.MatchString(raw) || dollarPattern.MatchString(raw) || percentPattern.MatchString(raw) || openCodeEnvPattern.MatchString(raw) {
308			addRedaction(row, RedactionEndpointTemplate)
309			row.Endpoint = "[dynamic]"
310			return
311		}
312		parsed, err := url.Parse(raw)
313		if err != nil || parsed.Opaque != "" || parsed.Scheme == "" || parsed.Host == "" || !schemePattern.MatchString(parsed.Scheme) || stringContainsControl(parsed.Host) || looksSecretString(parsed.Host) {
314			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidEndpoint)
315			return
316		}
317		if parsed.User != nil {
318			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLUserinfo)
319		}
320		if parsed.RawQuery != "" || parsed.ForceQuery {
321			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLQuery)
322		}
323		if parsed.Fragment != "" {
324			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLFragment)
325		}
326		endpoint := strings.ToLower(parsed.Scheme) + "://" + strings.ToLower(parsed.Host)
327		if parsed.EscapedPath() != "" && parsed.EscapedPath() != "/" {
328			endpoint += "/[path]"
329			addRedaction(row, RedactionURLPath)
330		} else if parsed.EscapedPath() == "/" {
331			endpoint += "/"
332		}
333		row.Endpoint = endpoint
334	}
335	
336	func addCredential(row *Declaration, credential CredentialReference) {
337		if credential.Name != "" && (!utf8.ValidString(credential.Name) || stringContainsControl(credential.Name) || len(credential.Name) > maximumReferenceBytes) {
338			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticInvalidReference)
339			return
340		}
341		for _, existing := range row.Credentials {
342			if existing == credential {
343				return
344			}
345		}
346		row.Credentials = append(row.Credentials, credential)
347	}
348	
349	func addRedaction(row *Declaration, redaction Redaction) {
350		for _, existing := range row.Redactions {
351			if existing == redaction {
352				return
353			}
354		}
355		row.Redactions = append(row.Redactions, redaction)
356	}
357	
358	func addCoverage(row *Declaration, code DiagnosticCode) {
359		for _, existing := range row.Coverage {
360			if existing.Code == code {
361				return
362			}
363		}
364		row.Coverage = append(row.Coverage, coverage(code))
365	}
366	
367	func addPolicy(row *Declaration, kind PolicyKind, value string, count int) {
368		fact := PolicyFact{Kind: kind, Value: value, Count: count}
369		for _, existing := range row.Policies {
370			if existing == fact {
371				return
372			}
373		}
374		row.Policies = append(row.Policies, fact)
375	}
376	
377	func addBooleanPolicy(row *Declaration, kind PolicyKind, value bool) {
378		addPolicy(row, kind, strconv.FormatBool(value), 0)
379	}
380	
381	func finalizeDeclaration(row *Declaration) {
382		sort.Slice(row.Credentials, func(i, j int) bool {
383			if row.Credentials[i].Kind != row.Credentials[j].Kind {
384				return row.Credentials[i].Kind < row.Credentials[j].Kind
385			}
386			return row.Credentials[i].Name < row.Credentials[j].Name
387		})
388		sort.Slice(row.Redactions, func(i, j int) bool { return row.Redactions[i] < row.Redactions[j] })
389		sort.Slice(row.Policies, func(i, j int) bool {
390			if row.Policies[i].Kind != row.Policies[j].Kind {
391				return row.Policies[i].Kind < row.Policies[j].Kind
392			}
393			if row.Policies[i].Value != row.Policies[j].Value {
394				return row.Policies[i].Value < row.Policies[j].Value
395			}
396			return row.Policies[i].Count < row.Policies[j].Count
397		})
398		sort.Slice(row.Coverage, func(i, j int) bool { return row.Coverage[i].Code < row.Coverage[j].Code })
399	}
400

```text
1	# MCP declarations
2	
3	Inspect static MCP server declarations across repositories and supported agent
4	configuration formats without starting servers or contacting endpoints.
5	
6	```bash
7	dev mcp list
8	dev mcp list --repo api
9	dev mcp list --all
10	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project --json
11	```
12	
13	The initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
14	Project, local, user, custom, system, and managed declarations remain separate
15	rows. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` describe fields present in source
16	configuration; they are not connectivity or authentication health.
17	
18	The scanner never executes agent MCP list/debug commands, configured commands,
19	header helpers, servers, or URLs. It does not expand environment placeholders,
20	read OAuth/token stores, or dereference OpenCode `{file:…}` values. Normalized
21	output retains only safe facts such as the command basename, credential reference
22	names, argument count, and a URL scheme/host with userinfo, path, query, and
23	fragment redacted.
24	
25	Static inventory cannot reproduce every runtime layer. Plugin caches, hosted
26	connectors, remote organization configuration, inline
27	`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted and reported
28	as coverage limits. Duplicate names in different files/scopes are not merged
29	into a guessed effective configuration.
30	
31	The MCP TUI view reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot, includes the exact startup
32	linked worktree when distinct, and offers navigation, filtering, and reload only.
33	It never starts, connects, adds, removes, or authenticates a server. Filters
34	include `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, and `state:`.
35
```

14	func newMCPCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

17			Short: "Inspect static agent MCP server declarations",
18			Long: `Inventory MCP declarations without starting servers or contacting endpoints.
19	
20	MCP rows are static, scope-qualified configuration declarations. They do not
21	claim that a declaration is the effective merged config, connected, healthy, or
22	authenticated. Secret-bearing values are redacted before rows are returned.`,
23		}
24		cmd.AddCommand(newMCPListCmd(app))
25		return cmd

28	func newMCPListCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
29		var (
30			all     bool
31			repoRef string
32			agents  []string
33			scopes  []string
34			jsonOut bool
35		)

37			Use:   "list",
38			Short: "List configured MCP server declarations",

41				if all && repoRef != "" {
42					return fmt.Errorf("choose at most one of --all or --repo")
43				}
44				agentFilter, err := parseMCPAgents(agents)
45				if err != nil {

47				}

51				}

91	func parseMCPAgents(values []string) (map[agentmcp.Agent]bool, error) {
92		allowed := map[string]agentmcp.Agent{
93			"claude-code": agentmcp.AgentClaudeCode,
94			"codex":       agentmcp.AgentCodex,
95			"cursor":      agentmcp.AgentCursor,
96			"gemini-cli":  agentmcp.AgentGeminiCLI,
97			"opencode":    agentmcp.AgentOpenCode,
98		}
99		result := map[agentmcp.Agent]bool{}
100		for _, value := range values {
101			value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
102			agent, ok := allowed[value]
103			if !ok {
104				return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported MCP agent %q", value)
105			}
106			result[agent] = true
107		}
108		return result, nil
109	}
110	
111	func parseMCPScopes(values []string) (map[agentmcp.Scope]bool, error) {
112		allowed := map[string]agentmcp.Scope{
113			"project":         agentmcp.ScopeProject,
114			"local":           agentmcp.ScopeLocal,
115			"user":            agentmcp.ScopeUser,
116			"custom":          agentmcp.ScopeCustom,
117			"system-defaults": agentmcp.ScopeSystemDefaults,
118			"system-override": agentmcp.ScopeSystemOverride,
119			"managed":         agentmcp.ScopeManaged,
120		}
121		result := map[agentmcp.Scope]bool{}
122		for _, value := range values {
123			value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
124			scope, ok := allowed[value]
125			if !ok {
126				return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported MCP scope %q", value)
127			}
128			result[scope] = true
129		}
130		return result, nil
131	}

133	func filterMCPDeclarations(rows []agentmcp.Declaration, agents map[agentmcp.Agent]bool, scopes map[agentmcp.Scope]bool) []agentmcp.Declaration {
134		filtered := make([]agentmcp.Declaration, 0, len(rows))
135		for _, row := range rows {
136			if len(agents) > 0 && !agents[row.Agent] || len(scopes) > 0 && !scopes[row.Scope] {
137				continue
138			}
139			filtered = append(filtered, row)
140		}
141		return filtered
142	}
143	
144	func filterMCPDiagnostics(rows []agentmcp.Diagnostic, agents map[agentmcp.Agent]bool, scopes map[agentmcp.Scope]bool) []agentmcp.Diagnostic {
145		filtered := make([]agentmcp.Diagnostic, 0, len(rows))
146		for _, row := range rows {
147			if len(agents) > 0 && !agents[row.Agent] || len(scopes) > 0 && !scopes[row.Scope] {
148				continue
149			}
150			filtered = append(filtered, row)
151		}
152		return filtered
153	}

155	func renderMCPTable(app *App, rows []agentmcp.Declaration) error {
156		if len(rows) == 0 {
157			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No MCP server declarations found.")
158			return nil
159		}
160		table := app.newTable("REPO", "SCOPE", "AGENT", "SERVER", "TRANSPORT", "STATE", "SOURCE", "TARGET", "CONFIG")
161		for _, row := range rows {
162			source := string(row.Source)
163			if row.Plugin != "" {
164				source += ":" + row.Plugin
165			}
166			target := row.Endpoint
167			if target == "" {
168				target = row.Command
169			}
170			table.Add(dash(row.Repository), string(row.Scope), string(row.Agent), row.Name,
171				string(row.Transport), mcpDeclaredState(row), source, dash(target), config.Contract(row.ConfigPath))
172		}
173		table.Render(app.Out)
174		return nil
175	}
176	
177	func renderMCPDiagnostics(app *App, diagnostics []agentmcp.Diagnostic) {
178		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
179			owner := string(diagnostic.Agent) + "/" + string(diagnostic.Scope)
180			if diagnostic.Repository != "" {
181				owner = diagnostic.Repository + "/" + owner
182			}
183			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "warning: MCP inventory %s (%s): %s\n",
184				owner, config.Contract(diagnostic.ConfigPath), diagnostic.Message)
185		}
186	}

188	func mcpDeclaredState(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {
189		if row.Enabled == nil {
190			return "configured"
191		}
192		if *row.Enabled {
193			return "enabled"
194		}
195		return "disabled"
196	}

Review target: `-- Review ONLY the named TUI/CLI lifecycle candidates in the current working tree; no edits, no comments. Require current observable defects with file:line and reproducer.`

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

210		target, err := agenttarget.Current(ctx, cwd)

212			return Result{}, err
213		}
214		return Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, options)

220		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
221			return Result{}, err
222		}
223		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
224		if !project && !global {
225			project, global = true, true
226		}

228		result := Result{RegistrySource: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion}
229		definitions := Registry()
230		if project {
231			for _, target := range agenttarget.Dedupe(targets) {
232				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
233					return result, err
234				}
235				rows, diagnostics := scanProjectScope(ctx, target, definitions)
236				result.Skills = append(result.Skills, rows...)
237				result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
238				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
239					return result, err
240				}
241			}
242		}
243		if global {
244			rows, diagnostics := scanGlobalScope(ctx, definitions)
245			result.Skills = append(result.Skills, rows...)
246			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
247			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
248				return result, err
249			}
250		}
251	
252		sortSkills(result.Skills)
253		sortDiagnostics(result.Diagnostics)
254		if options.Check {
255			result.Skills = CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
256			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
257				return result, err
258			}
259		}
260		return result, nil
261	}

283	func reservedSkillNameKey(value string) string {
284		value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
285		var builder strings.Builder
286		lastDash := false
287		for _, character := range value {
288			if character >= 'a' && character <= 'z' || character >= '0' && character <= '9' {
289				builder.WriteRune(character)
290				lastDash = false
291			} else if !lastDash {
292				builder.WriteByte('-')
293				lastDash = true
294			}
295		}
296		return strings.Trim(builder.String(), "-")
297	}

342	// FindProject returns one installed project-scoped skill by exact or normalized
343	// name. An exact name wins when normalized filesystem names collide.
344	func FindProject(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, name string) (Skill, error) {
345		rows, err := List(ctx, projectRoot, ListOptions{Project: true})
346		if err != nil {
347			return Skill{}, err
348		}
349		for _, row := range rows {
350			if row.Scope == ScopeProject && row.Presence == PresencePresent && row.Name == name {
351				return row, nil
352			}
353		}
354		want := normalizedName(name)
355		var matches []Skill
356		for _, row := range rows {
357			if row.Scope == ScopeProject && row.Presence == PresencePresent && normalizedName(row.Name) == want {
358				matches = append(matches, row)
359			}
360		}
361		if len(matches) == 1 {
362			return matches[0], nil
363		}
364		return Skill{}, fmt.Errorf("project skill %q is not installed", name)
365	}
366	
367	// MergeResults combines independently scanned targets while restoring the
368	// domain's deterministic ordering and registry metadata.
369	func MergeResults(results ...Result) Result {
370		merged := Result{RegistrySource: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion}
371		for _, result := range results {
372			merged.Skills = append(merged.Skills, result.Skills...)
373			merged.Diagnostics = append(merged.Diagnostics, result.Diagnostics...)
374			if result.RegistrySource != "" {
375				merged.RegistrySource = result.RegistrySource
376			}
377			if result.RegistryVersion != "" {
378				merged.RegistryVersion = result.RegistryVersion
379			}
380		}
381		sortSkills(merged.Skills)
382		sortDiagnostics(merged.Diagnostics)
383		return merged
384	}
385	
386	func sortSkills(rows []Skill) {
387		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
388			left, right := rows[i], rows[j]
389			if left.Scope != right.Scope {
390				return left.Scope == ScopeProject
391			}
392			if left.Repository != right.Repository {
393				return left.Repository < right.Repository
394			}
395			if left.Checkout != right.Checkout {
396				return left.Checkout < right.Checkout
397			}
398			leftName, rightName := strings.ToLower(left.Name), strings.ToLower(right.Name)
399			if leftName != rightName {
400				return leftName < rightName
401			}
402			if left.Name != right.Name {
403				return left.Name < right.Name
404			}
405			return left.Path < right.Path
406		})
407	}
408	
409	func sortDiagnostics(diagnostics []Diagnostic) {
410		sort.SliceStable(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool {
411			left, right := diagnostics[i], diagnostics[j]
412			if left.Repository != right.Repository {
413				return left.Repository < right.Repository
414			}
415			if left.Checkout != right.Checkout {
416				return left.Checkout < right.Checkout
417			}
418			if left.Scope != right.Scope {
419				return left.Scope < right.Scope
420			}
421			if left.Path != right.Path {
422				return left.Path < right.Path
423			}
424			if left.Name != right.Name {
425				return left.Name < right.Name
426			}
427			if left.Kind != right.Kind {
428				return left.Kind < right.Kind
429			}
430			return left.Message < right.Message
431		})
432	}
433	
434	func safeDisplayValue(value string) bool {
435		if value == "" || !utf8.ValidString(value) {
436			return false
437		}
438		return !strings.ContainsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
439			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf)
440		})
441	}
442	
443	func uniqueSorted(values []string) []string {
444		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
445		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
446		for _, value := range values {
447			if value == "" {
448				continue
449			}
450			if _, ok := seen[value]; ok {
451				continue
452			}
453			seen[value] = struct{}{}
454			out = append(out, value)
455		}
456		sort.Strings(out)
457		return out
458	}
459	
460	func homeDirectory() string {
461		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
462		if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(home) {
463			return ""
464		}
465		return home
466	}

461	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
462	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
463	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
464		var b strings.Builder
465		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
466		if flags := renderFlagSet(root.PersistentFlags()); flags != "" {
467			b.WriteString("### Global options\n\n")
468			b.WriteString(flags)
469			b.WriteString("\n")
470		}
471		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
472		return b.String()
473	}
474	
475	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
476		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" {
477			return
478		}
479		if depth > 0 {
480			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
481			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
482				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
483			}
484			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
485				b.WriteString(flags)
486				b.WriteString("\n")
487			}
488		}
489		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
490			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
491		}
492	}
493	
494	func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
495		return renderFlagSet(c.LocalNonPersistentFlags())
496	}
497	
498	func renderFlagSet(flags *pflag.FlagSet) string {
499		var b strings.Builder
500		flags.VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
501			if f.Hidden {
502				return
503			}
504			name := "--" + f.Name
505			if f.Shorthand != "" {
506				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
507			}
508			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
509		})
510		return b.String()
511	}
512	
513	func firstLine(s string) string {
514		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
515			return s[:i]
516		}
517		return s
518	}

Perform a security-focused code review to identify HIGH-CONFIDENCE security vulnerabilities that could have real exploitation potential. This is not a general code review - focus ONLY on security implications newly added by this PR. Do not comment on existing security concerns.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
1. MINIMIZE FALSE POSITIVES: Only flag issues where you're >80% confident of actual exploitability
2. AVOID NOISE: Skip theoretical issues, style concerns, or low-impact findings
3. FOCUS ON IMPACT: Prioritize vulnerabilities that could lead to unauthorized access, data breaches, or system compromise
4. EXCLUSIONS: Do NOT report the following issue types:
   - Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities, even if they allow service disruption
   - Secrets or sensitive data stored on disk (these are handled by other processes)
   - Rate limiting or resource exhaustion issues

SECURITY CATEGORIES TO EXAMINE:

**Input Validation Vulnerabilities:**
- SQL injection via unsanitized user input
- Command injection in system calls or subprocesses
- XXE injection in XML parsing
- Template injection in templating engines
- NoSQL injection in database queries
- Path traversal in file operations

**Authentication & Authorization Issues:**
- Authentication bypass logic
- Privilege escalation paths
- Session management flaws
- JWT token vulnerabilities
- Authorization logic bypasses

**Crypto & Secrets Management:**
- Hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens
- Weak cryptographic algorithms or implementations
- Improper key storage or management
- Cryptographic randomness issues
- Certificate validation bypasses

**Injection & Code Execution:**
- Remote code execution via deseralization
- Pickle injection in Python
- YAML deserialization vulnerabilities
- Eval injection in dynamic code execution
- XSS vulnerabilities in web applications (reflected, stored, DOM-based)

**Data Exposure:**
- Sensitive data logging or storage
- PII handling violations
- API endpoint data leakage
- Debug information exposure

Additional notes:
- Even if something is only exploitable from the local network, it can still be a HIGH severity issue

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY:

Phase 1 - Repository Context Research (Use file search tools):
- Identify existing security frameworks and libraries in use
- Look for established secure coding patterns in the codebase
- Examine existing sanitization and validation patterns
- Understand the project's security model and threat model

Phase 2 - Comparative Analysis:
- Compare new code changes against existing security patterns
- Identify deviations from established secure practices
- Look for inconsistent security implementations
- Flag code that introduces new attack surfaces

Phase 3 - Vulnerability Assessment:
- Examine each modified file for security implications
- Trace data flow from user inputs to sensitive operations
- Look for privilege boundaries being crossed unsafely
- Identify injection points and unsafe deserialization

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT:

You MUST output your findings in markdown. The markdown output should contain the file, line number, severity, category (e.g. `sql_injection` or `xss`), description, exploit scenario, and fix recommendation.

For example:

# Vuln 1: XSS: `foo.py:42`

* Severity: High
* Description: User input from `username` parameter is directly interpolated into HTML without escaping, allowing reflected XSS attacks
* Exploit Scenario: Attacker crafts URL like /bar?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute JavaScript in victim's browser, enabling session hijacking or data theft
* Recommendation: Use Flask's escape() function or Jinja2 templates with auto-escaping enabled for all user inputs rendered in HTML

SEVERITY GUIDELINES:
- **HIGH**: Directly exploitable vulnerabilities leading to RCE, data breach, or authentication bypass
- **MEDIUM**: Vulnerabilities requiring specific conditions but with significant impact
- **LOW**: Defense-in-depth issues or lower-impact vulnerabilities

CONFIDENCE SCORING:
- 0.9-1.0: Certain exploit path identified, tested if possible
- 0.8-0.9: Clear vulnerability pattern with known exploitation methods
- 0.7-0.8: Suspicious pattern requiring specific conditions to exploit
- Below 0.7: Don't report (too speculative)

FINAL REMINDER:
Focus on HIGH and MEDIUM findings only. Better to miss some theoretical issues than flood the report with false positives. Each finding should be something a security engineer would confidently raise in a PR review.

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING:

> You do not need to run commands to reproduce the vulnerability, just read the code to determine if it is a real vulnerability. Do not use the bash tool or write to any files.
>
> HARD EXCLUSIONS - Automatically exclude findings matching these patterns:
> 1. Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion attacks.
> 2. Secrets or credentials stored on disk if they are otherwise secured.
> 3. Rate limiting concerns or service overload scenarios.
> 4. Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.
> 5. Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields without proven security impact.
> 6. Input sanitization concerns for GitHub Action workflows unless they are clearly triggerable via untrusted input.
> 7. A lack of hardening measures. Code is not expected to implement all security best practices, only flag concrete vulnerabilities.
> 8. Race conditions or timing attacks that are theoretical rather than practical issues. Only report a race condition if it is concretely problematic.
> 9. Vulnerabilities related to outdated third-party libraries. These are managed separately and should not be reported here.
> 10. Memory safety issues such as buffer overflows or use-after-free-vulnerabilities are impossible in rust. Do not report memory safety issues in rust or any other memory safe languages.
> 11. Files that are only unit tests or only used as part of running tests.
> 12. Log spoofing concerns. Outputting un-sanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability.
> 13. SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF is only a concern if it can control the host or protocol.
> 14. Including user-controlled content in AI system prompts is not a vulnerability.
> 15. Regex injection. Injecting untrusted content into a regex is not a vulnerability.
> 16. Regex DOS concerns.
> 16. Insecure documentation. Do not report any findings in documentation files such as markdown files.
> 17. A lack of audit logs is not a vulnerability.
>
> PRECEDENTS -
> 1. Logging high value secrets in plaintext is a vulnerability. Logging URLs is assumed to be safe.
> 2. UUIDs can be assumed to be unguessable and do not need to be validated.
> 3. Environment variables and CLI flags are trusted values. Attackers are generally not able to modify them in a secure environment. Any attack that relies on controlling an environment variable is invalid.
> 4. Resource management issues such as memory or file descriptor leaks are not valid.
> 5. Subtle or low impact web vulnerabilities such as tabnabbing, XS-Leaks, prototype pollution, and open redirects should not be reported unless they are extremely high confidence.
> 6. React and Angular are generally secure against XSS. These frameworks do not need to sanitize or escape user input unless it is using dangerouslySetInnerHTML, bypassSecurityTrustHtml, or similar methods. Do not report XSS vulnerabilities in React or Angular components or tsx files unless they are using unsafe methods.
> 7. Most vulnerabilities in github action workflows are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a github action workflow vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path.
> 8. A lack of permission checking or authentication in client-side JS/TS code is not a vulnerability. Client-side code is not trusted and does not need to implement these checks, they are handled on the server-side. The same applies to all flows that send untrusted data to the backend, the backend is responsible for validating and sanitizing all inputs.
> 9. Only include MEDIUM findings if they are obvious and concrete issues.
> 10. Most vulnerabilities in ipython notebooks (*.ipynb files) are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a notebook vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path where untrusted input can trigger the vulnerability.
> 11. Logging non-PII data is not a vulnerability even if the data may be sensitive. Only report logging vulnerabilities if they expose sensitive information such as secrets, passwords, or personally identifiable information (PII).
> 12. Command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts are generally not exploitable in practice since shell scripts generally do not run with untrusted user input. Only report command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts if they are concrete and have a very specific attack path for untrusted input.
>
> SIGNAL QUALITY CRITERIA - For remaining findings, assess:
> 1. Is there a concrete, exploitable vulnerability with a clear attack path?

> - 4-6: Medium confidence, needs investigation
> - 7-10: High confidence, likely true vulnerability

91	func parseMCPAgents(values []string) (map[agentmcp.Agent]bool, error) {

95			"cursor":      agentmcp.AgentCursor,

97			"opencode":    agentmcp.AgentOpenCode,
98		}
99		result := map[agentmcp.Agent]bool{}
100		for _, value := range values {
101			value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
102			agent, ok := allowed[value]
103			if !ok {
104				return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported MCP agent %q", value)
105			}
106			result[agent] = true
107		}
108		return result, nil
109	}

115			"user":            agentmcp.ScopeUser,
116			"custom":          agentmcp.ScopeCustom,
117			"system-defaults": agentmcp.ScopeSystemDefaults,
118			"system-override": agentmcp.ScopeSystemOverride,
119			"managed":         agentmcp.ScopeManaged,
120		}
121		result := map[agentmcp.Scope]bool{}
122		for _, value := range values {
123			value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
124			scope, ok := allowed[value]

127			}
128			result[scope] = true
129		}
130		return result, nil
131	}

134		filtered := make([]agentmcp.Declaration, 0, len(rows))

155	func renderMCPTable(app *App, rows []agentmcp.Declaration) error {
156		if len(rows) == 0 {
157			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No MCP server declarations found.")
158			return nil
159		}
160		table := app.newTable("REPO", "SCOPE", "AGENT", "SERVER", "TRANSPORT", "STATE", "SOURCE", "TARGET", "CONFIG")
161		for _, row := range rows {
162			source := string(row.Source)
163			if row.Plugin != "" {
164				source += ":" + row.Plugin
165			}
166			target := row.Endpoint
167			if target == "" {
168				target = row.Command
169			}
170			table.Add(dash(row.Repository), string(row.Scope), string(row.Agent), row.Name,
171				string(row.Transport), mcpDeclaredState(row), source, dash(target), config.Contract(row.ConfigPath))
172		}
173		table.Render(app.Out)
174		return nil
175	}

177	func renderMCPDiagnostics(app *App, diagnostics []agentmcp.Diagnostic) {
178		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
179			owner := string(diagnostic.Agent) + "/" + string(diagnostic.Scope)
180			if diagnostic.Repository != "" {
181				owner = diagnostic.Repository + "/" + owner
182			}
183			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "warning: MCP inventory %s (%s): %s\n",
184				owner, config.Contract(diagnostic.ConfigPath), diagnostic.Message)
185		}
186	}

190			return "configured"
191		}
192		if *row.Enabled {
193			return "enabled"
194		}
195		return "disabled"

```text
1	# MCP declarations
2	
3	Inspect static MCP server declarations across repositories and supported agent
4	configuration formats without starting servers or contacting endpoints.
5	
6	```bash
7	dev mcp list
8	dev mcp list --repo api
9	dev mcp list --all
10	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project --json
11	```
12	
13	The initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
14	Project, local, user, custom, system, and managed declarations remain separate
15	rows. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` describe fields present in source
16	configuration; they are not connectivity or authentication health.
17	
18	The scanner never executes agent MCP list/debug commands, configured commands,
19	header helpers, servers, or URLs. It does not expand environment placeholders,
20	read OAuth/token stores, or dereference OpenCode `{file:…}` values. Normalized
21	output retains only safe facts such as the command basename, credential reference
22	names, argument count, and a URL scheme/host with userinfo, path, query, and
23	fragment redacted.
24	
25	Static inventory cannot reproduce every runtime layer. Plugin caches, hosted
26	connectors, remote organization configuration, inline
27	`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted and reported
28	as coverage limits. Duplicate names in different files/scopes are not merged
29	into a guessed effective configuration.
30	
31	The MCP TUI view reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot, includes the exact startup
32	linked worktree when distinct, and offers navigation, filtering, and reload only.
33	It never starts, connects, adds, removes, or authenticates a server. Filters
34	include `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, and `state:`.
35
```

1	# Agent skill and MCP inventory
2	
3	Use these inventories to answer two different questions:
4	
5	- `dev skill list`: which reusable instruction packages are present, and whether
6	  an explicit upstream source check reports newer lock-recorded content.
7	- `dev mcp list`: which external MCP capabilities are declared in supported
8	  static agent configuration files.
9	
10	Do not treat an MCP declaration as a skill, a live connection, or permission to
11	invoke tools.
12	
13	## Skill inventory
14	
15	```bash
16	dev skill list
17	dev skill list --repo <repo-or-checkout> --project
18	dev skill list --all
19	dev skill list --all --check --json
20	```
21	
22	Reads use a versioned snapshot of all 77 agent paths from `skills@1.5.23` plus
23	project/global locks. They never execute `skills`, Node, npm, `npx`, agent
24	detectors, or project code. `--all` scans canonical repositories; the TUI also
25	adds its startup linked checkout when distinct and scans global paths once.
26	
27	Keep status dimensions separate:
28	
29	- presence: local directory present or lock-only/missing;
30	- integrity: only embedded `dev-cli` files can be verified against the binary; additional user files are ignored;
31	- update: lock-recorded upstream content is unchecked/current/changed/missing or
32	  unverifiable.
33	
34	`--check` is the explicit network action. It groups equal Git source/ref pairs
35	and does not write installed skills or locks. `skill add` and `skill update` are
36	explicit mutations and require a directly installed `skills` executable; `dev`
37	never resolves a provider through repository-local npm bins.
38	
39	## MCP inventory
40	
41	```bash
42	dev mcp list
43	dev mcp list --repo <repo-or-checkout>
44	dev mcp list --all --json
45	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project
46	```
47	
48	Adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Rows remain
49	scope-qualified declarations; `dev` does not guess effective precedence across
50	files. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` are declaration facts, not health.
51	
52	The scanner never runs agent MCP commands, configured commands/helpers, servers,
53	or URLs. It never expands environment variables, reads OAuth/token stores, or
54	loads OpenCode `{file:…}` content. Normalized output retains only safe command
55	basenames, endpoint scheme/host, argument counts, credential reference names,
56	policy counts, and redaction markers.
57	
58	Omitted sources include plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization
59	configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs.
60	Treat the coverage metadata as part of the result.
61
```

2	// configuration inventories. It deliberately contains no skill, MCP, or UI
3	// policy so those domains can share one definition of a target.
4	package agenttarget
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"

15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"

17	)
18	
19	// Target identifies one concrete checkout of one repository. RepoPath is the
20	// repository's main navigation path (which may be a configured symlink alias),
21	// while CheckoutRoot is the exact worktree to inspect. Linked worktrees share
22	// RepoPath and CommonDir but remain distinct targets through CheckoutRoot.
23	type Target struct {
24		RepoName     string `json:"repo_name"`
25		RepoDisplay  string `json:"repo_display"`
26		RepoPath     string `json:"repo_path"`
27		CheckoutRoot string `json:"checkout_root"`
28		CommonDir    string `json:"common_dir"`
29	}
30	
31	// Key is stable for one checkout of one clone. It is intentionally stricter
32	// than gitx.Repo.Key, which identifies the clone regardless of checkout.
33	func (t Target) Key() string {
34		return comparablePath(t.CommonDir) + "\x00" + comparablePath(t.CheckoutRoot)
35	}
36	
37	// Current resolves the checkout containing cwd. A linked worktree remains the
38	// target checkout; outside Git, the absolute directory remains a useful project
39	// scope for agents that support configuration in ordinary folders.
40	func Current(ctx context.Context, cwd string) (Target, error) {
41		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, cwd)
42		if err == nil {
43			return target, nil
44		}
45		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
46			return Target{}, ctxErr
47		}
48		if !errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
49			return Target{}, err
50		}
51		root, pathErr := absoluteDirectory(cwd)
52		if pathErr != nil {
53			return Target{}, pathErr
54		}
55		name := filepath.Base(root)
56		return Target{
57			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: name, RepoPath: root,
58			CheckoutRoot: root, CommonDir: root,
59		}, nil
60	}
61	
62	// ResolvePath resolves an explicit path to the checkout containing it.
63	func ResolvePath(ctx context.Context, value string) (Target, error) {
64		absolute, err := absoluteDirectory(value)
65		if err != nil {
66			return Target{}, err
67		}
68		found, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, absolute)
69		if err != nil {
70			return Target{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve target path %q: %w", value, err)
71		}
72		return fromGit(found)
73	}
74	
75	// ResolveRepository resolves an explicit repository reference using repo's
76	// normal name/path rules, then probes the selected path so an explicit linked
77	// worktree path is preserved.
78	func ResolveRepository(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
79		found, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, roots, ref)
80		if err != nil {
81			return Target{}, err
82		}
83		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, found.Path)
84		if err != nil {
85			return Target{}, err
86		}
87		// A named canonical repository contributes its configured alias/category.
88		// An explicit linked-worktree path must keep the main repository identity
89		// discovered by Git instead of becoming the worktree directory basename.
90		if comparablePath(found.Path) == comparablePath(target.RepoPath) {
91			if found.Name != "" {
92				target.RepoName = found.Name
93			}
94			if display := found.Display(); display != "" {
95				target.RepoDisplay = display
96			}
97			target.RepoPath = navigationPath(found.Path)
98			target.CheckoutRoot = target.RepoPath
99		}
100		return target, nil
101	}
102	
103	// ResolveRepo is a concise compatibility name for ResolveRepository.
104	func ResolveRepo(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
105		return ResolveRepository(ctx, roots, ref)
106	}
107	
108	// FromRepository converts one canonical repo discovery result without another
109	// filesystem walk or Git process. Bare and non-Git inventory entries have no
110	// checkout to inspect and are skipped.
111	func FromRepository(found repo.Repo) (Target, bool) {
112		if !found.HasGit || found.Bare {
113			return Target{}, false
114		}
115		checkout := firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath)
116		commonDir := found.CommonDir
117		if checkout == "" || commonDir == "" {
118			return Target{}, false
119		}
120		// Preserve the first discovery root's navigation alias. CommonDir remains
121		// physical identity, so aliases still deduplicate correctly.
122		checkout = navigationPath(checkout)
123		repository := navigationPath(firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath, checkout))
124		commonDir = canonicalPath(commonDir)
125		name := found.Name
126		if name == "" {
127			name = filepath.Base(repository)
128		}
129		display := found.Display()
130		if display == "" {
131			display = name
132		}
133		return Target{
134			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: display, RepoPath: repository,
135			CheckoutRoot: checkout, CommonDir: commonDir,
136		}, true
137	}
138	
139	// FromRepo is a concise compatibility name for FromRepository.
140	func FromRepo(found repo.Repo) (Target, bool) { return FromRepository(found) }
141	
142	// FromRepositories converts an already-discovered repository inventory. This is
143	// the --all-style path: callers can reuse repo.Discover output and avoid a
144	// second walk. Bare and non-Git entries are omitted.
145	func FromRepositories(repositories []repo.Repo) []Target {
146		targets := make([]Target, 0, len(repositories))
147		for _, found := range repositories {
148			if target, ok := FromRepository(found); ok {
149				targets = append(targets, target)
150			}
151		}
152		return Dedupe(targets)
153	}
154	
155	// FromRepos is a concise compatibility name for FromRepositories.
156	func FromRepos(repositories []repo.Repo) []Target { return FromRepositories(repositories) }
157	
158	// WithCurrent appends the startup checkout when it is distinct from the
159	// canonical repository inventory, then returns the same deterministic order as
160	// other target builders.
161	func WithCurrent(targets []Target, current Target) []Target {
162		out := append([]Target(nil), targets...)
163		if current.CheckoutRoot != "" {
164			for _, target := range targets {
165				if comparablePath(target.CommonDir) == comparablePath(current.CommonDir) {
166					current.RepoName = target.RepoName
167					current.RepoDisplay = target.RepoDisplay
168					current.RepoPath = target.RepoPath
169					break
170				}
171			}
172			out = append(out, current)
173		}
174		return Dedupe(out)
175	}
176	
177	// All discovers configured repository roots once and converts the result to
178	// concrete main-checkout targets.
179	func All(ctx context.Context, roots []string) ([]Target, error) {
180		repositories, err := repo.Discover(ctx, roots, repo.DefaultOptions())
181		if err != nil {
182			return nil, err
183		}
184		return FromRepositories(repositories), nil
185	}
186	
187	// Dedupe returns one deterministic entry per common-directory plus checkout
188	// root. The first value supplies display metadata when aliases collide.
189	func Dedupe(targets []Target) []Target {
190		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(targets))
191		out := make([]Target, 0, len(targets))
192		for _, target := range targets {
193			key := target.Key()
194			if _, ok := seen[key]; ok {
195				continue
196			}
197			seen[key] = struct{}{}
198			out = append(out, target)
199		}
200		Sort(out)
201		return out
202	}
203	
204	// Sort orders targets by display name, repository, checkout, then common dir.
205	func Sort(targets []Target) {
206		sort.SliceStable(targets, func(i, j int) bool {
207			left, right := targets[i], targets[j]
208			leftDisplay, rightDisplay := strings.ToLower(left.RepoDisplay), strings.ToLower(right.RepoDisplay)
209			if leftDisplay != rightDisplay {
210				return leftDisplay < rightDisplay
211			}
212			if left.RepoDisplay != right.RepoDisplay {
213				return left.RepoDisplay < right.RepoDisplay
214			}
215			if left.RepoName != right.RepoName {
216				return left.RepoName < right.RepoName
217			}
218			if left.RepoPath != right.RepoPath {
219				return left.RepoPath < right.RepoPath
220			}
221			if left.CheckoutRoot != right.CheckoutRoot {
222				return left.CheckoutRoot < right.CheckoutRoot
223			}
224			return left.CommonDir < right.CommonDir
225		})
226	}
227	
228	func fromGit(found gitx.Repo) (Target, error) {
229		if found.Bare || found.Root == "" {
230			return Target{}, errors.New("repository has no working checkout")
231		}
232		repository := canonicalPath(found.MainRoot)
233		checkout := canonicalPath(found.Root)
234		commonDir := canonicalPath(found.GitCommonDir)
235		name := found.Name
236		if name == "" {
237			name = filepath.Base(repository)
238		}
239		return Target{
240			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: name, RepoPath: repository,
241			CheckoutRoot: checkout, CommonDir: commonDir,
242		}, nil
243	}
244	
245	func firstNonEmpty(values ...string) string {
246		for _, value := range values {
247			if value != "" {
248				return value
249			}
250		}
251		return ""
252	}
253	
254	func absoluteDirectory(value string) (string, error) {
255		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(value)
256		if err != nil {
257			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target path %q: %w", value, err)
258		}
259		if info, statErr := os.Stat(absolute); statErr == nil && !info.IsDir() {
260			absolute = filepath.Dir(absolute)
261		}
262		return filepath.Clean(absolute), nil
263	}
264	
265	func navigationPath(value string) string {
266		if value == "" {
267			return ""
268		}
269		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(value)
270		if err == nil {
271			value = absolute
272		}
273		return filepath.Clean(value)
274	}
275	
276	func canonicalPath(value string) string {
277		if value == "" {
278			return ""
279		}
280		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(value)
281		if err == nil {
282			value = absolute
283		}
284		if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(value); err == nil {
285			value = resolved
286		}
287		return filepath.Clean(value)
288	}
289	
290	func comparablePath(value string) string {
291		return canonicalPath(value)
292	}

140	// Registry returns the complete path snapshot with environment overrides
141	// resolved for this process. Results are sorted by stable agent ID.
142	func Registry() []AgentDefinition {
143		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
144		if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(home) {
145			home = ""
146		}
147		definitions := make([]AgentDefinition, 0, len(registrySnapshot))
148		for _, entry := range registrySnapshot {
149			base, environment := resolveGlobalBase(entry.base, home)
150			global := ""
151			if entry.base != baseNone && base != "" {
152				global = filepath.Join(base, filepath.FromSlash(entry.global))
153			}
154			definitions = append(definitions, AgentDefinition{
155				ID: entry.id, DisplayName: entry.display,
156				ProjectSkillsDir: filepath.FromSlash(entry.project),
157				GlobalSkillsDir:  global, GlobalEnvironment: environment,
158				RegistrySource: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion,
159			})
160		}
161		sort.Slice(definitions, func(i, j int) bool { return definitions[i].ID < definitions[j].ID })
162		return definitions
163	}
164	
165	func agentDisplayNames(ids []string) []string {
166		byID := make(map[string]string, len(registrySnapshot))
167		for _, entry := range registrySnapshot {
168			byID[entry.id] = entry.display
169		}
170		names := make([]string, 0, len(ids))
171		for _, id := range ids {
172			if name := byID[id]; name != "" {
173				names = append(names, name)
174			} else {
175				names = append(names, id)
176			}
177		}
178		return uniqueSorted(names)
179	}
180	
181	func resolveGlobalBase(base globalBase, home string) (string, string) {
182		switch base {
183		case baseNone:
184			return "", ""
185		case baseHome:
186			return home, ""
187		case baseConfigHome:
188			if value := absoluteEnvironment("XDG_CONFIG_HOME"); value != "" {
189				return value, "XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
190			}
191			if home == "" {
192				return "", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
193			}
194			return filepath.Join(home, ".config"), "XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
195		case baseCodexHome:
196			return environmentBase("CODEX_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".codex")), "CODEX_HOME"
197		case baseClaudeHome:
198			return environmentBase("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", filepath.Join(home, ".claude")), "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"
199		case baseVibeHome:
200			return environmentBase("VIBE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".vibe")), "VIBE_HOME"
201		case baseHermesHome:
202			return environmentBase("HERMES_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".hermes")), "HERMES_HOME"
203		case baseAutohandHome:
204			return environmentBase("AUTOHAND_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".autohand")), "AUTOHAND_HOME"
205		case baseGrokHome:
206			return environmentBase("GROK_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".grok")), "GROK_HOME"
207		case baseOpenClawHome:
208			if home == "" {
209				return "", ""
210			}
211			for _, candidate := range []string{".openclaw", ".clawdbot", ".moltbot"} {
212				path := filepath.Join(home, candidate)
213				if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
214					return path, ""
215				}
216			}
217			return filepath.Join(home, ".openclaw"), ""
218		default:
219			return home, ""
220		}
221	}
222	
223	func environmentBase(name, fallback string) string {
224		if value := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(name)); filepath.IsAbs(value) {
225			return filepath.Clean(value)
226		}
227		if filepath.IsAbs(fallback) {
228			return fallback
229		}
230		return ""
231	}
232	
233	func absoluteEnvironment(name string) string {
234		value := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(name))
235		if filepath.IsAbs(value) {
236			return filepath.Clean(value)
237		}
238		return ""
239	}

124	// dedupeScanLocations first coalesces identical registry paths, then aliases to
125	// the same physical directory. The latter retains every logical path and agent
126	// attribution while ensuring the directory is read only once.
127	func dedupeScanLocations(input []logicalScanLocation) []physicalScanLocation {
128		byLogical := map[string]*logicalScanLocation{}
129		for _, location := range input {
130			path := filepath.Clean(location.Path)
131			current := byLogical[path]
132			if current == nil {
133				copy := logicalScanLocation{Path: path}
134				byLogical[path] = &copy
135				current = &copy
136			}
137			current.AgentIDs = append(current.AgentIDs, location.AgentIDs...)
138		}
139		logicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byLogical))
140		for path := range byLogical {
141			logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, path)
142		}
143		sort.Strings(logicalPaths)
144	
145		byPhysical := map[string]*physicalScanLocation{}
146		for _, path := range logicalPaths {
147			logical := *byLogical[path]
148			logical.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(logical.AgentIDs)
149			physical := path
150			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
151				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
152			}
153			group := byPhysical[physical]
154			if group == nil {
155				group = &physicalScanLocation{Path: physical}
156				byPhysical[physical] = group
157			}
158			group.Logical = append(group.Logical, logical)
159		}
160		physicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byPhysical))
161		for path := range byPhysical {
162			physicalPaths = append(physicalPaths, path)
163		}
164		sort.Strings(physicalPaths)
165		result := make([]physicalScanLocation, 0, len(physicalPaths))
166		for _, path := range physicalPaths {
167			group := byPhysical[path]
168			sort.Slice(group.Logical, func(i, j int) bool { return group.Logical[i].Path < group.Logical[j].Path })
169			result = append(result, *group)
170		}
171		return result
172	}

269	func scanLocation(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, target agenttarget.Target, location physicalScanLocation) ([]scannedSkill, []Diagnostic) {

277				Message: fmt.Sprintf("could not read skills directory: %v", err),

282		var skills []scannedSkill

284		for _, entry := range entries {
285			if ctx.Err() != nil {

293			if err != nil {

295					Kind: DiagnosticSkillUnreadable, Scope: scope, Path: child,

297				}, target))
298				continue
299			}
300			if !info.IsDir() {
301				continue
302			}
303			name, present, err := readSkillName(filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"))
304			if !present {
305				continue
306			}
307			if err != nil {
308				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
309					Kind: DiagnosticSkillFrontmatter, Scope: scope,

313			}
314			physical := child

316				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)

319			for _, logical := range location.Logical {
320				logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, filepath.Join(logical.Path, entry.Name()))
321				agentIDs = append(agentIDs, logical.AgentIDs...)

324			agentIDs = uniqueSorted(agentIDs)

327				Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs), Integrity: IntegrityUnknown,
328			}

337	func readSkillName(filename string) (string, bool, error) {
338		info, err := os.Stat(filename)
339		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
340			return "", false, nil
341		}
342		if err != nil {
343			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not inspect SKILL.md: %w", err)
344		}
345		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
346			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md is not a regular file")
347		}
348		file, err := os.Open(filename)
349		if err != nil {
350			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", err)
351		}
352		defer file.Close()
353		if openedInfo, err := file.Stat(); err != nil || !openedInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
354			return "", true, errors.New("opened SKILL.md is not a regular file")
355		}
356	
357		// Bound only the frontmatter, not the skill body. A valid skill may have a
358		// large reference body, and inventory never needs to read it.
359		reader := bufio.NewReader(io.LimitReader(file, maxFrontmatterBytes+1))
360		first, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
361		consumed := int64(len(first))
362		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
363			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", readErr)
364		}
365		first = strings.TrimPrefix(first, string(rune(0xfeff)))
366		if strings.TrimSpace(first) != "---" {
367			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter")
368		}
369		var frontmatter strings.Builder
370		closed := false
371		for {
372			line, lineErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
373			consumed += int64(len(line))
374			if consumed > maxFrontmatterBytes {
375				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter exceeds %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
376			}
377			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "---" {
378				closed = true
379				break
380			}
381			frontmatter.WriteString(line)
382			if lineErr != nil {
383				if errors.Is(lineErr, io.EOF) {
384					break
385				}
386				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", lineErr)
387			}
388		}
389		if !closed {
390			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter is not closed within %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
391		}
392		var metadata struct {
393			Name        string `yaml:"name"`
394			Description string `yaml:"description"`
395		}
396		if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(frontmatter.String()), &metadata); err != nil {
397			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("invalid SKILL.md YAML frontmatter: %w", err)
398		}
399		metadata.Name = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Name)
400		metadata.Description = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Description)
401		if metadata.Name == "" || metadata.Description == "" {
402			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter requires name and description")
403		}
404		if len(metadata.Name) > 256 || normalizedName(metadata.Name) == "" || !safeDisplayValue(metadata.Name) {
405			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter name is invalid")
406		}
407		return metadata.Name, true, nil
408	}

410	func buildPresentRow(scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, name string, group *skillAggregate, lock LockMetadata, candidates []LockMetadata, matched bool) Skill {
411		installations := make([]Installation, 0, len(group.Installations))
412		for _, installation := range group.Installations {
413			installation.LogicalPaths = uniqueSorted(installation.LogicalPaths)
414			installation.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(installation.AgentIDs)
415			installation.Attribution = registryAttribution(installation.AgentIDs)
416			installations = append(installations, *installation)
417		}
418		sort.Slice(installations, func(i, j int) bool {
419			if installations[i].RealPath != installations[j].RealPath {
420				return installations[i].RealPath < installations[j].RealPath
421			}
422			return installations[i].Path < installations[j].Path
423		})
424		var agents []string
425		for _, installation := range installations {
426			agents = append(agents, installation.AgentIDs...)
427		}
428		agentIDs := uniqueSorted(agents)
429		agents = agentDisplayNames(agentIDs)
430		row := Skill{
431			Name: name, Scope: scope, ScopeRoot: scopeRoot,
432			Agents: agents, Repository: target.RepoDisplay, RepositoryPath: target.RepoPath,
433			Checkout: target.CheckoutRoot, Installations: installations, Presence: PresencePresent,
434			Integrity: IntegrityUnknown, Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs),
435			RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion, LockCandidates: append([]LockMetadata(nil), candidates...),
436			ManagedBy: ManagedByExternal, UpdateStatus: UpdateUnknown,
437			UpdateDetail: "not tracked by the skills CLI",
438		}
439		if len(installations) > 0 {
440			row.Path = installations[0].Path
441		}
442		if directManagedSkillName(name) {
443			if name == skill.Name {
444				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByDev
445				row.Source = "dev binary"
446				applyBundledIntegrity(&row)
447				row.UpdateStatus, row.UpdateDetail = bundledStatus(row.Integrity, row.IntegrityDetail)
448			} else {
449				row.UpdateDetail = "name is reserved for the binary-managed dev-cli skill"
450			}
451			return row
452		}
453		if matched {
454			copy := lock
455			row.Lock = &copy
456			row.ManagedBy = ManagedBySkills
457			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnchecked
458			row.UpdateDetail = ""
459			row.Source, row.SourceURL = sourceDisplay(lock.Source), sourceDisplay(lock.SourceURL)
460			row.SourceType = safeSourceType(lock.SourceType)
461			return row
462		}
463		if len(candidates) > 1 {
464			row.UpdateDetail = "ambiguous normalized lock names; no lock entry selected"
465		}
466		return row
467	}

496	
497	func applyBundledIntegrity(row *Skill) {
498		files, err := skill.Files()
499		if err != nil {
500			row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
501			row.IntegrityDetail = err.Error()
502			return
503		}
504		row.Integrity = IntegrityVerified
505		row.IntegrityDetail = "all embedded files match this dev binary"
506		for index := range row.Installations {
507			status, detail := bundledIntegrity(row.Installations[index].RealPath, files)
508			row.Installations[index].Integrity = status
509			row.Installations[index].IntegrityDetail = detail
510			if status == IntegrityDrifted {
511				row.Integrity = IntegrityDrifted
512				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
513			} else if status == IntegrityUnknown && row.Integrity != IntegrityDrifted {
514				row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
515				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
516			}
517		}
518	}
519	
520	func bundledIntegrity(directory string, files map[string][]byte) (Integrity, string) {
521		for relative, want := range files {
522			got, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(directory, relative))
523			if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
524				return IntegrityDrifted, "bundled skill differs; run `dev skill install`"
525			}
526		}
527		return IntegrityVerified, "all embedded files match this dev binary"
528	}
529	
530	// bundledStatus preserves the legacy update-status contract while deriving it
531	// from the already-computed aggregate integrity across every installation.
532	func bundledStatus(integrity Integrity, detail string) (UpdateStatus, string) {
533		if integrity == IntegrityVerified {
534			return UpdateCurrent, detail
535		}
536		if integrity == IntegrityDrifted {
537			return UpdateAvailable, detail
538		}
539		return UpdateFailed, detail
540	}

542	func sourceDisplay(value string) string {
543		if value == "" {
544			return ""
545		}
546		if !safeDisplayValue(value) {
547			return "[redacted]"
548		}
549		value = repo.RedactCloneRef(value)
550		parsed, err := url.Parse(value)

12	// AgentSkillOptions selects native scopes and the explicit remote freshness
13	// pass. With neither scope selected, project and global rows are both returned.
14	type AgentSkillOptions struct {
15		Project bool
16		Global  bool
17		Check   bool
18		Limiter *Limiter
19	}
20	
21	// CollectAgentSkills scans each repository target through the shared local
22	// process limiter, scans global paths once, and only then groups remote source
23	// checks across the complete result.
24	func CollectAgentSkills(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options AgentSkillOptions) (agentskill.Result, error) {
25		if ctx == nil {
26			ctx = context.Background()
27		}
28		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
29		if !project && !global {
30			project, global = true, true
31		}
32		targets = agenttarget.Dedupe(targets)
33		partCount := 0
34		if project {
35			partCount += len(targets)
36		}
37		globalIndex := -1
38		if global {
39			globalIndex = partCount
40			partCount++
41		}
42		parts := make([]agentskill.Result, partCount)
43		errs := make([]error, partCount)
44		limiter := options.Limiter
45		if limiter == nil {
46			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
47		}
48	
49		var wait sync.WaitGroup
50		launch := func(index int, scan func() (agentskill.Result, error)) {
51			wait.Go(func() {
52				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
53				if !ok {
54					errs[index] = ctx.Err()
55					return
56				}
57				defer release()
58				parts[index], errs[index] = scan()
59			})
60		}
61		if project {
62			for index, target := range targets {
63				target := target
64				launch(index, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
65					return agentskill.Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, agentskill.ListOptions{Project: true})
66				})
67			}
68		}
69		if global {
70			launch(globalIndex, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
71				return agentskill.Scan(ctx, nil, agentskill.ListOptions{Global: true})
72			})
73		}
74		wait.Wait()
75	
76		result := agentskill.MergeResults(parts...)
77		if options.Check && ctx.Err() == nil {
78			result.Skills = agentskill.CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
79		}
80		joined := errors.Join(errs...)
81		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
82			joined = errors.Join(joined, ctxErr)
83		}
84		return result, joined
85	}
86

The review contract here is broader than conventional exploit triage: a repository-controlled FIFO or infinite source is a correctness failure even when its only effect is hanging the CLI. I’ll therefore retain bounded/nonblocking violations that are concretely reachable, while rejecting any candidate whose input cannot come from repository content or whose path is already physically confined.

16	var errSymlinkLimit = errors.New("symlink limit reached")
17	
18	func (s *Scanner) readSourceFromDisk(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
19		if ctx.Err() != nil {
20			return readResult{}
21		}
22		resolved, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
23		if err != nil {
24			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
25				return readResult{}
26			}
27			if errors.Is(err, errSymlinkLimit) {
28				return readResult{code: DiagnosticSymlinkLimit}
29			}
30			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
31		}
32		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
33			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, resolved)
34			if err != nil || !inside {
35				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
36			}
37		}
38	
39		info, err := os.Stat(resolved)
40		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
41			return readResult{}
42		}
43		if err != nil {
44			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
45		}
46		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
47			return readResult{code: DiagnosticNotRegular}
48		}
49		if info.Size() > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
50			return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
51		}
52		file, err := os.Open(resolved)
53		if err != nil {
54			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return readResult{}
56			}
57			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
58		}
59		defer file.Close()
60		openedInfo, err := file.Stat()
61		if err != nil || !openedInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
62			return readResult{code: DiagnosticNotRegular}
63		}
64		if openedInfo.Size() > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
65			return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
66		}
67		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
68			currentPath, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
69			if err != nil {
70				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
71			}
72			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, currentPath)
73			currentInfo, statErr := os.Stat(currentPath)
74			if err != nil || !inside || statErr != nil || !os.SameFile(openedInfo, currentInfo) {
75				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
76			}
77		}
78	
79		var body bytes.Buffer
80		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
81		for {
82			if ctx.Err() != nil {
83				return readResult{}
84			}
85			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
86			if n > 0 {
87				if int64(body.Len()+n) > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
88					return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
89				}
90				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
91			}
92			if readErr != nil {
93				if !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
94					return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
95				}
96				break
97			}
98		}
99		if ctx.Err() != nil {
100			return readResult{}
101		}
102		return readResult{data: body.Bytes(), present: true}
103	}
104	
105	// resolveBoundedSymlinks follows symlinks in every path component while placing
106	// a small deterministic bound on cycles and unusually deep chains.
107	func resolveBoundedSymlinks(filename string, limit int) (string, error) {
108		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(filename)
109		if err != nil {
110			return "", err
111		}
112		return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(absolute), limit, 0)
113	}
114	
115	func resolveSymlinkPath(absolute string, limit, followed int) (string, error) {
116		volume := filepath.VolumeName(absolute)
117		root := volume + string(filepath.Separator)
118		relative := strings.TrimPrefix(absolute, root)
119		components := strings.FieldsFunc(relative, func(r rune) bool { return r == rune(filepath.Separator) })
120		current := root
121		for index, component := range components {
122			candidate := filepath.Join(current, component)
123			info, err := os.Lstat(candidate)
124			if err != nil {
125				return "", err
126			}
127			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
128				current = candidate
129				continue
130			}
131			if followed >= limit {
132				return "", errSymlinkLimit
133			}
134			target, err := os.Readlink(candidate)
135			if err != nil {
136				return "", err
137			}
138			if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
139				target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(candidate), target)
140			}
141			if index+1 < len(components) {
142				target = filepath.Join(target, filepath.Join(components[index+1:]...))
143			}
144			target, err = filepath.Abs(target)
145			if err != nil {
146				return "", err
147			}
148			return resolveSymlinkPath(filepath.Clean(target), limit, followed+1)
149		}
150		return filepath.Clean(current), nil
151	}

124	// dedupeScanLocations first coalesces identical registry paths, then aliases to
