> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Control MCP server access for your organization

> Restrict which MCP servers users can add or connect to with managed configuration files, allowlists, and denylists.

By default, anyone running Claude Code can connect any [MCP server](/docs/en/mcp) they choose. Anthropic reviews connectors against its [listing criteria](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/review-criteria) before adding them to the [Anthropic Directory](https://claude.ai/directory), but doesn't security-audit or manage any MCP server. As an administrator, you can restrict which servers run in your organization, from deploying a fixed approved set to disabling MCP entirely.

These restrictions cover the servers Claude Code loads itself, including the connectors it fetches from claude.ai. Connectors the desktop app delivers to its local and SSH sessions arrive in-process and are governed from your claude.ai organization settings instead; [How connectors reach Claude Code](/docs/en/mcp#how-connectors-reach-claude-code) shows which controls apply to connectors in each kind of session, including cloud sessions.

This page covers how to:

* [Choose a pattern](#choose-a-pattern) that matches how much control you need
* [Deploy a fixed server set with `managed-mcp.json`](#exclusive-control-with-managed-mcp-json), including how to [disable MCP entirely](#disable-mcp-entirely)
* [Control servers with allowlists and denylists](#policy-based-control-with-allowlists-and-denylists)
* [Tell users what to expect](#how-restrictions-appear-to-users) when a restriction blocks a server
* [Monitor which servers your organization actually uses](#monitor-mcp-usage)

<Note>
  The [Security](/docs/en/security) page covers the MCP threat model and how to evaluate a server before approving it. [Decide what to enforce](/docs/en/admin-setup#decide-what-to-enforce) covers MCP restrictions alongside the other administrative controls.
</Note>

## Choose a pattern

Claude Code supports a range of restriction levels. Each pattern uses one or both of the mechanisms covered below: `managed-mcp.json` for deploying a fixed set, and `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` for filtering what users configure.

| Pattern                 | What it does                                                                                                                          | Configure                                                                                                      |
| :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Disable MCP**         | No servers load, apart from [in-process servers the app that started the session registers](#exclusive-control-with-managed-mcp-json) | `managed-mcp.json` with an empty server map                                                                    |
| **Fixed deployment**    | Every user gets the same servers and can't add others                                                                                 | `managed-mcp.json` with the servers you want                                                                   |
| **Approved catalog**    | Publish a list of approved servers; users add the ones they want, anything else is blocked                                            | `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true`                                                       |
| **Plugin servers only** | Users can't add servers through `~/.claude.json` or `.mcp.json`; plugin servers still load                                            | [`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`](/docs/en/settings-reference#strictpluginonlycustomization) with `mcp` in the list |
| **Soft allowlist**      | Enforce an allowlist that users can broaden in their own settings                                                                     | `allowedMcpServers` without `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`                                                       |
| **Denylist only**       | Block known-bad servers, allow everything else                                                                                        | `deniedMcpServers`                                                                                             |
| **No restrictions**     | Users add anything                                                                                                                    | Don't deploy any managed MCP configuration                                                                     |

<Note>
  Claude Code doesn't have a built-in MCP server registry that users can browse and install from. For the approved-catalog pattern, share the approved list and its `claude mcp add` commands somewhere your users will find them, such as an internal wiki, or distribute the servers as plugins through a [managed plugin marketplace](/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces#managed-marketplace-restrictions) so users can browse and install them from `/plugin`.
</Note>

## Exclusive control with managed-mcp.json

If you deploy a `managed-mcp.json` file, Claude Code loads only the servers that file defines, plus any in-process servers the app that started the session registers, such as the VS Code extension's own server or the [connectors the desktop app delivers](/docs/en/mcp#how-connectors-reach-claude-code). Users can't add, modify, or use any other MCP servers, including plugin-provided servers and servers passed with the [`--mcp-config` CLI flag](/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags). The file also suppresses the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself unless you [allow them alongside the managed set](#allow-claude-ai-connectors-alongside-the-managed-set).

What a user sees when a session does receive `--mcp-config` servers depends on where the session runs:

* On a workstation, Claude Code exits at startup with `You cannot dynamically configure MCP servers when an enterprise MCP config is present`.
* In [cloud sessions](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) on a host where the file is deployed, such as a [self-hosted runner](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration#mcp-servers), Claude Code starts with the managed servers only and skips the claude.ai connectors and other servers the cloud host delivers through `--mcp-config`. Nothing in the session tells the user which servers were left out. Claude Code names them in a warning on its stderr, which a self-hosted runner records at the `debug` log level. Before v2.1.229, these sessions exited with the same error a workstation shows.

If a user passes `--strict-mcp-config`, Claude Code exits at startup on a workstation and in a cloud session alike, because that flag asks to replace the managed set.

Two other settings can further filter the managed set:

* `allowedMcpServers` and `deniedMcpServers` apply to managed servers too, so a managed server that doesn't pass them won't load.
* A user's own `deniedMcpServers` merges in from their settings, so users can block a managed server for themselves.

See [How a server is evaluated](#how-a-server-is-evaluated) for the full order of checks.

`managed-mcp.json` is a standalone file, so it cannot be delivered through [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings). Any process that can write to a system path with administrator privileges can deploy it. Across a fleet, that's usually through device management tooling, such as Jamf or a configuration profile on macOS, Group Policy or Intune on Windows, or your fleet management of choice on Linux. Claude Code looks for the file at one of these paths:

| Platform      | Path                                                       |
| :------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS         | `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-mcp.json` |
| Linux and WSL | `/etc/claude-code/managed-mcp.json`                        |
| Windows       | `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-mcp.json`             |

The file uses the same format as a project [`.mcp.json`](/docs/en/mcp#project-scope) file:

```json theme={null}
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "github": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
    },
    "sentry": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
    },
    "company-internal": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/usr/local/bin/company-mcp-server",
      "args": ["--config", "/etc/company/mcp-config.json"],
      "env": {
        "COMPANY_API_URL": "https://internal.example.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Authenticate with per-user credentials

Any user on the machine can read this file, so don't store API keys or other credentials in `env` blocks. Pass per-user credentials with one of these instead:

* [`${VAR}` expansion](/docs/en/mcp#environment-variable-expansion-in-mcp-json) to read secrets from each user's environment.
* [OAuth or per-user headers](/docs/en/mcp#authenticate-with-remote-mcp-servers) so each user authenticates as themselves.
* [`headersHelper`](/docs/en/mcp#use-dynamic-headers-for-custom-authentication) to generate credentials at connection time.

### Validate the configuration

To confirm the file is in effect, run two checks on a managed machine:

1. `claude mcp list` shows only the servers in `managed-mcp.json`. If a user's own servers still appear, the file isn't being read; check the path and permissions.
2. `claude mcp add --transport http test https://example.com/mcp` fails with `Cannot add MCP server: enterprise MCP configuration is active and has exclusive control over MCP servers`. The URL doesn't need to be a real server, since the policy check rejects the command before anything is contacted.

### Disable MCP entirely

Deploy a `managed-mcp.json` containing an empty server map to block every MCP server apart from [in-process servers the app that started the session registers](#exclusive-control-with-managed-mcp-json):

```json theme={null}
{
  "mcpServers": {}
}
```

`claude mcp add` fails with the enterprise-policy error above. Servers users had previously configured stop loading the next time they start a session, with no warning that policy is the reason.

### Allow claude.ai connectors alongside the managed set

By default, deploying `managed-mcp.json` suppresses the [claude.ai connectors](/docs/en/mcp#use-mcp-servers-from-claude-ai) Claude Code fetches itself, including connectors an administrator configured for the organization in the claude.ai admin console. To load those connectors alongside the servers in `managed-mcp.json`, set `"allowAllClaudeAiMcps": true` in a [managed settings source](/docs/en/admin-setup#decide-how-settings-reach-devices).

With the setting enabled, Claude Code loads the same claude.ai connectors it would load if `managed-mcp.json` weren't deployed. [Allowlists and denylists](#policy-based-control-with-allowlists-and-denylists) still apply to those connectors, so you can block specific ones with `deniedMcpServers`. The setting affects only the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself; plugin-provided servers stay suppressed.

Cloud sessions and the desktop app's local and SSH sessions receive connectors another way, described in [How connectors reach Claude Code](/docs/en/mcp#how-connectors-reach-claude-code). A `managed-mcp.json` on the host that runs a cloud session, such as a [self-hosted runner host](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration#mcp-servers), suppresses that session's connectors whether or not you set `allowAllClaudeAiMcps`. No `managed-mcp.json` reaches the connectors the desktop app delivers to its local and SSH sessions.

Claude Code reads `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` only from admin-controlled policy tiers: server-managed settings, an MDM-deployed plist or HKLM registry key, or a system `managed-settings.json` file. Placing it in user or project settings has no effect, so users cannot re-enable connectors that exclusive control suppressed.

## Policy-based control with allowlists and denylists

Allowlists and denylists filter which configured servers are allowed to load. They aren't a registry: a server still has to be added by a user, a plugin, or `managed-mcp.json` before the allowlist or denylist applies to it. To deploy servers to users, use [`managed-mcp.json`](#exclusive-control-with-managed-mcp-json). Both lists also filter servers passed with the [`--mcp-config` CLI flag](/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags), other than in-process `type: "sdk"` entries; `--strict-mcp-config` limits which configuration files load and doesn't bypass either list.

To make the allowlist authoritative, set `allowedMcpServers` and `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` together in a [managed settings source](/docs/en/admin-setup#decide-how-settings-reach-devices), such as server-managed settings or a deployed `managed-settings.json` file. [Restrict the allowlist to managed settings only](#restrict-the-allowlist-to-managed-settings-only) shows the configuration. Without `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, allowlists from every settings scope merge, including a user's own `~/.claude/settings.json`, so a user can broaden what your allowlist permits. Denylists merge from every scope regardless.

<Note>
  `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is separate from `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, which locks down [permission rules](/docs/en/permissions#managed-settings) only. Setting that flag does not enforce the MCP allowlist.
</Note>

### Match servers by URL, command, or name

`allowedMcpServers` and `deniedMcpServers` are lists of entries. Each entry is an object with a single key that identifies servers by their URL, their command, or their name:

| Key             | Matches                                                               | Use for                                |
| :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------- |
| `serverUrl`     | A remote server URL, exact or with `*` wildcards                      | HTTP and SSE servers                   |
| `serverCommand` | The exact command and arguments that start a stdio server             | Stdio servers                          |
| `serverName`    | The user-assigned label. Exact match only; wildcards are not expanded | Either type, but see the Warning below |

Leaving `allowedMcpServers` unset is different from setting it to an empty array:

| Setting             | Unset (default)     | Empty array `[]`   | Populated                     |
| :------------------ | :------------------ | :----------------- | :---------------------------- |
| `allowedMcpServers` | All servers allowed | No servers allowed | Only matching servers allowed |
| `deniedMcpServers`  | No servers blocked  | No servers blocked | Matching servers blocked      |

See [Invalid entries in managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings#invalid-entries-in-managed-settings) for what happens when an entry fails schema validation.

<Warning>
  A `serverName` entry, in either list, is not a security control. The name is the label a user assigns when running `claude mcp add` or editing a config file, not the underlying server, so a user can call any server `github`. For claude.ai connectors the name is the display name returned by claude.ai, which can change. To enforce which servers actually run, add `serverCommand` or `serverUrl` entries.
</Warning>

The `serverName` validation differs between the two lists:

* In `deniedMcpServers`, `serverName` accepts any non-empty string, so you can block [claude.ai connectors](/docs/en/mcp#use-mcp-servers-from-claude-ai) by their display name. For example, `{ "serverName": "claude.ai Slack" }` blocks the Slack connector. Prefer a `serverUrl` entry when you need the deny to be robust to renames, or when a connector name collides and gains a ` (N)` suffix.
* In `allowedMcpServers`, `serverName` is limited to letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Use `serverUrl` to allowlist a claude.ai connector Claude Code fetches itself; for connectors a cloud host delivers to self-hosted sessions, use the entries listed under [Connector traffic leaves your network](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-deploy#connector-traffic-leaves-your-network) instead.

To turn off all the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself, see [`disableClaudeAiConnectors`](/docs/en/mcp#disable-claude-ai-connectors).

### How a server is evaluated

Before loading a server, including one from `managed-mcp.json`, Claude Code runs the three checks below in order. In-process `type: "sdk"` servers, which the [app that started the session registers](/docs/en/mcp#how-connectors-reach-claude-code), skip all three.

1. **Merge the lists.** Allowlist and denylist entries from every settings scope combine into one allowlist and one denylist, with the managed scope's lists coming from the [managed source or sources Claude Code applies](/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources). When `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is `true`, only the managed allowlist is kept; the denylist always merges from every scope.
2. **Check the denylist.** A server that matches any denylist entry, by URL, command, or name, is blocked. Nothing overrides a denylist match.
3. **Check the allowlist.** If `allowedMcpServers` isn't set anywhere, every server that passed the denylist loads. If it is set, what the server must match depends on its type, shown in the table below. Built-in servers such as Claude in Chrome, the `ide` server Claude Code connects to in a running VS Code or JetBrains IDE, and servers the CLI itself configures skip this check.

| Server type          | Allowed when it matches                                                                                          |
| :------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Remote (HTTP or SSE) | A `serverUrl` entry. A `serverName` match counts only when the allowlist contains no `serverUrl` entries         |
| Stdio                | A `serverCommand` entry. A `serverName` match counts only when the allowlist contains no `serverCommand` entries |

Three matching rules apply inside those checks:

* **Commands match exactly.** Every argument, in order. `["npx", "-y", "server"]` does not match `["npx", "server"]` or `["npx", "-y", "server", "--flag"]`.
* **`serverCommand` and `serverUrl` values expand before matching.** Both the policy entry and the server's configured value go through [`${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expansion](/docs/en/mcp#environment-variable-expansion-in-mcp-json), so an entry written as `["${HOME}/bin/server"]` matches a server config that uses either the same reference or the expanded path. On Windows, reference an environment variable that is set there, such as `${USERPROFILE}` instead of `${HOME}`. `serverName` values match literally and never expand. The two sides read different environments; [How policy entries expand](#how-policy-entries-expand) covers which, and how allowlist and denylist entries differ.
* **URLs support `*` wildcards** anywhere in the pattern, including the scheme. Hostname matching is case-insensitive and ignores a trailing FQDN dot, so `https://Mcp.Example.com/*` matches `https://mcp.example.com/api`. Paths stay case-sensitive.

| Pattern                     | Allows                                                                 |
| :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `https://mcp.example.com/*` | All paths on a specific domain                                         |
| `https://mcp.example.com`   | Also all paths on that domain. A pattern with no path matches any path |
| `https://*.example.com/*`   | Any subdomain of `example.com`                                         |
| `http://localhost:*/*`      | Any port on localhost                                                  |
| `*://mcp.example.com/*`     | Any scheme to a specific domain                                        |

#### How policy entries expand

The server's configured value expands from the live process environment, like the rest of `.mcp.json`. A policy entry expands from a pinned environment instead, so a variable set by a project or user settings file can't change what an allowlist entry means. Because a policy entry still depends on the launching shell's value for any variable it references, use literal URLs and commands for entries you rely on for enforcement.

| Entry list          | Expands from                                                                                                                                                                                        | Expansion that would change a URL entry's scheme, host, or path scope |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allowedMcpServers` | The environment Claude Code started with, plus `env` values from managed settings                                                                                                                   | Claude Code ignores the entry                                         |
| `deniedMcpServers`  | The same, and a variable with no startup value and no `:-default` fills from settings files outside the repository, such as user or managed settings, which only ever widens what the entry matches | The entry still matches                                               |

Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

### Example configuration

The configuration below sets up a hard allowlist with a denylist. The highlighted lines change how the rest of the list is evaluated, and the callouts after the block explain each one:

```json {3,5,11} theme={null}
{
  "allowedMcpServers": [
    { "serverUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/*" },
    { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/*" },
    { "serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."] },
    { "serverCommand": ["python", "/usr/local/bin/approved-server.py"] },
    { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.example.com/*" },
    { "serverUrl": "https://*.internal.example.com/*" }
  ],
  "deniedMcpServers": [
    { "serverName": "dangerous-server" },
    { "serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "unapproved-package"] },
    { "serverUrl": "https://*.untrusted.example.com/*" }
  ]
}
```

* **Line 3**: the first `serverUrl` entry. Once one exists, every remote server must match a URL pattern, so a user can't get an unlisted remote server through by giving it an allowed name.
* **Line 5**: the first `serverCommand` entry. Same effect for stdio servers, so every local server must match a listed command exactly.
* **Line 11**: a `serverName` entry in the denylist. Denylist entries always apply, so any server named `dangerous-server` is blocked regardless of its URL or command.

A `serverName` entry in this allowlist would never match anything, since both transport types already have stricter entries.

The accordions below walk through how a server is evaluated against other allowlist and denylist combinations.

<Accordion title="URL-only allowlist">
  ```json theme={null}
  {
    "allowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.example.com/*" },
      { "serverUrl": "https://*.internal.example.com/*" }
    ]
  }
  ```

  | Server                                                | Result                                       |
  | :---------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------- |
  | HTTP server at `https://mcp.example.com/api`          | Allowed: matches URL pattern                 |
  | HTTP server at `https://api.internal.example.com/mcp` | Allowed: matches wildcard subdomain          |
  | HTTP server at `https://external.example.com/mcp`     | Blocked: doesn't match any URL pattern       |
  | Stdio server with any command                         | Blocked: no name or command entries to match |
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Command-only allowlist">
  ```json theme={null}
  {
    "allowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "approved-package"] }
    ]
  }
  ```

  | Server                                                | Result                            |
  | :---------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------- |
  | Stdio server with `["npx", "-y", "approved-package"]` | Allowed: matches command          |
  | Stdio server with `["node", "server.js"]`             | Blocked: doesn't match command    |
  | HTTP server named `my-api`                            | Blocked: no name entries to match |
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Mixed name and command allowlist">
  ```json theme={null}
  {
    "allowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverName": "github" },
      { "serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "approved-package"] }
    ]
  }
  ```

  | Server                                                                   | Result                                                                |
  | :----------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Stdio server named `local-tool` with `["npx", "-y", "approved-package"]` | Allowed: matches command                                              |
  | Stdio server named `local-tool` with `["node", "server.js"]`             | Blocked: command entries exist but doesn't match                      |
  | Stdio server named `github` with `["node", "server.js"]`                 | Blocked: stdio servers must match commands when command entries exist |
  | HTTP server named `github`                                               | Allowed: matches name                                                 |
  | HTTP server named `other-api`                                            | Blocked: name doesn't match                                           |
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Name-only allowlist">
  ```json theme={null}
  {
    "allowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverName": "github" },
      { "serverName": "internal-tool" }
    ]
  }
  ```

  | Server                                              | Result                           |
  | :-------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------- |
  | Stdio server named `github` with any command        | Allowed: no command restrictions |
  | Stdio server named `internal-tool` with any command | Allowed: no command restrictions |
  | HTTP server named `github`                          | Allowed: matches name            |
  | Any server named `other`                            | Blocked: name doesn't match      |
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Allowlist with denylist override">
  ```json theme={null}
  {
    "allowedMcpServers": [
      { "serverUrl": "https://*.example.com/*" }
    ],
    "deniedMcpServers": [
      { "serverUrl": "https://staging.example.com/*" }
    ]
  }
  ```

  | Server                                           | Result                                                    |
  | :----------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------- |
  | HTTP server at `https://mcp.example.com/api`     | Allowed: matches allowlist URL pattern, no denylist match |
  | HTTP server at `https://staging.example.com/api` | Blocked: matches both, but the denylist takes precedence  |
  | HTTP server at `https://other.com/mcp`           | Blocked: doesn't match the allowlist                      |
</Accordion>

### Restrict the allowlist to managed settings only

To make the managed allowlist the only one that applies, set `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` in the managed settings file:

```json theme={null}
{
  "allowManagedMcpServersOnly": true,
  "allowedMcpServers": [
    { "serverUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/*" },
    { "serverUrl": "https://*.internal.example.com/*" }
  ]
}
```

When `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is `true`, allowlists from user, project, and local settings are ignored. The denylist still merges from every settings scope, so users can always block servers for themselves.

## How restrictions appear to users

For what users see at startup when `managed-mcp.json` is deployed and the session also has `--mcp-config` servers, see [Exclusive control with managed-mcp.json](#exclusive-control-with-managed-mcp-json). Use this table to recognize the other reports and to tell users what to expect before you roll out a change:

| Restriction                                                          | What the user sees                                                                                         |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `managed-mcp.json` is present and the user runs `claude mcp add`     | `Cannot add MCP server: enterprise MCP configuration is active and has exclusive control over MCP servers` |
| The server is on a denylist and the user runs `claude mcp add`       | `Cannot add MCP server "<name>": server is explicitly blocked by enterprise policy`                        |
| The server isn't on the allowlist and the user runs `claude mcp add` | `Cannot add MCP server "<name>": not allowed by enterprise policy`                                         |
| A previously configured server is now blocked by policy              | The server silently disappears from `/mcp` and `claude mcp list` with no warning                           |

In the last case, the user gets no signal that policy is the reason their server disappeared, so tell affected users which servers are blocked when you roll out a new restriction.

## Monitor MCP usage

When [OpenTelemetry export](/docs/en/monitoring-usage) is configured, Claude Code can record which MCP servers and tools users invoke. Set `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` to include MCP server and tool names in tool events, then aggregate them in your collector to see which servers your users actually connect to. See [Monitoring](/docs/en/monitoring-usage) to set up the exporter and for the full event schema.

## Configuration summary

Every file and setting this page covers, what it controls, and how to deliver it:

| Surface                      | What it controls                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Where it lives                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | How to deliver                                                                                                                                                              |
| :--------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `managed-mcp.json`           | Fixed server set, exclusive control                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | System path: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, `/etc/claude-code/`, or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | MDM, GPO, fleet management, or any process with administrator privileges. Cannot be set through server-managed settings                                                     |
| `allowedMcpServers`          | Allowlist of permitted servers                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Any [settings scope](/docs/en/settings#where-settings-live); Claude Code merges the lists from every scope unless `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is set, and takes the managed scope's list from the one [managed source it selects](/docs/en/managed-settings#precedence-within-the-managed-tier) or [composes](/docs/en/managed-settings#compose-every-managed-source) | For enforcement, a [managed settings source](/docs/en/admin-setup#decide-how-settings-reach-devices): server-managed settings, `managed-settings.json`, MDM profile, or registry |
| `deniedMcpServers`           | Denylist of blocked servers                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Any settings scope; Claude Code merges the lists from every scope, and across managed sources as [how Claude Code combines managed sources](/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources) describes                                                                                                                                    | Same as `allowedMcpServers`                                                                                                                                                 |
| `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` | Locks the allowlist to managed sources only                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Managed settings sources only; the setting has no effect elsewhere                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Same as `allowedMcpServers`                                                                                                                                                 |
| `allowAllClaudeAiMcps`       | Loads the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself alongside `managed-mcp.json`. [A `managed-mcp.json` on the host that runs a cloud session still suppresses that session's connectors](#allow-claude-ai-connectors-alongside-the-managed-set) | Managed settings sources only; the setting has no effect elsewhere                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Same as `allowedMcpServers`                                                                                                                                                 |

Managed settings are the settings your organization deploys to every developer's machine. 106	func resolveAgentTargets(ctx context.Context, app *App, cwd string, all bool, repoRef string, project bool) ([]agenttarget.Target, error) {
107		if !project {
108			return nil, nil
109		}
110		if all {
111			return agenttarget.All(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots())
112		}
113		if repoRef != "" {
114			target, err := agenttarget.ResolveRepository(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repoRef)
115			if err != nil {
116				return nil, err
117			}
118			return []agenttarget.Target{target}, nil
119		}
120		target, err := agenttarget.Current(ctx, cwd)
121		if err != nil {
122			return nil, err
123		}
124		return []agenttarget.Target{target}, nil
125	}

167	func renderSkillJSON(app *App, rows []agentskill.Skill) error {
168		out := make([]skillJSON, 0, len(rows))
169		for _, row := range rows {
170			installations := make([]skillInstallationJSON, 0, len(row.Installations))
171			for _, installation := range row.Installations {
172				installations = append(installations, skillInstallationJSON{
173					Path: installation.Path, RealPath: installation.RealPath,
174					LogicalPaths: installation.LogicalPaths, AgentIDs: installation.AgentIDs,
175					Integrity: string(installation.Integrity), IntegrityDetail: installation.IntegrityDetail,
176				})
177			}
178			item := skillJSON{
179				Name: row.Name, Scope: string(row.Scope), ScopeRoot: row.ScopeRoot,
180				Path: row.Path, Agents: row.Agents, Source: row.Source,
181				SourceURL: row.SourceURL, SourceType: row.SourceType,
182				ManagedBy: string(row.ManagedBy), UpdateStatus: string(row.UpdateStatus),
183				UpdateDetail: row.UpdateDetail, Repo: row.Repository, RepoPath: row.RepositoryPath,
184				Checkout: row.Checkout, Installations: installations, Presence: string(row.Presence),
185				Integrity: string(row.Integrity), IntegrityDetail: row.IntegrityDetail,
186				AgentIDs: row.Attribution.AgentIDs, RegistrySource: row.Attribution.Registry,
187				RegistryVersion: row.RegistryVersion,
188			}
189			if row.Lock != nil {
190				item.LockVersion, item.Ref, item.SkillPath = row.Lock.Version, row.Lock.Ref, row.Lock.SkillPath
191				item.Plugin, item.InstalledAt, item.UpdatedAt = row.Lock.PluginName, row.Lock.InstalledAt, row.Lock.UpdatedAt
192				item.WellKnownDigest = row.Lock.WellKnownDigest
193			}
194			out = append(out, item)
195		}
196		enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
197		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
198		return enc.Encode(out)
199	}

201	func renderSkillTable(app *App, rows []agentskill.Skill, targets []agenttarget.Target, project, global bool) error {
202		if !project && !global {
203			project = true
204		}
205		if project {
206			if len(targets) == 1 {
207				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "project root  %s\n\n", config.Contract(targets[0].CheckoutRoot))
208			} else {
209				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "project roots  %d repositories\n\n", len(targets))
210			}
211		}
212		if len(rows) == 0 {
213			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No agent skills found.")
214			return nil
215		}
216		style := app.outStyle()
217		t := app.newTable("REPO", "SCOPE", "SKILL", "INSTALL", "UPDATE", "AGENTS", "SOURCE", "PATH")
218		for _, row := range rows {
219			path := "—"
220			if row.Path != "" {
221				path = config.Contract(row.Path)
222			}
223			t.Add(dash(row.Repository), style.dim(string(row.Scope)), row.Name,
224				style.updateState(skillInstallLabel(row)), style.updateState(shortUpdate(row.UpdateStatus)),
225				compactAgents(row.Agents), dash(row.Source), path)
226		}
227		t.Render(app.Out)
228		return nil
229	}

231	func skillInstallLabel(row agentskill.Skill) string {
232		if row.Presence == agentskill.PresenceMissing {

245	func renderSkillDiagnostics(app *App, diagnostics []agentskill.Diagnostic) {
246		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {

256	func compactAgents(agents []string) string {
257		if len(agents) == 0 {
258			return "—"
259		}
260		names := append([]string(nil), agents...)
261		sort.Strings(names)
262		if len(names) <= 3 {
263			return strings.Join(names, ", ")
264		}
265		return strings.Join(names[:3], ", ") + fmt.Sprintf(" +%d", len(names)-3)
266	}

268	func shortUpdate(status agentskill.UpdateStatus) string {
269		switch status {
270		case agentskill.UpdateAvailable:
271			return "update"
272		case agentskill.UpdateMissing:
273			return "missing"
274		case agentskill.UpdateUnknown:
275			return "unknown"
276		case agentskill.UpdateFailed:
277			return "failed"
278		default:
279			return string(status)
280		}
281	}

461	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
462	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
463	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
464		var b strings.Builder
465		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
466		if flags := renderFlagSet(root.PersistentFlags()); flags != "" {
467			b.WriteString("### Global options\n\n")
468			b.WriteString(flags)
469			b.WriteString("\n")
470		}
471		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
472		return b.String()
473	}
474	
475	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
476		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" {
477			return
478		}
479		if depth > 0 {
480			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
481			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
482				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
483			}
484			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
485				b.WriteString(flags)
486				b.WriteString("\n")
487			}
488		}
489		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
490			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
491		}
492	}
493	
494	func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
495		return renderFlagSet(c.LocalNonPersistentFlags())
496	}
497	
498	func renderFlagSet(flags *pflag.FlagSet) string {
499		var b strings.Builder
500		flags.VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
501			if f.Hidden {
502				return
503			}
504			name := "--" + f.Name
505			if f.Shorthand != "" {
506				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
507			}
508			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
509		})
510		return b.String()
511	}
512	
513	func firstLine(s string) string {
514		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
515			return s[:i]
516		}
517		return s
518	}

125				source := "built-in defaults"
126				if configured {
127					source = config.Contract(app.Cfg.Source)
128				}
129				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "tool bindings from %s\n\n", source)
130	
131				t := app.newTable("KEY", "NAME", "MODE", "RUNS", "AVAILABLE")
132				style := app.outStyle()
133				configuredTools := app.Cfg.EffectiveTools()
134				for i, tool := range externalTools(app) {
135					status := "yes"
136					if tool.Probe != nil && !tool.Probe(ctxOf()) {
137						status = style.warning("no — not on PATH")
138					} else {
139						status = style.success(status)
140					}
141					// Command is [shell, -c/-lic, run]; show the run itself.
142					run := tool.Command[len(tool.Command)-1]
143					mode := "shell"
144					if i < len(configuredTools) && configuredTools[i].Interactive {
145						mode = "interactive"
146					}
147					t.Add(tool.Key, tool.Name, mode, run, status)
148				}
149				t.Render(app.Out)
150	
151				if !configured {
152					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nOverride them with [[tui.tools]] in your config; see \"dev tui tools --help\".")
153				}
154				fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nA tool cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.")
155				return nil
156			},
157		}
158	}

160	// interactive reports whether a real terminal is attached. Piping `dev` into
161	// anything must produce the plain listing, not terminal control sequences.
162	func interactive() bool {
163		for _, f := range []*os.File{os.Stdin, os.Stdout} {
164			info, err := f.Stat()
165			if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice == 0 {
166				return false
167			}
168		}
169		return true
170	}

190	func tuiRemoteCloneDestination(app *App, name string) (string, error) {
191		projectRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot)
192		if err := os.MkdirAll(projectRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
193			return "", err
194		}
195		destination, err := pathx.JoinChild(projectRoot, name)
196		if err != nil {
197			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote repository name %q is not a safe clone destination: %w", name, err)
198		}
199		return destination, nil
200	}

231			}

249			repositories := make([]repo.Repo, 0, len(locals))
250			for _, row := range locals {

252					repositories = append(repositories, row.Repo)
253				}
254			}
255			targets := agenttarget.FromRepositories(repositories)

259			}

267			targets, err := capabilityTargets(ctx, locals)
268			if err != nil {
269				return nil, err
270			}
271			result, err := inventory.CollectAgentSkills(ctx, targets, inventory.AgentSkillOptions{})
272			if err != nil {
273				return result.Skills, err
274			}
275			if len(result.Diagnostics) > 0 {

277			}
278			return result.Skills, nil

289			if len(result.Diagnostics) > 0 {

291			}

318				RuntimeHandle: handle.Handle,
319			}, nil
320		}

443			// Open is navigation-only. The model rejects missing/unregistered and
444			// cold worktree tasks before this callback so reconciliation and writer
445			// ownership remain explicit `dev sweep` / `dev resume` operations.

449					return tui.OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("%s has no checkout — run `dev resume %s`", t.Title(), t.ID)
450				}
451				// Enter is navigation only. Claiming a writer is an explicit
452				// `dev resume`/start action with collision checks.
453				return openResolved(ctx, checkout, t.Title(), "")

500			CloneRemote: func(ctx context.Context, r tui.RemoteRow) (tui.OpenResult, string, error) {
501				dest, err := tuiRemoteCloneDestination(appState.Current(), r.Repo.Name)
502				if err != nil {
503					return tui.OpenResult{}, "", err
504				}
505				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
506					return tui.OpenResult{}, "", fmt.Errorf("%s already exists; add it to scan_roots or clone somewhere explicit",
507						config.Contract(dest))
508				}
509				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, filepath.Dir(dest), "clone", r.Repo.CloneURL, dest); err != nil {
510					return tui.OpenResult{}, "", err
511				}
512				opened, err := openResolved(ctx, dest, r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName)
513				if err != nil {
514					return tui.OpenResult{}, "", fmt.Errorf("cloned to %s, but could not open it: %w", config.Contract(dest), err)
515				}
516				if opened.Directory != "" {
517					opened.Status = "cloned " + r.Repo.FullName + " to " + config.Contract(dest)
518				} else {
519					opened.Status = fmt.Sprintf("cloned %s to %s; %s", r.Repo.FullName, config.Contract(dest), opened.Status)
520				}
521				return opened, dest, nil
522			},

524			Park: func(ctx context.Context, selected *task.Task, next string) (string, error) {
525				active := appState.Current()
526				current, err := active.Tasks.Get(selected.ID)
527				if err != nil {
528					return "", err
529				}
530				updated := *current
531				if next != "" {
532					updated.Next = next
533				}
534				runtimeForTask(active, &updated) // normalize empty handle/name provenance
535				if updated.RuntimeHandle != "" {
536					if _, _, err := closeTaskRuntime(ctx, active, &updated, checkoutOf(&updated)); err != nil {
537						return "", err
538					}
539				}
540				// The dashboard only parks warm: going cold removes a checkout,
541				// which is too consequential for a single keystroke.
542				updated.State, updated.Owner = task.Warm, config.Hostname()
543				if err := active.Tasks.Save(&updated); err != nil {
544					return "", err
545				}
546				return updated.Title() + " parked warm — worktree and branch kept", nil
547			},

549			SetNext: func(ctx context.Context, selected *task.Task, next string) error {
550				active := appState.Current()
551				current, err := active.Tasks.Get(selected.ID)
552				if err != nil {
553					return err
554				}
555				updated := *current
556				updated.Next = next
557				if err := active.Tasks.Save(&updated); err != nil {
558					return err
559				}
560				annotate(active, runtimeForTask(active, &updated), &updated)
561				return nil
562			},

564			// Start is the bridge from "here are my repositories" to "here is what
565			// I am working on" — the step that otherwise means dropping out of the
566			// dashboard to type a command.
567			Start: func(ctx context.Context, r tui.RepoRow, name string) (string, error) {
568				active := appState.Current()
569				rt, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
570				if err != nil {
571					return "", err
572				}
573				actionApp := *active
574				actionApp.runtimeInstance = rt
575				spec, err := buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx, &actionApp, r.Repo, startRequest{
576					Name: name, Mode: task.ModeWorktree,
577				})
578				if err != nil {
579					return "", err
580				}
581				started, err := executeStartSpec(ctx, &actionApp, spec, nil)
582				if err != nil {
583					return "", err
584				}
585				return fmt.Sprintf("started %s on %s", name, started.Task.Branch), nil
586			},

588			StartDirect: func(ctx context.Context, r tui.RepoRow, name string) (string, error) {
589				active := appState.Current()
590				rt, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
591				if err != nil {
592					return "", err
593				}
594				if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, active, rt, r.Repo.Path); err != nil {
595					return "", err
596				}
597				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Repo.Path)
598				if err != nil {
599					return "", err
600				}
601				if st.Detached || st.Branch == "" {
602					return "", fmt.Errorf("direct task needs a named branch; this repo has detached HEAD")
603				}
604				id := task.MakeID(r.Repo.Name, st.Branch)
605				if existing, err := active.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil && existing.State != task.Done {
606					return "", fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s)", existing.ID, existing.State)
607				}
608				handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, r.Repo.Path, r.Repo.Name+"/"+name)
609				if err != nil {
610					return "", err
611				}
612				t := &task.Task{
613					Name: name, Repo: r.Repo.Name, RepoPath: r.Repo.Path,
614					Branch: st.Branch, Base: st.Branch, Mode: task.ModeDirect,
615					State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(),
616				}
617				setTaskRuntime(t, rt, handle)
618				if err := active.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
619					return "", err
620				}
621				annotate(active, rt, t)
622				return fmt.Sprintf("tracking %s directly on %s; no branch/worktree created", name, st.Branch), nil
623			},

625			LoadStats: func(ctx context.Context, repoName string) (tui.StatsPanel, error) {
626				active := appState.Current()
627				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(active.Cfg.StateDir()))
628				if err != nil {
629					return tui.StatsPanel{}, err
630				}
631				defer store.Close()
632				until := time.Now()
633				since := until.AddDate(-1, 0, 0)
634				totals, err := store.DayTotals(stats.Query{
635					Since: since, Until: until, Repo: repoName, ExactRepo: true,
636				})
637				if err != nil {
638					return tui.StatsPanel{}, err
639				}
640				seconds, days := 0, 0
641				for _, value := range totals {
642					seconds += value
643					if value > 0 {
644						days++
645					}
646				}
647				return tui.StatsPanel{
648					Repo: repoName, Seconds: seconds, ActiveDays: days,
649					Since: since, Until: until,
650					Heatmap: stats.Heatmap(totals, stats.HeatmapOptions{
651						Since: since, Until: until, Legend: true, WeekdayLabels: true,
652					}),
653				}, nil
654			},
655	
656			BackfillStats: func(ctx context.Context, repoName string) error {
657				active := appState.Current()
658				r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, active.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repoName)
659				if err != nil {
660					return err
661				}
662				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(active.Cfg.StateDir()))
663				if err != nil {
664					return err
665				}
666				defer store.Close()
667				_, err = stats.BackfillGit(ctx, store, []repo.Repo{r}, time.Now().AddDate(-1, 0, 0), "")
668				return err
669			},

686			},
687	
688			ReloadConfig: func(ctx context.Context) (tui.ConfigUpdate, string, error) {
689				currentRuntime, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
690				if err != nil {
691					return tui.ConfigUpdate{}, "", err
692				}
693				oldRuntime := currentRuntime.Name()
694				next, err := appState.Prepare(ctx)
695				if err != nil {
696					return tui.ConfigUpdate{}, "", err
697				}
698				status := "config + data reloaded"
699				if nextRuntime := next.Runtime().Name(); nextRuntime != oldRuntime {
700					status += fmt.Sprintf("; restart TUI to switch runtime %s → %s", oldRuntime, nextRuntime)
701				}
702				return tui.ConfigUpdate{
703					Apply:       func() { appState.Commit(next) },
704					Tools:       externalTools(next),
705					RepoColumns: next.Cfg.EffectiveRepoColumns(),
706					RepoSort:    next.Cfg.EffectiveRepoSort(),
707					RepoReverse: next.Cfg.TUI.Repos.Reverse,
708				}, status, nil
709			},
710		}
711	
712		// Enter the alternate screen immediately. Local inventory is loaded by
713		// Init in the background rather than making the terminal appear frozen
714		// while dozens of repos are probed.
715		model := tui.New(actions, nil, nil).WithTrace(app.trace).WithContext(runCtx).BeginLoading()
716		finishSetup(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
717		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIProgramRunBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
718		final, err := tea.NewProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen()).Run()
719		cancelRun()
720		app.finishTrace()
721		if err != nil {
722			return err
723		}
724		// A directory choice can only be honoured once the alternate screen is
725		// torn down, and only by the shell wrapper.
726		if m, ok := final.(tui.Model); ok {
727			if dir := m.Chosen(); dir != "" {
728				return app.cdDirective(dir)
729			}
730			if handle := m.Activation(); handle != "" {
731				rt, resolveErr := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctxOf())
732				if resolveErr != nil {
733					return resolveErr
734				}
735				return activateRuntime(ctxOf(), rt, handle)
736			}
737		}
738		return nil
739	}
740	
741	func collectTries(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, includeAll bool) ([]tui.TryRow, error) {
742		options := experiment.ListOptions{All: includeAll}
743		return collectTriesWithOptions(ctx, app, rt, options, nil, false)
744	}
745	
746	func collectTriesWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options experiment.ListOptions,
747		sessions []runtime.Session, sessionsSet bool) ([]tui.TryRow, error) {
748		service, err := newExperimentService(app)
749		if err != nil {
750			return nil, err
751		}
752		items, diagnostics, listErr := service.List(ctx, options)
753		warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
754		if !sessionsSet {
755			sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
756		}
757		rows := make([]tui.TryRow, 0, len(items))
758		for _, item := range items {
759			row := tui.TryRow{Item: item}
760			if item.Entry != nil {
761				if location, ok := item.Entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname()); ok {
762					copy := location
763					row.Location = &copy
764				}
765			}
766			sizeRepo := item.Live.Repo
767			if sizeRepo == nil && item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
768				if discovered, discoverErr := gitx.Discover(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath); discoverErr == nil {
769					sizeRepo = &discovered
770				}
771			}
772			if sizeRepo != nil {
773				worktreeCount := 0
774				if worktrees, worktreeErr := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath); worktreeErr == nil && len(worktrees) > 1 {
775					worktreeCount = len(worktrees) - 1
776				}
777				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.FromGit(*sizeRepo, worktreeCount)
778			} else if item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
779				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.Plain(item.Live.CurrentPath)
780			}
781			if item.Live.Present && item.Live.Repo != nil {
782				row.Topology, row.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath)
783			}
784			if item.Live.Present {
785				for _, session := range sessions {
786					if session.Covers(item.Live.CurrentPath) ||
787						(item.Live.RealPath != "" && session.Covers(item.Live.RealPath)) {
788						row.Live = true
789						row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = rt.Name(), session.Handle, session.AgentStatus
790						break
791					}
792				}
793			}
794			rows = append(rows, row)
795		}
796		return rows, listErr
797	}
798	
799	func applyTryAction(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, request tui.TryRequest) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
800		service, err := newExperimentService(app)
801		if err != nil {
802			return tui.TryActionResult{}, err
803		}
804		resolve := func() (experiment.Item, error) {
805			item, diagnostics, resolveErr := service.ResolveWithOptions(ctx, request.ID, experiment.ResolveOptions{
806				IncludeDeprecated: true, IncludeArchived: true,
807				IncludeEvicted: true, IncludeGraduated: true,
808			})
809			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
810			return item, resolveErr
811		}
812		open := func(item experiment.Item, status string) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
813			if !item.Live.Present || item.Live.CurrentPath == "" {
814				return tui.TryActionResult{}, fmt.Errorf("Try %s is not present on this host", item.DisplayName())
815			}
816			handle, openErr := openCheckout(ctx, rt, item.Live.CurrentPath, item.DisplayName())
817			if openErr != nil {
818				return tui.TryActionResult{}, openErr
819			}
820			result := tui.TryActionResult{Status: status, RefreshRepos: true}
821			if rt.Name() == "none" {
822				result.CD = item.Live.CurrentPath
823			} else {
824				result.Status += fmt.Sprintf(" in %s (%s)", rt.Name(), handle.Handle)
825				result.RuntimeHandle = handle.Handle
826			}
827			if _, touchErr := service.Touch(ctx, item.ID); touchErr != nil {
828				return result, fmt.Errorf("%s, but could not record activity: %w", status, touchErr)
829			}
830			return result, nil
831		}
832	
833		switch request.Action {
834		case tui.TryOpen:
835			item, resolveErr := resolve()
836			if resolveErr != nil {
837				return tui.TryActionResult{}, resolveErr
838			}
839			return open(item, "opened "+item.DisplayName())
840	
841		case tui.TryCreate:
842			created, createErr := service.ResolveOrCreate(ctx, experiment.CreateRequest{
843				Name: request.Name, Clone: request.Clone, NoGit: request.NoGit,
844			})
845			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, created.Diagnostics)
846			if created.InitWarning != nil {
847				app.warnf("could not git init: %v", created.InitWarning)
848			}
849			if createErr != nil {
850				return tui.TryActionResult{}, createErr
851			}
852			status := "created " + created.Item.DisplayName()
853			if created.Existing {
854				status = "opened existing " + created.Item.DisplayName()
855			}
856			result, openErr := open(created.Item, status)
857			result.RefreshRepos = true
858			return result, openErr
859	
860		case tui.TryMark:
861			item, resolveErr := resolve()
862			if resolveErr != nil {
863				return tui.TryActionResult{}, resolveErr
864			}
865			desired := catalog.NormalizeTags(request.Tags)
866			remove := append([]string(nil), item.Tags...)
867			note := request.Note
868			updated, diagnostics, patchErr := service.Patch(ctx, experiment.PatchRequest{
869				Ref: item.ID, AddTags: desired, RemoveTags: remove, Note: &note,
870			})
871			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
872			return tui.TryActionResult{
873				Status: "updated metadata for " + updated.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
874			}, patchErr
875	
876		case tui.TryDeprecate:
877			transition, transitionErr := service.Deprecate(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
878			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
879			return tui.TryActionResult{Status: "deprecated " + transition.Item.DisplayName()}, transitionErr
880	
881		case tui.TryReactivate:
882			transition, transitionErr := service.Reactivate(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
883			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
884			return tui.TryActionResult{Status: "reactivated " + transition.Item.DisplayName()}, transitionErr
885	
886		case tui.TryArchive:
887			transition, transitionErr := service.Archive(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
888			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
889			return tui.TryActionResult{
890				Status: "archived " + transition.Item.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
891			}, transitionErr
892	
893		case tui.TryRestore:
894			transition, transitionErr := service.Restore(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID, To: request.To})
895			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
896			return tui.TryActionResult{
897				Status: "restored " + transition.Item.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
898			}, transitionErr
899	
900		case tui.TryGraduate:
901			graduated, graduateErr := service.Graduate(ctx, experiment.GraduateRequest{
902				Ref: request.ID, Category: request.Category, Name: request.Name,
903			})
904			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, graduated.Diagnostics)
905			if graduateErr != nil {
906				return tui.TryActionResult{}, graduateErr
907			}
908			result, openErr := open(graduated.Item, "graduated "+graduated.Plan.Name)
909			result.RefreshRepos = true
910			return result, openErr
911		}
912		return tui.TryActionResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown Try action %q", request.Action)
913	}
914	
915	// repoCollectOptions leaves an opt-in path for the future TRY view while the
916	// ordinary repository inventory suppresses active and deprecated Tries.
917	type repoCollectOptions struct {
918		IncludeTries bool
919		Sessions     []runtime.Session
920		SessionsSet  bool
921		Tasks        []*task.Task
922		TasksSet     bool
923		Repos        []repo.Repo
924		ReposSet     bool
925		Limiter      *inventory.Limiter
926	}
927	
928	// collectRepos builds the default repository view: what exists, plus how much
929	// of it is in flight, excluding cataloged active/deprecated Tries.
930	func collectRepos(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
931		return collectReposWithOptions(ctx, app, rt, repoCollectOptions{})
932	}
933	
934	func collectReposWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options repoCollectOptions) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
935		repos := options.Repos
936		var err error
937		if !options.ReposSet {
938			repos, err = repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
939			if err != nil {
940				return nil, err
941			}
942		}
943		assets, catalogComplete, err := joinRepoAssets(app, repos)
944		if err != nil {
945			return nil, err
946		}
947		if !options.IncludeTries {
948			visibleRepos := make([]repo.Repo, 0, len(repos))
949			visibleAssets := make([]*catalog.Entry, 0, len(repos))
950			for index, repository := range repos {
951				if suppressTryRepo(assets[index], catalogComplete) {
952					continue
953				}
954				visibleRepos = append(visibleRepos, repository)
955				visibleAssets = append(visibleAssets, assets[index])
956			}
957			repos, assets = visibleRepos, visibleAssets
958		}
959		tasks := options.Tasks
960		if !options.TasksSet {
961			tasks, err = app.Tasks.List()
962			if err != nil {
963				return nil, err
964			}
965		}
966		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
967		for _, t := range tasks {
968			byRepo[t.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[t.RepoPath], t)
969		}
970		sessions := options.Sessions
971		if !options.SessionsSet {
972			sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
973		}
974		notesByRepo := map[string][]*note.Note{}
975		if app.Notes != nil {
976			allNotes, noteErr := app.Notes.List("")
977			if noteErr != nil {
978				return nil, noteErr
979			}
980			for _, n := range allNotes {
981				notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID] = append(notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID], n)
982			}
983		}
984	
985		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, len(repos))
986		// Each repo needs status, worktree and remote subprocesses. Serialising
987		// ~3*56 git processes was the measured 4.2s startup bottleneck; eight
988		// workers brings that down without forking hundreds at once. TUI callers
989		// share the limiter with task enrichment.
990		limiter := options.Limiter
991		if limiter == nil {
992			limiter = inventory.NewLimiter(8)
993		}
994		var wg sync.WaitGroup
995		for i, r := range repos {
996			wg.Add(1)
997			go func(i int, r repo.Repo) {
998				defer wg.Done()
999				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
1000				if !ok {
1001					return
1002				}
1003				defer release()
1004	
1005				row := tui.RepoRow{Repo: r, Asset: assets[i]}
1006				if row.Asset != nil {
1007					repoNotes := notesByRepo[row.Asset.ID]
1008					row.NoteCount = len(repoNotes)
1009					if len(repoNotes) > 0 {
1010						row.LatestNote = repoNotes[0]
1011					}
1012				}
1013				if r.HasGit {
1014					row.Topology, row.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, r.Path)
1015				}
1016				row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.Path]...)
1017				if r.RealPath != "" && r.RealPath != r.Path {
1018					row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.RealPath]...)
1019				}
1020				row.Context = inventory.CollectRepoContext(ctx, r, row.Tasks, sessions, rt.Name())
1021				row.LastActivity = row.Context.LastActivity
1022				row.Worktrees = row.Context.WorktreeCount
1023				if main, ok := row.Context.Main(); ok {
1024					row.Status = main.Status
1025				}
1026				if !r.Bare {
1027					row.RemoteForge, row.RemoteName = forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
1028				}
1029				if live := row.Context.Sessions(); len(live) > 0 {
1030					row.Live, row.Runtime = true, rt.Name()
1031					row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = live[0].Handle, live[0].AgentStatus
1032				}
1033				if r.HasGit {
1034					row.SizeTarget = diskusage.FromGit(gitx.Repo{
1035						Root: r.Path, GitDir: r.GitDir, GitCommonDir: r.CommonDir,
1036						MainRoot: r.MainRoot, Name: r.Name, Bare: r.Bare,
1037					}, row.Worktrees)
1038				} else {
1039					row.SizeTarget = diskusage.Plain(r.Path)
1040				}
1041				out[i] = row
1042			}(i, r)
1043		}
1044		wg.Wait()
1045		return out, ctx.Err()
1046	}
1047	
1048	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
1049	//
1050	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
1051	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
1052	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
1053	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
1054		var out []tui.Tool
1055		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
1056			run := t.Run
1057			name := t.Name
1058			if name == "" {
1059				name = firstWord(run)
1060			}
1061			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
1062			if t.Interactive {
1063				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
1064				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
1065				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
1066				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
1067				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
1068			}
1069			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
1070				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
1071				Probe: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
1072			})
1073		}
1074		return out
1075	}
1076	
1077	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
1078	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself. The
1079	// returned probe is run by a bounded Bubble Tea command, never by View.
1080	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func(context.Context) bool {
1081		return func(ctx context.Context) bool { return checkCommandRunnable(ctx, run, interactive) }
1082	}
1083	
1084	func checkCommandRunnable(ctx context.Context, run string, interactive bool) bool {
1085		if ctx == nil {
1086			ctx = context.Background()
1087		}
1088		word := firstWord(run)
1089		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
1090			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
1091			if word == "" {
1092				return false
1093			}
1094			word = firstWord(word)
1095		}
1096		if word == "" {
1097			return false
1098		}
1099		if interactive {
1100			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
1101			// cannot see aliases or functions.
1102			probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
1103			defer cancel()
1104			probe := exec.CommandContext(probeCtx, shellPath(), "-lic",
1105				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
1106			return probe.Run() == nil
1107		}
1108		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
1109			_, err := os.Stat(word)
1110			return err == nil
1111		}
1112		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
1113		return err == nil
1114	}
1115	
1116	func firstWord(s string) string {
1117		f := strings.Fields(s)
1118		if len(f) == 0 {
1119			return ""
1120		}
1121		return f[0]
1122	}
1123	
1124	func shellPath() string {
1125		if s := os.Getenv("SHELL"); s != "" {
1126			return s
1127		}
1128		return "/bin/sh"
1129	}
1130	
1131	// remoteCachePath is private because the inventory can contain names and URLs
1132	// of private repositories.
1133	func remoteCachePath() string {
1134		return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "remotes.json")
1135	}
1136	
1137	func remoteCacheSourceID(app *App) string {
1138		parts := []string{
1139			"forge-source-v1",
1140			"GH_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GH_HOST"),
1141			"GITLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GITLAB_HOST"),
1142			"GLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GLAB_HOST"),
1143		}
1144		for _, target := range app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps {
1145			parts = append(parts, "azure="+target.Organization+"\x00"+target.Project)
1146		}
1147		sort.Strings(parts)
1148		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\x00")))
1149		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum[:])
1150	}
1151	
1152	// cachedRemoteRows reads only the private JSON cache — no repository scan or
1153	// subprocess — so it is safe on the startup path. Local clone markers are
1154	// filled when the background local inventory arrives.
1155	func cachedRemoteRows(app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool, bool) {
1156		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1157		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
1158		if !ok || cache.SourceID != sourceID {
1159			return nil, false, false
1160		}
1161		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
1162		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
1163			out = append(out, tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr})
1164		}
1165		return out, true, !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID)
1166	}
1167	
1168	// cachedRemotesForRepoRows uses the local repo data the dashboard already
1169	// collected, avoiding another process-spawning scan on startup.
1170	func cachedRemotesForRepoRows(app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
1171		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1172		if !ok || !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1173			return nil, false
1174		}
1175		return matchRemoteRepoRows(cache.Repos, locals), true
1176	}
1177	
1178	func matchRemoteRepoRows(remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo, locals []tui.RepoRow) []tui.RemoteRow {
1179		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
1180		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1181		for _, r := range locals {
1182			if r.RemoteForge == forge.Unknown || r.RemoteName == "" {
1183				continue
1184			}
1185			key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)
1186			if ambiguous[key] {
1187				continue
1188			}
1189			if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
1190				delete(byRemote, key)
1191				ambiguous[key] = true
1192				continue
1193			}
1194			byRemote[key] = r
1195		}
1196		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1197		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1198			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1199			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1200				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
1201				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1202				if local.Asset != nil {
1203					row.LocalKind = local.Asset.Kind
1204				}
1205			}
1206			out = append(out, row)
1207		}
1208		return out
1209	}
1210	
1211	// cachedRemotes returns a fresh, already-local-matched cache for instant TUI
1212	// navigation. Local paths are recomputed rather than cached because clones can
1213	// move independently of the forge inventory.
1214	func cachedRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
1215		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1216		if !ok || !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1217			return nil, false
1218		}
1219		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), true
1220	}
1221	
1222	func cachedRemotesAny(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, forge.Cache, bool) {
1223		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1224		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1225			return nil, forge.Cache{}, false
1226		}
1227		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), cache, true
1228	}
1229	
1230	// collectRemotes aggregates configured forge CLIs, caches the normalised response, then
1231	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
1232	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
1233	type remoteCollectOptions struct {
1234		Locals       []tui.RepoRow
1235		LocalsSet    bool
1236		Providers    []forge.Forge
1237		ProvidersSet bool
1238	}
1239	
1240	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1241		return collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx, app, remoteCollectOptions{})
1242	}
1243	
1244	func collectRemotesForRows(ctx context.Context, app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1245		return collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx, app, remoteCollectOptions{Locals: locals, LocalsSet: true})
1246	}
