```text
220		}
221		m.viewErrors[int(view)] = err

223			View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageFinished,
224			Source: state.source, Freshness: state.freshness, Outcome: outcome,
225			Generation: generation,
```

```text
+	}
+	return []agenttarget.Target{target}, nil
```

```text
195	// ProjectRoot uses the current linked-worktree checkout root. Falling back to
196	// cwd outside Git keeps project-scoped skills useful for ordinary folders too.
197	func ProjectRoot(ctx context.Context, cwd string) string {
198		abs, err := filepath.Abs(cwd)
199		if err == nil {
200			cwd = abs
201		}
202		if repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd); err == nil && repository.Root != "" {
203			return repository.Root
204		}
205		return filepath.Clean(cwd)

209	func Inventory(ctx context.Context, cwd string, options ListOptions) (Result, error) {
210		target, err := agenttarget.Current(ctx, cwd)
211		if err != nil {
212			return Result{}, err
213		}
214		return Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, options)
215	}

217	// Scan inventories the requested targets. Global paths are scanned only once,
218	// regardless of target count.
219	func Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options ListOptions) (Result, error) {
220		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
221			return Result{}, err
222		}
223		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
224		if !project && !global {
225			project, global = true, true
226		}
227	
228		result := Result{RegistrySource: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion}
229		definitions := Registry()
230		if project {
231			for _, target := range agenttarget.Dedupe(targets) {
232				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
233					return result, err
234				}
235				rows, diagnostics := scanProjectScope(ctx, target, definitions)
236				result.Skills = append(result.Skills, rows...)
237				result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
238				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
239					return result, err
240				}
241			}
242		}
243		if global {
244			rows, diagnostics := scanGlobalScope(ctx, definitions)
245			result.Skills = append(result.Skills, rows...)
246			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
247			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
248				return result, err
249			}
250		}
251	
252		sortSkills(result.Skills)
253		sortDiagnostics(result.Diagnostics)
254		if options.Check {
255			result.Skills = CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
256			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
257				return result, err
258			}
259		}
260		return result, nil
261	}

289				builder.WriteRune(character)

291			} else if !lastDash {
292				builder.WriteByte('-')

295		}
296		return strings.Trim(builder.String(), "-")
297	}

299	func lockUpdateable(entry LockMetadata) bool {

301			return false

303		switch entry.SourceType {

305			return false
306		default:
307			return true
308		}
309	}

342	// FindProject returns one installed project-scoped skill by exact or normalized
343	// name. An exact name wins when normalized filesystem names collide.
344	func FindProject(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, name string) (Skill, error) {
345		rows, err := List(ctx, projectRoot, ListOptions{Project: true})
346		if err != nil {
347			return Skill{}, err

367	// MergeResults combines independently scanned targets while restoring the
368	// domain's deterministic ordering and registry metadata.
369	func MergeResults(results ...Result) Result {
370		merged := Result{RegistrySource: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion}
371		for _, result := range results {
372			merged.Skills = append(merged.Skills, result.Skills...)
373			merged.Diagnostics = append(merged.Diagnostics, result.Diagnostics...)
374			if result.RegistrySource != "" {
375				merged.RegistrySource = result.RegistrySource
376			}
377			if result.RegistryVersion != "" {
378				merged.RegistryVersion = result.RegistryVersion
379			}
380		}
381		sortSkills(merged.Skills)
382		sortDiagnostics(merged.Diagnostics)
383		return merged

386	func sortSkills(rows []Skill) {
387		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
388			left, right := rows[i], rows[j]
389			if left.Scope != right.Scope {
390				return left.Scope == ScopeProject
391			}
392			if left.Repository != right.Repository {
393				return left.Repository < right.Repository
394			}
395			if left.Checkout != right.Checkout {
396				return left.Checkout < right.Checkout
397			}
398			leftName, rightName := strings.ToLower(left.Name), strings.ToLower(right.Name)
399			if leftName != rightName {
400				return leftName < rightName
401			}
402			if left.Name != right.Name {
403				return left.Name < right.Name
404			}
405			return left.Path < right.Path
406		})
407	}

410		sort.SliceStable(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool {
411			left, right := diagnostics[i], diagnostics[j]
412			if left.Repository != right.Repository {
413				return left.Repository < right.Repository
414			}
415			if left.Checkout != right.Checkout {
416				return left.Checkout < right.Checkout
417			}
418			if left.Scope != right.Scope {
419				return left.Scope < right.Scope
420			}
421			if left.Path != right.Path {
422				return left.Path < right.Path
423			}
424			if left.Name != right.Name {
425				return left.Name < right.Name
426			}
427			if left.Kind != right.Kind {
428				return left.Kind < right.Kind
429			}
430			return left.Message < right.Message
431		})
432	}

434	func safeDisplayValue(value string) bool {
435		if value == "" || !utf8.ValidString(value) {
436			return false
437		}
438		return !strings.ContainsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
439			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf)
440		})
441	}
442	
443	func uniqueSorted(values []string) []string {
444		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
445		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
446		for _, value := range values {
447			if value == "" {
448				continue
449			}
450			if _, ok := seen[value]; ok {
451				continue
452			}
453			seen[value] = struct{}{}
454			out = append(out, value)
455		}
456		sort.Strings(out)
457		return out
458	}

462		if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(home) {
463			return ""
464		}
465		return home
```

```text
21	// MutationProvider describes the explicit installer boundary without running
22	// it. Repository-scoped mutations require a direct executable: invoking npx in
23	// an untrusted checkout could substitute a repository-local binary.
24	type MutationProvider struct {
25		Available bool
26		Command   string
27		Path      string
28		Detail    string
29	}
30	
31	// MutationProviderStatus performs path lookup only. It is suitable for doctor
32	// and other read-only status surfaces because it never starts skills, npx, npm,
33	// or project code.
34	func MutationProviderStatus() MutationProvider {
35		return MutationProviderStatusFor("")
36	}
37	
38	// MutationProviderStatusFor rejects a provider inside projectRoot in addition
39	// to npm-local shims. The selected repository never supplies the program that
40	// mutates it.
41	func MutationProviderStatusFor(projectRoot string) MutationProvider {
42		if path, err := exec.LookPath("skills"); err == nil {
43			if resolved, trusted := trustedSkillsExecutable(path, projectRoot); trusted {
44				return MutationProvider{Available: true, Command: "skills", Path: resolved, Detail: "skills executable available"}
45			}
46			return MutationProvider{Path: path, Detail: "skills executable resolves inside a repository or node_modules; install a trusted global executable"}
47		}
48		if path, err := exec.LookPath("npx"); err == nil {
49			return MutationProvider{
50				Path:   path,
51				Detail: "npx found but not invoked from repository checkouts; install the `skills` executable for add/update",
52			}
53		}
54		return MutationProvider{Detail: "skills executable is not installed"}
55	}
56	
57	func trustedSkillsExecutable(path, projectRoot string) (string, bool) {
58		if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
59			return "", false
60		}
61		clean := filepath.Clean(path)
62		if pathUsesNodeModulesBin(clean) || projectRoot != "" && lexicalPathInside(projectRoot, clean) {
63			return "", false
64		}
65		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(clean)
66		if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(resolved) || pathUsesNodeModulesBin(resolved) {
67			return "", false
68		}
69		resolved = filepath.Clean(resolved)
70		if projectRoot != "" {
71			inside, err := pathx.Contains(projectRoot, resolved)
72			if err != nil || inside {
73				return "", false
74			}
75		}
76		return resolved, true
77	}
78	
79	func pathUsesNodeModulesBin(path string) bool {
80		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(path), "/")
81		for index := 0; index+1 < len(parts); index++ {
82			if parts[index] == "node_modules" && parts[index+1] == ".bin" {
83				return true
84			}
85		}
86		return false
87	}

103	func canonicalMutationRoot(root string, allowMissing bool) (string, error) {
104		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(root)
105		if err != nil {
106			return "", err
107		}
108		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absolute)
109		if err != nil {
110			if allowMissing && os.IsNotExist(err) {
111				return filepath.Clean(absolute), nil
112			}
113			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve skill mutation root: %w", err)
114		}
115		info, err := os.Stat(resolved)
116		if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
117			return "", errors.New("skill mutation root is not a directory")
118		}
119		return filepath.Clean(resolved), nil
120	}

122	func lexicalPathInside(root, candidate string) bool {
123		root, rootErr := filepath.Abs(root)
124		candidate, candidateErr := filepath.Abs(candidate)
125		if rootErr != nil || candidateErr != nil {
126			return false
127		}
128		relative, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.Clean(root), filepath.Clean(candidate))
129		return err == nil && !filepath.IsAbs(relative) && relative != ".." &&
130			!strings.HasPrefix(relative, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
131	}

141	// AddCommand opens the upstream interactive installer in projectRoot.
142	func AddCommand(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, source string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
143		if source == "" {
144			source = DefaultSource
145		}

152		}

154		if err != nil {
155			return nil, err
156		}

160	// InstallCommand installs an explicit set of skills for explicit agents in
161	// project scope. The caller owns confirmation; --yes only suppresses the
162	// provider's duplicate prompt after that decision.
163	func InstallCommand(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, source string, names, agents []string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
164		if source == "" {
165			source = DefaultSource
166		}
167		if !safeProviderArgument(source) {
168			return nil, errors.New("skill source is not safe to pass to the provider")
169		}
170		if len(names) == 0 {
171			return nil, errors.New("at least one skill is required")
172		}
173		for _, name := range names {
174			if !safeProviderSkillName(name) {
175				return nil, errors.New("skill name is not safe to pass to the provider")
176			}
177		}
178		if len(agents) == 0 {
179			return nil, errors.New("at least one agent is required")
180		}
181		for _, agent := range agents {
182			if !safeProviderArgument(agent) {
183				return nil, errors.New("agent name is not safe to pass to the provider")
184			}
185		}
186		p, err := interactiveProvider(projectRoot)
187		if err != nil {
188			return nil, err
189		}
190		args := []string{"add", source, "--skill"}
191		args = append(args, names...)
192		args = append(args, "--agent")
193		args = append(args, agents...)
194		args = append(args, "--yes")
195		root, err := canonicalMutationRoot(ProjectRoot(ctx, projectRoot), true)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, err
198		}
199		return p.command(ctx, root, args...), nil
200	}

202	// UpdateCommand updates exactly one lock-managed skill in exactly one scope.
203	func UpdateCommand(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, name string, scope Scope) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
204		if directManagedSkillName(name) {
205			return nil, errors.New("dev-cli is managed by the dev binary, not the skills provider")
206		}
207		if !safeProviderSkillName(name) {
208			return nil, errors.New("skill name is not safe to pass to the provider")
209		}
210		if scope != ScopeProject && scope != ScopeGlobal {
211			return nil, errors.New("skill update requires project or global scope")
212		}
213		p, err := interactiveProvider(projectRoot)
214		if err != nil {
215			return nil, err
216		}
217		args := []string{"update", "--yes"}
218		if scope == ScopeGlobal {
219			args = append(args, "--global")
220		} else {
221			args = append(args, "--project")
222		}
223		args = append(args, name)
224		root, err := canonicalMutationRoot(projectRoot, false)
225		if err != nil {
226			return nil, err
227		}
228		return p.command(ctx, root, args...), nil
229	}
230	
231	// ProviderVersion reports a directly installed skills executable. It never
232	// falls back to npx, even with --no-install, because version probes are reads.
233	func ProviderVersion(ctx context.Context, cwd string) (string, error) {
234		status := MutationProviderStatusFor(cwd)
235		if !status.Available {
236			return "", errors.New(status.Detail)
237		}
238		p := provider{bin: status.Path, label: "skills"}
239		cmd := p.command(ctx, cwd, "--version")
240		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
241		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
242		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
243			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
244			if detail == "" {
245				detail = err.Error()
246			}
247			return "", fmt.Errorf("skills: %s", detail)
248		}
249		return "skills " + strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
250	}
```

```text
61	// CheckUpdates compares lock-recorded content with current Git sources. Source

70	func checkUpdatesWith(ctx context.Context, rows []Skill, deps updateCheckDeps) []Skill {
71		out := append([]Skill(nil), rows...)
72		groupsByKey := map[string][]updateMember{}
73		for index := range out {
74			metadata := skillLock(out[index])
75			if out[index].ManagedBy != ManagedBySkills || metadata == nil {

77			}

86				out[index].UpdateDetail = "invalid skill path in lock entry"
87				continue
88			}
89			normalized := *metadata
90			if normalized.RecordedHash == "" || normalized.HashKind == "" {
91				normalizeRecordedHash(&normalized)
92			}
93			if normalized.RecordedHash == "" || normalized.HashKind == "" {
94				out[index].UpdateStatus = UpdateUnknown
95				out[index].UpdateDetail = "lock entry has no comparable content hash"
96				continue
97			}
98			key := url + "\x00" + metadata.Ref
99			groupsByKey[key] = append(groupsByKey[key], updateMember{index: index, url: url, ref: metadata.Ref})
100		}
101	
102		keys := make([]string, 0, len(groupsByKey))
103		for key := range groupsByKey {
104			keys = append(keys, key)
105		}
106		sort.Strings(keys)
107		groups := make([]updateGroup, 0, len(keys))
108		for _, key := range keys {
109			groups = append(groups, updateGroup{key: key, members: groupsByKey[key]})
110		}

161						cached := map[string]rowUpdate{}
162						for _, member := range group.members {
163							if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {

172							if previous, ok := cached[cacheKey]; ok {

243	func cloneSource(ctx context.Context, url, ref string) (string, error) {
244		if !safeFetchRef(ref) {
245			return "", errors.New("skill source ref is not safe to pass to Git")
246		}
247		parent, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-skill-check-*")
248		if err != nil {
249			return "", err
250		}
251		dir := filepath.Join(parent, "source")
252		if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, "", "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", "--", url, dir); err != nil {
253			_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
254			return "", err
255		}
256		if ref != "" {
257			if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "fetch", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", "--", "origin", ref); err != nil {
258				_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
259				return "", err
260			}
261			if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, dir, "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", "FETCH_HEAD"); err != nil {
262				_ = os.RemoveAll(parent)
263				return "", err
264			}
265		}
266		return dir, nil
267	}

269	func safeFetchRef(ref string) bool {
270		if ref == "" {
271			return true
272		}
273		if strings.TrimSpace(ref) != ref || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "-") {
274			return false
275		}
276		return !strings.ContainsFunc(ref, func(r rune) bool {
277			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf)
278		})

281	func normalizeRecordedHash(metadata *LockMetadata) {
282		metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = "", ""
283		computed := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.ComputedHash)
284		folder := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.SkillFolderHash)
285		content := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.ContentHash)
286	
287		setFolderHash := func(hash string) bool {
288			switch {
289			case validHexHash(hash, 40):
290				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "git-tree"
291				return true
292			case validHexHash(hash, 64):
293				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "sha256-folder"
294				return true
295			default:
296				return false
297			}
298		}
299		if metadata.Scope == ScopeGlobal {
300			if setFolderHash(folder) {
301				return
302			}
303			if validHexHash(content, 64) {
304				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
305			}
306			return
307		}
308		if validHexHash(computed, 64) {
309			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = computed, "sha256-folder"
310			return
311		}
312		// Scope-less package tests and older callers may still supply either global
313		// representation; parsed project-v1 locks never reach this branch with them.
314		if metadata.Scope == "" && setFolderHash(folder) {
315			return
316		}
317		if metadata.Scope == "" && validHexHash(content, 64) {
318			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
319		}
320	}
321	
322	func validHexHash(value string, length int) bool {
323		if len(value) != length {
324			return false
325		}
326		_, err := hex.DecodeString(value)
327		return err == nil
328	}

330	func checkOneResult(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, row Skill) (UpdateStatus, string) {
331		entry := skillLock(row)
332		if entry == nil {
333			return UpdateUnknown, "skill has no lock metadata"
334		}
335		folder, ok := safeSkillFolder(entry.SkillPath)
336		if !ok {
337			return UpdateUnknown, "invalid skill path in lock entry"
338		}
339		abs := filepath.Join(repoDir, filepath.FromSlash(folder))
340		info, err := os.Stat(abs)
341		if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
342			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
343				return UpdateMissing, "skill path no longer exists upstream"
344			}
345			return UpdateFailed, "could not inspect upstream skill path"
346		}
347		if !insidePath(repoDir, abs) {
348			return UpdateUnknown, "skill path escapes the fetched source"
349		}
350	
351		expected, kind := entry.RecordedHash, entry.HashKind
352		if expected == "" {
353			copy := *entry
354			normalizeRecordedHash(&copy)
355			expected, kind = copy.RecordedHash, copy.HashKind
356		}
357		var actual string
358		var hashErr error
359		switch kind {
360		case "git-tree":
361			spec := "HEAD^{tree}"
362			if folder != "" {
363				spec = "HEAD:" + folder
364			}
365			actual, hashErr = gitOutput(ctx, repoDir, "rev-parse", spec)
366		case "sha256-folder":
367			actual, hashErr = folderHashContext(ctx, abs)
368		case "sha256-skill-file":
369			actual, hashErr = fileHashContext(ctx, filepath.Join(abs, "SKILL.md"))
370		}
371		if hashErr != nil {
372			if ctx.Err() != nil {
373				return UpdateFailed, "update check canceled"
374			}
375			return UpdateFailed, "could not compute upstream content hash"
376		}
377		if expected == "" || actual == "" {
378			return UpdateUnknown, "lock entry has no comparable content hash"
379		}
380		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(actual), strings.TrimSpace(expected)) {
381			return UpdateCurrent, "matches the recorded upstream content"
382		}
383		return UpdateAvailable, "upstream content changed"
384	}

386	func safeSkillFolder(skillPath string) (string, bool) {
387		p := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(skillPath), "\\", "/")
388		if p == "" || strings.ContainsRune(p, '\x00') {
389			return "", false
390		}
391		// filepath.VolumeName follows the host OS, so reject a Windows drive prefix
392		// explicitly even when dev is checking a lock file on Unix.
393		if len(p) >= 2 && p[1] == ':' && ((p[0] >= 'a' && p[0] <= 'z') || (p[0] >= 'A' && p[0] <= 'Z')) {
394			return "", false
395		}
396		if strings.EqualFold(path.Base(p), "SKILL.md") {
397			p = path.Dir(p)
398		}
399		if p == "." {
400			p = ""
401		}
402		clean := path.Clean(p)
403		if clean == "." {
404			clean = ""
405		}
406		if path.IsAbs(clean) || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") || filepath.VolumeName(filepath.FromSlash(clean)) != "" {
407			return "", false
408		}
409		return clean, true
410	}

416	func folderHashContext(ctx context.Context, dir string) (string, error) {
417		type file struct {
418			name string
419			path string
420		}
421		var files []file
422		err := filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(filename string, entry fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
423			if err != nil {
424				return err
425			}
426			if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
427				return ctxErr
428			}
429			if entry.IsDir() && filename != dir && (entry.Name() == ".git" || entry.Name() == "node_modules") {
430				return filepath.SkipDir
431			}
432			if entry.Type().IsRegular() {
433				relative, err := filepath.Rel(dir, filename)
434				if err != nil {
435					return err
436				}
437				files = append(files, file{name: filepath.ToSlash(relative), path: filename})
438			}
439			return nil
440		})
441		if err != nil {
442			return "", err
443		}
444		collator := collate.New(language.English)
445		sort.SliceStable(files, func(i, j int) bool {
446			if order := collator.CompareString(files[i].name, files[j].name); order != 0 {
447				return order < 0
448			}
449			return files[i].name < files[j].name
450		})
451		hash := sha256.New()
452		buffer := make([]byte, 32*1024)
453		for _, file := range files {
454			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
455				return "", err
456			}
457			_, _ = io.WriteString(hash, file.name)
458			input, err := os.Open(file.path)
459			if err != nil {
460				return "", err
461			}
462			for {
463				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
464					_ = input.Close()
465					return "", err
466				}
467				read, readErr := input.Read(buffer)
468				if read > 0 {
469					_, _ = hash.Write(buffer[:read])
470				}
471				if readErr != nil {
472					_ = input.Close()
473					if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
474						break
475					}
476					return "", readErr
477				}
478			}
479		}
480		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
481	}

484		info, err := os.Lstat(filename)

497		if err != nil || !openedInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
```

```text
1	package inventory

3	import (
4		"context"

10	)
11	
12	// AgentSkillOptions selects native scopes and the explicit remote freshness
13	// pass. With neither scope selected, project and global rows are both returned.
14	type AgentSkillOptions struct {
15		Project bool
16		Global  bool
17		Check   bool
18		Limiter *Limiter
19	}
20	
21	// CollectAgentSkills scans each repository target through the shared local
22	// process limiter, scans global paths once, and only then groups remote source
23	// checks across the complete result.
24	func CollectAgentSkills(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options AgentSkillOptions) (agentskill.Result, error) {
25		if ctx == nil {
26			ctx = context.Background()
27		}
28		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
29		if !project && !global {
30			project, global = true, true
31		}
32		targets = agenttarget.Dedupe(targets)
33		partCount := 0
34		if project {
35			partCount += len(targets)
36		}
37		globalIndex := -1
38		if global {
39			globalIndex = partCount
40			partCount++
41		}
42		parts := make([]agentskill.Result, partCount)
43		errs := make([]error, partCount)
44		limiter := options.Limiter
45		if limiter == nil {
46			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
47		}
48	
49		var wait sync.WaitGroup
50		launch := func(index int, scan func() (agentskill.Result, error)) {
51			wait.Go(func() {
52				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
53				if !ok {
54					errs[index] = ctx.Err()
55					return
56				}
57				defer release()
58				parts[index], errs[index] = scan()
59			})
60		}
61		if project {
62			for index, target := range targets {
63				target := target
64				launch(index, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
65					return agentskill.Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, agentskill.ListOptions{Project: true})
66				})
67			}
68		}
69		if global {
70			launch(globalIndex, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
71				return agentskill.Scan(ctx, nil, agentskill.ListOptions{Global: true})
72			})
73		}
74		wait.Wait()
75	
76		result := agentskill.MergeResults(parts...)
77		if options.Check && ctx.Err() == nil {
78			result.Skills = agentskill.CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
79		}
80		joined := errors.Join(errs...)
81		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
82			joined = errors.Join(joined, ctxErr)
83		}
84		return result, joined
85	}
86
```

```text
10	// LocalLoadRequest identifies the three view generations sharing one source
11	// snapshot. Each result remains independently replaceable.
12	type LocalLoadRequest struct {
13		CycleGeneration uint64
14		TasksGeneration uint64
15		ReposGeneration uint64
16		TriesGeneration uint64
17		ShowAllTries    bool
18		ForceSizes      bool
19	}

21	// LocalResult is one terminal TASKS, REPOS, or TRY snapshot.
22	type LocalResult struct {
23		View       View
24		Generation uint64
25		Tasks      []inventory.Row
26		Repos      []RepoRow
27		Tries      []TryRow
28		Valid      bool
29		Err        error
30	}
31	
32	// LocalLoad is a cancellable stream owned by the caller's context.
33	type LocalLoad struct {
34		ID      uint64
35		Request LocalLoadRequest
36		Results <-chan LocalResult
37	}
38	
39	// LocalActions starts one shared local source cycle.
40	type LocalActions struct {
41		Start func(context.Context, LocalLoadRequest) LocalLoad
42	}
43

45		load   LocalLoad
46		result LocalResult

48	}

50	func (m Model) startLocalLoad() tea.Cmd {
51		if m.actions.Local.Start == nil {
52			return nil
53		}
54		request := LocalLoadRequest{
55			CycleGeneration: m.localGeneration,
56			TasksGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTasks).generation,
57			ReposGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).generation,
58			TriesGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTries).generation,
59			ShowAllTries:    m.showAllTries,
60			ForceSizes:      m.forceSizeReload,
61		}
62		load := m.actions.Local.Start(m.localReadContext(), request)
63		load.Request = request
64		if load.ID == 0 || load.Results == nil {
65			return nil
66		}
67		return waitForLocal(load)
68	}
69

71		return func() tea.Msg {
72			result, ok := <-load.Results
73			if !ok {
74				return localMsg{load: load, done: true}
75			}
76			return localMsg{load: load, result: result}
77		}
78	}
```

```text
2	// Events deliberately carry only fixed categorical fields and relative times:

70

91	const (
92		FreshnessFresh Freshness = "fresh"
93		FreshnessStale Freshness = "stale"
94	)

96	// Outcome is a fixed terminal result class. Raw errors are intentionally absent.
97	type Outcome string
98	
99	const (
100		OutcomeSuccess    Outcome = "success"
101		OutcomePartial    Outcome = "partial"
102		OutcomeFailed     Outcome = "failed"
103		OutcomeCanceled   Outcome = "canceled"
104		OutcomeSuperseded Outcome = "superseded"

107	// Fields are the optional categorical dimensions accepted by a trace event.
108	type Fields struct {

111		Source     Source

114		Generation uint64
115		Rows       *int

118	// Event is one immutable entry in the versioned trace.
119	type Event struct {
120		Sequence   uint64    `json:"sequence"`
121		AtMicros   int64     `json:"at_us"`
122		DurationUS int64     `json:"duration_us,omitempty"`
123		Name       Name      `json:"name"`
124		View       View      `json:"view,omitempty"`
125		Stage      Stage     `json:"stage,omitempty"`
126		Source     Source    `json:"source,omitempty"`
127		Freshness  Freshness `json:"freshness,omitempty"`
128		Outcome    Outcome   `json:"outcome,omitempty"`
129		Generation uint64    `json:"generation,omitempty"`
130		Rows       *int      `json:"rows,omitempty"`
131	}
132	
133	// Snapshot is the complete frozen on-disk document.
134	type Snapshot struct {
135		SchemaVersion int     `json:"schema_version"`
136		DroppedEvents uint64  `json:"dropped_events"`
137		Events        []Event `json:"events"`
138	}
139	
140	// Recorder is safe for concurrent producers. A nil recorder is a no-op.
141	type Recorder struct {
142		mu sync.Mutex
143	
144		clock  func() time.Time
145		origin time.Time
146		limit  int
147	
148		next    uint64
149		dropped uint64
150		events  []Event
151		once    map[Name]struct{}
152		frozen  bool
153	}
154	
155	// New starts a recorder at the current time.
156	func New(limit int) *Recorder {
157		return NewWithClock(time.Now, limit)
158	}
159	
160	// NewWithClock supplies deterministic time for tests.
161	func NewWithClock(clock func() time.Time, limit int) *Recorder {
162		if clock == nil {
163			clock = time.Now
164		}
165		if limit <= 0 {
166			limit = DefaultLimit
167		}
168		return &Recorder{
169			clock: clock, origin: clock(), limit: limit,
170			events: make([]Event, 0, min(limit, 64)), once: map[Name]struct{}{},
171		}
172	}
173	
174	// Mark records an instantaneous event.
175	func (r *Recorder) Mark(name Name, fields Fields) {
176		if r == nil {
177			return
178		}
179		r.record(name, fields, r.clock(), 0)
180	}
181	
182	// MarkOnce records only the first occurrence of name.
183	func (r *Recorder) MarkOnce(name Name, fields Fields) {
184		if r == nil {
185			return
186		}
187		r.mu.Lock()
188		if r.frozen {
189			r.mu.Unlock()
190			return
191		}
192		if _, exists := r.once[name]; exists {
193			r.mu.Unlock()
194			return
195		}
196		r.once[name] = struct{}{}
197		now := r.clock()
198		r.recordLocked(name, fields, now, 0)
199		r.mu.Unlock()
200	}
201	
202	// Start returns a closure that records one span. Calling the closure more than
203	// once is harmless.
204	func (r *Recorder) Start(name Name, fields Fields) func(Outcome) {
205		if r == nil {
206			return func(Outcome) {}
207		}
208		started := r.clock()
209		var once sync.Once
210		return func(outcome Outcome) {
211			once.Do(func() {
212				fields.Outcome = outcome
213				finished := r.clock()
214				duration := finished.Sub(started)
215				duration = max(duration, 0)
216				r.record(name, fields, started, duration)
217			})
218		}
219	}
220	
221	// Freeze stops the recorder and returns an independent snapshot. Late events are
222	// ignored so background Bubble Tea commands cannot race trace persistence.
223	func (r *Recorder) Freeze() Snapshot {
224		if r == nil {
225			return Snapshot{SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, Events: []Event{}}
226		}
227		r.mu.Lock()
228		defer r.mu.Unlock()
229		r.frozen = true
230		return Snapshot{
231			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion,
232			DroppedEvents: r.dropped,
233			Events:        append([]Event(nil), r.events...),
234		}
235	}
236	
237	func (r *Recorder) record(name Name, fields Fields, at time.Time, duration time.Duration) {
238		r.mu.Lock()
239		defer r.mu.Unlock()
240		if r.frozen {
241			return
242		}
243		r.recordLocked(name, fields, at, duration)
244	}
245	
246	func (r *Recorder) recordLocked(name Name, fields Fields, at time.Time, duration time.Duration) {
247		if len(r.events) >= r.limit {
248			r.dropped++
249			return
250		}
251		r.next++
252		offset := max(at.Sub(r.origin), 0)
253		r.events = append(r.events, Event{
254			Sequence: r.next, AtMicros: offset.Microseconds(), DurationUS: duration.Microseconds(),
255			Name: name, View: fields.View, Stage: fields.Stage, Source: fields.Source,
256			Freshness: fields.Freshness, Outcome: fields.Outcome,
257			Generation: fields.Generation, Rows: fields.Rows,
258		})
259	}
260	
261	// WriteNew writes a trace without overwriting an existing path. Traces are
262	// diagnostics rather than durable state, so an interrupted write is removed.
263	func WriteNew(path string, snapshot Snapshot) error {
264		if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
265			return errors.New("performance trace path must be absolute")
266		}
267		if snapshot.SchemaVersion == 0 {
268			snapshot.SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion
269		}
270		if snapshot.Events == nil {
271			snapshot.Events = []Event{}
272		}
273		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(snapshot, "", "  ")
274		if err != nil {
275			return fmt.Errorf("encode performance trace: %w", err)
276		}
277		data = append(data, '\n')
278	
279		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
280		if err != nil {
281			return fmt.Errorf("create performance trace: %w", err)
282		}
283		remove := true
284		defer func() {
285			if remove {
286				_ = os.Remove(path)
287			}
288		}()
289		if _, err := file.Write(data); err != nil {
290			_ = file.Close()
291			return fmt.Errorf("write performance trace: %w", err)
292		}
293		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
294			_ = file.Close()
295			return fmt.Errorf("sync performance trace: %w", err)
296		}
297		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
298			return fmt.Errorf("close performance trace: %w", err)
299		}
300		remove = false
301		return nil
302	}
303
```

```text
1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8	
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20	
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28	
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37	
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54	
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69	
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76	
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89	
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104	
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129	
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}
```

```bash
func reviewWrite(t *testing.T, path, body string) {
    t.Helper()
    if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }

func reviewOptions(home, cwd string) Options {
    return Options{HomeDir: home, WorkingDirectory: cwd, Concurrency: 1, MaxFileBytes: DefaultMaxFileBytes, MaxSymlinkDepth: 4}
}

func reviewTarget(display, root string) Target {
    return Target{RepoName: display, RepoDisplay: display, RepoPath: root, CheckoutRoot: root, CommonDir: root}
}

func reviewLocalOrProjectRow(t *testing.T, rows []Declaration, scope Scope, name string) Declaration {
    t.Helper()
    for _, row := range rows { if row.Scope == scope && row.Name == name { return row } }
    t.Fatalf("missing %s/%s row: %+v", scope, name, rows)
    return Declaration{}
}

func TestReviewApprovalFalseDoesNotClearTrue(t *testing.T) {
    base := t.TempDir(); home := filepath.Join(base, "home"); repo := filepath.Join(base, "repo")
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(repo, ".mcp.json"), `{"mcpServers":{"server":{"command":"server"}}}`)
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(repo, ".claude", "settings.json"), `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers":true}`)
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(repo, ".claude", "settings.local.json"), `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers":false}`)
    result, err := NewScanner(reviewOptions(home, repo)).Scan(context.Background(), []Target{reviewTarget("repo", repo)})
    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    row := reviewLocalOrProjectRow(t, result.Declarations, ScopeProject, "server")
    body, _ := json.Marshal(row)
    t.Logf("settings.json=true + settings.local.json=false => %s", body)
    if row.Enabled == nil || !*row.Enabled { t.Fatalf("fixture no longer reproduces: %+v", row) }
}

func TestReviewUserApprovalIsIgnored(t *testing.T) {
    base := t.TempDir(); home := filepath.Join(base, "home"); repo := filepath.Join(base, "repo")
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(repo, ".mcp.json"), `{"mcpServers":{"server":{"command":"server"}}}`)
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "settings.json"), `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers":true}`)
    result, err := NewScanner(reviewOptions(home, repo)).Scan(context.Background(), []Target{reviewTarget("repo", repo)})
    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    row := reviewLocalOrProjectRow(t, result.Declarations, ScopeProject, "server")
    body, _ := json.Marshal(row)
    t.Logf("~/.claude/settings.json enableAll=true => %s", body)
    if row.Enabled != nil { t.Fatalf("fixture no longer reproduces: %+v", row) }
}

func TestReviewParentWinsBeforeExactNestedTarget(t *testing.T) {
    base := t.TempDir(); home := filepath.Join(base, "home"); parent := filepath.Join(base, "repo"); child := filepath.Join(parent, "nested")
    reviewWrite(t, filepath.Join(home, ".claude.json"), `{"projects":{`+strconvQuote(child)+`:{"mcpServers":{"server":{"command":"server"}}}}}`)
    targets := []Target{reviewTarget("a-parent", parent), reviewTarget("z-child", child)}
    result, err := NewScanner(reviewOptions(home, parent)).Scan(context.Background(), targets)
    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    row := reviewLocalOrProjectRow(t, result.Declarations, ScopeLocal, "server")
    t.Logf("project key=%q, targets=[parent, exact child] => repo=%q checkout=%q", child, row.Repository, row.Checkout)
    if row.Repository != "a-parent" || row.Checkout != parent { t.Fatalf("fixture no longer reproduces: %+v", row) }
}

func strconvQuote(s string) string { b, _ := json.Marshal(s); return string(b) }

    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    for _, d := range result.Diagnostics { t.Logf("malformed ~/.claude.json => scope=%q path=%q code=%q", d.Scope, d.ConfigPath, d.Code) }

func TestReviewLocalProjectKeysAreDropped(t *testing.T) {
```

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-02 05:07:21Z)**_

Upstream schemas now resolve the key ambiguities: Gemini defines `url` as SSE and precedence `httpUrl → url → command` (no `tcp` field); Claude treats `streamable-http` as an alias of `http` but the normalized model has distinct values; Codex places `scopes` and `oauth_resource` directly on each server; OpenCode’s config-dir override contains extension assets, not config JSON files. Cursor officially documents `${env:VAR}` plus built-in path placeholders, but not bare `$VAR`/`%VAR%`, so those extraction forms need provider-by-provider validation rather than blanket acceptance.

 `https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/configuration/`

```text
### Accepted syntax

For string values in `settings.json` and `gemini-extension.json`, the documented forms are:

- `$VAR_NAME`
- `${VAR_NAME}`
- `${VAR_NAME:-DEFAULT_VALUE}` — uses the fallback when the variable is unset

### Not documented as supported

- `%VAR%`
- `${env:VAR}`

### Supported fields

Expansion applies to **string-valued fields** in those JSON files. Since `mcpServers` is configured in `settings.json`, this includes its string fields, such as `command`, `args`, `env` values, `cwd`, URLs, headers, and descriptions. Numeric or Boolean fields are not applicable.
```

```text
30		parent, err := os.Stat(filepath.Dir(path))
31		if err != nil {

33		}
34		if !parent.IsDir() {
```

```bash
root="$base/shadow-project"; localbin="$root/node_modules/.bin"; globalbin="$base/global-bin"
mkdir -p "$localbin" "$globalbin"
python3 - "$localbin/skills" "$base/local.marker" "$globalbin/skills" "$base/global.marker" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys
for exe, marker in [(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]),(sys.argv[3],sys.argv[4])]:
    Path(exe).write_text('#!/bin/sh\nprintf ran > "'+marker+'"\n')
    Path(exe).chmod(0o755)
PY
set +e
shadow_out=$(cd "$root" && PATH="$localbin:$globalbin:/usr/bin:/bin" "$bin/dev" skill add owner/repo 2>&1)
shadow_status=$?
set -e
printf 'SHADOW status=%s local=%s global=%s output=%s\n' "$shadow_status" "$(test -e "$base/local.marker" && printf ran || printf no)" "$(test -e "$base/global.marker" && printf ran || printf no)" "$shadow_out"

# C: CLI canonicalizes a selected subdirectory to its Git root and rejects a sibling provider.
repo="$base/same-repo"; sub="$repo/sub"; repobin="$repo/tools"; mkdir -p "$sub" "$repobin"; git -C "$repo" init -q
python3 - "$repobin/skills" "$base/same.marker" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys
Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text('#!/bin/sh\nprintf ran > "'+sys.argv[2]+'"\n')
Path(sys.argv[1]).chmod(0o755)
PY
set +e
same_out=$(cd "$sub" && PATH="$repobin:/usr/bin:/bin" "$bin/dev" skill add owner/repo 2>&1)
same_status=$?
set -e
printf 'SAME_REPO_SUBDIR status=%s ran=%s output=%s\n' "$same_status" "$(test -e "$base/same.marker" && printf yes || printf no)" "$same_out"

# D: an executable housed in an unrelated Git repository is accepted.
selected="$base/selected"; other="$base/other-repo"; otherbin="$other/tools"; mkdir -p "$selected" "$otherbin"; git -C "$selected" init -q; git -C "$other" init -q
python3 - "$otherbin/skills" "$base/other.marker" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys
Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text('#!/bin/sh\nprintf "cwd=%s argv=%s" "$PWD" "$*" > "'+sys.argv[2]+'"\n')
Path(sys.argv[1]).chmod(0o755)
PY
(cd "$selected" && PATH="$otherbin:/usr/bin:/bin" "$bin/dev" skill add owner/repo)
printf 'OTHER_REPO '; tr '\n' ' ' < "$base/other.marker"; printf '\n'

printf 'FIXTURE=%s\n' "$base"
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` currently has a useful SKILLS view, but it only inventories the current checkout plus global scope by delegating reads to the external `skills` CLI. That creates three connected problems: repositories outside the current checkout are invisible, lock-recorded skills cannot be shown when the provider is absent, and the `npx --no-install skills` fallback still performs npm registry resolution before npm cancels on the missing `skills@1.5.23` package. MCP configuration is not modeled at all, even though agents store declarations in different files and scopes. Separately, the TUI Tasks table omits repository identity even though `Task.Repo`, filtering, details, and `dev ls --json` already carry it.
4	
5	The intended result is a provider-independent, no-network skill inventory across repositories with explicit upstream freshness checks; a separate secret-safe MCP declaration inventory; and an unambiguous responsive Tasks table. Read paths must never execute `npx`, start MCP servers, resolve credentials, or claim live MCP health.
6	
7	## Agreed product behavior
8	
9	- Whole-machine TUI scans use each canonical repository checkout once **plus the exact startup checkout when it is a distinct linked worktree**. CLI default behavior remains the exact current checkout; `--all` scans canonical repositories, and `--repo` can name an explicit checkout path.
10	- Native skill discovery covers the complete path registry represented by upstream `skills` v1.5.23 (77 agent IDs), with a versioned, table-driven snapshot. Shared paths such as `.agents/skills` are reported as registry-compatible rather than pretending `dev` detected every installed agent executable.
11	- Skill reads are fully native. Remote source checks remain opt-in through `--check` or TUI `c`; no persistent freshness cache is added. **Implementation security note:** the approved plan initially retained `npx` for explicit mutations, but independent review proved that running it in a selected repository could substitute a repository-local `skills` bin. Final add/install/update operations therefore require a directly installed `skills` executable.
12	- MCP is an independent domain and user surface: `dev mcp list` plus a lazy MCP TUI view. Initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
13	- MCP rows represent static declarations, not effective merged runtime configuration or connectivity. Duplicate declarations remain scope-qualified rows; unsupported/runtime-only sources are diagnosed as partial coverage.
14	
15	# Implementation plan
16	
17	## 1. Resolve reusable repository scan targets
18	
19	- Add a small neutral target type under `internal/agenttarget/` containing repository name/display, canonical path/common-dir identity, and the exact checkout root being scanned.
20	- Build targets by reusing `config.Config.DiscoveryRoots`, `repo.Discover`, `repo.Resolve`, and `gitx.Discover` rather than adding another filesystem walk.
21	- Encode selection policy in this package, not Cobra handlers:
22	  - current mode resolves the exact current checkout, including a linked worktree;
23	  - `--all` returns non-bare canonical discovered checkouts once;
24	  - `--repo` accepts existing repository references and explicit linked-worktree paths;
25	  - TUI aggregation appends the startup checkout when it is not the accepted canonical REPOS row;
26	  - targets are deduplicated by common-dir plus checkout root and sorted deterministically.
27	- Reuse accepted `tui.RepoRow` snapshots for lazy TUI loads so SKILLS/MCP do not rediscover repositories or delay initial startup.
28	
29	## 2. Replace provider-based skill reads with native inventory
30	
31	Refactor `internal/agentskill/agentskill.go` into focused types/registry/scanner/lock/freshness/provider files while preserving the existing mutation command API.
32	
33	### Registry and filesystem scan
34	
35	- Check in a provenance/version-tagged Go registry corresponding to upstream `skills@1.5.23` agent paths, including project/global paths and supported environment overrides (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, XDG config roots, and the other registry-defined homes).
36	- Collapse identical logical directories before reading them; scan only immediate child directories with a valid, size-bounded `SKILL.md` rather than recursively walking repositories or home directories.
37	- Parse the skill frontmatter name with a real YAML parser, merge duplicate logical installations by `(scope, target checkout, normalized skill name)`, and retain all installation paths/agent IDs. Resolve physical symlinks for deduplication without losing the logical path that explains agent attribution.
38	- Treat shared paths as compatible with the registry entries that consume that path; expose an attribution/registry-version field so this is not confused with executable detection.
39	- Make exact lock names win. Only use normalized-name matching when unique; emit a deterministic diagnostic for collisions instead of selecting a random Go map entry.
40	
41	### Locks and local status
42	
43	- Split project and global lock decoding and normalize them internally:
44	  - project `<checkout>/skills-lock.json` (current v1 fields such as source, ref, skill path, and `computedHash`);
45	  - global v3 metadata and compatible older fields from `$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is absolute, otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
46	- Bound lock reads and distinguish missing, malformed, unreadable, unsupported-version, and structurally invalid files. Missing is normal; the other cases become safe per-source diagnostics while other repositories continue.
47	- Include lock-only entries whose installation is absent, and unlocked installed directories as externally managed rows.
48	- Add repository/checkout identity, logical installations, local presence, attribution, and normalized lock metadata to `agentskill.Skill`/result types without removing existing fields.
49	- Keep upstream freshness (`unchecked/current/update_available/upstream_missing/unverifiable/check_failed`) separate from local presence/integrity. Only the embedded `dev-cli` skill receives verified/drifted byte-integrity status; do not claim generic lock hashes verify installed bytes.
50	- Convert `Managed` and `FindProject` to the native lock/scanner primitives so repository scaffolding and selected-skill updates no longer require provider JSON.
51	
52	### Explicit freshness and mutation boundary
53	
54	- Preserve and isolate the existing `safeSkillFolder`, folder hashing, Git-source derivation, and grouped `(source URL, ref)` comparisons.
55	- Aggregate all project/global rows first, then run one bounded, cancellation-aware freshness pass so a shared source/ref is cloned once across all repositories. Preserve deterministic row order, clean every temporary clone, and mark only affected rows failed.
56	- Keep local/node_modules/well-known sources unverifiable unless their lock metadata provides a supported comparison; do not silently reinterpret them as Git.
57	- Delete the read-time `npx --no-install skills` path. Read/list/provider-version checks must not invoke npm, a registry, or project Node code.
58	- Retain `interactiveProvider` for explicit add/install/update operations, but require a directly installed `skills` executable after the security review found repository-local `npx` provider substitution. Update `dev doctor` to describe native inventory as always available and report the optional mutation provider separately.

61	
62	- Add an inventory collector (representatively `internal/inventory/agent_skills.go`) that scans project targets with the existing context-aware `inventory.Limiter`, scans global paths exactly once, merges diagnostics, and optionally performs one grouped freshness check.
63	- Extend `dev skill list` in `internal/cli/skill.go` with mutually exclusive `--all` and `--repo <ref>` target selection while preserving `--project`, `--global`, `--check`, and the current-checkout default.
64	- Keep the existing JSON array and every existing key/type; add repository/checkout, installations, presence/integrity, attribution/registry-version, and normalized lock fields. Write partial diagnostics to stderr so JSON stdout stays valid.
65	- Add `--repo` to project `dev skill update`; reject repo targeting for global updates. In the TUI, update a selected project skill from that row’s checkout root, while the interactive add wizard continues to use the startup checkout.
66	- Render a repository-aware human table and keep global rows repository-less rather than duplicating them per target.
67	
68	## 4. Add a normalized, secret-safe MCP domain
69	
70	Create `internal/agentmcp/` with normalized types, a scanner, sanitization helpers, and one adapter per supported agent.
71	
72	### Static sources covered
73	
74	- **Claude Code:** project `.mcp.json`; user and per-project local declarations in `~/.claude.json`.
75	- **Codex:** `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` or `~/.codex/config.toml`; trusted-project `.codex/config.toml`; direct and plugin override declarations.
76	- **Cursor:** project `.cursor/mcp.json`; user `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
77	- **Gemini CLI:** project `.gemini/settings.json`; user `~/.gemini/settings.json`; readable documented system default/override files, with source scope retained.
78	- **OpenCode:** project `opencode.json`/`opencode.jsonc`; XDG user config; an explicit local `OPENCODE_CONFIG` file and readable managed files. Do not fetch remote `.well-known` config or parse inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` as durable inventory.
79	- Use the existing BurntSushi TOML dependency for Codex, `encoding/json` for strict JSON, and a maintained JSONC normalizer for OpenCode rather than an ad-hoc comment stripper.
80	
81	### Normalization and safety
82	
83	- Normalize only non-secret facts: server name, agent, declaration scope, repository, config path, managed/direct source, declared enabled/required/trust policy, transport, safe endpoint host or command basename, argument count, and names/kinds of credential references.
84	- Keep each declaration scope-qualified; do not emulate undocumented merge/precedence rules or label a row “effective.” When transport cannot be proven (for example a Cursor URL declaration), report `remote/unknown` rather than guessing.
85	- Sanitize during adapter conversion so raw values never enter normalized rows, diagnostics, traces, CLI JSON, or TUI state:
86	  - never expand environment variables or `{env:…}`/`${…}` placeholders;
87	  - never read OpenCode `{file:…}` targets or OAuth/token stores;
88	  - never retain env/header/OAuth values or raw command arguments;
89	  - reduce commands to a safe basename and URLs to a credential-free representation with userinfo/query/fragment removed or redacted;
90	  - use fixed diagnostic codes/messages that cannot echo decoder snippets containing secrets;
91	  - reject control characters and bound config size;
92	  - confine project config symlinks to the selected checkout, while allowing bounded user-config symlinks for dotfile managers.
93	- Never invoke agent MCP list/debug commands, helper commands, servers, URLs, or health checks. Document omitted plugin caches, hosted connectors, runtime-only config, remote organization config, and unsupported agent formats as coverage limitations.
94	
95	## 5. Add MCP CLI and TUI surfaces
96	
97	- Register a new `dev mcp list [--repo <ref> | --all] [--agent ...] [--scope ...] [--json]` command in `internal/cli/root.go`/a new `internal/cli/mcp.go`.
98	- Human output shows repo, scope, agent, server, transport, declared state, source, sanitized target, and config path.

100	- Add `ViewMCP` next to SKILLS and parallel model/action/message/filter/detail state in `internal/tui/`. It is lazy and depends on the accepted REPOS generation just like the broadened SKILLS view.
101	- Generalize the existing Fleet REPOS-dependency pattern so waiting, invalidation, superseding generations, and cancellation work for SKILLS and MCP. Preserve existing rows during refresh/check (stale-while-revalidate) instead of replacing them with a progress-only screen.
102	- Add repository-aware structured filters:

104	  - MCP: `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, `state:`.
105	- Give MCP only navigation/filter/reload actions; it has no start/connect/add/remove operation. Update the tab strip to remain within narrow terminals after adding the seventh view.
```

```text
### Supported Cursor MCP template variables

- `"${env:NAME}"` — environment-variable reference; use for credentials such as API keys, tokens, or OAuth client values.
- `"${userHome}"` — the user’s home-directory path.
- `"${workspaceFolder}"` — the project-root path.
- `"${workspaceFolderBasename}"` — the project-root folder name.
- `"${pathSeparator}"` — the operating system’s path separator.
- `"${/}"` — an OS-independent path separator.

### Examples

- Put an API key or authorization token into an `env` or header value through the environment-variable form.
- Build a local script argument from the workspace root plus a relative script path.
- Use the home-directory variable for globally located files.
- Use either separator variable when constructing portable filesystem paths.

The environment form is the credential-capable reference. The other five are non-secret path or project-location substitutions. Interpolation is supported in server commands, arguments, environment values, URLs, and headers.
```
