//go:build !windows

package agentskill

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"sync"
	"testing"
)

func TestMutationCommandSerializesProviderProcesses(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())
	state := t.TempDir()
	active := filepath.Join(state, "active")
	overlap := filepath.Join(state, "overlap")
	script := filepath.Join(state, "provider")
	writeExecutable(t, script, "#!/bin/sh\nif test -e \""+active+"\"; then printf overlap > \""+overlap+"\"; fi\nprintf active > \""+active+"\"\nsleep 0.15\nrm -f \""+active+"\"\n")

	commands := []*MutationCommand{
		{Command: exec.Command(script), ctx: context.Background()},
		{Command: exec.Command(script), ctx: context.Background()},
	}
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errors := make(chan error, len(commands))
	for _, command := range commands {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			errors <- command.Run()
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	close(errors)
	for err := range errors {
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(overlap); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("provider processes overlapped: %v", err)
	}
}

30		}()
31		<-started

156	func New(limit int) *Recorder {
157		return NewWithClock(time.Now, limit)

160	// NewWithClock supplies deterministic time for tests.
161	func NewWithClock(clock func() time.Time, limit int) *Recorder {
162		if clock == nil {
163			clock = time.Now
164		}
165		if limit <= 0 {
166			limit = DefaultLimit
167		}
168		return &Recorder{

170			events: make([]Event, 0, min(limit, 64)), once: map[Name]struct{}{},
171		}
172	}
173

```text
1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	### Added
10	
11	- Agent skill inventory is now provider-independent and repository-aware. A
12	  versioned snapshot of the `skills@1.5.23` 77-agent path registry scans the
13	  current checkout, a selected repository, or every canonical repository plus
14	  global scope without executing Node; explicit source checks group shared
15	  Git/ref inputs once and keep local presence/integrity separate from upstream
16	  freshness.
17	- `dev mcp list` and a lazy MCP TUI view inventory static declarations for
18	  Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Output is scope-qualified,
19	  never claims runtime health/effective precedence, and strips command arguments,
20	  environment/header/OAuth values, URL credentials, and indirect file contents.
21	- Wide TASKS tables now show the repository for each row; compact terminals keep
22	  the previous layout and the detail pane continues to show the full repo/path.
23	- Stable releases now render and publish `Formula/dev-cli.rb` to
24	  `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. The release job requires a fine-grained
25	  `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, fails visibly when the distribution update cannot be
26	  published, and has a manual workflow for retrying or backfilling an existing
27	  stable release without creating another tag. Homebrew installs remain
28	  package-manager-owned rather than letting `dev upgrade` overwrite a Cellar
29	  binary.
30	
31	### Fixed
32	
33	- Read-only skill listing no longer treats the presence of `npx` as proof that
34	  the `skills` package is cached. It never runs `npx --no-install skills`, so npm
35	  cannot resolve a missing package from the registry and cancel the inventory.
36	- Repository-scoped skill mutations now require a directly installed `skills`
37	  executable, use the canonical lock key, reject option-like names, and pin the
38	  confirmed checkout through TUI post-update verification. This prevents selected
39	  repositories from substituting an npm-local provider or redirecting a named
40	  update to a broader scope.
41	- Explicit skill source checks terminate Git option parsing and reject unsafe
42	  refs before fetch, preventing lock-controlled refs from becoming Git options.
43	  Native skill/MCP readers reject non-regular files before opening them, unsafe
44	  terminal names never reach tables, and malformed hashes stay unverifiable.
45	- MCP command strings containing inline arguments are now redacted as a whole;
46	  Codex dynamic header helpers, Claude project approval state, OpenCode project
47	  config layers, Eve subagent skills, and MCP policy/required/trust details are
48	  represented without exposing their values.
49	
50	## [0.2.3] - 2026-09-01
51	
52	### Added
53	
54	- The TUI can write an opt-in, versioned performance trace when
55	  `DEV_TUI_TRACE` names an absolute new file. Relative timings distinguish CLI
56	  load, initial view construction, requested-tab cache/live snapshots, aggregate
57	  row counts, producer completion, discarded stale generations, and key-update
58	  work without recording repository/task/host/tool names, paths, commands, key
59	  values, URLs, handles, or raw errors. Traces are bounded, private, local-only,
60	  and written after the alternate screen is restored; activity `stats.db`
61	  remains unchanged.
62	- TASKS, REPOS, and TRY now publish independently from one shared local load
63	  cycle. Each cycle reads task intent, runtime sessions, and repository discovery
64	  once, shares an eight-slot TASKS/REPOS enrichment limit, and lets FLEET and
65	  REMOTE reuse the accepted REPOS snapshot instead of rescanning local projects.
66	
67	### Fixed
68	
69	- TUI construction and rendering no longer wait for runtime auto-detection,
70	  project-root discovery, cache decoding, interactive shell tool probes, or the
71	  passive release refresh. Per-view generations reject late results, cancel
72	  superseded reads, retain usable rows on refresh failure, and distinguish a
73	  successful empty result from no result.
74	- Successful empty forge refreshes now replace obsolete cached repositories;
75	  fleet cache identity includes the SSH port; forge cache identity includes
76	  configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets; GitLab inventory no longer infers its
77	  host from cwd; canceled refreshes cannot commit cache state; oversized or
78	  malformed forge/fleet caches are ignored; and cached repository names cannot
79	  escape `project_root` when cloning.
80	
81	## [0.2.2] - 2026-08-31
82	
83	### Added
84	
85	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch an explicit command to the
86	  exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree.
87	  `--focus` remains an independent opt-in for switching to that workspace;
88	  reuse, fallback, non-Herdr runtimes, non-worktree modes, and `--json` fail
89	  closed without guessing another pane.
90

387	### The dashboard
388	
389	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens seven lists, switched with `tab`:
390	
391	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.

406	- **MCP** — sanitized static MCP declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
407	  Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. It reports configured scopes, not connection health
408	  or an effective merged runtime configuration.

1	# MCP declarations
2	
3	Inspect static MCP server declarations across repositories and supported agent
4	configuration formats without starting servers or contacting endpoints.
5	
6	```bash
7	dev mcp list
8	dev mcp list --repo api
9	dev mcp list --all
10	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project --json
11	```
12	
13	The initial adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
14	Project, local, user, custom, system, and managed declarations remain separate
15	rows. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` describe fields present in source
16	configuration; they are not connectivity or authentication health.
17	
18	The scanner never executes agent MCP list/debug commands, configured commands,
19	header helpers, servers, or URLs. It does not expand environment placeholders,
20	read OAuth/token stores, or dereference OpenCode `{file:…}` values. Normalized
21	output retains only safe facts such as the command basename, credential reference
22	names, argument count, and a URL scheme/host with userinfo, path, query, and
23	fragment redacted.
24	
25	Static inventory cannot reproduce every runtime layer. Plugin caches, hosted
26	connectors, remote organization configuration, inline
27	`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted and reported
28	as coverage limits. Duplicate names in different files/scopes are not merged
29	into a guessed effective configuration.
30	
31	The MCP TUI view reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot, includes the exact startup
32	linked worktree when distinct, and offers navigation, filtering, and reload only.
33	It never starts, connects, adds, removes, or authenticates a server. Filters
34	include `repo:`, `agent:`, `scope:`, `transport:`, `managed:`, and `state:`.
35
```

```text
1	# Agent skills
2	
3	A provider-independent inventory of agent skills in the current checkout, any
4	selected repository, every configured repository, and global agent paths.
5	
6	## Reading the inventory
7	
8	```bash
9	dev skill list                         # current checkout + global
10	dev skill list --repo api --project    # one repository/checkout
11	dev skill list --all                   # canonical repositories + global once
12	dev skill list --all --check --json    # explicit upstream freshness check
13	```
14	
15	Project/global copies of one skill remain separate rows. Repository identity,
16	logical installations, compatible agent paths, local presence/integrity, source,
17	and update freshness are reported independently.
18	
19	## Where the data comes from
20	
21	Reads are native. `dev` scans a versioned snapshot of all 77 paths in the
22	`skills@1.5.23` registry plus project/global lock files. It never runs `skills`,
23	Node, npm, `npx`, agent detectors, or project code to list inventory. Shared
24	paths such as `.agents/skills` report registry compatibility; they do not claim
25	the corresponding agent executables are installed.
26	
27	Project scope defaults to the exact current checkout, including a linked
28	worktree. `--all` scans canonical configured repositories. The TUI reuses its
29	accepted REPOS snapshot and additionally includes the startup checkout when it
30	is a distinct linked worktree. Global paths are scanned once.
31	
32	A missing lock is normal. Malformed, unreadable, oversized, unsupported, or
33	ambiguous lock data is diagnosed without hiding valid neighboring rows. Absolute
34	`$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` is the global lock when configured;
35	otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` is used.
36	
37	## Freshness and integrity
38	
39	Listing is local-only. `--check` (or TUI `c`) is the explicit network operation:
40	it groups equal Git source/ref pairs and compares current upstream content with
41	the lock-recorded hash without modifying installed files or locks.
42	
43	`current` therefore means upstream still matches the lock record. It does not
44	prove installed bytes are intact. Presence is tracked separately, and only the
45	embedded `dev-cli` skill can verify that every bundled file matches; additional user files are not treated as drift.
46	
47	## Updating
48	
49	```bash
50	dev skill add
51	dev skill update <name> --project [--repo api]
52	dev skill update <name> --global
53	```
54	
55	Only explicit add/install/update operations invoke the provider to change
56	skills. They require a directly installed `skills` executable and may access the
57	network; `dev doctor` may separately run that trusted executable's `--version`
58	probe. `dev` never invokes `npx` from a repository checkout, so a local
59	`node_modules/.bin/skills` cannot substitute for the provider. Updates require one explicit scope
60	and confirmation (or `--yes`); no bulk update is implied by inventory.
61	
62	`dev doctor` reports native inventory separately from the optional mutation
63	provider.
64	
65	## dev's own skill is different
66	
67	The `dev-cli` skill is compiled into the binary. It updates when `dev` updates,
68	not through the upstream provider, and `make install` links it into agent
69	directories. The inventory marks it as directly managed and can verify its local
70	content against the embedded files.
71
```
</details></tool-use>

283	run  = "vibe"
284	interactive = true
285	
286	[[tui.tools]]
287	key  = "P"
288	name = "plans here"
289	run  = "claude-plans-here"
290	interactive = true
291	```
292	
293	A configured list replaces the defaults entirely. Commands run through
294	`$SHELL` in the selected row's checkout, so arguments, environment variables
295	and executable scripts work. `interactive = true` runs through `$SHELL -lic`
296	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's
297	`vibe` alias and `claude-plans-here` function work. Prefer a real script on PATH
298	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.
299	The dashboard resolves availability in a bounded background load after the first
300	view; rendering itself never launches the shell. Unknown or missing bindings are
301	hidden and fail closed until the current config generation has been checked.
302	
303	Keys are case-sensitive. A tool cannot take one the dashboard owns; config
304	loading reports the collision instead of silently shadowing movement or quit.
305

1	# Agent skill and MCP inventory
2	
3	Use these inventories to answer two different questions:
4	
5	- `dev skill list`: which reusable instruction packages are present, and whether
6	  an explicit upstream source check reports newer lock-recorded content.
7	- `dev mcp list`: which external MCP capabilities are declared in supported
8	  static agent configuration files.
9	
10	Do not treat an MCP declaration as a skill, a live connection, or permission to
11	invoke tools.
12	
13	## Skill inventory
14	
15	```bash
16	dev skill list
17	dev skill list --repo <repo-or-checkout> --project
18	dev skill list --all
19	dev skill list --all --check --json
20	```
21	
22	Reads use a versioned snapshot of all 77 agent paths from `skills@1.5.23` plus
23	project/global locks. They never execute `skills`, Node, npm, `npx`, agent
24	detectors, or project code. `--all` scans canonical repositories; the TUI also
25	adds its startup linked checkout when distinct and scans global paths once.
26	
27	Keep status dimensions separate:
28	
29	- presence: local directory present or lock-only/missing;
30	- integrity: only embedded `dev-cli` files can be verified against the binary; additional user files are ignored;
31	- update: lock-recorded upstream content is unchecked/current/changed/missing or
32	  unverifiable.
33	
34	`--check` is the explicit network action. It groups equal Git source/ref pairs
35	and does not write installed skills or locks. `skill add` and `skill update` are
36	explicit mutations and require a directly installed `skills` executable; `dev`
37	never resolves a provider through repository-local npm bins.
38	
39	## MCP inventory
40	
41	```bash
42	dev mcp list
43	dev mcp list --repo <repo-or-checkout>
44	dev mcp list --all --json
45	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project
46	```
47	
48	Adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Rows remain
49	scope-qualified declarations; `dev` does not guess effective precedence across
50	files. `configured`, `enabled`, and `disabled` are declaration facts, not health.
51	
52	The scanner never runs agent MCP commands, configured commands/helpers, servers,
53	or URLs. It never expands environment variables, reads OAuth/token stores, or
54	loads OpenCode `{file:…}` content. Normalized output retains only safe command
55	basenames, endpoint scheme/host, argument counts, credential reference names,
56	policy counts, and redaction markers.
57	
58	Omitted sources include plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization
59	configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs.
60	Treat the coverage metadata as part of the result.
61
```

```text
1	---
2	description: Record dev-cli dependencies, upstream preview status, documentation constraints, and behavior that is intentionally incomplete.
3	authority: project-and-upstream
4	status: evolving
5	verified_on: 2026-09-01
6	tested_with: Claude Code 2.1.250
7	---
8	
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| native skill inventory | local filesystem plus the versioned `skills@1.5.23` path registry | always available; explicit add/update requires a directly installed `skills` executable and may use the network; repository-local npm bins are never provider candidates |
25	| static MCP inventory | readable supported agent config files | missing sources are empty; malformed/unsupported sources produce partial diagnostics, and runtime health is intentionally unavailable |
26	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
27	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
28	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
29	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
30	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
31	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
32	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` prints the package manager's upgrade command instead |
33	
34	## Confirmed project limitations
35	
36	### MCP inventory is static and intentionally incomplete
37	
38	`dev mcp list` reads documented static files for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. It does not start servers, execute helpers, contact endpoints, query health, resolve credentials, or reproduce each agent's runtime merge. Plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted. Keep the JSON `coverage` object and scope-qualified duplicate rows when automating against this inventory.
39	
40	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
41	
42	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
43	
44	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
45	
46	### Pull-request completion is not tracked automatically
47	
48	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge to infer that a request later merged. Verify integration and finish/reconcile deliberately; do not assume remote merge implies local DONE.
49	
50	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
51	
52	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
53	
54	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
55	
56	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Freshness also requires a source fingerprint matching the configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets, so an endpoint change is never hidden by the zero TTL. Legacy source-less caches remain available only through explicit `--cached` and are reported stale. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
57	
58	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
59	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
60	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
61	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
62	inventory has been searched.
63	
64	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
65	
66	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
67	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
68	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
69	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
70	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
71	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
72	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
73	and printed message remain the recovery path.
74	
75	### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
76	
77	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
78	
79	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
80	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
81	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
82	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
83	
84	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
85	
86	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
87	
88	## Current behaviors that are implemented
89	
90	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
```
</details></tool-use>

10	# 相容性與已知限制
11	
12	!!! note "術語規則"
13	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
14	
15	這頁把 graceful degradation 與真正 limitation 分開。Command/runtime code 或 version-sensitive Claude Code 文件變動時必須重新驗證。
16	
17	## dev-cli capability matrix
18	
19	| Capability | Dependency | 缺少時 |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| 核心 repository/task/worktree 操作 | Git | 無法使用；Git 是唯一 hard runtime dependency |
22	| grouped runtime 與 agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` 改試 tmux、Zellij，最後 none |
23	| named terminal session | tmux 或相容 Zellij | `none` 保留核心 behavior 與 shell navigation |
24	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | authenticated `gh` | Git 可用時 branch 仍能 push，可能需 browser/manual flow |
25	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | authenticated `glab` | 同樣 graceful fallback |
26	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` 或 `glab` | local repository/scaffold 仍可使用；wizard 會說明如何 login |
27	| remote repository snapshot template | Git，加上 source 所需的 network/authentication | validation 會在建立 destination 前失敗，rendered URL userinfo 會 redact；local template 仍可使用 |
28	| native skill inventory | local filesystem 加 versioned `skills@1.5.23` path registry | 永遠可用；explicit add/update 需要直接安裝的 `skills` executable，且可能使用 network；repository-local npm bins 絕不作為 provider candidate |
29	| static MCP inventory | 可讀取的 supported agent config files | 缺少 source 代表 empty；malformed/unsupported source 產生 partial diagnostics，runtime health 刻意不提供 |
30	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider 與 entrypoint interpreter | 未選取的 skill 會跳過；selected required setup 若缺少 interpreter，會在 scaffold mutation 前失敗；先取得的 clone 會保留 |
31	| staged lazygit message prefill | 會讀取 `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` 的 lazygit version | files 仍保持 staged，dev 會印出建議 message；一般 Git commit 仍可使用 |
32	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager（`uv`、npm、Cargo 等） | plan 回報 missing tool 並保留 checkout |
33	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | 透過 pipe 執行 bare `dev` 時輸出 plain task list |
34	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` 與 FTS5 | 不需要外部 `sqlite3` executable |
35	| Windows 上的 terminal multiplexing | tmux/Zellij/Herdr（僅 POSIX） | Windows 一律使用 `none` backend；`dev shell-init powershell` 仍能移動 shell |
36	| in-place self-update | standalone install（非 Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`） | `dev upgrade` 改為印出對應套件管理器的升級指令 |
37	
38	## 已確認的專案限制
39	
40	### MCP inventory 是 static 且刻意不完整
41	
42	`dev mcp list` 會讀取 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 與 OpenCode 的 documented static files；不會啟動 server、執行 helper、連線 endpoint、查詢 health、解析 credentials，或重現每個 agent 的 runtime merge。Plugin caches、hosted connectors、remote organization config、inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` 與 command-line-only inputs 都會省略。對 inventory 做 automation 時必須保留 JSON `coverage` object 與 scope-qualified duplicate rows。
43	
44	### Note search 與 filesystem durability 依文字及平台而異
45	
46	Latin note query 使用 term-wise prefix FTS 與 SQLite ranking。Non-ASCII query 改用 literal term-wise substring matching，因為 SQLite 的 `unicode61` tokenizer 不會切分任意 CJK substrings；這些結果不使用相同的 FTS ranking。
47	
48	所有支援平台的 note write 都會 sync file 並 atomic rename。Unix 也會在 rename/delete 後 sync containing directory。Windows implementation 無法提供 directory-fsync 步驟，因此 sudden power loss 時的 durability guarantee 較窄。Cooperating `dev` processes 的 concurrent mutations 會被 serialized，且每次 Markdown replacement 都是 atomic；任意 external writer 不會參與這個 lock。
49	
50	### Pull request completion 不會自動追蹤
51	
52	`dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。目前 `dev sweep` 不會 query forge 推斷 request 後來已 merge。請驗證 integration 後再刻意 finish/reconcile；不能假設 remote merge 代表 local DONE。
53	
54	### Agent session capture 只有保留欄位，尚未接線
55	
56	Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
57	
58	### Built-in forge cache TTL 與 generated config 不同
59	
60	`dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 也要求 source fingerprint 符合 configured GH/GL hosts 與 Azure targets，因此 endpoint change 不會被 zero TTL 隱藏。Legacy source-less cache 只能透過 explicit `--cached` 使用，並會標為 stale。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
61	
62	較舊的 generated config 可能包含 `forge.remote_limit = 100`。此欄位仍可解析，
63	但 forge inventory 現在會完整 pagination，因此不再限制 synchronization。
64	`dev config init` 不再寫入它；`dev repo remote --limit` 只在完整 inventory 搜尋
65	完成後限制 rendered matches。
66	
67	### Lazygit staged-message prefill 是 best effort
68	
69	`repo --check-in=stage` 會在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入 pending message。
70	[Lazygit v0.59.0 的小寫 `c` 會使用該
71	檔案](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，但這是 lazygit implementation detail，不是 Git
72	interface；大寫 `C` 與一般 `git commit` 不會讀取它。Dev 不會覆寫內容不同的既有
73	draft。Draft write failure 只會產生 warning；staging 仍視為成功且不會 rollback。若
74	upstream integration 日後改變，staged index 與已印出的 message 仍是 recovery path。
75	
76	### Windows 是 build target，不是 full-feature 平台
77	
78	`dev` 可在 `windows/amd64` 與 `windows/arm64` 編譯並執行，每個 release 都會附各自的 `.zip`。核心的 repository、task 與 worktree 操作可用。差異：
79	
80	- 沒有 tmux、Zellij 或 Herdr，因此 runtime backend 一律是 `none`。Grouped runtime/agent activity 與 named session 無法使用；`cd` 指令與 PowerShell wrapper 仍可運作。
81	- Shell integration 是 `dev shell-init powershell`。POSIX shell 透過 file descriptor 3 回傳目錄；PowerShell 無法繼承它，wrapper 改用 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳入 temp-file path。
82	- `dev fleet open` 會啟動子 shell（`%COMSPEC%`），而非取代 process，因為 Windows 沒有 `exec(2)`。
83	- Domain test suites 仍有部分假設 POSIX filesystem，因此 Windows CI 的 test 僅供參考，compilation、`go vet` 與 build 則為強制項。
84	
85	### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
86	
87	Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
88	
89	## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
90	
91	以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
92	
93	- `dev repo new|create`、`repo clone` 與 `repo setup` 共用 preset-driven bootstrap pipeline。Plain explicit `repo new NAME` 仍維持 minimal；清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name 會改走 clone acquisition，保留 source history/remote。無參數 wizard 的第一個欄位也會偵測同樣 reference；建立新 repository 時，預設為 no 的 customization gate 讓正常 `agent-ready` flow 保持精簡。Text fields 使用 TTY inline editor，因此 cursor keys 會編輯內容，不會插入 raw escape bytes；non-TTY reader 維持 line-oriented behavior。
94	- `repo new` 可從 local directory/repository 或 Git source 的 optional branch、tag、commit 與 confined subdirectory 建立 fresh-history snapshot。未 pin 的 local Git tree 包含 tracked 加 untracked non-ignored files；non-Git directory 包含完整 current tree。Source `.git` metadata 會排除、URL userinfo 會 redact，不安全的 file types/paths 會在 destination 建立前失敗，held root/file handles 會限制 mutable-path races。Human plan 會預覽 paths 並警告 live snapshot，preset 也可選擇 catalog-repository subfolder。
95	- Repository setup 支援 `--check-in=commit|stage|none`（`auto` 用於 preset compatibility）。Staged setup 會執行 before-commit setup 與 `git add -A`，但不執行 `after_commit` phase；它不能 publish 或 handoff 到 `start`，並可依前述方式預填 lazygit 小寫 `c`。
```

35	```
36

35	## High-value structured interfaces
36	
37	```bash
38	dev ls --json
39	dev repo list --json
40	dev repo context [repo]
41	dev repo remote --json
42	dev repo new NAME --json
43	dev repo clone <ref> --json
44	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
45	dev note list [repo] --json
46	dev note search <query> --json
47	dev note show <note-id> --json
48	dev skill list --all --json
49	dev mcp list --all --json
50	dev bootstrap --json
51	```
52	
53	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract.
54	
55	`dev skill list --json` keeps its existing array and keys while adding repository, checkout, installation, presence/integrity, registry, and lock metadata. `dev mcp list --json` begins with a `servers`/`diagnostics`/`coverage` envelope; every server field is already sanitized, and declaration state must not be interpreted as health or effective precedence.
56	
57	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
58	
59	## Repository bootstrap
60	
61	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
62	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
63	reference:
64	
65	| Command | Behavior |
66	|---|---|
67	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
68	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
69	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
70	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
71	
72	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
73	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
74	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
75	
76	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
77	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
78	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
79	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
80	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
81	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
82	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
83	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
84	availability.
85	
86	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
87	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
88	
89	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
90	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
91	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
92	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
93	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
94	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
95	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
96	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
97	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
98	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
99	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
```

10	This site mixes product documentation, external specifications, fast-moving harness behavior, project policy, and history. Every page identifies which kind of statement it contains and when it was checked.

12	## Authority order
13

15	2. **Git semantics:** current `git-scm.com` manuals for the relevant installed Git version.

19	6. **Historical context:** dated archives and older project essays, never a current operating rule.
20	7. **Project policy:** explicitly labeled recommendations; not presented as an upstream guarantee.
21	
22	A lower item may explain motivation but cannot override a higher authority's implementation claim.

35	```

1086	dev skill sync                 # regenerate the command reference from the command tree

1091	wizard. It never selects all skills or agents. Listing is native and never runs

 	if err != nil {

+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
 	}
 	lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")

1	// Package safefile provides bounded reads that reject non-regular files
2	// without blocking on repository-controlled FIFOs.
3	package safefile
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	)
12	
13	var (
14		ErrNotRegular = errors.New("file is not regular")
15		ErrTooLarge   = errors.New("file exceeds size limit")
16	)
17	
18	// OpenRegular opens path without blocking on Unix special files and verifies
19	// the opened descriptor rather than trusting a path-level stat.
20	func OpenRegular(path string) (*os.File, os.FileInfo, error) {
21		file, err := openReadOnly(path)
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, nil, err
24		}
25		info, err := file.Stat()
26		if err != nil {
27			_ = file.Close()
28			return nil, nil, err
29		}
30		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
31			_ = file.Close()
32			return nil, nil, ErrNotRegular
33		}
34		return file, info, nil
35	}
36	
37	// ReadAll reads at most max bytes from an already verified descriptor.
38	func ReadAll(ctx context.Context, file *os.File, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
39		if ctx == nil {
40			ctx = context.Background()
41		}
42		var body bytes.Buffer
43		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
44		for {
45			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
46				return nil, err
47			}
48			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
49			if n > 0 {
50				if int64(body.Len()+n) > max {
51					return nil, ErrTooLarge
52				}
53				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
54			}
55			if readErr != nil {
56				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
57					return body.Bytes(), nil
58				}
59				return nil, readErr
60			}
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// ReadRegular opens and reads a regular file under a hard byte bound.
65	func ReadRegular(ctx context.Context, path string, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
66		file, info, err := OpenRegular(path)
67		if err != nil {
68			return nil, err
69		}
70		defer file.Close()
71		if info.Size() > max {
72			return nil, ErrTooLarge
73		}
74		return ReadAll(ctx, file, max)
75	}
76

```text
1	// Package lockx provides a cross-platform advisory lock over a directory.
2	//
3	// It is a leaf package on purpose. Both the catalog store and Git transaction
4	// code need to serialize mutations, and neither should have to depend on the
5	// other to get a lock.
6	package lockx
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"os"
13		"path/filepath"
14		"sync"
15	)
16	
17	// Lease holds one acquired directory lock until Close. Close is idempotent.
18	type Lease struct {
19		lock  *fileLock
20		label string
21		once  sync.Once
22		err   error
23	}
24	
25	// AcquireDir acquires the same cross-process lock used by WithDir. The lock file
26	// lives beside dir rather than inside it, so locking never adds a file to the
27	// directory being protected.
28	func AcquireDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (*Lease, error) {
29		if ctx == nil {
30			ctx = context.Background()
31		}
32		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
33			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
34		}
35		absoluteDir, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
36		if err != nil {
37			return nil, fmt.Errorf("make %s directory absolute for lock: %w", label, err)
38		}
39		canonicalDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absoluteDir)
40		if err != nil {
41			return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
42		}
43		lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")
44		lock, err := acquire(ctx, lockPath)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, fmt.Errorf("acquire %s lock: %w", label, err)
47		}
48		return &Lease{lock: lock, label: label}, nil
49	}
50	
51	// Close releases the acquired directory lock.
52	func (l *Lease) Close() error {
53		if l == nil {
54			return nil
55		}
56		l.once.Do(func() {
57			if err := l.lock.Close(); err != nil {
58				l.err = fmt.Errorf("release %s lock: %w", l.label, err)
59			}
60		})
61		return l.err
62	}
63	
64	// WithDir runs operation while holding an exclusive lock for dir.
65	func WithDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string, operation func() error) (err error) {
66		if operation == nil {
67			return fmt.Errorf("%s lock requires an operation", label)
68		}
69		lease, err := AcquireDir(ctx, dir, label)
70		if err != nil {
71			return err
72		}
73		defer func() { err = errors.Join(err, lease.Close()) }()
74		return operation()
75	}
76

1	//go:build unix
2	
3	package lockx
4	
5	import (
6		"context"
7		"errors"
8		"os"
9		"time"
10	
11		"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
12	)
13	
14	type fileLock struct {
15		file *os.File
16	}
17	
18	func acquire(ctx context.Context, path string) (*fileLock, error) {
19		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
20			return nil, err
21		}
22		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
23		if err != nil {
24			return nil, err
25		}
26		lock := &fileLock{file: file}
27		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
28		defer ticker.Stop()
29		for {
30			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
31				_ = file.Close()
32				return nil, err
33			}
34			err = unix.Flock(int(file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_EX|unix.LOCK_NB)
35			if err == nil {
36				return lock, nil
37			}
38			if !errors.Is(err, unix.EWOULDBLOCK) && !errors.Is(err, unix.EAGAIN) && !errors.Is(err, unix.EINTR) {
39				_ = file.Close()
40				return nil, err
41			}
42			select {
43			case <-ctx.Done():
44				_ = file.Close()
45				return nil, ctx.Err()
46			case <-ticker.C:
47			}
48		}
49	}
50	
51	func (l *fileLock) Close() error {
52		unlockErr := unix.Flock(int(l.file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_UN)
53		return errors.Join(unlockErr, l.file.Close())
54	}
55

11		"golang.org/x/sys/windows"
12	)
13	
14	type fileLock struct {
15		file       *os.File
16		overlapped windows.Overlapped
17	}
18	
19	func acquire(ctx context.Context, path string) (*fileLock, error) {
20		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
21			return nil, err
22		}
23		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
24		if err != nil {
25			return nil, err
26		}
27		lock := &fileLock{file: file}
28		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
29		defer ticker.Stop()
30		for {
31			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
32				_ = file.Close()
33				return nil, err
34			}
35			err = windows.LockFileEx(windows.Handle(file.Fd()),
36				windows.LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK|windows.LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY,
37				0, 1, 0, &lock.overlapped)
38			if err == nil {
39				return lock, nil
40			}
41			if !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION) && !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_IO_PENDING) {
42				_ = file.Close()
43				return nil, err
44			}
45			select {
46			case <-ctx.Done():
47				_ = file.Close()
48				return nil, ctx.Err()
49			case <-ticker.C:
50			}
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func (l *fileLock) Close() error {
55		unlockErr := windows.UnlockFileEx(windows.Handle(l.file.Fd()), 0, 1, 0, &l.overlapped)
56		return errors.Join(unlockErr, l.file.Close())
57	}

70			} else if errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrNotRegular) {
71				message = "lock path is not a regular file"

165		groups := map[string][]string{}

168			if normalized == "" {
169				normalized = normalizedName(name)
170			}
171			groups[normalized] = append(groups[normalized], name)

211	// find applies deterministic lock matching: exact spelling wins; a normalized
212	// spelling is accepted only when it identifies one lock entry.
213	func (document lockDocument) find(name string) (LockMetadata, bool) {
214		if entry, ok := document.Entries[name]; ok {
215			return entry, true
216		}
217		names := document.namesByNormalized()[normalizedName(name)]
218		if len(names) != 1 {
219			return LockMetadata{}, false
220		}
221		entry, ok := document.Entries[names[0]]
222		return entry, ok
223	}
224	
225	func (document lockDocument) candidates(normalized string) []LockMetadata {
226		names := document.namesByNormalized()[normalized]
227		entries := make([]LockMetadata, 0, len(names))
228		for _, name := range names {
229			entries = append(entries, document.Entries[name])
230		}
231		return entries
232	}
233	
234	func globalLockPath() string {
235		if stateHome := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XDG_STATE_HOME")); filepath.IsAbs(stateHome) {
236			return filepath.Join(filepath.Clean(stateHome), "skills", ".skill-lock.json")
237		}
238		home := homeDirectory()
239		if home == "" {
240			return ""
241		}
242		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", ".skill-lock.json")
243	}
244	
245	// GlobalLockPath returns the native global lock location. Relative
246	// XDG_STATE_HOME values are ignored as required by the XDG specification.
247	func GlobalLockPath() string { return globalLockPath() }
248	
249	func normalizedName(value string) string {
250		value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
251		var builder strings.Builder
252		lastDash := false
253		for _, character := range value {
254			valid := character >= 'a' && character <= 'z' || character >= '0' && character <= '9' || character == '.' || character == '_'
255			if valid {
256				builder.WriteRune(character)
257				lastDash = false
258			} else if !lastDash {
259				builder.WriteByte('-')
260				lastDash = true
261			}
262		}
263		return strings.Trim(builder.String(), "-")
264	}
265
```

103	func globalScanLocations(definitions []AgentDefinition) []physicalScanLocation {
104		logical := make([]logicalScanLocation, 0, len(definitions))
105		for _, definition := range definitions {
106			if definition.GlobalSkillsDir == "" {
107				continue
108			}
109			logical = append(logical, logicalScanLocation{
110				Path: definition.GlobalSkillsDir, AgentIDs: []string{definition.ID},
111			})
112		}
113		return dedupeScanLocations(logical)
114	}

116	// dedupeScanLocations first coalesces identical registry paths, then aliases to
117	// the same physical directory. The latter retains every logical path and agent
118	// attribution while ensuring the directory is read only once.
119	func dedupeScanLocations(input []logicalScanLocation) []physicalScanLocation {
120		byLogical := map[string]*logicalScanLocation{}
121		for _, location := range input {
122			path := filepath.Clean(location.Path)
123			current := byLogical[path]
124			if current == nil {
125				copy := logicalScanLocation{Path: path}
126				byLogical[path] = &copy
127				current = &copy
128			}
129			current.AgentIDs = append(current.AgentIDs, location.AgentIDs...)
130		}
131		logicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byLogical))
132		for path := range byLogical {
133			logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, path)
134		}
135		sort.Strings(logicalPaths)
136	
137		byPhysical := map[string]*physicalScanLocation{}
138		for _, path := range logicalPaths {
139			logical := *byLogical[path]
140			logical.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(logical.AgentIDs)
141			physical := path
142			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
143				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
144			}
145			group := byPhysical[physical]
146			if group == nil {
147				group = &physicalScanLocation{Path: physical}
148				byPhysical[physical] = group
149			}
150			group.Logical = append(group.Logical, logical)
151		}
152		physicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byPhysical))
153		for path := range byPhysical {
154			physicalPaths = append(physicalPaths, path)
155		}
156		sort.Strings(physicalPaths)
157		result := make([]physicalScanLocation, 0, len(physicalPaths))
158		for _, path := range physicalPaths {
159			group := byPhysical[path]
160			sort.Slice(group.Logical, func(i, j int) bool { return group.Logical[i].Path < group.Logical[j].Path })
161			result = append(result, *group)
162		}
163		return result
164	}

166	func scanScope(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, locations []physicalScanLocation, document lockDocument) ([]Skill, []Diagnostic) {
167		diagnostics := decorateDiagnostics(document.Diagnostics, target)
168		var scanned []scannedSkill
169		for _, location := range locations {
170			if ctx.Err() != nil {
171				break
172			}
173			found, foundDiagnostics := scanLocation(ctx, scope, target, location)
174			scanned = append(scanned, found...)
175			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, foundDiagnostics...)
176		}
177	
178		groups := map[string]*skillAggregate{}
179		normalizedInstalled := map[string][]string{}
180		for _, found := range scanned {
181			group := groups[found.Name]
182			if group == nil {
183				group = &skillAggregate{Installations: map[string]*Installation{}}
184				groups[found.Name] = group
185			}
186			group.Names = append(group.Names, found.Name)
187			normalized := normalizedName(found.Name)
188			normalizedInstalled[normalized] = append(normalizedInstalled[normalized], found.Name)
189			physical := found.Installation.RealPath
190			installation := group.Installations[physical]
191			if installation == nil {
192				copy := found.Installation
193				group.Installations[physical] = &copy
194				installation = &copy
195			} else {
196				installation.LogicalPaths = append(installation.LogicalPaths, found.Installation.LogicalPaths...)
197				installation.AgentIDs = append(installation.AgentIDs, found.Installation.AgentIDs...)
198			}
199			installation.LogicalPaths = uniqueSorted(installation.LogicalPaths)
200			installation.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(installation.AgentIDs)
201			if len(installation.LogicalPaths) > 0 {
202				installation.Path = installation.LogicalPaths[0]
203			}
204			installation.Attribution = registryAttribution(installation.AgentIDs)
205		}
206	
207		for normalized, names := range normalizedInstalled {
208			names = uniqueSorted(names)
209			normalizedInstalled[normalized] = names
210			if len(names) > 1 {
211				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
212					Kind: DiagnosticNameCollision, Scope: scope, Name: normalized,
213					Message: fmt.Sprintf("installed skill names %s normalize to %q", strings.Join(names, ", "), normalized),
214				}, target))
215			}
216		}
217		exactNames := make([]string, 0, len(groups))
218		for name := range groups {
219			exactNames = append(exactNames, name)
220		}
221		sort.Strings(exactNames)
222		consumedLocks := map[string]bool{}
223		rows := make([]Skill, 0, len(groups)+len(document.Entries))
224		for _, name := range exactNames {
225			group := groups[name]
226			normalized := normalizedName(name)
227			var lock LockMetadata
228			candidates := document.candidates(normalized)
229			matched := false
230			if exact, ok := document.Entries[name]; ok {
231				lock, matched = exact, true
232			} else if len(normalizedInstalled[normalized]) == 1 && len(candidates) == 1 {
233				lock, matched = candidates[0], true
234			}
235			if matched {
236				consumedLocks[normalized] = true
237			}
238			rows = append(rows, buildPresentRow(scope, scopeRoot, target, name, group, lock, candidates, matched))
239		}
240	
241		lockGroups := document.namesByNormalized()
242		lockNormalized := make([]string, 0, len(lockGroups))
243		for normalized := range lockGroups {
244			lockNormalized = append(lockNormalized, normalized)
245		}
246		sort.Strings(lockNormalized)
247		for _, normalized := range lockNormalized {
248			if consumedLocks[normalized] {
249				continue
250			}
251			candidates := document.candidates(normalized)
252			if len(candidates) == 0 {
253				continue
254			}
255			selected := candidates[0]
256			rows = append(rows, buildMissingRow(scope, scopeRoot, target, selected, candidates))
257		}
258		return rows, diagnostics
259	}

261	func scanLocation(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, target agenttarget.Target, location physicalScanLocation) ([]scannedSkill, []Diagnostic) {
262		entries, err := os.ReadDir(location.Path)
263		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
264			return nil, nil
265		}
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, []Diagnostic{decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
268				Kind: DiagnosticSkillUnreadable, Scope: scope, Path: location.Path,
269				Message: fmt.Sprintf("could not read skills directory: %v", err),
270			}, target)}
271		}
272		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Name() < entries[j].Name() })
273	
274		var skills []scannedSkill
275		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
276		for _, entry := range entries {
277			if ctx.Err() != nil {
278				break
279			}
280			child := filepath.Join(location.Path, entry.Name())
281			info, err := os.Stat(child)
282			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
283				continue
284			}
285			if err != nil {
286				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
287					Kind: DiagnosticSkillUnreadable, Scope: scope, Path: child,
288					Message: fmt.Sprintf("could not inspect skill directory: %v", err),
289				}, target))
290				continue
291			}
292			if !info.IsDir() {
293				continue
294			}
295			name, present, err := readSkillName(filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"))
296			if !present {
297				continue
298			}
299			if err != nil {
300				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
301					Kind: DiagnosticSkillFrontmatter, Scope: scope,
302					Path: filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"), Message: err.Error(),
303				}, target))
304				continue
305			}
306			physical := child
307			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(child); err == nil {
308				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
309			}
310			var logicalPaths, agentIDs []string
311			for _, logical := range location.Logical {
312				logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, filepath.Join(logical.Path, entry.Name()))
313				agentIDs = append(agentIDs, logical.AgentIDs...)
314			}
315			logicalPaths = uniqueSorted(logicalPaths)
316			agentIDs = uniqueSorted(agentIDs)
317			installation := Installation{
318				RealPath: physical, LogicalPaths: logicalPaths, AgentIDs: agentIDs,
319				Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs), Integrity: IntegrityUnknown,
320			}
321			if len(logicalPaths) > 0 {
322				installation.Path = logicalPaths[0]
323			}
324			skills = append(skills, scannedSkill{Name: name, Installation: installation})
325		}
326		return skills, diagnostics
327	}

329	func readSkillName(filename string) (string, bool, error) {
330		file, _, err := safefile.OpenRegular(filename)
331		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
332			return "", false, nil
333		}
334		if errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrNotRegular) {
335			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md is not a regular file")
336		}
337		if err != nil {
338			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", err)
339		}
340		defer file.Close()
341	
342		// Bound only the frontmatter, not the skill body. A valid skill may have a
343		// large reference body, and inventory never needs to read it.
344		reader := bufio.NewReader(io.LimitReader(file, maxFrontmatterBytes+1))
345		first, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
346		consumed := int64(len(first))
347		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
348			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", readErr)
349		}
350		first = strings.TrimPrefix(first, string(rune(0xfeff)))
351		if strings.TrimSpace(first) != "---" {
352			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter")
353		}
354		var frontmatter strings.Builder
355		closed := false
356		for {
357			line, lineErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
358			consumed += int64(len(line))
359			if consumed > maxFrontmatterBytes {
360				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter exceeds %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
361			}
362			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "---" {
363				closed = true
364				break
365			}
366			frontmatter.WriteString(line)
367			if lineErr != nil {
368				if errors.Is(lineErr, io.EOF) {
369					break
370				}
371				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", lineErr)
372			}
373		}
374		if !closed {
375			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter is not closed within %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
376		}
377		var metadata struct {
378			Name        string `yaml:"name"`
379			Description string `yaml:"description"`
380		}
381		if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(frontmatter.String()), &metadata); err != nil {
382			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("invalid SKILL.md YAML frontmatter: %w", err)
383		}
384		metadata.Name = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Name)
385		metadata.Description = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Description)
386		if metadata.Name == "" || metadata.Description == "" {
387			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter requires name and description")
388		}
389		if len(metadata.Name) > 256 || normalizedName(metadata.Name) == "" || !safeDisplayValue(metadata.Name) {
390			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter name is invalid")
391		}
392		return metadata.Name, true, nil
393	}

395	func buildPresentRow(scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, name string, group *skillAggregate, lock LockMetadata, candidates []LockMetadata, matched bool) Skill {
396		installations := make([]Installation, 0, len(group.Installations))
397		for _, installation := range group.Installations {
398			installation.LogicalPaths = uniqueSorted(installation.LogicalPaths)
399			installation.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(installation.AgentIDs)
400			installation.Attribution = registryAttribution(installation.AgentIDs)
401			installations = append(installations, *installation)
402		}
403		sort.Slice(installations, func(i, j int) bool {
404			if installations[i].RealPath != installations[j].RealPath {
405				return installations[i].RealPath < installations[j].RealPath
406			}
407			return installations[i].Path < installations[j].Path
408		})
409		var agents []string
410		for _, installation := range installations {
411			agents = append(agents, installation.AgentIDs...)
412		}
413		agentIDs := uniqueSorted(agents)
414		agents = agentDisplayNames(agentIDs)
415		row := Skill{
416			Name: name, Scope: scope, ScopeRoot: scopeRoot,
417			Agents: agents, Repository: target.RepoDisplay, RepositoryPath: target.RepoPath,
418			Checkout: target.CheckoutRoot, Installations: installations, Presence: PresencePresent,
419			Integrity: IntegrityUnknown, Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs),
420			RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion, LockCandidates: append([]LockMetadata(nil), candidates...),
421			ManagedBy: ManagedByExternal, UpdateStatus: UpdateUnknown,
422			UpdateDetail: "not tracked by the skills CLI",
423		}
424		if len(installations) > 0 {
425			row.Path = installations[0].Path
426		}
427		if directManagedSkillName(name) {
428			if name == skill.Name {
429				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByDev
430				row.Source = "dev binary"
431				applyBundledIntegrity(&row)
432				row.UpdateStatus, row.UpdateDetail = bundledStatus(row.Integrity, row.IntegrityDetail)
433			} else {
434				row.UpdateDetail = "name is reserved for the binary-managed dev-cli skill"
435			}
436			return row
437		}
438		if matched {
439			copy := lock
440			row.Lock = &copy
441			row.ManagedBy = ManagedBySkills
442			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnchecked
443			row.UpdateDetail = ""
444			row.Source, row.SourceURL = sourceDisplay(lock.Source), sourceDisplay(lock.SourceURL)
445			row.SourceType = safeSourceType(lock.SourceType)
446			return row
447		}
448		if len(candidates) > 1 {
449			row.UpdateDetail = "ambiguous normalized lock names; no lock entry selected"
450		}
451		return row
452	}

454	func buildMissingRow(scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, lock LockMetadata, candidates []LockMetadata) Skill {
455		copy := lock
456		row := Skill{
457			Name: lock.Name, Scope: scope, ScopeRoot: scopeRoot, Agents: []string{},
458			Source: sourceDisplay(lock.Source), SourceURL: sourceDisplay(lock.SourceURL),
459			SourceType: safeSourceType(lock.SourceType),

482	func applyBundledIntegrity(row *Skill) {
483		files, err := skill.Files()
484		if err != nil {
485			row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
486			row.IntegrityDetail = err.Error()
487			return
488		}
489		row.Integrity = IntegrityVerified
490		row.IntegrityDetail = "all embedded files match this dev binary"
491		for index := range row.Installations {
492			status, detail := bundledIntegrity(row.Installations[index].RealPath, files)
493			row.Installations[index].Integrity = status
494			row.Installations[index].IntegrityDetail = detail
495			if status == IntegrityDrifted {
496				row.Integrity = IntegrityDrifted
497				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
498			} else if status == IntegrityUnknown && row.Integrity != IntegrityDrifted {
499				row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
500				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
501			}
502		}
503	}
504	
505	func bundledIntegrity(directory string, files map[string][]byte) (Integrity, string) {
506		for relative, want := range files {
507			got, err := safefile.ReadRegular(context.Background(), filepath.Join(directory, relative), int64(len(want))+1)
508			if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
509				return IntegrityDrifted, "bundled skill differs; run `dev skill install`"
510			}
511		}
512		return IntegrityVerified, "all embedded files match this dev binary"
513	}
514	
515	// bundledStatus preserves the legacy update-status contract while deriving it
516	// from the already-computed aggregate integrity across every installation.
517	func bundledStatus(integrity Integrity, detail string) (UpdateStatus, string) {
518		if integrity == IntegrityVerified {
519			return UpdateCurrent, detail
520		}
521		if integrity == IntegrityDrifted {
522			return UpdateAvailable, detail
523		}
524		return UpdateFailed, detail
525	}
526	
527	func sourceDisplay(value string) string {
528		if value == "" {
529			return ""
530		}
531		if !safeDisplayValue(value) {
532			return "[redacted]"
533		}
534		value = repo.RedactCloneRef(value)
535		parsed, err := url.Parse(value)
536		if err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" {
537			parsed.User = nil
538			parsed.RawQuery = ""
539			parsed.ForceQuery = false
540			parsed.Fragment = ""
541			return parsed.String()
542		}
543		return value
544	}
545	
546	func safeSourceType(value string) string {
547		if value == "" || safeDisplayValue(value) {
548			return value
549		}
550		return "[redacted]"
551	}
552	
553	func registryAttribution(agentIDs []string) Attribution {
554		return Attribution{Registry: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion, AgentIDs: uniqueSorted(agentIDs)}
555	}
556	
557	func decorateDiagnostics(input []Diagnostic, target agenttarget.Target) []Diagnostic {
558		result := make([]Diagnostic, len(input))
559		for index, diagnostic := range input {
560			result[index] = decorateDiagnostic(diagnostic, target)
561		}
562		return result
563	}
564	
565	func decorateDiagnostic(diagnostic Diagnostic, target agenttarget.Target) Diagnostic {
566		diagnostic.Repository = target.RepoDisplay
567		diagnostic.RepositoryPath = target.RepoPath
568		diagnostic.Checkout = target.CheckoutRoot
569		return diagnostic
570	}

23	// MutationProvider describes the explicit installer boundary without running
24	// it. Repository-scoped mutations require a direct executable: invoking npx in
25	// an untrusted checkout could substitute a repository-local binary.
26	type MutationProvider struct {
27		Available bool
28		Command   string
29		Path      string
30		Detail    string
31	}
32	
33	// MutationCommand keeps provider execution behind one host-wide lock. Callers
34	// may either Run directly or Prepare the underlying process for Bubble Tea.
35	type MutationCommand struct {
36		Command *exec.Cmd
37		ctx     context.Context
38	}
39	
40	// Prepare acquires the provider mutation lock and returns an idempotent
41	// completion callback that joins process and release errors.
42	func (m *MutationCommand) Prepare() (*exec.Cmd, func(error) error, error) {
43		if m == nil || m.Command == nil {
44			return nil, nil, errors.New("skill mutation command is empty")
45		}
46		ctx := m.ctx
47		if ctx == nil {
48			ctx = context.Background()
49		}
50		cache, err := os.UserCacheDir()
51		if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(cache) {
52			return nil, nil, errors.New("could not resolve the user cache for skill mutation locking")
53		}
54		lease, err := lockx.AcquireDir(ctx, filepath.Join(cache, "dev-cli", "skill-mutation"), "agent skill mutation")
55		if err != nil {
56			return nil, nil, err
57		}
58		var once sync.Once
59		var result error
60		finish := func(processErr error) error {
61			once.Do(func() { result = errors.Join(processErr, lease.Close()) })
62			return result
63		}
64		return m.Command, finish, nil
65	}
66	
67	// Run executes the provider while holding the host-wide mutation lock.
68	func (m *MutationCommand) Run() error {
69		command, finish, err := m.Prepare()
70		if err != nil {
71			return err
72		}
73		return finish(command.Run())
74	}

76	// MutationProviderStatus performs path lookup only. It is suitable for doctor
77	// and other read-only status surfaces because it never starts skills, npx, npm,
78	// or project code.
79	func MutationProviderStatus() MutationProvider {
80		return MutationProviderStatusFor("")
81	}

83	// MutationProviderStatusFor rejects a provider inside projectRoot in addition
84	// to npm-local shims. The selected repository never supplies the program that
85	// mutates it.
86	func MutationProviderStatusFor(projectRoot string) MutationProvider {
87		var rejected string
88		for _, path := range skillsExecutableCandidates() {
89			if resolved, trusted := trustedSkillsExecutable(path, projectRoot); trusted {
90				return MutationProvider{Available: true, Command: "skills", Path: resolved, Detail: "skills executable available"}
91			}
92			if rejected == "" {
93				rejected = path
94			}
95		}
96		if rejected != "" {
97			return MutationProvider{Path: rejected, Detail: "skills executable resolves inside the selected repository or node_modules; install a trusted global executable"}
98		}
99		if path, err := exec.LookPath("npx"); err == nil {
100			return MutationProvider{
101				Path:   path,
102				Detail: "npx found but not invoked from repository checkouts; install the `skills` executable for add/update",
103			}
104		}
105		return MutationProvider{Detail: "skills executable is not installed"}

108	func skillsExecutableCandidates() []string {
109		seen := map[string]bool{}
110		var candidates []string
111		for _, directory := range filepath.SplitList(os.Getenv("PATH")) {
112			if directory == "" {
113				directory = "."
114			}
115			candidate, err := filepath.Abs(filepath.Join(directory, "skills"))
116			if err != nil {
117				continue
118			}
119			found, err := exec.LookPath(candidate)
120			if err != nil {
121				continue
122			}
123			key := filepath.Clean(found)
124			if seen[key] {

128			candidates = append(candidates, found)

148			if err != nil || inside {

150			}
151		}

199		candidate, candidateErr := filepath.Abs(candidate)

205			!strings.HasPrefix(relative, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))

238	func InstallCommand(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, source string, names, agents []string) (*MutationCommand, error) {

265		p, err := interactiveProvider(root)
266		if err != nil {

268		}
269		args := []string{"add", source, "--skill"}
270		args = append(args, names...)
271		args = append(args, "--agent")
272		args = append(args, agents...)
273		args = append(args, "--yes")
274		return &MutationCommand{Command: p.command(ctx, root, args...), ctx: ctx}, nil
275	}

277	// UpdateCommand updates exactly one lock-managed skill in exactly one scope.
278	func UpdateCommand(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, name string, scope Scope) (*MutationCommand, error) {
279		if directManagedSkillName(name) {
280			return nil, errors.New("dev-cli is managed by the dev binary, not the skills provider")
281		}
282		if !safeProviderSkillName(name) {
283			return nil, errors.New("skill name is not safe to pass to the provider")
284		}

286			return nil, errors.New("skill update requires project or global scope")
287		}
288		root, err := canonicalMutationRoot(projectRoot, false)
289		if err != nil {
290			return nil, err
291		}
292		p, err := interactiveProvider(root)
293		if err != nil {

295		}
296		args := []string{"update", "--yes"}
297		if scope == ScopeGlobal {
298			args = append(args, "--global")
299		} else {
300			args = append(args, "--project")
301		}
302		args = append(args, name)
303		return &MutationCommand{Command: p.command(ctx, root, args...), ctx: ctx}, nil
304	}

307	// falls back to npx, even with --no-install, because version probes are reads.
308	func ProviderVersion(ctx context.Context, cwd string) (string, error) {
309		status := MutationProviderStatusFor(cwd)
310		if !status.Available {
311			return "", errors.New(status.Detail)
312		}

314		cmd := p.command(ctx, cwd, "--version")
315		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
316		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
317		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
318			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
319			if detail == "" {
320				detail = err.Error()
321			}
322			return "", fmt.Errorf("skills: %s", detail)
323		}
324		return "skills " + strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
325	}

286	func normalizeRecordedHash(metadata *LockMetadata) {
287		metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = "", ""

289		folder := strings.TrimSpace(metadata.SkillFolderHash)

292		setFolderHash := func(hash string) bool {
293			switch {
294			case validHexHash(hash, 40):
295				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "git-tree"
296				return true
297			case validHexHash(hash, 64):
298				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = hash, "sha256-folder"
299				return true
300			default:
301				return false
302			}
303		}
304		if metadata.Scope == ScopeGlobal {
305			if setFolderHash(folder) {
306				return
307			}
308			if validHexHash(content, 64) {
309				metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
310			}
311			return
312		}
313		if validHexHash(computed, 64) {
314			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = computed, "sha256-folder"
315			return
316		}
317		// Scope-less package tests and older callers may still supply either global
318		// representation; parsed project-v1 locks never reach this branch with them.
319		if metadata.Scope == "" && setFolderHash(folder) {
320			return
321		}
322		if metadata.Scope == "" && validHexHash(content, 64) {
323			metadata.RecordedHash, metadata.HashKind = content, "sha256-skill-file"
324		}
325	}

330		}

335	func checkOneResult(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, row Skill) (UpdateStatus, string) {
336		entry := skillLock(row)
337		if entry == nil {
338			return UpdateUnknown, "skill has no lock metadata"
339		}
340		folder, ok := safeSkillFolder(entry.SkillPath)
341		if !ok {
342			return UpdateUnknown, "invalid skill path in lock entry"
343		}
344		expected, kind := entry.RecordedHash, entry.HashKind
345		if expected == "" {
346			copy := *entry
347			normalizeRecordedHash(&copy)
348			expected, kind = copy.RecordedHash, copy.HashKind
349		}
350		var actual string
351		var hashErr error
352		switch kind {
353		case "git-tree":
354			spec := "HEAD^{tree}"
355			if folder != "" {
356				spec = "HEAD:" + folder
357			}
358			actual, hashErr = gitOutput(ctx, repoDir, "rev-parse", "--verify", spec)
359		case "sha256-folder":
360			actual, hashErr = gitFolderHashContext(ctx, repoDir, folder)
361		case "sha256-skill-file":
362			actual, hashErr = gitSkillFileHashContext(ctx, repoDir, folder)
363		}
364		if hashErr != nil {
365			switch {
366			case ctx.Err() != nil:
367				return UpdateFailed, "update check canceled"
368			case errors.Is(hashErr, errGitSkillPathMissing):
369				return UpdateMissing, "skill path no longer exists upstream"
370			case errors.Is(hashErr, errProviderHashOrdering):
371				return UpdateUnknown, "lock hash ordering is unverifiable for non-ASCII paths"
372			default:
373				return UpdateFailed, "could not compute upstream content hash"
374			}
375		}
376		if expected == "" || actual == "" {
377			return UpdateUnknown, "lock entry has no comparable content hash"
378		}
379		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(actual), strings.TrimSpace(expected)) {
380			return UpdateCurrent, "matches the recorded upstream content"
381		}
382		return UpdateAvailable, "upstream content changed"
383	}

385	func safeSkillFolder(skillPath string) (string, bool) {
386		p := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(skillPath), "\\", "/")
387		if p == "" || strings.ContainsRune(p, '\x00') {
388			return "", false
389		}
390		// filepath.VolumeName follows the host OS, so reject a Windows drive prefix
391		// explicitly even when dev is checking a lock file on Unix.
392		if len(p) >= 2 && p[1] == ':' && ((p[0] >= 'a' && p[0] <= 'z') || (p[0] >= 'A' && p[0] <= 'Z')) {
393			return "", false
394		}
395		if strings.EqualFold(path.Base(p), "SKILL.md") {
396			p = path.Dir(p)
397		}
398		if p == "." {
399			p = ""
400		}
401		clean := path.Clean(p)
402		if clean == "." {
403			clean = ""
404		}
405		if path.IsAbs(clean) || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") || filepath.VolumeName(filepath.FromSlash(clean)) != "" {
406			return "", false
407		}
408		return clean, true
409	}

416	func gitFolderHashContext(ctx context.Context, repoDir, folder string) (string, error) {
417		files, err := gitTreeFiles(ctx, repoDir, folder)
418		if err != nil {

428			if order := collator.CompareString(files[i].name, files[j].name); order != 0 {
429				return order < 0
430			}
431			return files[i].name < files[j].name
432		})
433		hash := sha256.New()
434		for _, file := range files {
435			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
436				return "", err

438			_, _ = io.WriteString(hash, file.name)
439			if err := writeGitBlob(ctx, repoDir, file.oid, hash); err != nil {
440				return "", err
441			}
442		}
443		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
444	}
