171				codes = append(codes, code)
172				continue
173			}
174			convertClaudeServer(&row, server)
175			if state != nil {
176				enabled, disabled := state.enabled[row.Name], state.disabled[row.Name]
177				switch {
178				case enabled && disabled:
179					addPolicy(&row, PolicyAllowed, "declared", 0)
180					addPolicy(&row, PolicyExcluded, "declared", 0)
181					addCoverage(&row, DiagnosticInvalidDeclaration)
182				case enabled:
183					value := true
184					row.Enabled = &value
185					addPolicy(&row, PolicyAllowed, "declared", 0)
186				case disabled:
187					value := false
188					row.Enabled = &value
189					addPolicy(&row, PolicyExcluded, "declared", 0)
190				}
191			}
192			finalizeDeclaration(&row)
193			rows = append(rows, row)
194		}
195		return rows, codes
196	}

198	func convertClaudeServer(row *Declaration, server claudeServer) {
199		setCommand(row, server.Command)
200		inspectArguments(row, server.Args)
201		inspectEnvironment(row, server.Env)
202		setEndpoint(row, server.URL)
203		inspectHeaders(row, server.Headers)
204		inspectHelper(row, strings.TrimSpace(server.HeadersHelper) != "")
205		if server.AlwaysLoad != nil {
206			addBooleanPolicy(row, PolicyAlwaysLoad, *server.AlwaysLoad)
207		}
208		if server.OAuth != nil {
209			addPolicy(row, PolicyOAuth, "configured", 0)
210			inspectOAuthValue(row, "client-id", server.OAuth.ClientID)
211			inspectOAuthValue(row, "metadata-url", server.OAuth.AuthServerMetadataURL)
212			inspectOAuthValue(row, "scopes", server.OAuth.Scopes)
213		}
214	
215		typeName := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(server.Type))
216		hasCommand := strings.TrimSpace(server.Command) != ""
217		hasURL := strings.TrimSpace(server.URL) != ""
218		if hasCommand && hasURL {
219			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticConflictingTransport)
220		}
221		switch typeName {
222		case "stdio":
223			if hasCommand {
224				row.Transport = TransportStdio
225			}
226		case "http":
227			if hasURL {
228				row.Transport = TransportHTTP
229			}
230		case "streamable-http":
231			if hasURL {
232				row.Transport = TransportStreamableHTTP
233			}
234		case "sse":
235			if hasURL {
236				row.Transport = TransportSSE
237			}
238		case "ws", "websocket":
239			if hasURL {
240				row.Transport = TransportWebSocket
241			}
242		case "":
243			if hasCommand && !hasURL {
244				row.Transport = TransportStdio
245			}
246		}
247		if row.Transport == TransportUnknown {
248			addCoverage(row, DiagnosticUnknownTransport)
249		}
250	}

254		for _, name := range names {
255			if normalized, ok := normalizedName(name); ok {
256				set[normalized] = true
257			}
258		}
259		return set
260	}

262	func sortedRawNames(values map[string]json.RawMessage) []string {
263		names := make([]string, 0, len(values))
264		for name := range values {
265			names = append(names, name)
266		}
267		sort.Strings(names)

271	func matchClaudeTarget(projectPath string, targets []Target) (Target, bool) {
272		if projectPath == "" || stringContainsControl(projectPath) {
273			return Target{}, false
274		}
275		candidate, err := filepath.Abs(projectPath)
276		if err != nil {
277			return Target{}, false
278		}
279		candidate = filepath.Clean(candidate)
280		candidateCanonical := candidate
281		if resolved, err := pathx.Canonical(candidate); err == nil {
282			candidateCanonical = resolved
283		}
284	
285		for _, target := range targets {
286			checkout := filepath.Clean(target.CheckoutRoot)
287			checkoutCanonical := checkout
288			if resolved, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout); err == nil {
289				checkoutCanonical = resolved
290			}
291			if candidate == checkout || candidateCanonical == checkoutCanonical {
292				return target, true
293			}
294		}
295	
296		bestIndex, bestDepth := -1, -1
297		for index, target := range targets {
298			inside, err := pathx.Contains(target.CheckoutRoot, candidate)
299			if err != nil || !inside {
300				continue
301			}
302			checkout := filepath.Clean(target.CheckoutRoot)
303			if resolved, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout); err == nil {
304				checkout = resolved
305			}
306			if depth := len(checkout); depth > bestDepth {
307				bestIndex, bestDepth = index, depth
308			}
309		}
310		if bestIndex >= 0 {
311			return targets[bestIndex], true
312		}
313		return Target{}, false
314	}

317		if value == nil {
318			return nil
319		}
320		copy := *value
321		return &copy
322	}

224	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
225		if ctx == nil {

228		targets = normalizeTargets(targets, s.options.WorkingDirectory)

239		reads := map[string]*cachedRead{}
240		readSource := func(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
241			key := spec.path + "\x00" + spec.projectRoot
242			readMu.Lock()
243			entry := reads[key]
244			if entry == nil {
245				entry = &cachedRead{ready: make(chan struct{})}
246				reads[key] = entry
247				readMu.Unlock()
248				entry.result = s.readSource(ctx, spec)
249				close(entry.ready)
250				return entry.result
251			}
252			readMu.Unlock()

254			case <-ctx.Done():
255				return readResult{}

257				return entry.result

263				finalizeResult(&result)

333	func normalizeOptions(options Options) Options {
334		if options.WorkingDirectory == "" {
335			options.WorkingDirectory, _ = os.Getwd()
336		}
337		if options.XDGConfigHome != "" && !filepath.IsAbs(options.XDGConfigHome) {
338			options.XDGConfigHome = ""
339		}
340		if options.CodexHome != "" && !filepath.IsAbs(options.CodexHome) {
341			options.CodexHome = ""
342		}
343		if options.GeminiCLIHome != "" && !filepath.IsAbs(options.GeminiCLIHome) {
344			options.GeminiCLIHome = ""
345		}
346		for _, path := range []*string{&options.ClaudeUserConfigPath, &options.ClaudeUserSettingsPath, &options.ClaudeManagedConfigPath} {
347			if *path != "" && !filepath.IsAbs(*path) {
348				*path = ""
349			}
350		}
351		managedSettings := options.ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths[:0]
352		for _, path := range options.ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths {
353			if filepath.IsAbs(path) {
354				managedSettings = append(managedSettings, filepath.Clean(path))
355			}
356		}
357		options.ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths = managedSettings
358		if options.Concurrency <= 0 {
359			options.Concurrency = defaultConcurrency
360		} else if options.Concurrency > maximumConcurrency {
361			options.Concurrency = maximumConcurrency
362		}
363		if options.MaxFileBytes <= 0 {
364			options.MaxFileBytes = DefaultMaxFileBytes
365		} else if options.MaxFileBytes > maximumMaxFileBytes {
366			options.MaxFileBytes = maximumMaxFileBytes
367		}
368		if options.MaxSymlinkDepth <= 0 {
369			options.MaxSymlinkDepth = defaultSymlinkDepth
370		} else if options.MaxSymlinkDepth > maximumSymlinkDepth {
371			options.MaxSymlinkDepth = maximumSymlinkDepth
372		}
373		return options
374	}

376	func normalizeTargets(targets []Target, cwd string) []Target {
377		out := make([]Target, 0, len(targets))
378		for _, target := range targets {
379			if strings.TrimSpace(target.CheckoutRoot) == "" {
380				continue
381			}
382			checkout := target.CheckoutRoot
383			if !filepath.IsAbs(checkout) {
384				checkout = filepath.Join(cwd, checkout)
385			}
386			absolute, err := filepath.Abs(checkout)
387			if err != nil {
388				continue
389			}
390			target.CheckoutRoot = filepath.Clean(absolute)
391			if target.RepoPath == "" {
392				target.RepoPath = target.CheckoutRoot
393			} else if !filepath.IsAbs(target.RepoPath) {
394				target.RepoPath = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(cwd, target.RepoPath))
395			}
396			target.RepoDisplay = strings.TrimSpace(target.RepoDisplay)
397			if target.RepoDisplay == "" {
398				target.RepoDisplay = target.RepoName
399			}
400			if target.CommonDir == "" {
401				target.CommonDir = target.RepoPath
402			}
403			out = append(out, target)
404		}
405		return agenttarget.Dedupe(out)

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
106		if err != nil {
107			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
108			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
109			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
110			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
111		}
112		switch {
113		case rel == ".":
114			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
115		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
117		default:
118			return canonicalCandidate, nil
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
123	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
125		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
126		if err == nil {
127			return true, nil
128		}
129		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
130			return false, nil
131		}
132		return false, err
133	}
134	
135	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
136	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
137		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
138		if err != nil {
139			return false, err
140		}
141		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
142		if err != nil {
143			return false, err
144		}
145		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
146			return true, nil
147		}
148		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
149	}
150	
151	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
152	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
153	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
154	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
157			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
158		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
159			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
160		case component == "." || component == "..":
161			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
162		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
163			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
164		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
165			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
166		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
167			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
168		default:
169			return nil
170		}
171	}
172	
173	// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
174	// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
175	// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
176	// single component.
177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
178		if len(components) == 0 {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
180		}
181		for i, component := range components {
182			if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
183				return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
184			}
185		}
186		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
187		if err != nil {
188			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
189		}
190		return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
191	}
192	
193	func driveQualified(component string) bool {
194		if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
195			return false
196		}
197		letter := component[0]
198		return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'
199	}
200	
201	func hasParentTraversal(path string) bool {
202		for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool {
203			return r == '/' || r == '\\'
204		}) {
205			if component == ".." {
206				return true
207			}
208		}
209		return false
210	}

// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
// decision is made.
package pathx

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strings"
)

var (
	// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
	ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
	// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
	ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
	// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
	ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
	// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
	ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
)

// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
// before creating or moving anything into it.
func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
	if path == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
	}
	absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
	}
	absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)

	probe := absolute
	var missing []string
	for {
		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
		if err == nil {
			slices.Reverse(missing)
			parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
			return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
		}
		if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
		}
		// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
		// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
		// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
		// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
		// still-missing suffix.
		if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
			target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
			if readErr != nil {
				return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
			}
			if hasParentTraversal(target) {
				return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
			}
			if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
				target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
			}
			resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
			if resolveErr != nil {
				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
			}
			slices.Reverse(missing)
			parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
			return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
		} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
		if parent == probe {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
		}
		missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
		probe = parent
	}
}

// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
	if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
	}
	canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
	}
	canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
	}

	rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
	if err != nil {
		// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
		// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
		// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
	}
	switch {
	case rel == ".":
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
	case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
	default:
		return canonicalCandidate, nil
	}
}

// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
	_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
	if err == nil {
		return true, nil
	}
	if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
		return false, nil
	}
	return false, err
}

// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
	canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
		return true, nil
	}
	return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
}

// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
	switch {
	case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
		return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
	case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
		return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
	case component == "." || component == "..":
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	default:
		return nil
	}
}

// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
// single component.

	if len(components) == 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)

217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true

241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}

268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308

10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are

12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
16		// its own entry below the shared common directory.

26		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
27		MainRoot string
28		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
29		Bare bool
30	}
31	
32	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
33	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
34	
35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {

82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}

90	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
91	// a full Discover.
92	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
93		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
94		return err == nil

97	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
98	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
99	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
100	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
101	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
102		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
103			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
104				return b
105			}
106		}
107		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
108			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
109				return cand
110			}
111		}
112		return ""
113	}
114	
115	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
116	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
117		if name == "" {
118			name = "origin"
119		}
120		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return ""
123		}
124		return out
125	}
126	
127	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
128	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
129	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
130	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
131	// semantics should use Remote instead.
132	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
133		if commonDir == "" {
134			return ""
135		}
136		if name == "" {
137			name = "origin"
138		}
139		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
140		if err != nil {
141			return ""
142		}
143		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
144		section := ""
145		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
146			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
147			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
148				continue
149			}
150			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
151				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
152				continue
153			}
154			if section != want {
155				continue
156			}
157			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
158			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
159				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
160			}
161		}
162		return ""
163	}

```text
1	# Agent skills
2	
3	A provider-independent inventory of agent skills in the current checkout, any
4	selected repository, every configured repository, and global agent paths.
5	
6	## Reading the inventory
7	
8	```bash
9	dev skill list                         # current checkout + global
10	dev skill list --repo api --project    # one repository/checkout
11	dev skill list --all                   # canonical repositories + global once
12	dev skill list --all --check --json    # explicit upstream freshness check
13	```
14	
15	Project/global copies of one skill remain separate rows. Repository identity,
16	logical installations, compatible agent paths, local presence/integrity, source,
17	and update freshness are reported independently.
18	
19	## Where the data comes from
20	
21	Reads are native. `dev` scans a versioned snapshot of all 77 paths in the
22	`skills@1.5.23` registry plus project/global lock files. It never runs `skills`,
23	Node, npm, `npx`, agent detectors, or project code to list inventory. Shared
24	paths such as `.agents/skills` report registry compatibility; they do not claim
25	the corresponding agent executables are installed.
26	
27	Project scope defaults to the exact current checkout, including a linked
28	worktree. `--all` scans canonical configured repositories. The TUI reuses its
29	accepted REPOS snapshot and additionally includes the startup checkout when it
30	is a distinct linked worktree. Global paths are scanned once.
31	
32	A missing lock is normal. Malformed, unreadable, oversized, unsupported, or
33	ambiguous lock data is diagnosed without hiding valid neighboring rows. Absolute
34	`$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json` is the global lock when configured;
35	otherwise `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` is used.
36	
37	## Freshness and integrity
38	
39	Listing is local-only. `--check` (or TUI `c`) is the explicit network operation:
40	it groups equal Git source/ref pairs and compares Git tree/blob object bytes with
41	the lock-recorded hash without checking out remote content or modifying installed
42	files/locks. Checkout filters and `core.autocrlf` therefore cannot execute or alter
43	the comparison. Provider folder hashes containing non-ASCII paths are reported
44	unverifiable because upstream `localeCompare` ordering is locale-dependent.
45	
46	`current` therefore means upstream still matches the lock record. It does not
47	prove installed bytes are intact. Presence is tracked separately, and only the
48	embedded `dev-cli` skill can verify that every bundled file matches; additional user files are not treated as drift.
49	
50	## Updating
51	
52	```bash
53	dev skill add
54	dev skill update <name> --project [--repo api]
55	dev skill update <name> --global
56	```
57	
58	Only explicit add/install/update operations invoke the provider to change
59	skills. They require a directly installed `skills` executable and may access the
60	network; `dev doctor` may separately run that trusted executable's `--version`
61	probe. `dev` never invokes `npx` from a repository checkout, so a local
62	`node_modules/.bin/skills` cannot substitute for the provider; an ineligible PATH
63	shim is skipped when a later trusted executable exists. Unknown/source-less lock
64	entries are not mutation-eligible, and cooperating `dev` processes serialize the
65	entire provider run. Updates require one explicit scope and confirmation (or
66	`--yes`); no bulk update is implied by inventory.
67	
68	`dev doctor` reports native inventory separately from the optional mutation
69	provider.
70	
71	## dev's own skill is different
72	
73	The `dev-cli` skill is compiled into the binary. It updates when `dev` updates,
74	not through the upstream provider, and `make install` links it into agent
75	directories. The inventory marks it as directly managed and can verify its local
76	content against the embedded files.
77

1	// Package lockx provides a cross-platform advisory lock over a directory.
2	//
3	// It is a leaf package on purpose. Both the catalog store and Git transaction
4	// code need to serialize mutations, and neither should have to depend on the
5	// other to get a lock.
6	package lockx
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"os"
13		"path/filepath"
14		"sync"
15	)
16	
17	// Lease holds one acquired directory lock until Close. Close is idempotent.
18	type Lease struct {
19		lock  *fileLock
20		label string
21		once  sync.Once
22		err   error
23	}
24	
25	// AcquireDir acquires the same cross-process lock used by WithDir. The lock file
26	// lives beside dir rather than inside it, so locking never adds a file to the
27	// directory being protected.
28	func AcquireDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (*Lease, error) {
29		if ctx == nil {
30			ctx = context.Background()
31		}
32		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
33			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
34		}
35		absoluteDir, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
36		if err != nil {
37			return nil, fmt.Errorf("make %s directory absolute for lock: %w", label, err)
38		}
39		canonicalDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absoluteDir)
40		if err != nil {
41			return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
42		}
43		lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")
44		lock, err := acquire(ctx, lockPath)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, fmt.Errorf("acquire %s lock: %w", label, err)
47		}
48		return &Lease{lock: lock, label: label}, nil
49	}
50	
51	// Close releases the acquired directory lock.
52	func (l *Lease) Close() error {
53		if l == nil {
54			return nil
55		}
56		l.once.Do(func() {
57			if err := l.lock.Close(); err != nil {
58				l.err = fmt.Errorf("release %s lock: %w", l.label, err)
59			}
60		})
61		return l.err
62	}
63	
64	// WithDir runs operation while holding an exclusive lock for dir.
65	func WithDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string, operation func() error) (err error) {
66		if operation == nil {
67			return fmt.Errorf("%s lock requires an operation", label)
68		}
69		lease, err := AcquireDir(ctx, dir, label)
70		if err != nil {
71			return err
72		}
73		defer func() { err = errors.Join(err, lease.Close()) }()
74		return operation()
75	}
76

1	//go:build unix

3	package lockx
4	
5	import (
6		"context"
7		"errors"
8		"os"
9		"time"
10	
11		"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
12	)
13	
14	type fileLock struct {
15		file *os.File
16	}
17	
18	func acquire(ctx context.Context, path string) (*fileLock, error) {
19		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
20			return nil, err
21		}
22		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
23		if err != nil {
24			return nil, err
25		}
26		lock := &fileLock{file: file}
27		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
28		defer ticker.Stop()
29		for {
30			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
31				_ = file.Close()
32				return nil, err
33			}
34			err = unix.Flock(int(file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_EX|unix.LOCK_NB)
35			if err == nil {
36				return lock, nil
37			}
38			if !errors.Is(err, unix.EWOULDBLOCK) && !errors.Is(err, unix.EAGAIN) && !errors.Is(err, unix.EINTR) {
39				_ = file.Close()
40				return nil, err
41			}
42			select {
43			case <-ctx.Done():
44				_ = file.Close()
45				return nil, ctx.Err()
46			case <-ticker.C:
47			}
48		}
49	}
50	
51	func (l *fileLock) Close() error {
52		unlockErr := unix.Flock(int(l.file.Fd()), unix.LOCK_UN)
53		return errors.Join(unlockErr, l.file.Close())
54	}
55

12	)
13	
14	type fileLock struct {
15		file       *os.File
16		overlapped windows.Overlapped
17	}
18	
19	func acquire(ctx context.Context, path string) (*fileLock, error) {
20		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
21			return nil, err
22		}
23		file, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o600)
24		if err != nil {
25			return nil, err
26		}
27		lock := &fileLock{file: file}
28		ticker := time.NewTicker(10 * time.Millisecond)
29		defer ticker.Stop()
30		for {
31			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
32				_ = file.Close()
33				return nil, err
34			}
35			err = windows.LockFileEx(windows.Handle(file.Fd()),
36				windows.LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK|windows.LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY,
37				0, 1, 0, &lock.overlapped)
38			if err == nil {
39				return lock, nil
40			}
41			if !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION) && !errors.Is(err, windows.ERROR_IO_PENDING) {
42				_ = file.Close()
43				return nil, err
44			}
45			select {
46			case <-ctx.Done():
47				_ = file.Close()
48				return nil, ctx.Err()
49			case <-ticker.C:
50			}
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func (l *fileLock) Close() error {
55		unlockErr := windows.UnlockFileEx(windows.Handle(l.file.Fd()), 0, 1, 0, &l.overlapped)
56		return errors.Join(unlockErr, l.file.Close())
57	}

148	// send feeds a sequence of key presses through Update, running any command the
149	// model returns so the action callbacks actually fire — that is what makes
150	// these tests exercise the real key bindings rather than the model's fields.
151	func send(m tui.Model, msgs ...tea.Msg) tui.Model {
152		var cur tea.Model = m
153		for _, msg := range msgs {
154			var cmd tea.Cmd
155			cur, cmd = cur.Update(msg)
156			// Follow the command chain, so an action's resulting message (and the
157			// reload it triggers) is applied too. Commands that do not return
158			// promptly are the cursor's blink timers; running those would make the
159			// suite sleep for half a second per keystroke.
160			for i := 0; cmd != nil && i < 8; i++ {
161				out, ok := runQuickly(cmd)
162				if !ok || out == nil {
163					break
164				}
165				if _, isBatch := out.(tea.BatchMsg); isBatch {
166					break
167				}
168				cur, cmd = cur.Update(out)
169			}
170		}
171		return cur.(tui.Model)
172	}
173	
174	// runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
175	// practice means the cursor blink timers.
176	func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
177		done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
178		go func() { done <- cmd() }()
179		select {
180		case msg := <-done:
181			return msg, true
182		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
183			return nil, false
184		}
185	}
186

191		case "esc":

193		case "down":
194			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown}
195		case "up":
196			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp}
197		}
198		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(s)}
199	}

207		}

198		r.recordLocked(name, fields, now, 0)

203	// once is harmless.
204	func (r *Recorder) Start(name Name, fields Fields) func(Outcome) {
205		if r == nil {
206			return func(Outcome) {}
207		}
208		started := r.clock()
209		var once sync.Once
210		return func(outcome Outcome) {
211			once.Do(func() {
212				fields.Outcome = outcome
213				finished := r.clock()
214				duration := finished.Sub(started)
215				duration = max(duration, 0)
216				r.record(name, fields, started, duration)

21	// CollectAgentSkills scans each repository target through the shared local

23	// checks across the complete result.
24	func CollectAgentSkills(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options AgentSkillOptions) (agentskill.Result, error) {
25		if ctx == nil {
26			ctx = context.Background()
27		}
28		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
29		if !project && !global {
30			project, global = true, true
31		}
32		targets = agenttarget.Dedupe(targets)
33		partCount := 0
34		if project {
35			partCount += len(targets)
36		}
37		globalIndex := -1
38		if global {
39			globalIndex = partCount
40			partCount++
41		}
42		parts := make([]agentskill.Result, partCount)
43		errs := make([]error, partCount)
44		limiter := options.Limiter
45		if limiter == nil {
46			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
47		}
48	
49		var wait sync.WaitGroup
50		launch := func(index int, scan func() (agentskill.Result, error)) {
51			wait.Go(func() {
52				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
53				if !ok {
54					errs[index] = ctx.Err()
55					return
56				}
57				defer release()
58				parts[index], errs[index] = scan()
59			})
60		}
61		if project {
62			for index, target := range targets {
63				target := target
64				launch(index, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
65					return agentskill.Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, agentskill.ListOptions{Project: true})
66				})
67			}
68		}
69		if global {
70			launch(globalIndex, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
71				return agentskill.Scan(ctx, nil, agentskill.ListOptions{Global: true})
72			})
73		}
74		wait.Wait()
75	
76		result := agentskill.MergeResults(parts...)
77		if options.Check && ctx.Err() == nil {
78			result.Skills = agentskill.CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
79		}
80		joined := errors.Join(errs...)
81		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
82			joined = errors.Join(joined, ctxErr)
83		}
84		return result, joined
85	}

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-02 07:20:14Z)**_

- `internal/agentmcp/scanner.go:351-355` — `normalizeOptions` compacts `ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths` into the caller’s existing slice backing array. Concurrent independent `NewScanner(options)` calls sharing one `Options` value produce a confirmed race between lines 352 and 354. Reproduction: synchronize multiple goroutines calling `NewScanner` with the same nonempty `ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths` slice and run under `go test -race`; the detector reports concurrent reads/writes in `normalizeOptions`.

- `internal/agentskill/agentskill.go:299-307` — mutation eligibility accepts any nonempty `SkillPath` rather than applying `safeSkillFolder` from `internal/agentskill/update.go:385-408`. Reproduction: a lock with `Name: "demo"`, `SourceType: "github"`, `Source: "owner/repo"`, and `SkillPath: "../../outside/SKILL.md"` makes `lockUpdateable` and `CanUpdate` return true, although `safeSkillFolder` rejects the path. Consequently `ManagedName` treats the malformed entry as provider-updateable and allows it through the mutation gate.
